Terminal AI coding agent, inspired by charmbracelet/crush. It talks to eleven provider type keys over nine engines, runs thirty-eight built-in tools on every launch behind hooks and a six-mode permission gate, keeps per-turn workspace checkpoints with undo and rewind, prunes and compacts its own context, runs sub-agents you can watch and message, and reads skills, memory, MCP servers, workflows and SQLite-backed sessions. It also serves a WebSocket API with a browser UI and an Agent Client Protocol agent for editors, all on the sugar-core render loop with Markdown replies. With no configuration it runs offline on the built-in echo provider.

Install

composer require sugarcraft/candy-code

Requires PHP ^8.3. The package declares its sugarcraft/* siblings with the @dev constraint (composer.json), so a host project must allow dev-stability packages: set "minimum-stability": "dev" with "prefer-stable": true in that host, or run it from a checkout of the monorepo. The package's own composer.json declares both keys (lines 111-112), but Composer reads stability settings from the root project only, so that declaration does not reach a host. A container build is described in docs/DOCKER.md.

Quickstart

Step 1. Run it with nothing configured. The binary falls back to the offline echo provider, so no network and no key are needed. This is the output of a real run, captured with no provider environment and an empty HOME:

$ candy-code -p "explain the Width helper"
You said:

> explain the Width helper

The line candy-code: no provider configured (…); answering from the offline echo provider. goes to stderr, which is why it is not in the output above. -p is the one-shot mode: it never attaches to the terminal and never opens the alternate screen. Run candy-code with no arguments for the full TUI.

Step 2. Point it at a real model. The provider is chosen by CANDY_CODE_PROVIDER, and the provider's own environment variables supply the key (see the providers table below):

export CANDY_CODE_PROVIDER=openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
export CANDY_CODE_MODEL=gpt-4o     # optional; the provider default otherwise
candy-code

A provider run needs a key and network access, so its output is not captured on this page. The offline run above is the reference output.

Step 3. One-shot with JSON output, for scripts. The unattended -p mode starts in the default permission mode and refuses any tool call that would ask, so pass --permission-mode when a script needs tools. This is the captured output (the session_id differs on every run):

$ candy-code -p "audit this" --output-format json
{"schema":1,"result":"You said:\n\n> audit this","refusals":[],"session_id":"3b8c2910e15dae8b"}

$ candy-code -p "audit this" --output-format json | jq -r .result
You said:

> audit this

For a provider-free backend, CANDY_CODE_BACKEND_CMD names a script that reads the JSON history on stdin and writes the reply to stdout; CANDY_CODE_BACKEND_CMD_STREAM is the token-stream variant. Every variable is listed in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md. The step-by-step first run is in docs/TUTORIAL.md.

What it is

Eleven type keys, nine enginesOne ProviderInterface with capability introspection (supportsStreaming(), supportsVision(), contextWindow(), costPer1kTokens()), streaming, function calling and embeddings. OpenAI and Azure share one engine; Anthropic, Claude Code CLI, Codex, SGLang, Bedrock, Vertex, Gemini, and custom (with OpenRouter as a preset) make up the rest. The Claude Code and Codex routes run each turn inside the vendor's own signed-in CLI.
Bounded agent loopEngineBackend::complete() calls the provider, runs the returned tool calls through the hook gate, feeds results back, and repeats until the model answers without calling a tool or maxSteps is reached.
Thirty-eight built-in tools on every launchShell, file read, edit and write, ApplyPatch (multi-file patches, all or nothing), search, web fetch and search, skills, language server queries (Lsp), memory, repo map, todo, context pruning and compression, workflows, team board, user questions, plan exit, schedules, sub-agent messaging, media generation, canvas pages, scripts, and background and interactive shells. Path tools are jailed to the project root, plus any read-only roots in the user-tier references setting, and an edit is refused on a file that changed since it was read. Six more tools join only when their condition holds; the full list is in the tools section. Implement Tools\Tool for your own.
Hooks that can say noPre- and post-tool-use guards return allow, deny, modify or ask. Built-ins are ProtectFilesHook, ConfirmRemoveHook and AuditHook (registered by HookManager::registerBuiltIns()), plus BashEscapeDenyHook when a worktree root is set, and PermissionGateHook last, which adapts the six-mode PermissionGate onto the same chain. Hooks load from YAML, and an external ScriptHook chooses its outcome by exit code.
Progressive skillsFrontmatter SKILL.md files inject prompt context. The system prompt carries only each skill's name and description; the model loads a full body through the Skill tool. Ten built-ins ship with the app, and you can add more under ~/.candy-code/skills and <project>/.candy-code/skills, or import them from Claude Code and opencode.
Sub-agents, teams & worktreesThe Task tool delegates to agent presets, each with its own model, tools, skills and permission mode. Runs can go in parallel, nest, run in the background, or run in a git worktree of their own, and each one can be resumed. Each run gets a live line, an agents strip and an Agent View with its own transcript, where you can message, pause, cancel, or send it to the background with Ctrl+X b. SendMessage, Subagents and InterruptAgent steer sub-agents, a parallel batch shares a board, and teammates claim tasks from a shared SQLite board through the Team tool.
WorkflowsWorkflowEngine runs multi-stage agent pipelines (sequential, fan-out parallel, chained, and task-then-verifier) from a PHP DSL or YAML. A run can be paused at a stage boundary and resumed, each task can name its own agent preset, and hard token and cost budgets pause a run when they are reached.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) client & hostA multi-server client over stdio and HTTP reads .mcp.json, with ${VAR} interpolation. A project's servers start only after you trust them. The stdio host, candy-code mcp serve, exposes a fixed read-only tool roster (Read, Glob, Grep, Ls, RepoMap) to the client that spawns it. Per-preset mcpServers allowlists are enforced.
SQLite sessionsSessions, messages and tool calls persist in a WAL-mode SQLite database (~/.candy-code/session.db), with foreign-key cascades and fork, rename and resume. Opt-in retention (sessionRetentionDays) removes sessions idle for that long that have no name you gave them, skipping pinned and sub-agent sessions. A title the model generated does not count as a name, so those sessions are removed too. The database is not encrypted.
Context engineCompaction tiers with absolute token caps, summaries requested ahead of need, in-turn pruning of stale tool output, the agent's own Prune, Compress and Recall tools, re-injection after a compaction, and recovery from context overflows, cut-off replies and dropped streams.
Permissions & checkpointsSix permission modes, with rules that match a tool name and an optional argument glob. The TUI asks by default. Alt+M toggles plan mode, and the model leaves plan mode with PlanExit, which puts its plan to you for approval. Shell lines proven read-only, such as simple sed scripts that only read or for and while read loops over read-only bodies, run unasked when permissions.autoAllowReadOnly is on. A per-turn workspace checkpoint sits behind /undo, /redo, /rewind and /diff. An optional sandbox confines Bash: Seatbelt on macOS and Bubblewrap elsewhere, and it is off by default. See permissions and safety.
MemoryNotes are indexed into the prompt. A Memory tool saves, edits, deletes and recalls them with BM25 ranking, and the agent consolidates memory at the end of a turn, with a periodic review pass. A git history of the memory directory lets you restore an earlier state.
Server mode & web UIcandy-code serve runs sessions headless behind an authenticated WebSocket that speaks candy-code.v1. The CandyCodeWeb browser UI and candy-code attach drive those sessions. Remote access is gated by --allowed-host and --allowed-ips, and --allow-dir-browse (confined to --browse-root) lets a client pick a project directory for a new session. candy-code acp serves editors over the Agent Client Protocol on stdio.
Prompts from anywhere@file, @diff and @https://… attachments, $skill mentions for one turn, !command shell lines, opt-in AI! comments saved in your editor, /handoff into a fresh session seeded with a state summary, and /newrule to draft a project rule from the conversation.
Model–Update–View render loopA sugar-core Model and Program tree with buffer-diffed output: Markdown-rendered replies through SugarMarkdown, a live tool-call lifecycle, unified diffs for Edit results, inline images through sugar-image, mouse zones and text selection through sugar-mouse, and a command palette with fuzzy filtering.

Providers and models

Select a provider with CANDY_CODE_PROVIDER, which accepts openai, azure, anthropic, claude-code, codex, sglang, bedrock, vertex, gemini, openrouter or custom — the eleven type keys in the table below — or with a provider entry in ~/.candy-code/config.json, or from the /model command, which persists the choice. Each type's required and optional keys are validated by ProviderFactory (TYPE_SCHEMAS), and each type's environment reads are in ProviderFactory::defaultConfig(). The engine column names the class that serves the type. Full per-provider setup is in docs/PROVIDERS.md, and adding a new type is covered in docs/ADDING_A_PROVIDER.md.

Type keyEngine (class)EnvironmentDefault model
openaiOpenAIProviderOPENAI_API_KEY (required), OPENAI_ORG_ID, OPENAI_BASE_URLgpt-4o
azureOpenAIProviderAZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY; a resource or a full baseUrl in configgpt-4o
anthropicAnthropicProviderANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URLclaude-sonnet-4-6
claude-codeClaudeCodeProvidernone; runs the signed-in claude CLI (claudePath, default claude)claude-sonnet-4-6
codexCodexProvidernone; runs the signed-in codex CLI (codexPath, default codex)gpt-5.1-codex-mini
sglangSglangProviderOPENAI_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:30000), optional SGLANG_API_KEYQwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8
bedrockBedrockProviderAWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION (default us-east-1)us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
vertexVertexProviderGCP_PROJECT_ID (required); location defaults to us-central1claude-sonnet-4-6
geminiGeminiProviderGEMINI_API_KEY, GEMINI_BASE_URLgemini-2.5-flash
openrouterCustomProvider (OpenAI-compatible preset)OPENROUTER_API_KEYopenai/gpt-4o
customCustomProviderOPENAI_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8080); in config, name, baseUrl and model are requiredgpt-4o

Types that have a cheaper auxiliary model for titles and other small calls: anthropic and vertex (claude-haiku-4-5), bedrock (us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5) and openai (gpt-4o-mini), per ProviderFactory::AUXILIARY_MODEL_BY_TYPE. CANDY_CODE_MODEL overrides the conversation model for whichever provider runs.

A "running" placeholder in a saved transcript is a tool call whose process is gone, so it comes back as the same "interrupted" error row reviveCheckpointMessage() makes for /rewind; left as a placeholder it would spin forever for a result that cannot arrive.

enqueueToolEvent(ToolStarted|ToolFinished $event, ?int $generation = null): voidAppend a tool-lifecycle event to the live inbox ($liveToolEvents).
liveToolEvents(): arrayTool-lifecycle events queued by the backend but not yet folded into the transcript, oldest first.
enqueueToken(string $text, ?int $generation = null): voidAppend one fragment of assistant text to the live inbox ($liveToolEvents) — the text counterpart of enqueueToolEvent(), written through by a Backend's $onToken callback (Phase 0 item 13).

streamingText(): stringThe in-flight reply as far as it has arrived; empty outside a turn, and outside a turn the model has actually started answering.
reasoningText(): stringThe model's thinking for the current step as far as it has arrived; empty outside a turn, and outside a turn whose backend reports reasoning at all.
queuedPrompts(): arrayPrompts typed and sent while a turn was in flight, oldest first — see the constructor param's docblock.
withReadLedger(\SugarCraft\Code\Tools\ReadLedger $ledger): selfName the session read ledger (roadmap 3.I-2) the tools this Chat runs record into — the \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\ReadLedger an embedder's registerTool() callbacks' Read/Edit/Write/ ApplyPatch share. Each Chat-native call runs in its own forked child (forkToolCalls()), whose copy of the ledger dies with it; with the ledger named here the child carries what it recorded home on its result payload and collectToolResult() merges it, so a file read by one call is known to the next call's staleness check.
readLedger(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Tools\ReadLedgerThe read ledger withReadLedger() named, or null when none was.
view(): string|\SugarCraft\Core\ViewReturns the full literal frame every call. This used to compute its own cell-level diff (via Buffer/DiffEncoder) and return only the changed bytes - but Program (see bin/candy-code, a plain new Program(Bootstrap::chat(), ...)) ALSO diffs whatever a Model's view() returns, line-by-line, against the previous call's return value (sugar-core's own Renderer::render(), which every other Model in this framework relies on for exactly this). Chat's pre-diffed cursor-jump escape bytes were never literal display text, so Program's Renderer was diffing one diff's raw bytes against the previous diff's raw bytes as if they were screen content - any time the two differed (i.e. almost always) that produced cursor placement that had no relationship to the actual frame, which is what made typed input / replies appear to land in the wrong row (e.g. the status bar) once a conversation grew past a single frame. Program's Renderer already does correct, safe diffing on real text; doing it a second time here was redundant at best.
backgroundJobCount(): intBackground work this session can still see: sessions the supervisor reports active, plus the shells this session owns (or the untagged ones) that are running. Counted per paint, so a finished job drops off the status bar on the next frame.
static mouseMode(): MouseModeHow the terminal is asked to report mouse events (§8 E1).
static mouseClicksEnabled(): boolWhether click/drag hit-testing is live. False when either CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE (no tracking at all) or CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS (clicks off, wheel kept) is set, or the mouse / mouseClicks setting is off (roadmap N-P4g).
static zoneAt(int $col, int $row): ?ZoneThe marked zone under a reported pointer cell, or null when there is none — the one hit-test entry point every future click handler goes through, so CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS is enforced in exactly one place instead of at each call site.
static clickTracker(): ZoneClickTrackerThe shared Press+Release pairing state machine (sugar-mouse's ZoneClickTracker), which is what makes a press on a tab followed by a release somewhere else — a drag, or a text selection started on the tab strip — dispatch nothing instead of switching sessions.
static textSelection(): ?TextSelectionThe mouse text selection in progress or just copied, or null.
static textSelectionInProgress(): boolTrue between a press that anchored a selection and its release.
static clearTextSelection(): voidDrop any selection; for tests and for hosts that stop painting the chat.
scrollOffset(): intHow far back the transcript is scrolled, in lines from the newest one. 0 means pinned to the bottom. Read by Renderer::render().
withScrollOffset(int $offset): selfScroll the transcript back $offset lines from the newest one.
static programOptions(): ProgramOptionsRuntime options bin/candy-code starts the chat Program with. Exists so the mouse-mode decision above is made once, next to the state it governs, instead of being duplicated in the entrypoint script.
backend(): Backend
withBackend(Backend $backend): selfSwap the backend — also the live half of a settings save that rebuilds the engine (applySettings()), which only ever calls this between turns: the completion handlers of a running turn close over the backend it started on.
applySettings(array $changed, ?string $savedTo = null): arrayMake a settings save take effect (roadmap N-P3, Appendix N §4.6): each changed key goes by its \SugarCraft\Code\Config\Settings\ApplyMode.
pendingSettingsApply(): arrayThe settings keys parked until the running turn ends (applySettings()).
settingsToast(): ?\SugarCraft\Toast\ToastThe settings-save toast to paint, or null (applySettings()).
agentPoolConfig(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentPoolConfigGet the agent pool config, if set.
pool(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentWorkerPoolGet the effective worker pool, if set.
workspace(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Host\WorkspaceContextThe launch's workspace — the host services (Appendix O §4.3) this Chat resolves — or null for a Chat built without one (tests, embedders).
agentManager(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentManagerGet the agent manager, if set.
backgroundSupervisor(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSupervisorThe background-session supervisor /bg and /fork dispatch onto, if set.
withBackgroundSupervisor(?\SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSupervisor $supervisor): selfAttach the supervisor /bg and /fork spawn onto.
withScheduleRegistry(?\SugarCraft\Code\Background\ScheduleRegistry $registry): selfWire the AUT-1 roster (see the constructor note: shared by IDENTITY, like the supervisor — a wither clone must keep pointing at the same clock, or the /schedules surface and the pump diverge).
scheduleRegistry(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Background\ScheduleRegistryThe AUT-1 roster this session fires from, if any.
memoryStore(): ?MemoryStoreGet the memory store, if set.
rulesState(): RulesStateThe session's rulebook toggle set — the state /rules reads and writes (P6.S3).
projectRoot(): stringThe directory this session is rooted at, already resolved — the configured $projectRoot (--root), else the process directory.
sessionStore(): \SugarCraft\Code\Session\SessionStore|\SugarCraft\Code\Session\EnhancedSessionStore|nullGet the session store, if set.
incognito(): boolWhether this launch keeps nothing (C-SES-7.c, --incognito).
withSessionStore(\SugarCraft\Code\Session\SessionStore|\SugarCraft\Code\Session\EnhancedSessionStore|null $sessionStore): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit session store.
currentSessionId(): ?stringGet the current session ID, if any.
openTabs(): SessionTabsThe tabs opened this run (ISS-102): the model Renderer's session tab strip renders and cycleSessionTab() switches through. Thin delegate onto the SessionTabState fold (v4 S3) — the renderer keeps reading this entry point.
contextLedgerView(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Context\Pruning\ContextLedgerThis session's context ledger as its turn runner holds it, or null when it holds none yet (roadmap 3.B-3) — the copy the transcript's pruned / distilled badges and its compressed-block rows read. Never the store: \SugarCraft\Code\Host\TurnRunner::heldLedger() is a memory read, so Renderer may call this per frame. Kept current by every save — a turn's settle, a live ledger frame, /sweep.
measureContextCmd(): ?\ClosureP-CTX.d: schedule one context measurement OFF the loop. The pane never measures in view() — assembling prompt sections touches disk — so a settle, a landed compaction, or a dock hand hands this closure to the runner, which resolves it against the memo-backed prompt assembly and answers with a \SugarCraft\Code\App\ContextMeasuredMsg repaint nudge once \SugarCraft\Code\Host\TurnRunner::heldContext() is fresh. The state the pass reads is captured at schedule time, so a slow answer still stamps the transcript it was measured against. No wall-clock timer is armed anywhere (E646): the pass is a single prompt assembly.
withCurrentSessionId(string $currentSessionId): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit current session ID.
currentSessionName(): ?stringName of the current session, or null while it is still unnamed.
currentSessionTitleSource(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Session\TitleSourceWho set currentSessionName() — see $currentSessionTitleSource.
titleEditor(): ?\SugarCraft\Forms\TextInput\TextInputThe open inline session-title editor, or null — read by Renderer.
withCurrentSessionName(?string $currentSessionName): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit session name. Passing null clears the name, which re-arms the one-shot auto-title.
withTitleBackend(?Backend $titleBackend): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit small-model Backend used only for the background session-title call. See the constructor's $titleBackend docblock for why it is deliberately a separate instance from the conversation backend.
workerPool(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentWorkerPoolBackward-compatible alias for pool().
executeAgents(array $agents, \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\CompleteRequest $request): \GeneratorExecute multiple agents in parallel via the worker pool.
withWorkerPool(\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentWorkerPool $pool): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit worker pool.
withAgentPoolConfig(\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentPoolConfig $config): selfCreate a new Chat with an agent pool config (used to build the worker pool on demand).
withMemoryStore(MemoryStore $memoryStore): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit memory store.
withWorkflowEngine(WorkflowEngineInterface $engine): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit workflow engine.
workflowEngine(): ?WorkflowEngineInterfaceGet the workflow engine, if set.
mosaic(): ?\SugarCraft\Image\MosaicGet the shared sugar-image probe-once capability instance, if wired (see this class's $mosaic constructor docblock, W1.G2/E2).
hooks(): ?HookManagerThe hook chain gating this Chat's own tool calls, if wired (see the $hooks constructor docblock).
withHooks(HookManager $hooks): selfGate this Chat's registerTool() calls through $hooks, the same HookManager the engine pipeline already runs its calls through (§1 E1).
expanded(): arrayTool-call ids whose output the user has expanded (§1 E5). Renderer::render() reads this to decide which tool bodies to paint in full; ids absent from the map are collapsed.
isToolOutputExpanded(string $id): boolTrue when $id's tool output is currently expanded: its entry in the expanded map, else the default — collapsed, or expanded for a tool call under the expandToolOutput setting (expandedByDefault()).
toggleToolOutput(string $id): selfFlip one tool call's collapsed/expanded state. Returning a call to its default REMOVES the key - see the constructor's $expanded docblock for why the map only ever holds what the user changed.
static isDeniedResult(ToolResult $result): boolTrue when $result is a refusal - a call the user or a hook stopped - rather than a call that ran and failed.
static isInterruptedResult(ToolResult $result): boolTrue when $result stands in for a tool call that never finished because the process running it went away - see reviveCheckpointMessage(). Distinct from isDeniedResult(): nobody refused this call, it simply lost its runner, and the two deserve different words on screen.
static reviveCheckpointMessage(array $row): MessageRebuild one checkpointed history row into a Message, healing a checkpoint that was taken while a tool call was still in flight (§1 E7).
latestThoughtKey(): ?stringThe $expanded key of the newest thought on screen, or null when there is none: the in-flight thought (Renderer::THOUGHT_LIVE_KEY) while one is being written, otherwise the newest history entry carrying reasoning - a settled reply, or a tool row (or its running placeholder) the thought was parked on. Public because Renderer offers the Ctrl+O hint on exactly the row this names.
lastActivityAt(): ?\DateTimeImmutableTimestamp of the last real user prompt submitted through submit(), or null if none has been recorded yet on this instance.
withLastActivity(\DateTimeImmutable $lastActivityAt): selfCreate a new Chat with an explicit last-activity timestamp. Mainly useful for tests that need to simulate an idle session.
resumeCostGuardArmed(): boolC-SES-7.d: whether the next real prompt will be cost-checked as a resume re-send (see the field docblock). Read by the guard in submit() and pinned by the guard's tests.
liveStep(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Events\StepStartedThe step the turn on screen last reported (roadmap 1.C-4), or null when no turn is running or the running one reports no steps (a command backend, a workflow, the echo default).
liveUsage(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Events\UsageUpdatedThe usage the turn on screen last reported (roadmap 1.C-4); null as for liveStep().
stopRequested(): boolWhether the turn on screen has been asked to stop at its next step boundary (first Escape).
withStreaming(bool $enable): self
onToken(callable $callback): self
registerTool(string $name, callable $callback): selfRegister a tool callback the AI can call on this Chat: the name joins the Chat's own tool map, which invokeTool() consults and runs at dispatch. The shipped CLI registers nothing here — its tools reach the model as catalogued tool classes wired onto the backend — so this seam is filled only by embedders. Registration is immutable: a new Chat carrying the merged map is returned.
onToolCall(callable $callback): selfRegister a callback for tool call events.
withOnConfigChange(callable $callback): selfRegister a callback(string $key, string $value): void fired when any of FOUR DOORS applies a choice: the Ctrl+P palette's Switch Model row, /model <provider>, the palette's Switch Theme row, and /theme <name>.
withLaunchNotices(array $notices): selfSeed the transcript with the warnings a LAUNCH produced, so they are readable from inside the alt screen.
withNoticeDrain(bool $drains): selfAppoints (or dismisses) this Chat as the reader of the shared runtime notice inbox — the drainsRuntimeNotices field's flag, moved.
isStreaming(): bool
tools(): array
getTools(): arrayBC forwarder for the pre-rename accessor name.
queueOwnsTab(): boolWhether a bare Tab QUEUES the draft for after the running turn (roadmap 1.C-3, chat.queue) — the follow-up half of "Enter steers, Tab queues" (Codex, nanobot). Only mid-turn, with a draft that would be sent (not a slash command, which is refused mid-turn), and only when neither completion owns Tab and no modal is up — the same reachability contract as slashMenuOwnsTab(): the shell yields Tab on exactly this predicate, so a yielded Tab always lands on a live arm.
runCommand(string $commandText): arrayRun a command line on the user's behalf — a menu-bar row, Ctrl+N, the shell's provider picker — WITHOUT touching the draft.
runPaletteAction(string $label): arrayRun a palette-only action (a CommandRegistry row flagged slashVisible: false, e.g. "New session") on the user's behalf, by its palette label — the runCommand() twin for rows submit() has no arm for.
abandonActiveHookGroups(): intQuit reaps the hook processes still running, the same way \SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentWorkerPool::cancelAll() reaps its workers: SIGTERM the group, then SIGKILL after a 2-second grace if it has not gone. The grace runs on the loop, so the quit is not held up by it.
static reportField(string $value): stringOne caller-supplied value, made safe to be PART OF A REPORT LINE — see \SugarCraft\Code\Host\Commands\PermissionsCommand::reportField(), where the /permissions report moved (roadmap O-2h). Kept here because Commands\NoticesCommand, Commands\MemoryHistoryCommand and the provider switch's report all render through this name.
switchProvider(string $provider): arrayThe public twin of the /model <provider> command for the shell (C-TUI-5.e): the first-run wizard's Finish hands the provider it chose through this door, so the wizard and the slash command are one path and cannot drift — the workspace rebuild, the persistence hook and the model-catalog priming all live in the command and ride here.
promptSuggestion(): ?stringThe grayed suggestion the empty input box shows, or null when there is none to show: none has arrived, a turn is running, or the conversation has moved since it was written (see the $promptSuggestion docblock).
primaryAgentName(): ?stringThe roster preset this session runs as its PRIMARY agent, or null when it runs the plain launch default (C-AGT-4.b). The status line's agent badge reads this; so does the Alt+A cycle, to know where it stands.
withLaunchPrimaryAgent(string $name): selfApply --agent <name> at launch — C3 (RS-AGENT). This is NOT a second switch: it travels switchPrimaryAgent() with $echo on, so the flag, /agent use <name> and Alt+A share one code path, one roster, one refusal vocabulary (unknown name answers with the same host.agents.use_unknown transcript row). A launch has no turn in flight, so the mid-turn door can only pass; a refused name leaves the plain default agent in place and costs nothing but the row.
shouldWatchIdleCompaction(): boolWhether the idle auto-compaction watch (CTX-5, compaction.idleAuto) should have a tick running. The membership gate for \SugarCraft\Code\App\App::subscriptions()'s keyed tick — deliberately reading only SESSION-scoped state, never the transcript's size: a session that could fold asks occasionally, and whether THIS minute is a folding minute is the tick's own re-check.
sessionPicker(): ?SessionPickerThe open session picker overlay, or null when it is closed.
rewindToCheckpoint(int $stepsBack): arrayRewind the conversation to the checkpoint N prompts back — the message picker's Accept chord (C-TUI-3.d). One row is one step back, the same newest-first counting \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\MessagePicker\MessagePicker::open() gives its rows, and the restore seeds the checkpoint's prompt into the composer exactly as the typed /rewind N --chat does (handleRewindCommand(), applyCommandResult()).
expandPasteChips(string $text): stringISS-051: replace every chip in $text with the payload it filed. Called by each reader that sends the draft's text — submit, queue, the AskUser/permission answer, the scope editor and the agent-mailbox send — so the model and the transcript never see the marker. CC-QA-5: the match is STRUCTURAL, not byte-exact — a bracketed run carrying a filed '#N' id and a '+' count tail expands even after a caret splice or a width rewrap moved a character inside the chip; silently dropping the payload behind one mis-clicked key was the defect. Text whose id was never filed — hand-typed chip shapes included — survives literally.
inputCursorOffset(): intWhere the cursor is in $inputBuf, as a codepoint offset from the start of the whole draft (newlines counted as one codepoint each).
draft(): arrayThe composer's state as the shell's window stash saves it (P-AGENT.b): the draft text and the flat caret offset — the two halves withDraft() puts back. A snapshot of the same pair Renderer::renderInput() and the checkpoint capture see.
withDraft(string $text, int $cursor): selfReplace the composer's whole state (P-AGENT.b): text first through withInputBuf() — which owns the slash/mention-menu re-highlight law and the widget reseed — then the caret through the same seek the alt-chords use, so a stale cursor from a stashed viewport clamps to the restored draft instead of pointing past its end.
slashMenuMatches(): arrayCommands from CommandRegistry matching the in-progress "/name" being typed - the "/" popup's data source (Renderer::renderSlashMenu()). Returns [] (hiding the popup) when inputBuf isn't slash-prefixed, or once it contains a space: at that point the command name is already fixed and the user is typing arguments, so there is nothing left to filter/complete.
slashCommandRows(): arrayEvery row the "/" popup and /help may list: the built-in slash-visible rows with this session's file-based commands merged over them by NAME.
customCommands(): arrayThe file-based commands this session discovered, name => spec.
slashMenuMatchResults(): arrayslashMenuMatches()'s rows with their matched-character indices kept, in the SAME order and the same length - the spec list is derived from this one inside CommandRegistry::filter(), so the two cannot fall out of step.
slashMenuIndex(): intThe "/" popup's currently-highlighted row index into slashMenuMatches()'s current result - always in range for it, never needs clamping by a caller (see withInputBuf()'s docblock).
slashMenuOwnsTab(): boolWhether a bare Tab completes the "/" popup's highlighted row RIGHT NOW.
mentionOwnsTab(): boolWhether a bare Tab completes an @file mention — or a $skill one (roadmap 5.14l) — rather than cycling panes: the caret ends such a token in the draft and no modal is up. The modal guards are slashMenuOwnsTab()'s four, for the reason its docblock gives - a shell that yields Tab on a condition update() does not answer turns Tab into a dead key.
mentionPopupOpen(): boolTUI-1: whether the fuzzy @ file popup is up RIGHT NOW — the one predicate the Escape arm, the ↑/↓/Enter arms and the renderer all read, mirroring how slashMenuOwnsTab() is the one predicate both the shell's Tab yield and the completion arm read.
mentionPopupRows(): arrayThe popup's rows for the mention token under the caret, best match first (MentionIndex::rank()). Empty for a $skill token — those keep their prefix-only completion — and on a non-git root, where the cold-index fallback (FileMentions::complete() via Tab) stays the whole feature.
mentionMenuIndex(): intThe highlighted popup row, clamped — a caret move between two mention tokens can leave the stored index past the end of a shorter list.
theme(): ThemeThe active color theme, resolved from the stored name on every call - cheap (a handful of Color/Theme factory calls, no I/O) and keeps Chat's own stored state to a plain string rather than an object.
withThemeName(string $themeName): self
palette(): ?PaletteStateThe Ctrl+P command palette's current mode/query/selection, or null when closed.
paletteMatches(): arrayFuzzy-filtered (or full, when the query is empty) item labels for the palette's current mode, ranked best-match-first via SmithWatermanMatcher - the same matcher phlix-console-client's own Ctrl+P palette already uses for the same purpose - and holding only labels that contain EVERY query character in order (see $paletteMatcher). Returns [] when the palette is closed.
paletteMatchResults(): arraypaletteMatches()'s rows with their matched-character indices kept, in the SAME order - the label list is just this list's haystacks (§4 E3: the indices used to be discarded here, so Renderer::renderPalette() had nothing to highlight with and could only bold whole rows).
paletteCategory(string $label): ?stringThe grouping label ("Session", "Model", …) the palette renders above a root row, or null for a row that has none (provider/theme names).
paletteMru(): arrayPalette rows the user has run, most recent first (§4 E7).
currentPermissionMode(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionModeThe mode this session's gate runs in, or null without a gate — what the status bar's mode badge reads (Renderer).
static modeChangeNotice(\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionMode $from, \SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionMode $to): stringThe model-visible row for a switch from $from to $to: which mode now governs, that it supersedes earlier switches, and what it allows — \SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionMode::description(), the sentence /permissions shows, measured against the gate.
activeThemeName(): stringThe name of the theme in use, canonicalised to a member of Theme::names() (theme() resolves the stored spelling through Theme::byName()). The Ctrl+P themes picker reads it to mark the active row (ISS-104).
dirPicker(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Tui\DirectoryPicker\DirectoryPickerThe /new folder picker, while it is up.
historySearch(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Tui\HistorySearchThe Ctrl+G history search, while it is up (plan_comparison TUI-2).
pendingRelaunch(): ?stringThe directory /new chose to restart candy-code in, once the program has quit; null for an ordinary exit.
subscriptions(): ?\SugarCraft\Core\SubscriptionsDeclare the recurring work this model needs the runtime to drive (section 5 E4).
backgroundStatuses(): arrayLast status reported to the user for each background session, keyed by session id.
rows(): intReal terminal row count, from the last WindowSizeMsg this Chat received - falls back to TuiRenderer::terminalSize()'s own detection only when no WindowSizeMsg has arrived yet (a Chat built directly, e.g. in a test, without going through a real Program).
cols(): int
withSize(int $cols, int $rows): selfThe same size a WindowSizeMsg would have recorded, as a wither.
shouldPromptIdleCompaction(int $tokenCount, ?\DateTimeImmutable $lastActivityAt = null): boolCheck if idle compaction should be prompted based on token count and idle time.
contextUsagePercent(): floatCurrent history's estimated size as a fraction of contextTokenLimit() - for the status bar's context-usage indicator (Renderer).
contextTokens(): intThe numerator behind contextUsagePercent(): the current history's size in tokens. Exposed so the status bar can print an absolute count next to the percentage instead of multiplying the fraction back out against a limit it would have to hardcode.
contextTokenLimit(): intThe denominator behind contextUsagePercent() and the budget every context tier is a percentage of: the 70% reminder, the 85% automatic compaction, the 95% blocking refusal and the idle-compaction prompt.
contextWindowAssumed(): boolWhether contextTokenLimit() is the assumed fallback rather than the backend's own window (#6): the status bar and /context must say so, because the same 100,000 shown bare reads as a fact about the model.
spentUsd(): floatThis session's provider-reported spend in US dollars.
hasReportedSpend(): boolWhether any settled turn this session actually reported usage.
maxCostUsd(): ?floatThe spend ceiling /budget and $CANDY_CODE_MAX_COST set, or null when this session has none. Always a positive finite number when non-null — isUsableSpendCap(), enforced in the constructor.
usageSummary(): stringThe token/cost line /budget prints — TokenTracker::summary(), so the wording lives with the buckets it describes rather than being re-spelled here.
static isUsableSpendCap(float $cap): boolWhether $cap is a spend ceiling this app will act on: a positive, finite number of dollars.
static isCompactionBoundary(Message $message): boolWhether $message is the boundary row a compaction wrote — \SugarCraft\Code\Host\CompactionService::isCompactionBoundary().
abandonActiveBackendChildren(bool $async = false): intCC-QA-2: kill any command children the backend spawned but has not reaped, announced once on stderr when anything dies. The two command backends own a live-children registry; the API-path backends (EngineBackend and the summariser) never spawn a process tree and answer 0 here, so this is safe to call from every quit path. Async true while the loop still ticks (the Ctrl+C / double-Escape arms), false from the bin funnel where the loop is already stopped.

ClaudeCodeMcpClient final class

MCP client that connects to Claude Code via stdio transport. Sends JSON-RPC 2.0 messages and receives responses using non-blocking I/O so the TUI loop stays responsive.

MethodSummary

One turn in a chat conversation. Immutable, role-tagged, timestamped. The chat history is a list<Message> carried on the Chat model.

withLoopGuardStoppedBy(?string $toolName): selfAttach (or clear, via null) the loop guard's "this turn was ended" verdict — see $loopGuardStoppedBy's docblock. A row minted in this process gets its identity from the store's first save of it instead, keyed by its rowKey() so a wither's copy is the same row to it, and read back live through \SugarCraft\Code\Host\TranscriptStore::identityOf(). withStepId(?string $stepId): selfTag (or clear, via null) the engine step that produced this row - see $stepId's docblock.

Renderer final class

Pure view function for Chat — the renderer that actually paints the transcript a real user running bin/candy-code sees.

MethodSummary
static toolRowPrefix(): stringFixed head of a finished tool row, ahead of the model-chosen tool name. Named because renderToolResults() subtracts its width from the row budget and a boundary spelled twice is a boundary that drifts. The word is translated, so the head is built per call and measured by width.
static skillRowPrefix(): stringThe head prefix of a Skill tool row — ✨ skill: <name> instead of the generic 🔧 tool: Skill, so the collapsed transcript says WHICH skill loaded (lane B, skills-qa F1). Pairs with toolRowPrefix(): same shape, same verbatim-prefix law for the click zones.
static toolOutputExpandedByDefault(): boolWhether a settled tool call's output is shown in full until the user collapses it: the expandToolOutput setting (roadmap N-P4g, default off — hide-on-success, §1 E5). Chat::expanded() then records only the calls that differ from it, so a false entry is a call the user closed. Thoughts keep their own collapsed default.
static markDividerCell(string $sideValue, int $absRow, int $frameRows, int $width = 1): stringThe marked segment for one band row of a side's resize seam: divider:<side>:r<absRow> wrapping $width cells (the side box's border, any stacked divider column, and the centre's border — see \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\Renderer::dividerZones()).
static markStackGapRow(string $sideValue, int $slotIndex, int $absRow, int $frameRows, int $width): stringThe marked segment for one stacked side's whole intra-stack gap row: stackdiv:<side>:<slotIndex>:r<absRow> wrapping $width cells, where slotIndex is the slot ABOVE the gap. Same degrade rules — and the same one-zone-per-line invariant — as markDividerCell().
static markSideRow(string $paneId, string $key, int $absRow, int $frameRows, int $width): stringA siderow:<paneId>:<key> grab span of $width blanks for the scanner scratch row — or plain blanks when clicks are off or the id cannot be marked. Same validation as markDockedPaneHeader(): a key is provider- or model-authored (a tool-call id), and a bad one must cost its row the click, never the frame its zones.
static markDockedPaneHeader(string $paneId, int $absRow, int $frameRows, int $width): stringThe marked header row of a docked pane: pane:<paneId> across the side block's width — the dock-drag gesture's press target. Same degrade rules and one-zone-per-line invariant as markDividerCell().
static scanner(): ScannerZone registry produced by the most recent scanRoot() pass. Hit-tested by Chat::zoneAt().
static publishedFrame(): RenderFrameThe frame this renderer currently owns: the last COMPLETED paint. A render in flight builds its own next frame (renderView's $drawing) and swaps it into this slot only when the frame is whole, so between and after paints this accessor answers the same frame today's statics did. All fourteen per-frame fields live on RenderFrame and are reached through this slot; the RenderFrame class docblock owns the serial-render story for why collecting them into one object matters.
static setZoneOrigin(int $col, int $row): voidDeclare where the frame scanRoot() just scanned ended up on the terminal, in 0-based column/row deltas.
static zoneOrigin(): array
static setPaletteAbandoned(bool $abandoned): voidDeclare whether the hosted palette is abandoned for the frame being composited. Called by the shell compositor around its render, never by a standalone Chat render.
static setAgentsPaneDocked(bool $docked): voidDeclare whether the Agents sidepane is docked for the frame being composited. Called by the shell compositor around its render, never by a standalone Chat render.
static setBackgroundJobCount(int $count): voidDeclare how many background jobs are running for the frame being composited, for the status bar's "N bg" segment. Same per-paint lineage as setAgentsPaneDocked(): the shell sets it around one paint, and the default 0 keeps the segment absent everywhere else. Storage: RenderFrame (its backgroundJobCount() read).
static setAgentView(?array $view): voidDeclare the Agent View for the frame being composited (roadmap P-C2), as \SugarCraft\Code\App\App::agentViewFrame() built it, or null for the parent transcript.
static setFocusedToolRowKeys(array $keys): voidDeclare the row-unit keys the shell's SETTLED Ctrl+F cursor stands on for the frame being composited (v2:a11y-F1, W7-B), or the empty list when no cursor is settled.
static clearZones(): voidDrop the click-zone registry and reset the origin and the abandonment signal.
static maxScrollOffset(): intUpper clamp for Chat::scrollOffset(), measured on the last rendered frame. 0 when the transcript fits the window (nothing to scroll) or when nothing has been rendered yet.
static keyHelpMaxOffset(): intUpper clamp for Chat::keyHelp(), measured on the last rendered reference. 0 when the whole list fits, or when it has never been drawn.
static scanRoot(string $frame, int $width, ?RenderFrame $render = null): stringThe zone-scan pass, run exactly ONCE per frame and only at the root.
static render(Chat $chat): stringThe frame's text bytes only, discarding any pixel-graphics image layer renderView() collected.
static renderView(Chat $chat, ?string $agentStripFocus = null, array $agentStripDismissed = []): ViewThe full frame plus the pixel-graphics layer for any image-bearing tool result in the transcript (§9 E3).
static selectableRegion(): ?arrayThe rectangle of the last frame a mouse drag may select text in, as inclusive [rowFrom, rowTo, colFrom, colTo] cells of that frame, or null when nothing on it is selectable. The cells are 1-based — the space SGR mouse reports, zones and sugar-mouse's \SugarCraft\Mouse\Selection use — so frame line R is selectableLines()[R - 1].
static selectableLines(): arrayThe last frame's lines, unhighlighted — what a finished selection is read from. Static for scanner()'s reason: the release that copies arrives between frames and can only read the one on screen.
static modeBadgeForms(\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionMode $mode): arrayThe badge's forms, widest first. plan names its way out, because a mode that refuses every edit is the one a user most needs to leave.
static thoughtKey(string $reasoning): stringThe Chat::expanded() key of a settled thought: derived from the text alone, so the running placeholder a thought rides on and the finished row that replaces it (a new Message, new timestamp) resolve to the same open/closed state.
static recallKey(Message $msg): stringThe Chat::expanded() key of a structured memory-recall row (C-CTX-6.e): derived from the row's sentence and titles, so the same recall of the same notes keeps its open/closed state across repaints and the row rides the transcript's existing tool-row click affordance — same registry, same key space, no new key binding.
static collapseToolOutput(string $output, int $maxLines, int $maxChars): arrayClip a tool's raw output to at most $maxLines lines AND $maxChars characters, reporting whether anything was dropped ( §1 E5).
static styleDiffLine(string $line, Theme $theme, bool $isHeader): StylePick the Style for one unified-diff line from its marker column. The ---/+++ file headers are matched before the bare -/+ markers they start with, otherwise a diff's own header would render as a giant removal followed by a giant addition.

Role enum

Conversation role for a Message. Mirrors the Anthropic / OpenAI / Ollama wire vocabulary so backend adapters can pass the value through without translation.

static stepRequestedAWrite(?array $toolCalls): boolWhether one step of the agentic loop asked for a tool that could have written the working tree.
run(App $app, ?callable $onEvent = null, ?callable $onPermissionRequest = null, ?callable $onToken = null, ?callable $onProgress = null, ?callable $onHeartbeat = null, ?callable $onRequest = null): \GeneratorRun a completion and handle tool calls.
static hookInput(array $arguments): stringThe JSON text a hook reads as CRUSH_TOOL_INPUT (and its _FILE twin).
assembledSystemPrompt(App $app): stringThe system prompt $app would send, as the assembled string itself — the raw half the Backend\DumpsSystemPrompt capability hands to /context --raw (GAP-PRM-15). One fold behind the very method a turn builds with, so the dumped bytes ARE the sent bytes, and they sum to the promptSectionSizes() rows exactly — the identity the dump test pins. The transcript never sees this string; it only ever reaches a file the user named (or the exports shelf), which is WHY this arm exists beside the panel rather than inside it.
promptSectionSizes(App $app): arrayThe system prompt $app would send, measured per layer — what /context shows (roadmap 5.6). Built from the very section list run() assembles, through the one fold (assembleSections()), so the bytes counted are the bytes sent: every row's bytes includes the "\n\n" separator its block carries, and the rows sum to the assembled prompt's length exactly. Empty layers fold away here as they do there.
static planInstructionDocuments(\SugarCraft\Code\Context\InstructionFileLoader $loader): arrayWhich instruction documents one prompt build inlines and which it defers to a pointer line — C3's budget, as one definition.
static planEnabledSkills(array $enabledSkills, \SugarCraft\Code\Context\CompactorConfig $budget): arrayWhat each enabled skill contributes to one prompt build, in enabled order — its body, or, over budget, its heading and a pointer — and why a deferred one was deferred.
skillDeferrals(): arrayThe enabled skills whose bodies the most recent prompt build deferred for budget, keyed by skill name, mapped to why.
turnContext(App $app): Context\TurnContextBlockThe volatile per-step context (step 1.A-1): the git section of this Runtime's environment snapshot — so the write signal markWriteSinceLastRender() sets still decides whether the diffs render — plus the files this conversation's Edit/Write calls touched, and the files changed on disk since the turn's tools read them (step 3.I-2, from the Tools\ReadLedger those tools share).
primeInstructionDiff(App $app): voidFill the instruction-diff slot in the process that OUTLIVES the turn — the parent-side sibling of primeSessionPrompt(), called by EngineBackend right after that prime, before a turn's fork and before a summary's (C-CTX-1).
withSessionPromptMemo(Context\SessionPromptMemo $memo): selfShare one Context\SessionPromptMemo with this Runtime, so its PerSession layers (static <env>, repo map, project memory, standing instruction slab) are read from — and filled into — a memo that outlives the turn. Without one the Runtime keeps a private memo, which is the pre-1.A-1 per-Runtime memoisation exactly.
primeSessionPrompt(App $app): voidFill the session memo's PerSession layers for $app without sending anything — the parent-side prime of step 1.A-2. EngineBackend calls it before forking a turn's child, so the static <env>, repo map, project memory and standing instruction slab are read ONCE, in the process that outlives the turn, and every child inherits them warm. Builds exactly the section list run() would, so the slots it fills are the ones the child reads.
withTurnContextPersisted(): selfA copy whose run() does not append the <turn-context> row, because the caller persists it into the history before each step (step 1.A-2). A clone, like withSessionPromptMemo().
withTurnInbox(\SugarCraft\Code\Backend\TurnInbox $inbox): selfA copy that probes $inbox before each sequential tool call (roadmap 1.C-3): once a mid-turn message is waiting, the step's unstarted calls are skipped (executeToolCalls()). The inbox itself is drained by the step loop that owns it (EngineBackend::runTurn). A clone, like withSessionPromptMemo().
memoryRecall(App $app): Context\MemoryRecallBlockThe memory notes recalled for $app's latest user message (roadmap 5.3-2), carried by the <turn-context> row (turnContext()).
primeMemoryRecall(App $app, string $query, ?\Closure $embedder): Context\MemoryRecallBlockRank $app's memory notes against $query and keep the result as this session's recall — the priming half of roadmap 5.3-2, run by EngineBackend in the process that assembles the request (the forked turn child, or the blocking fallback with no child) since ISS-072, so the note reads and the one embedding request ($embedder, null for keyword-only) happen once per turn off the parent's event loop.
primeSymbolMap(App $app): Context\SymbolMapBlockCapture the symbol-level repo map for $app's session once, into the session memo the turn's prompt reads (roadmap 5.5-5). EngineBackend calls it in the parent before forking a turn; after the first turn of a session — and until a refresh point forgets the session's layers — it returns the held capture without touching the checkout, so the bytes the prompt carries never move inside a session. A capture that came back empty is held too: the session stays without the map rather than gaining it mid-session and moving message 0.
shouldPromptIdleCompaction(App $app, int $tokenCount): boolDetermine whether to prompt the user about idle-session compaction.

A named colour theme for Renderer's chrome (borders, user/assistant/ system labels), the whole src/Tui/ shell (menu bar and its dropdown, pane boxes, sidebars, status colours) and SugarMarkdown's markdown rendering, resolved from the two theme classes that already exist elsewhere in the monorepo rather than inventing a third colour system:

static contrast(Color $a, Color $b): floatContrast ratio between two colours, WCAG 2.1 §1.4.3: the lighter relative luminance plus 0.05 over the darker plus 0.05, so 1.0 is "identical" and 21.0 is black on white.
static byName(string $name): selfResolve a theme name — a built-in (builtInNames(), matched case-insensitively), a discovered file under ~/.candy-code/themes/ (ThemeFile), or neither.
static adaptive(): selfThe dark/light preset the attached terminal actually calls for, kept under the name adaptive so the choice re-resolves on every read (and on every launch) instead of being frozen at pick time.
static legibleOn(Color $colour, Color $background): Color$colour if it already reaches CONTRAST_MIN on $background, else the same colour nudged along its own HSL lightness axis, away from the background, until it does - the background-only half of project()'s nudge, for a colour a theme did not declare.
static dark(): selfThe house default palette: the shipped dark theme. Named for the palette rather than default() because ::new() is the factory root and ::default() is a banned name; mirrors the descriptive-name spelling of sugar-style's Theme::ansi().
static names(): arrayEverything byName() answers: the six built-ins in their fixed order, then the custom theme files discovered under ~/.candy-code/themes/, sorted. A custom file whose stem collides with a built-in name keeps the built-in — the person's palette file never shadows a name the docs and validators promise.
static builtInNames(): arrayThe machine-independent half: exactly the shipped palettes, in the fixed order, no directory scan behind them. Documentation, the settings validator's advertised list, and any test that must mean "everywhere this runs" quote THIS, so a machine's private theme files never leak into a page another machine reads.
static isBuiltInName(string $name): boolWhether a name is one of the shipped palettes, matched case-insensitively like byName().
static canonicalBaseName(string $name): ?stringThe canonical spelling of a base theme name, or null when it is not one.
static suggest(string $name): ?stringThe advertised name closest to a misspelling, or null when nothing is close. Folded (case, - and _ dropped) equality wins outright, else one edit for short names and two for longer ones — the \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::suggestKey() budget, so both places that guess a name guess with the same tolerance.
static resetForTesting(): voidForget the discovered files, the parses, and which names have warned — tests move HOME between cases, and each home is its own theme world.

static diffTextsOf(string $diff): arrayA unified diff as the before/after text of each hunk: what an editor that renders a change from its two sides (the Agent Client Protocol's {type: "diff", path, oldText, newText}, roadmap 5.9-2) needs, where $diff is the patch a terminal renders. Context and removed lines make oldText, context and added lines newText; a hunk that starts at -0,0 created the file, so its oldText is null. The path is the +++ b/ header's, without the a//b/ prefix.
toEngineResult(): EngineToolResultAdapt this Chat-side result to the canonical engine-side EngineToolResult the Tools\Tool interface, Runtime and \SugarCraft\Code\Events\ToolFinished speak ( §1 E1).

Called once per launch by \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::applyMediaRenderMode() with the resolved ui.imageRenderMode value; empty or whitespace-only input normalises to 'auto', asking the terminal. The word is stored normalised (trimmed, lower-cased) because mosaic's own vocabulary comparator is, and the memo key must not fork on spelling noise.
static renderMode(): stringThe currently configured render-mode word (see setRenderMode()).
static resetRenderMode(): voidDiscard every cached probe in the per-mode memo (W5.7, crush_media §8.2) so the next mosaic() re-derives instead of answering from a ??= hit. This resets the CACHES, not the word — the word only changes through setRenderMode() (and the boot-time precedence in \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::applyMediaRenderMode(), where CANDY_CODE_MEDIA_RENDER_MODE reasserts itself at the next launch). The /rendermode command calls set-then-reset together; a bare reset is the seam for any future caller that re-detects the terminal without changing the requested mode.
static mosaic(): MosaicPublic accessor for the same probe-once Mosaic instance probeMosaic() caches -- the shared instance \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::chat() threads into \SugarCraft\Code\Chat's mosaic: constructor parameter (W1.G2/E2), so a future renderer (E3) reads the SAME detected protocol this class's own image-bearing results were built from, rather than re-probing the TTY independently.
toWire(): arrayConvert to array for serialization (wire format).

Usage final readonly class

What one provider call — or a whole turn's worth of them summed — actually cost, in PROVIDER-COUNTED tokens and dollars (Phase 5 item 7). Since prompt_plan.md P4.S1 (backlog E17) it also carries the provider's own token BUCKETS — input/output, the two cache sides, and (since qwen.md §Q6) the completion-side reasoning side — null until a provider reports each one, and never defaulted to a number a provider did not say.

MethodSummary
static new(int $totalTokens = 0, float $costUsd = 0.0, ?int $inputTokens = null, ?int $outputTokens = null, ?int $cacheReadTokens = null, ?int $cacheCreationTokens = null, ?int $reasoningTokens = null, ?string $unpricedModel = null, int $delegatedTokens = 0, int $webSearchRequests = 0): self

plus(self $other): selfThis usage plus $other's — the operation an agentic TURN needs, because one turn is N provider calls, not one.

promptTokens(): ?intThe prompt-side total, the identity the cache-bucket split exists to make computable: promptTokens = cacheRead + cacheCreation + input (prompt_plan.md P4.S1, backlog E17; prompt_expand.md §9.14).
withInputTokens(?int $tokens): selfThe usage with a reported/unreported input bucket set. Passing null clears it back to unreported; the other buckets ride along untouched — that is what the paired bool $xSet sentinels on mutate() are for (repo convention; canonical sugar-style/src/Style.php).
withOutputTokens(?int $tokens): selfAs withInputTokens(), for the completion side.
withCacheReadTokens(?int $tokens): selfAs withInputTokens(), for the cache-read bucket.
withCacheCreationTokens(?int $tokens): selfAs withInputTokens(), for the cache-creation bucket.
withReasoningTokens(?int $tokens): selfAs withInputTokens(), for the completion-side reasoning bucket.
static sum(array $usages): ?selfSum of a list of per-call usages, or null when the list is empty or holds only nulls — preserving the "nothing reported" answer rather than turning it into a zero.
toArray(): arrayPlain-array form for the Backend\EngineBackend::completeAsync() fork boundary, whose parent unserializes with allowed_classes => false and so cannot receive the object itself — same rule Backend\EngineBackend::encodeEvent() follows for tool events.

AgentMentions final class

The typed-prompt door of @researcher fix the flaky parser — an address, not a new channel (WAVE-R RS-AGENT-C2).

MethodSummary
static draft(string $text, ?\Closure $roster): ?stringRewrite a line-initial @<name> address into the @agent:<name> spelling the existing mention leg resolves, or hand back null to say "this line is not an address" — and null means the line travels byte- identical from here.
static routes(string $name, \Closure $roster): boolWhether $name is an addressable agent: a roster is open, the spelling is not a reserved keyword head, and the roster holds it. The refusal notice reads the SAME truth value from the SAME two predicates, so the door that rewrites and the door that refuses cannot drift.
static refuses(string $name, \Closure $roster): boolWhether $name is an address the run will NEVER route: not a reserved keyword head (those keep their channel meaning whatever the roster says — the keyword leg answers for them) and not a preset the roster holds. This is the ONE shared predicate behind both doors: draft() rewrites exactly what routes() accepts, the refusal fires exactly on what refuses() answers true for, and a name can never be both.
static addressedName(string $text): ?stringThe bare name ONLY a line-initial address token carries; null whenever the first token of the line is not @-plus-a-name — mid-line mentions, reserved keyword colons, domains and emails, a bare @, and a token that opens the line but continues past the name all answer null here, and their lines keep every byte they arrived with.
static isReservedHead(string $name): boolWhether the bare name collides with the mention channel's reserved heads, and so is never an address whatever the roster holds.
static draftThrough(?AgentManager $manager, string $text): ?stringThe '@coder fix X' addressing door (RS-AGENT-C2) wired to a live manager: a line-initial address to a preset this run holds is rewritten into the reserved '@agent:<name>' spelling the mention channel already resolves. Null — the line keeps every byte it arrived with — for anything that is not an address, for names the roster does not hold (refusalThrough() beside this door handles those), and for a run with no agent manager at all, where bare '@' names are prose because there is nothing to delegate TO. The roster closure is the SAME predicate the mention leg and the headless host hold, built the same way \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::userTurnMessage() wires its agentRoster.
static refusalThrough(?AgentManager $manager, string $text): ?stringThe refusal behind that door: why a line-initial '@<name>' the roster doesn't hold costs a notice instead of a turn — the same economy \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::unknownSlashNotice() argues for the slash door: sending it to the model spends a paid turn to answer a typo with an essay, and here the essay would additionally be the model's guess at who 'name' is. The notice names the roster this run holds. Deliberately NOT Lang-wrapped, matching the mention channel's own roster notices in \SugarCraft\Code\Attachments\ContextMentions::agent(), which answer the identical question in plain English — inventing a lang key here would fork one message across two channels. A run with no agent manager refuses nothing: with no roster to name, '@anything' stays the prose it always was.

AgentWorkerPool final class

Worker pool for parallel agent execution.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly ?int $maxConcurrent = null, ?ExecutorInterface $executor = null, private readonly ?array $workerProvider = null, private readonly ?ExecutorInterface $forkedExecutor = null, private readonly bool $probeLoop = true)
__clone(): voidA clone (see withStopOnFirstFailure()) gets its own IPC directory so the two instances never observe each other's results and neither destructor removes files the other still owns.
__destruct()Stop and collect this pool's forked workers, then remove its private IPC directory — if this process created it.
executeAll(array $agents, CompleteRequest $request, ?\Closure $toolGrantResolver = null, ?\Closure $systemPromptResolver = null): \GeneratorExecute all agents, yielding results as they complete.
executeOne(SubAgent $agent, CompleteRequest $request): AgentResultExecute a single agent and return its result.
activeCount(): intNumber of agents currently executing.
cap(): ?intThe width cap this pool was built with, or null when it dispatches every agent it is given at once.
queuedCount(): intAgents submitted but not yet dispatched because the cap is full. Always 0 for an uncapped pool, which drains its queue straight into dispatch.
fallbackReason(): ?stringWhy agents are running sequentially in the parent rather than forked, or null while every dispatch has been concurrent. Names the cause the operator can act on: no pcntl, or a fork that failed.
queueSize(): intNumber of agents waiting to execute.
cancel(string $agentId): voidCancel a specific agent by ID.
cancelAll(): voidCancel all pending and running agents.
withStopOnFirstFailure(bool $stop): selfConfigure stopOnFirstFailure behavior for this pool instance.
withTimeBudget(?float $seconds): selfA pool whose every executeAll() run (and executeOne()) is bounded by $seconds of wall-clock time in total; null removes the bound.
withMaxRetries(int $retries): selfA pool that re-runs every failed or timed-out agent up to $retries times — or up to the agent's own SubAgent::$maxRetries, when that is higher. The pool-wide half of the retry rule: AgentPoolConfig::$maxRetries reaches a pool through here. 0 (the default) leaves each agent to its own count; a negative value is 0.
withRetryGate(?\Closure $gate): selfwf-impl P1-7: a pool that asks $gate before re-running a failed agent (see $retryGate); a refusal settles the agent on the attempt that ran, its error naming why it was not retried. Null removes it. A clone, like withTimeBudget().
maxRetries(): intThe pool-wide retry floor withMaxRetries() set. Public for the reason workerProvider() is: WorkflowEngine rebuilds a pool per parallel stage and must carry this across.
executor(): ?ExecutorInterfaceReturns the executor instance used by this pool.
static enterTurnOwnedLoop(): voidMark this process as a forked turn child whose turn runs on its own event loop, so a teardown inside it never arms its kill timers there.
static leaveTurnOwnedLoop(): voidUndo enterTurnOwnedLoop().
forkFailureCount(): intHow many pcntl_fork() calls this pool has actually lost (E261).
workerProvider(): ?arrayThe provider spec this pool hands to the default executor it builds.
forkedExecutor(): ?ExecutorInterfaceThe executor this pool runs on its FORKING path, if a caller supplied one.

ModelChoice final class

The model ladder: what a bounded run actually dials when someone asked for a model by name. One copy on purpose (S2, wf-g2g3) — TaskTool consults it for a delegation's model parameter and the agent's preset, and EngineExecutor consults it for a workflow stage's model:, so the same id answers the same way in both doors: same session equality, same tier-alias walk, same "which provider serves what" verdicts.

MethodSummary
static decide(EngineBackend $engine, Agent $agent, string $requested): arrayDecide the run's model from the ask, the agent's preset, and the engine it would dial on. Answers [pin, null] — nothing to do, or a model the engine can serve — or [null, parts] when the ask cannot be honoured, with the raw 'asked' id, the 'origin' that asked, and the 'why' the engine cannot serve it. WHAT HAPPENS TO A FALLBACK is the caller's law (annotated continuation vs refusal), which is why the note sentence is NOT composed here.

AgentInbox final class

Messages to running sub-agents, over the Mailbox (roadmap P-D1, Appendix P §5.3–5.4).

MethodSummary
static new(Mailbox $mailbox, #[\SensitiveParameter] ?string $key = null): selfAn inbox over $mailbox. $key signs and verifies from:'user' messages; with no key, user messages can be neither sent nor accepted.
static forSession(string $sessionId, #[\SensitiveParameter] ?string $key = null, ?string $root = null): ?selfThe inbox of session $sessionId's sub-agents, below $root (default defaultRoot()), signing with $key (default launchKey()). Null when there is no root to keep it under.
static defaultRoot(): ?string~/.candy-code/mailboxes, beside the sub-agent transcript logs: derived from SubAgentTranscriptLog::defaultRoot(), so it is under the same owned home, or the test bootstrap's sandbox when that is pinned. Null when there is no owned home.
static launchKey(): stringThis launch's message key: 32 random bytes, minted on the first call and then fixed for the life of the process and every process forked from it. See the class doc for why it must be minted in the parent.
send(string $agentId, AgentMessage $message): AgentMessagePut $message in agent $agentId's mailbox, signed when it is from the user. Answers the message as written.
control(string $agentId, string $verb, string $from = AgentMessage::FROM_USER): AgentMessageSend agent $agentId a harness verb (CONTROL_VERBS, or BACKGROUND_VERB) as a MessageMode::Control message. The agent's run reads it with takeControls(), never as conversation text.
drain(string $agentId, ?\Closure $onRejected = null): arrayEvery unread message for $agentId that the running agent reads now (MessageMode::deliveredMidRun()), oldest first, each handed out once. Follow-ups and controls stay unread for their own readers (takeFollowups(), takeControls()).
takeControls(string $agentId, ?\Closure $onRejected = null): arrayEvery unread MessageMode::Control message for $agentId, oldest first, each handed out once and validated exactly as drain() validates.
takeFollowups(string $agentId, ?\Closure $onRejected = null): arrayEvery unread MessageMode::Followup message for $agentId, oldest first, each handed out once and validated exactly as drain() validates (roadmap 4.4). A followup is for the conversation's NEXT run, so the run it was sent to never reads it: the run that continues the conversation does (\SugarCraft\Code\Tools\BuiltIn\TaskTool on a resume), from the mailbox of every earlier run of that conversation.
pending(string $agentId): boolWhether an unread, valid message for $agentId asks to skip the current step's unstarted calls (MessageMode::skipsUnstartedCalls()). It hands nothing out.
size(string $agentId): intThe size of $agentId's mailbox file in bytes (0 when it has none); a stat, not a read.
rejection(string $agentId, AgentMessage $message): ?stringWhy $message, read from $agentId's mailbox, must not be delivered, or null when it may. A user message needs this inbox's key and an HMAC that verifies under it; any other sender must not claim one.

A real id answers only runs whose frames carried that parentSessionId: a legacy run that carried none stays invisible to a scoped view and visible to the unscoped one.

MethodSummary
static thresholdSeconds(): intThe effective threshold for this render, seconds: the stored setting pushed through clampThreshold(). Also the settings schema's reader symbol for agentStallSeconds.
static clampThreshold(int $raw): intThe threshold law, pure: zero or below is OFF (never a negative countdown), a set value below FLOOR_SECONDS rises to the floor, anything else rides unchanged.
static idleSeconds(AgentLiveRegistry $registry, ?string $runId): ?intWhole seconds since the run's last accepted frame, or null when there is nothing to measure: an unknown id, a run that never folded a beat, or a finished run (its row stands as history; time since its last word is not a stall). The answer reads only stored state — the registry's clock as of the last AgentLiveRegistry::advance().
static stallSeconds(AgentLiveRegistry $registry, ?string $runId, ?int $threshold = null): ?intThe stall verdict: idle seconds when the run is silent for STRICTLY more than the threshold, null for anything else — detector OFF, no row to measure, or a gap still within budget. Strictly-over, not at-or-over, because a threshold of N seconds promises N quiet seconds before it flags, not N minus one.

A valid message past $limit stays.

All three inputs are caller state, never model state (FirstRunWizard::shouldOffer()): no provider was SELECTED for this launch (env tier, --provider, or a persisted provider key — the same reads \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap makes to build the backend), no provider carries a usable API key in the user config, and the terminal is a live interactive tty. Both seams are injectable for pins: the tty probe is guarded by is_resource on each stream because tests/bootstrap.php frees the PHP-level \STDIN resource during its fd-0 repair — an unguarded stream_isatty(STDIN) THROWS on that invalid resource under strict_types rather than answering false — and with the guard the freed STDIN plus a piped stdout answer false, so the default never fires in a test run; the stamp path reads the real cache corner by default.

ContextMentions final class

The keyword @-mentions (roadmap 5.8): context that is not a file on disk, attached to a prompt the way @file attaches one (FileMentions).

MethodSummary
static isPrNumber(string $number): boolWhether $number is the whole pull-request number the @pr leg reads. /review --pr <n> validates through here before assembling its prompt, the same door-law isDiffRef() enforces for @diff (C-AGT-2): a command can never submit a mention the scanner would refuse to attach.
static isDiffRef(string $ref): boolWhether $ref survives the scanner's own round trip (GIT-1, C-AGT-2: /review <ref> validates through here before assembling its prompt, so a command can never submit a diff mention the scanner would refuse to attach and the review would silently run against nothing). The check is the full walk, not just the pattern: a spelling the trailing-punctuation trim would cut back (HEAD@{1, a path that cannot close) is refused. Since C-AGT-6.b a range survives in exactly its two git shapes — A..B and A...B, each side itself surviving this walk — because diff() learned to run those against git; a malformed range (a.., a..b..c, a side that reads as an option) is refused here, at the scanner's door, the same way a misspelled single ref always was.
static diffRangeSides(string $ref): ?arrayThe two sides of a @diff range, cut the way git cuts them: the three-dot spelling is looked for first, so a...b cuts at its ... and a plain ..-bearing spelling cuts at its first ... Returns [left, right, threeDot] for ANY separator-bearing spelling — including malformed ones (a.., a..b..c) whose sides the caller must still run through isRefSide() — and null when $ref is no range at all.

The per-root arm drops ALL THREE memos: a root that was primed and then deleted no longer resolves, and its entries still answer to the caller's canonical string (rank() keys its memo the same realpath ?: $root way), so the drop stays total whichever way the directory left.
