CancellationToken final class

A shared, mutable cancel flag threaded from \SugarCraft\Code\Chat into a \SugarCraft\Code\Backend's Backend::completeAsync() call for one turn. Deliberately NOT one of Chat's immutable with*() value-object fields — the whole point is a single shared instance both sides can see mutate, so Chat's later double-Escape handler can flip it after the async Cmd closure has already captured it.

MethodSummary
__construct()
cancel(): void
isCancelled(): bool
asyncToken(): \SugarCraft\Async\CancellationTokenThe sugar-async token over the same source, for \SugarCraft\Async\ChildRun::withCancellation(): cancelling this token cancels it, so a child run on the loop is killed through the same ladder.
cancelSoft(): voidAsk the work to stop at its next boundary rather than at once. Polled, like isCancelled(); it fires no listener, because those are the hard stop's.
isSoftCancelled(): boolWhether cancelSoft() (or the stronger cancel()) was called.
cancelTool(string $callId): voidAsk the work to stop ONE running tool call now (roadmap 1.C-4b, cancel_tool{callId}): a forked engine turn's parent takes it with takeToolCancels() on the tick it polls this token on and sends it down; the call settles as cancelled and the rest of the turn goes on. Each id is queued once, however often it is asked. A holder that cannot stop a single call never takes them.
takeToolCancels(): arrayThe call ids cancelTool() queued since the last call, oldest first, each handed out once.
isToolCancelled(string $callId): boolWhether cancelTool() was ever called for $callId.
cancelAgent(string $agentId, string $callId): voidHard-stop ONE delegated run (roadmap P-E1, agent_cancel{agentId, callId}): $agentId is the run, $callId the Task call of this turn it runs under. A forked engine turn's parent takes it with takeAgentCancels() on its cancel tick and sends it down; the turn child SIGTERMs that member's process (SIGKILL after two seconds) or, for a lone Task in its own process, stops it at its next boundary. Each run is queued once, however often it is asked.
takeAgentCancels(): arrayThe runs cancelAgent() queued since the last call, oldest first, each handed out once.
isAgentCancelled(string $agentId): boolWhether cancelAgent() was ever called for $agentId.
onCancel(\Closure $listener): \ClosureRun $listener when this token is cancelled — at once, when it already is. Returns the detach: call it when the work $listener would stop is over, so a token that outlives that work (Chat keeps a turn's token until the turn settles) does not keep its objects alive or act on them.
steer(string $text): ?stringQueue $text for delivery into the running turn at its next step boundary, and answer the steer's id — or null when the turn is already stopping (cancelled, or soft-cancelled: a turn on its way out has no next boundary to deliver at).
takeSteers(): arrayThe steers queued since the last call, oldest first, each handed out once — the turn's parent writes each down as a steer frame.
acknowledgeSteer(string $steerId, int $step): voidRecord the child's steer_ack: $steerId was delivered at $step.
acknowledgedSteers(): arrayThe steers the turn acknowledged, steerId => the step each was delivered at.

ChildChannel final class

The turn child's half of the two-way frame channel (roadmap 1.C-1 = Appendix O §5.1, frame vocabulary decision D1).

MethodSummary
__construct(private $socket, private readonly \Closure $writeFrame, private readonly \Closure $drainFrames, private readonly string $mode, private readonly int $ownerPid, private readonly ?string $projectRoot = null)
static releaseInherited(): intClose this process's copy of every channel socket it inherited rather than built (roadmap 1.C-5, the RELAY design's "the grandchild closes its copy of the turn socket"). Called by a forked member that has a channel of its own: the turn's frame writers it inherited also hold the socket, and a write from here would interleave with the turn child's frames — with the copy closed, such a write fails instead. The turn child's own end is untouched (a separate descriptor table).
static new($socket, \Closure $writeFrame, \Closure $drainFrames, string $mode = '', ?string $projectRoot = null): self
approver(): \ClosureThe approver EngineBackend::withPermissionApprover() takes: put the question to the parent and grant only on an actual once/always.
ask(ToolCall $call, HookResult $ask): PermissionResolvedPut one ASK to the parent and block until it is answered or the parent is gone.
clientCaller(): \ClosureThe caller \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\RelaysClientToolCalls::withClientCaller() takes: hand one announced call to the parent, block until the client's answer arrives or the parent is gone.
callClient(string $toolCallId, string $name, array $arguments, int $deadlineSeconds): ToolResultPut one client-hosted call to the parent and block until the answer arrives or the parent is gone (C-TOOL-6.h).
send(string $kind, array $fields = []): boolWrite one child→parent frame that is not a round trip of its own (steer_ack, usage, step). Neither ask nor client_call goes through here: each carries its own pending state and must ride its builder (ask(), callClient()).
takeSteers(): arraySteers the parent sent, in arrival order, each handed out once. Polls the socket without blocking first, so a steer is seen at a step boundary even when no ask was open to buffer it.
takeControls(): arrayBuffered cancel_soft / cancel_tool / agent_cancel frames, each handed out once.
softCancelRequested(): boolWhether the parent has asked the turn to stop at its next step boundary (cancel_soft, roadmap 1.C-4). Polls the socket without blocking first, and takes every cancel_soft out of the buffered controls while leaving any other control (cancel_tool) for takeControls(). Latched: once true it stays true, however many times it is asked.
takeToolCancels(): arrayThe call ids the parent has asked to stop (cancel_tool{callId}, roadmap 1.C-4b), each handed out once, in arrival order. Polls the socket without blocking first, and takes only the cancel_tool frames out of the buffered controls, so a cancel_soft waiting for softCancelRequested() is never consumed here.
takeAgentCancels(): arrayThe delegated runs the parent has asked to hard-stop (agent_cancel{agentId, callId}, roadmap P-E1), each handed out once, in arrival order. Polls without blocking first and takes only the agent_cancel frames, leaving every other control where it is.
isClosed(): boolTrue once the parent's end has been seen closed (or the stream stopped parsing): every later ask settles unanswered without writing.

Like summaryReply()'s App, this reuses the session's memo after the first prime rather than re-walking the repository map and instruction files.

Fresh guard per call, as there.

completeAsync(array $history, ?callable $onToken = null, ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?callable $onEvent = null, ?callable $onReasoning = null, bool $interactive = false, ?callable $onStep = null): PromiseInterfaceRuns complete() - one or more real, blocking provider HTTP calls plus any tool execution the agentic loop drives - in a forked child so the caller's event loop (the TUI's render/input loop) never blocks on it. Without this, Program's futureTick()-scheduled Cmd execution calls this method's factory closure directly on the loop: the old implementation wrapped a *synchronous* complete() call in a React\Promise\Promise whose executor runs immediately (that's the Promise constructor's contract, not deferred), so the "async" call was really just a blocking one wearing a Promise - the whole terminal froze (no spinner animation, no keystrokes, no Ctrl+C) for the full duration of every provider round-trip. Forking moves that blocking work off the loop entirely; the parent only watches a non-blocking socket via Loop::addReadStream() for the result, so rendering and input keep flowing while a turn is in flight - same rationale as \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::executeToolsParallel()'s R14b fork fix, extended here to cross the ReactPHP loop boundary rather than just fanning out sibling tool calls.

The child attaches a ChildChannel approver in place of whatever approver this backend carries; the parent owns the policy. $onStep takes the turn's step/usage frames (roadmap 1.C-4), as on completeAsync().

Null or blank is the turn's own model, the default, because that is the one whose prefix the provider has cached.

PendingAsk final class

The reply handle for one open ASK raised inside a running turn (Appendix O §5.1, decision D1) — what a \SugarCraft\Code\Events\PermissionAsked hands its receiver so a LATER answer can reach the process that is blocked on the question.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $askId, public readonly string $toolCallId, public readonly string $tool, public readonly array $arguments, public readonly string $reason, public readonly string $source, public readonly string $mode, public readonly array $suggestions, public readonly array $alwaysScope, private readonly \Closure $settle, public readonly ?\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\AskOrigin $origin = null, public readonly string $alwaysAsks = '', public readonly ?string $diff = null, public readonly ?int $askedAt = null)

static describe(ToolCall $call, HookResult $ask, string $mode, ?string $projectRoot = null): arrayThe ask frame for $call, which \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime::settleAsk() has ALREADY rebuilt with the question's rewrite applied — so the arguments here are what will execute, never the model's proposal.
static alwaysAsksReason(string $tool, HookResult $ask): stringWhy a question always cannot remember is put every time, in words for the modal — '' for the model's own questions, which say what they are themselves.
static source(ToolCall $call, HookResult $ask): stringWho put the question: gate for the permission gate alone, hook:<names> when hooks asked, and tool:<name> for an ask no hook raised — the call's own question, which is what AskUser and PlanExit put through \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\RelaysPermissionAsks (roadmap 5.7-2). That last one used to read hook:unknown, naming a hook that did not exist.
question(): ?stringThe question tool whose own question this is — AskUser or PlanExit — or null for a permission question about a call. Read off the source() the asking process wrote, so a hook's ask about an AskUser call stays a permission question.
choices(): arrayThe choices an AskUser question offers, in order (option 1 is the recommended one) — what the modal's number keys pick. Empty for any other ask, or one whose arguments carry none.
static fromFrame(array $frame, \Closure $settle): ?selfRebuild the handle from an ask frame, or null when the frame is not a shape describe() writes. The frame was unserialized with allowed_classes => false, so every field is checked rather than trusted; an out-of-shape suggestions entry is dropped, and a list that ends up without reject gets it back — refusing must always be on offer.
offers(PermissionReply $reply): boolWhether $reply is one of the answers this question offers.
reply(PermissionReply $reply, ?string $note = null): boolAnswer the question. An always on a question that does not offer it settles as once: the caller gets the call it approved, and nothing is remembered for a question that must be put every time.
cancel(string $reason = ''): boolSettle the question as unanswered: the turn is going away under it.
isSettled(): bool
resolution(): ?PermissionResolvedHow the question was settled, or null while it is still open.
askedAt(): ?intThe mint stamp, or null when the handle never got one (which hasExpired() treats as aged).
hasExpired(?int $now = null): boolWhether the question has aged out of EXPIRY_SECONDS, decided here at consume time against an injected clock — no timer anywhere (E646). Expiry lands AT equality (the PairingCodes law), and an un-stamped handle is already aged: fail-closed toward refusal.

BackgroundShellRegistry final class

The launch's table of background shells — the state behind Bash's run_in_background, ShellOutput and ShellStop (SHL-1).

MethodSummary
static clampLifetime(?int $seconds): intThe wall a shell gets: the caller's lifetime_seconds clamped to [MIN_LIFETIME_SECONDS, MAX_LIFETIME_CEILING_SECONDS], or MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS when none was asked for.
static forSession(string $sessionId, ?string $root = null, ?callable $sleeper = null): selfOpen the shell table for one session. $root relocates the tree wholesale (a test seam); the default roots at HomeDirectory::owned() — an unestablishable home throws rather than parking a shell log under a world-writable stand-in. The directory itself is created on first start(), so building the registry touches no disk.
static defaultRoot(): stringThe HOME-rooted tree every default session shares one level above.
directoryPath(): stringAbsolute path of this table's session directory (created lazily by start()).
start(string $command, string $label, array $envOverrides = [], ?string $owner = null, ?int $lifetimeSeconds = null): arraySpawn $command detached and record it. The command string is the CALLER's job (Bash builds the same bash -c + cd-guard + sandbox stack the synchronous path runs); this method adds only the exit-code trailer, the file sinks, and the containment spawn.
startInteractive(string $command, string $label, int $cols = self::INTERACTIVE_COLS, int $rows = self::INTERACTIVE_ROWS, array $envOverrides = [], ?string $owner = null, ?int $lifetimeSeconds = null): arrayStart a shell that OUTLIVES every tool call: a relay process owns a real pty, the shell runs on it with a controlling terminal, and input arrives later through send().
send(string $shellId, string $bytes, string $origin = 'model', ?string $owner = null): arrayFeed bytes to an interactive shell's pty and answer where its output stood BEFORE the write.
status(string $shellId, ?string $owner = null): ?arrayOne row with its LIVE state resolved, plus ageSeconds, the lifetime verdict, and the exitNote a cap death is narrated with. Enforces the max-lifetime wall on a live shell before answering.
read(string $shellId, int|string $cursor = 0, ?int $maxBytes = null, ?string $owner = null): arrayThe output of one shell from $cursor forward — a TWO-PART token "<stdout offset>.<stderr offset>", one offset per stream, each advancing in its own file. At most $maxBytes (clamped to MAX_READ_BYTES, default DEFAULT_READ_BYTES) come back. A bare integer is a legacy combined offset and decodes with today's arithmetic (stdout first, the remainder stderr) — exact only while stdout is frozen at decode time, which is precisely why the token replaced it (C-TOOL-1: a single global offset skipped stdout bytes written after stderr had been read, and replayed those stderr bytes). Only a DEFAULT fresh read is tail-wins: when its backlog exceeds the budget the OLDEST bytes are skipped and skippedBytes says how many. An explicit window or a threaded cursor paginates without skipping — pagination never destroys unread output. The returned cursor is the token just past the last byte handed back for EACH stream; it never rewinds and never lies about position. An offset past the end of a log that has since SHRUNK clamps to that stream's true end; because the other stream's offset is its own, a shrink can never strand unread bytes of it — the per-stream rule absorbs what the old lastStdoutSize remap existed for (SHL-1).
stop(string $shellId, ?string $owner = null): arrayStop one shell: TERM to the group, a bounded grace, KILL to the same the same group, then a bounded confirmation. Unknown ids answer found false; an already-settled shell is a no-op success — the ladder never signals a pid it has no claim on. grouped says whether the recorded pid actually led a process group (false where the host had no setsid at spawn — then confirmed speaks only of the wrapper).
teardown(): voidKill every live shell (TERM→grace→KILL each) and release every handle. The launch's teardown guarantee: no background child of this registry survives it. Output files stay on disk for a post-mortem read.
ids(): array
ownedBy(?string $owner): arrayThe ids one caller may see — its own rows plus the untagged ones — in insertion order. This is the whole visibility law read as a list: a null $owner (a caller bound to no session) sees every row, which is what keeps the launch's own tools, panels, and teardown working for a row started before the first session existed.
toArray(): arrayThe plain-array payload for the fork boundary: scalars only, by construction (no handles — those live in the local $handles map).
merge(mixed $payload): voidFold an export from a forked child (or the same export again — idempotent by the laws below). A row that reports an exit code beats one that does not; among equally informed rows the later spawnedAt wins. Malformed rows are skipped, never fatal.
forgetHandles(array $ids): voidDrop this process's handle copies for $ids. Wired through dropForkInheritedHandles() on entry to every public method from a pid other than the one that spawned: after a fork, both processes' copies point at the same kernel children, and a copy its holder never spawned can honestly neither be waited (one waitpid, either process) nor be terminated without reaching into the owner's child. The owner keeps its handles; every later non-owner entry forgets again, cheaply and idempotently.
localIds(): arrayThe ids whose spawn this process itself performed (handle present).
static pathFor(string $directory, string $id): arrayThe file set one shell id owns inside a launch directory. Public and static because the interactive relay (PtyRelay) is a separate process that receives only the directory and the id on its argv, and must derive the very same names — one spelling for both sides, since a relay inventing its own paths is how a sweep starts orphaning files a row still addresses. The three plain-path sinks plus the interactive trio: .pid (the pty child's pid, the registry's kill-ladder handle), .in (the FIFO the model's keystrokes arrive through), and .cmd (the staged command file, read and unlinked by the relay before the shell ever starts — no command text on argv or environ).

permissionAskChannel(string $sessionId): ?arrayThe permission-relay channel of a session (ISS-004): the .ask file a relayed daemon writes its questions to and the answer file the server writes the human's answers back to. The answer path is the SPAWN-MINTED nonce name (F1) when this process minted one or adopted a record that names one; the pre-mint derived .answer shape is the fallback, which is what a daemon born before the mint still polls. Null for a session this process does not hold IPC for, or one whose paths are not a session buffer's — a TUI /bg daemon never asked for a channel and has none.
permissionAsks(string $sessionId): arrayThe questions a session's daemon has relayed and not settled, oldest first, deduped by ask id with the newest line winning. Malformed lines are unread and untrusted — a torn write can only ever cost the one question it names, which the daemon's own timeout falls through to the legacy refusal. A {"askId":…,"settled":…} line (F4) closes the question it names rather than opening one, and a later ask line for the same id — the identical replay with a fresh token — opens it again.
permissionSettledAskIds(string $sessionId): arrayThe ask ids a session's daemon has settled on its own (F4: timed-out questions), in file order. A settle line is the daemon's notice that nobody answered inside its window; readers drop the question from the open set, permission.pending stops listing it, and the host emits its settled event.
permissionAnswers(string $sessionId): arrayThe human answers recorded for a session (ISS-004, F3): every valid row of the session's answer file, oldest first, deduped by <askId>:<askToken> with the newest line winning. This is the record a RESTARTED server consults before re-announcing anything — a question answered while an earlier server lived was answered for good, and the file is where that fact survived.
answerPermissionAsk(string $sessionId, string $askId, string $reply, string $note = ''): boolAppend one human answer for a relayed question (ISS-004). The daemon polls this file inside its server.askTimeoutSeconds window; whoever answers first is whoever's line the daemon finds, and the same answer read twice changes nothing — the file is the record.
hasActiveSessions(): boolReturn true when there is at least one active session.
spawnSession(string $name, Agent $agent, string $task, string $workingDirectory, int $timeoutSeconds = 3600, ?array $tags = null, ?string $forkedSessionId = null, ?array $delegation = null, ?string $permissionMode = null, ?float $permissionAskTimeout = null): BackgroundSessionSpawn a new background session as a child process with IPC.
spawnSessionAsync(string $name, Agent $agent, string $task, string $workingDirectory, int $timeoutSeconds = 3600, ?array $tags = null, ?string $forkedSessionId = null, ?array $delegation = null, ?string $permissionMode = null, ?float $permissionAskTimeout = null): PromiseInterfacespawnSession() without the wait. The daemon is launched and its handshake is left to advanceSpawns(), which the event loop drives through tick(). The promise resolves with the session once the daemon authenticates, and rejects after SPAWN_AUTH_TIMEOUT_SECS with the message the synchronous spawn throws. Argument errors and a launch that cannot start still throw here, before any promise exists.
advanceSpawns(?float $now = null): voidAdvance every spawn still waiting on its daemon's handshake. Never blocks: queued connections are accepted, readable bytes are read, and a spawn is finished, or failed once its deadline has passed. Driven by tick(), and by the synchronous spawnSession() while it waits.
teardown(): voidFail every spawn still waiting on its daemon's handshake, so nothing is left pending when this supervisor goes away. Each one is rejected, its launcher is retired and its IPC files are removed; the daemon, which never registers, exits on its own when its connect to the removed socket fails.

stopSessionAsync(string $sessionId): PromiseInterfaceThe rungs of stopSession(), run as a loop-driven state machine. The promise resolves with the outcome once advanceStops() (driven by tick()) settles it; nothing here sleeps or waits on a socket. Answers that need no rung resolve at once.

reconnect(?string $workingDirectory = null): arrayReconnect to background sessions when a TUI (re)opens: the ones this supervisor already holds, and — given the project they were spawned for — the ones a PREVIOUS process spawned (roadmap 4.3-3).
adoptHandedOff(): arrayAdopt every session a process forked from this one spawned on its behalf (roadmap 4.3-2), and return them.
ownedActiveSummaries(): arrayThe running background sessions this process owns, as the index records them — its own /bg sessions and the background Task runs handed to it — newest last (roadmap 4.3-2: the "Active subagents" row a turn's dispatch carries). Read from the index rather than this instance's table, so any supervisor of the process gives the same answer. Settled sessions are gone from the index, so they are not listed.
resetReconnected(): voidReset the reconnect flag — useful when supervisor restarts fresh.
stallWarnings(): arrayReturn all agents currently flagged as stalled via their token throughput.
getStallWarnings(): arrayBC forwarder for the pre-rename accessor name.
onSessionCompleted(BackgroundSession $session): void
onSessionFailed(BackgroundSession $session): void
onSessionStopped(BackgroundSession $session): voidForward a stop to a listener that can tell it from a failure, and to onSessionFailed() otherwise (see SessionStopNotificationInterface).
onSessionStalled(BackgroundSession $session): void
onSessionResumed(BackgroundSession $session): void
onSessionStreaming(BackgroundSession $session, string $chunk): void
withListener(?SessionNotificationInterface $listener): selfCreate a new supervisor with a different listener.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $major)

PtyRelay final class

The relay process that keeps an interactive background shell's pty master alive past the tool call that started it.

MethodSummary
static main(): intRun one relay session from the launch argv. Returns the process exit code; the -r snippet the registry spawns turns it into the process status. Never throws: every failure path answers 2 (refused-to-run) or a recorded exit file, because a relay that fatalled mid-wait would strand a row as running-until-the-24h-sweep exactly like a corpse.

Schedule final class

One repeating prompt: a name, a cadence, the task, and when it next fires.

MethodSummary
__construct(string $name, int $everySeconds, string $prompt, ?string $provider = null, ?string $permissionMode = null, ?int $nextDue = null, bool $enabled = true, bool $persisted = true, ?string $root = null, ?string $sessionId = null, ?int $timeoutSeconds = null, ?string $createdBy = null, string $kind = self::KIND_TASK)
static fromArray(array $row, int $now): selfParse one file row at the boundary. A value that cannot be trusted is refused HERE, naming the field, rather than entering the roster.
toArray(): arrayThe file-row form. model/reuseSession-style keys are NOT part of this format — the plan's row is these eleven fields and nothing else.
isDue(int $now): boolWhether this row should run at $now. Cadence and enablement decide; nothing else.
nextDueAfter(int $now): intThe next due stamp after $now, skipping every occurrence missed since the current one. A host that was down for a week fires ONCE when it returns and reschedules for the next live slot — the overrun skip is this arithmetic, not a queue, so missed counts cannot burst (the bound on this path is due-COUNTS; no timer bounds the act of firing itself. The run a fire spawns does carry the ordinary background-session wall-clock bound — default 3600s, per-row raisable, self::$timeoutSeconds — which is a daemon ceiling, not a timeout on any model request; E646 untouched).
withNextDue(int $nextDue): self
withEnabled(bool $enabled): self
withKind(string $kind): self

ScheduleFactory final class

The single creation path for persisted schedule rows (C-AGT-5.a).

MethodSummary
static modelRowCount(ScheduleRegistry $registry, ?string $hostRoot): intHow many persisted rows this root has that carry the model tag. The comparison is strict on BOTH sides: a null root matches only unbound rows (which the factory no longer creates, but a legacy file may carry), and operator-tagged or untagged rows never count.
static deleteRefusal(Schedule $row, ?string $hostRoot, bool $includeOperatorRows): ?stringThe guard on a tool-side delete: the refusal sentence, or null when this row may go. Arms in order of breadth — the human-spelled door opens everything, then the creation tag, then the root. The operator-row sentence is byte-frozen from C-AGT-5.a (it is pinned there); the cross-root sentence is new in C-AGT-5.b and names the fact it refuses on so the model can tell "wrong project" from "not mine to touch".

ScheduleRegistry final class

The roster of Schedule rows, the file behind them, and the clock.

MethodSummary
static loadDefault(?string $hostRoot = null): selfThe default home-backed registry: ~/.candy-code/schedules.json. With no vouchsafe home there is nowhere durable to keep rows, so the registry still exists — it just cannot persist (a persisted add refuses loudly, /loop keeps working in memory).
static atPath(string $path, ?string $hostRoot = null): selfA registry over an explicit path (tests, --config homes), bound to $hostRoot.
static inMemory(): selfA registry with NO backing file: the /loop half works, persistence refuses loudly.
all(): array
get(string $name): ?Schedule
hasEnabled(): boolWhether any tick has work to watch for: one enabled row keeps the pump subscription alive.
isWatchable(): boolWhether a hand-edit on disk could ARRIVE later — the slow watch's door (C-AGT-7.a). True for exactly the file-backed registries: an in-memory roster has no external writer, so nothing on disk can ever change it and a watch would only burn a timer. The reload itself is the registry's own reloadIfChanged() digest latch; this method only answers "is there a file to latch against".
loadErrors(): array
due(int $now): array
dueEphemeralFor(string $sessionId, int $now): array
removeEphemeralFor(string $sessionId): intDrop every ephemeral row belonging to this session; returns how many went.
add(Schedule $schedule): voidInsert or replace a row. Duplicate names refuse — a name is an identity (and a lock-file stem), silently shadowing one row with another would let the second writer steal the first's clock.
remove(string $name): bool
setEnabled(string $name, bool $enabled): ?Schedule
noteNextDue(string $name, int $nextDue): voidReplace one row's clock slot. Used by the pumps: the ephemeral fire path advances in memory only, and the persisted path is advanced by fireDue() itself.
persist(): voidWrite the PERSISTED rows (and only those) back to disk, under the file lock, and only when the roster actually differs from what the lock was taken to protect. A caller holding no lock that cannot take one inside FILE_LOCK_RETRIES polls refuses loudly — a /schedules delete that silently did not delete would be worse than an error the human can repeat.
reloadIfChanged(): boolRead the file if its content digest moved since the last touch. A host that edited schedules.json by hand (or another host's persist) lands here within one tick, without this process holding a watcher.
fireDue(int $now, \Closure $spawn): PromiseInterfaceEvaluate every due PERSISTED row THIS HOST owns: claim the row's lock, skip when another host holds it or a run of this name is still in flight, re-read the disk inside the claim, advance the clock, spawn through $spawn, and remember the session so the pump can clearFired() when it settles.
noteFired(string $name, string $sessionId): voidMark the row busy with the session that is running it.
busySession(string $name): ?stringThe daemon whose run still counts as this row's current fire, if any.
clearFired(string $name): voidCalled by the pump when the named row's session settles (or vanishes).
firedNames(): array
lastOutcome(string $name): ?arrayThe last fireDue decision naming this row, or null when this process has never evaluated it (a legacy-era view: nothing recorded, nothing shown).
lastOutcomes(): array
load(): voidRead schedules.json. Never throws: every failure mode — and every permission-mode coercion, which is a note beside a row that still loaded — becomes a named entry in loadErrors(), with the roster (re)built from whatever is trustworthy.

ScheduleSpawner final class

The one way a due Schedule becomes a running daemon (AUT-1).

MethodSummary

The suffix rides the SPAWN, never the stored row, so /schedules list shows the human's prompt, and a row flipped to task on disk mid-flight cannot de-instruct an already-spawned heartbeat (the tag, not the row, is what the pump consults).

static isHeartbeat(BackgroundSession $session): boolWhether a settled daemon is a heartbeat fire (the tag — see tagsFor()).

SugarCraft\Code\Bundles

Bundle final class

One installed Claude-format plugin bundle: a directory carrying a .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest (a bare top-level plugin.json is accepted too — the format's own README shows both shapes).

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $dir, public readonly string $name, public readonly string $tier, public readonly string $version = '', public readonly string $description = '', public readonly array $manifest = [], public readonly ?string $ownedBy = null)
static fromDir(string $dir, string $tier, ?string $ownedBy = null): ?selfLoad the bundle rooted at $dir, or null when $dir is not a readable, parseable bundle. Absent and malformed manifests both answer null — hasManifest() is how the caller tells "not a bundle" (skip quietly) from "broken bundle" (warn by name).
static readManifest(string $dir): arrayThe parsed manifest of $dir, or [] when there is no readable, decodable one. The installer's name lookup rides this; fromDir() keeps its own stricter read (no manifest OR no decode means no bundle AT ALL — discovery skips, the installer refuses with a named reason).
static hasManifest(string $dir): boolTrue when $dir carries either manifest shape, readable or not.
static manifestPath(string $dir): ?stringThe manifest $dir carries, or null. The first manifest shape that is a file decides: when its real path escapes the bundle directory, the whole bundle is refused (a real bare manifest beside a linked hidden one does not rescue it). A link that resolves inside the bundle loads like any file. discovery's guard() bounds the bundle DIRECTORY, and is_file() would otherwise follow a link planted at the manifest or at its .claude-plugin container out to a file nothing bounded.
static refusedManifest(string $dir): ?stringThe bundle-relative path of the manifest $dir carries that manifestPath() refused for resolving outside the bundle, or null. Lets the installer and discovery name the link instead of reporting the manifest as absent.
skillsPaths(): array
commandsPaths(): array
agentsPaths(): array
mcpFile(): ?stringThe bundle's MCP config file, when it ships or declares one. DECLINED AT THE WIRE: discovery surfaces the path so the launch notice can name it, and the operator may import it deliberately through candy-code mcp import; nothing in candy-code starts servers from here.
hooksPaths(): arrayEvery path in the bundle that would register hooks — a hooks manifest entry, an INLINE hooks object, or the conventional hooks/ directory. TRUST-GATED (code-chat §10 P1, owner reversal D1): \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::hooks() registers these files for a bundle the user trusted by name, and only there — the entries are raw manifest bytes, so the consumer re-asserts containment, the private-bytes gate and loadability before anything is registered. An untrusted bundle's hooks still decline with a launch notice naming it, so the operator learns the bundle is not running whole rather than wondering why its statusline vanished. An inline declaration answers the manifest path, because the hooks ride inside plugin.json itself (C-EXT-7); that path currently refuses itself at parse — the plugin.json shape is not the hooks-file shape — and the notice says so (recorded seam: an inline-hooks reader is deferred).
hasTrustGatedContent(): boolWhether name trust gates anything this bundle carries: channel or subscriber entrypoints, or hook files. Commands, skills and agents load for every bundle, so a project-tier copy of a trusted name without this content withholds nothing, and no trust-refusal notice may name it.
entrypoints(): arrayThe manifest's entrypoints declaration: contributor KIND => the files it names, each with the class it promises. This is a PARSE, not a load — no bytes of any named file are read here. The decision whether an entrypoint is ever required lives behind the trust gate of the bundle channel loader, which refuses an untrusted bundle before its file is touched; this method only answers what the manifest itself names.

shadowedTrustedCopies(): arrayThe project-tier copies of trusted names that the last discover() dropped for a user-tier twin. They are absent from discover()'s list, so a caller that announces trust refusals reads them here; the shadow warning alone says nothing about trust.

The user-tier record of ADDED marketplaces — and the gate every install from one must pass.

MethodSummary
static loadDefault(): selfThe home-backed registry: ~/.candy-code/marketplaces.json. No vouchsafe home means no backing file — the empty catalog answers, and every mutation refuses rather than writing wherever ~ fell back to.

The refusal sentence names the rule that bit; null means it landed (and landed DURABLE — an unbacked registry refuses, because a catalog that evaporates at process exit would let a later install believe it had been added).

Path rows are the operator's explicit word (the same verdict every other user-tier path setting draws) and carry the directory itself.

installEntry(Marketplace $marketplace, string $entryName, array $allowlist = []): ?MarketplaceEntryThe entry an install may act on, with the registry's pinned commit stamped onto its provenance, or null when installGate() refuses.

Attach final class

candy-code attach [<session>] [--url <url>] — the TUI as a client of a running candy-code serve (roadmap O-8a, Appendix O §4.9).

MethodSummary
static run(ParsedArgs $args): int
static connect(string $url, string $token, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?\Closure $after = null, ?Backoff $redialBackoff = null): PromiseInterfaceOpen the candy-code.v1 WebSocket at $url (ws://host:port/ws) with $token as the bearer credential: the HTTP upgrade via stream(), then a RemoteSessionHost over the socket — carrying the same dial as its re-dial, so a dropped connection resumes rather than dies (ISS-114). A refusal rejects with the status line and the server's own reason.
static stream(string $url, string $token, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): PromiseInterfaceThe dial behind connect(): connect, send the HTTP upgrade, check its answer (101, the accept key, the subprotocol echoed), and hand back the duplex socket plus whatever bytes the handshake read beyond its end. Twice the same call means twice the same session's front door — which is what a resume re-dials (ISS-114).
static websocketUrl(string $url): ?stringws://host:port/ws for an http(s):// or ws(s):// address — the URL serve prints and server.json records — or null when $url is neither, or is a malformed address the library refuses (a bracketed host that is not an IPv6 literal, an unbracketed IPv6 host, a bad zone id). A path other than the WebSocket's is replaced, so the address a browser opens works here as given.
static lockHolderOffer(string $sessionId, ?int $holderPid): ?stringThe sentence a read-only session's notice adds when the process holding its lock is the running candy-code serve: how to drive that session from this terminal instead. Null when the holder is not the server (another TUI), unknown, or no server is running.

Bootstrap final class

Wires up the CLI's shared, side-effecting collaborators: backend selection, the built-in coding tools, and the real on-disk SessionStore/MemoryStore/InstructionFileLoader that back /branch, /rewind, and /memory (P6.S9/S11/S12/S15).

Malformed entries degrade to "that one pattern is ignored" exactly as forcedInstructions() does, because both lists are hand-authored in a config file; a pattern that will not compile matches nothing, so exclusion fails OPEN — this key removes context the operator asked to remove and never removes more on a parse ambiguity.

static sessionRetentionDays(): intHow many days an unnamed session survives without being touched, from CANDY_CODE_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS, else the sessionRetentionDays setting (roadmap N-P4g).
static seedSession(\SugarCraft\Code\Session\SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore $store, string $provider = 'candy-code', string $model = 'unknown'): arrayGive the CLI a real session row to run against, resuming the most recent one when the store already has sessions and creating one when it does not (§5 E1's sketch).
static selectedProviderLabel(): arrayDelegates to LaunchContext::selectedProviderLabel() — the body moved in the S1b composition split (W7-E C3); this keeps the door (and its visibility) every caller and the settings-schema reader citations name.
static selectedProviderName(): ?stringDelegates to LaunchContext::selectedProviderName() — the body moved in the S1b composition split (W7-E C3); this keeps the door (and its visibility) every caller and the settings-schema reader citations name.
static backendCommandTierIsSelected(): boolWhether this run is on one of backend()'s two shell-out tiers — $CANDY_CODE_BACKEND_CMD or $CANDY_CODE_BACKEND_CMD_STREAM.
static titleBackend(): ?BackendA deliberately cheap Backend for Chat's one-shot session-title call, or null when this run has no provider to build one from.
static summaryBackend(?Backend $main = null): ?BackendThe session's summary backend (Phase 5 item 6; roadmap 2.4-2), or null when this run has no provider to build one from.
static summaryModel(): ?stringDelegates to LaunchContext::summaryModel() — the body moved in the S1b composition split (W7-E C3); this keeps the door (and its visibility) every caller and the settings-schema reader citations name.
static advisorBackend(): ?BackendThe advisor backend (C-PRV-3.d, roadmap W24), or null — and null is the DEFAULT answer, deliberately, unlike its two siblings.
static maxCostUsd(): ?floatThe spend ceiling for this launch, in US dollars — from the --max-cost flag (useMaxCost()), else $CANDY_CODE_MAX_COST, else the maxCostUsd setting (persistedMaxCostUsd()) — or null for no cap (Phase 5 item 7, flag half of ISS-006).
static keybindingsSetting(): arrayThe keybindings override map as the launch should apply it.
static reportKeybindingCollisions(): voidAnnounce every registered keybindings override that landed on another binding's SHIPPED chord (rv6 follow-up to ISS-047).
static reportSkippedClaudeSettingsEvents(): voidDrain the skip-and-record accumulators: an event a foreign Claude Code settings file names that \SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\HookEvent has no case for is skipped at parse (ClaudeSettingsHooks), and since C-EXT-1.b so are entries of an unsupported string type and entries carrying keys this dialect does not speak. All of it is announced HERE as ONE aggregate row whatever the count — the reportSkillSkips() contract. Reached from chat()'s drain block, which runs AFTER workspace() construction read every hook file, so one call sees every parse the launch made. Supersedes the old hard refusal for the CC dialect ONLY (R3's native hooks.yaml refusal is untouched — a foreign vendor's evolving event list must not brick every launch; that blast radius WAS the defect).
static reportHomeDirectoryStandIn(): voidv1:m-1: say it out loud ONCE when this launch resolved ~ through the temp-directory stand-in (\SugarCraft\Code\Support\HomeDirectory::standInUsed()). The stand-in itself is unchanged — the loud paths that REFUSE on it (cli.refuse.no_home) stay exactly as they were; what was missing is that every NON-refusing reader kept working off /tmp/.candy-code with no signal that the home resolution had degraded. One row whatever the call count: the seam de-dupes by message identity.
static reportHomeFromPasswd(): voidS-H03: the one-line stderr notice for the launches that never reach the TUI drain (-p/run, serve) when ~ resolved through the passwd database because $HOME and $USERPROFILE are both unset. Notice only — the directory is a real one and nothing refuses on it. Once per process (the seam de-dupes by message).
static terminalGuidanceNotice(string $term, bool $tty, bool $consoleVtEnabled = false): ?stringThe dumb-family test, split out as a pure function so the gate is pinned by a table instead of a fake terminal. THE FAMILY: '' (TERM unset — nothing was advertised), and any dumb…/unknown… prefix, case- and whitespace-insensitively. xterm, screen, vt100 and friends get nothing — a normal launch stays byte-unchanged, which is the polarity the existing transcript pins keep asserting.
static consoleVtEnabled(): boolWhether the Windows console on STDOUT has virtual-terminal processing on. Only ever true on native Windows; sapi_windows_vt100_support() with no second argument only asks, it does not switch the mode on.
static reportTerminalGuidance(?bool $tty = null, ?bool $consoleVtEnabled = null): voidv2:a11y-F3: guide a launch on a TTY that can NOT speak TUI — before, TERM=dumb users met a wall of bytes with no pointer at the paths that work for them. Gated on the tty as well as the family: the -p/scripted shapes answer on pipes all day and need no advice. The $tty seam defaults to reading stdout for real (the sugar-readline q3 idleSleeper pattern — an injectable observation point so the positive half is pinned without minting a pty in the suite).
static reportBundleRecommendations(?string $root = null, ?MarketplaceRegistry $registry = null, ?string $stampFile = null, ?string $installedRoot = null): voidC-EXT-4.d: the marketplace bundles that fit the project being opened, named at launch, once per project per marketplace pin, from local bytes only.
static reloadKeybindings(): void/keys reload: re-read the keybindings setting and re-apply it to the LIVE registry — plan_comparison TUI-4a. NO file watcher: the user edits the file and says the word, the same stance the MCP digest detection takes, and for the same reason — re-applying a repository- adjacent choice without being asked re-arms surprises the freeze closed. Absent launch digest (an embedder that never booted through chat()) means the first reload APPLIES rather than claiming anything.
static macAltNotice(string $osFamily, bool $kittyCapable): ?stringplan_comparison TUI-5 stage 1: the Option-as-Meta hint for macOS launches. PURE so every quadrant is pinned on a Linux host.
static terminalSpeaksKittyKeyboard(): boolWhether the ambient terminal environment names a kitty-speaking emulator — delegated to MacAltNotice::terminalSpeaksKittyKeyboard(), which since C-TUI-7.b also reads the emulator identity variables that survive tmux, so a Mac inside tmux-on-kitty is no longer misread as needing the Option-as-Meta lecture.
static memoryStore(?string $root = null): MemoryStoreReal, on-disk memory store backing /memory. MemoryStore's constructor requires its directory to already exist and be writable, so the directory is created here first.
static memoryStoreOrNull(?string $root = null): ?MemoryStorememoryStore(), or null if it cannot be opened.
static trustedConfigDirPath(): stringconfigDirPath() for the two files that are SECURITY POLICY rather than preference — config.json (permission mode, permission rules, trustedProjectHooks) and hooks.yaml (shell commands run on tool calls) — and therefore the one path resolution that may not fall back to a directory anybody else can write.
static capabilityPresent(string $binary, ?string $pathList = null): boolIs $binary installed and executable?
static systemConfigPath(): stringThe managed tier's read target — \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH unless a pin has aimed it elsewhere through useSystemConfigPath(). --config does NOT move this path: that override replaces layer 4 and nothing else, and the settings editor's doors never consult this method at all — no write seam in src/ resolves to the managed path, which \SugarCraft\Code\Tests\Config\ConfigWriteProducerDocumentationDriftTest pins as structure.
static useSystemConfigPath(?string $path): voidAim the managed-tier READ at another path, for pins; null (or blank, same law as useProjectRootForSettings()'s blank refusal) restores the fixed /etc/candy-code/config.json. Deliberately not an environment variable — see \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH for why a movable managed path is the tier's own defeat. Not stored through LaunchContext: this is a test seam, not a launch flag, and keeping it here says so.
static managedLayer(): arrayTHE MANAGED TIER SITS ON TOP OF THE SESSION TIER (G1-L7, CCOPS-6): the read-only machine-wide file (\SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::systemLayer(), aimed by systemConfigPath()) outranks the session tier as well — its whole purpose is a control the person being managed cannot undo by re-choosing in the settings view — while the environment and flags still outrank it, for exactly the stated SessionSettings reason. It carries only \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::LAYERED_KEYS, so no unlayered permission key reaches a reader through it, and like the session tier it is laid on the merged result, not handed to LayeredSettings::merge(). Both halves of the tool-removal diff get it too, so a managed narrowing can never read as a project-tier removal — and can never be blamed on one.
static useSessionLaunchPresetId(?string $sessionId): voidDelegates to LaunchContext::useSessionLaunchPresetId() — D1 (RS-DRIVER a): --session-id registers on the same launch-context seam as the mode/target pair, so the one funnel every session-opening surface reads is also the one that sees the preset.
static sessionLaunchPresetId(): ?stringThe id --session-id pre-allocated for this launch, if any.
static useAgentPreset(?string $name): voidRegister --agent <name> for this process — delegates to LaunchContext::useAgentPreset(), the launch-context shelf where the store lives beside the model and permission registers (C3, RS-AGENT).
static trustedBundleChannelNames(): arrayThe bundle NAMES allowed to load their declared channel entrypoints in-process, frozen for the life of this process — the third gate on that door, and the only one a bundle can never touch, since the list is read exclusively from the user's own configuration file.

DoctorChannelsChecks final class

The three channel/bundle legs of doctor, kept out of DoctorChecks so the roster file stays a thin seat (SourceSizeRatchet) and its own no-read law (exactly one file_get_contents for config file) stays pinned.

MethodSummary
static channelsStoreRow(?callable $configDir = null): arraychannels store — the 0600 cred store: presence, readability, mode, and (loudly) corruption. A corrupt store reads as [] at boot; without this row that failure is invisible until "my channels vanished".
static channelBundlesRow(?string $root = null, ?array $bundles = null, ?array $trustedNames = null, ?ChannelsStore $store = null): arraychannel bundles — read-only preview of next launch's quarantine: stale trusted names, entry points that escape their bundle or sit on loose bytes, and first-sight entry points the loader would hold back. Mirrors BundleChannelLoader's decision order without its writes or its require_once — the loader executes quarantined bytes only AFTER they were seen clean twice; doctor never executes anything at all.
static inboundLogRow(?callable $configDir = null): arrayinbound log — the durable inbound ledger's posture: presence, mode (the 0600 law), and how many .corral-* quarantine siblings it has left behind. Names only, never rows(): the corralled bytes failed to parse once and must not be re-parsed to answer a status question.

DoctorChecks final class

The install checks behind candy-code doctor AND the in-session /doctor command — one roster, read two ways.

MethodSummary
static run(?string $root): arrayEvery check, run in roster order, each one wrapped individually.
static sessionStoreRow(int $count, int $bytes): arrayThe session store verdict, kept off the probe so the WARN edge is pin-testable without engineering a two-gigabyte database.
static probes(?string $root): arrayThe doctor's checks, as label => closure returning {status: 'OK'|'WARN'|'FAIL', detail: string}.
static otlpExportRow(bool $exporting, array $health): arrayThe otlp export verdict (S-O27), kept off the probe so each edge is pin-testable. Reads counters only — never dials, never names the endpoint (it can carry credentials). The tally is THIS process's: a fresh candy-code doctor honestly reports none recorded, while the in-session /doctor reports the live session's losses.

HeadlessPermissionPrompt final class

Settles a HookResult::ask() for a run that has a CONSOLE but no TUI. Two callers attach it, and the tty probe below decides opposite ways for them: the -p "<prompt>" / run "<prompt>" one-shot path in NonInteractive, which owns stdin and is answered at a real terminal; and the background-session daemon (\SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSessionRunner::backend()), whose fd 0 is /dev/null from the spawn site, so it always takes the refusal branch — attached there for the REFUSAL's text, not for a prompt nobody would see.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly PermissionMode $mode, $in = null, $err = null, private readonly ?bool $interactive = null)
approver(): \ClosureThis prompt as the \Closure(ToolCall, HookResult): bool that \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::withPermissionApprover() takes.
static requireUnattendedAnswer(string ...$hookNames): void
static forgetUnattendedAnswers(): voidBack to "nobody opted in" — the test-shape twin of pinTurnHooksForTesting.
static demandsUnattendedAnswer(HookResult $ask): boolWhether $ask came (wholly or partly) from a rostered hook. Every name in HookResult::$askedBy is consulted, not just HookResult::refusingHook()'s first: the chain put the first question, but a LATER asker that demanded an answer does not consent to being auto-answered by an earlier one's silence.
__invoke(ToolCall $call, HookResult $ask): boolPut one ASK to the console and return whether it was granted.

The suite pins false for the same reason the renderer cache is pinned there — a byte-identity pin must not inherit the width of whatever terminal happens to run phpunit. Mirrors pretendHostArchiveForTesting().

static version(): stringReturn the --version line for the candy-code binary, newline-terminated.

Pretends the process was launched from the phar at $path — pass null to restore auto-detection. Without it the DST-1 metadata arm of versionString() is unreachable from the suite, because a phpunit process never lives inside an archive; the non-injected self-update pin drives the real resolution path through here.

LaunchContext final class

The launch-context shelf: the process-wide stores that the launch wiring fills — what bin/candy-code registered from argv and environment — and that the composition roots read thousands of lines and several objects away.

MethodSummary
static useConfigPath(?string $path): voidPoint every reader of the per-user config.json at $path instead of the discovered ~/.candy-code/config.json — what --config <path> does.
static useModel(?string $model): voidRegister --model <name> for this process.
static useTuiErrorLog(?string $destination): voidRegister where the TUI's error_log redirect landed — Bootstrap::app() passes on TuiErrorLog::install()'s answer from bin/candy-code.
static useSessionLaunch(bool $continue, bool $resume = false, ?string $target = null): voidRegister the session -c/--continue or --resume asked for, for this process — the same process-wide seam as useModel(), and under the same clear-what-you-set test contract documented there.
static useSessionLaunchPresetId(?string $sessionId): voidRegister the id --session-id pre-allocated — D1 (RS-DRIVER a). The same clear-as-set contract as useSessionLaunch(): passing null (no flag) clears the static, so bin's registration and the -p funnel's idempotent re-registration agree on every answer.
static useIncognito(bool $incognito): voidRegister --incognito (C-SES-7.c): this launch keeps no session row, no transcript and no automatic memory writes. The parser has already refused the flag beside --continue/--resume, so an incognito launch can only be opening a NEW session — there is nothing stored to reopen.
static useRestricted(bool $restricted): voidRegister --restricted (C-SEC-7.b): this launch cannot run code — the shell-subject tools and the agent/workflow/MCP-call shapers leave the model-facing set at \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::filterToolSet().
static useSafeMode(bool $safeMode): voidRegister --safe-mode (C-SEC-7.b): this launch ignores every trust grant, bundle and foreign import, as if no root had ever been trusted.
static pinPromptHistoryPath(?string $path): voidPoint the prompt history at $path instead of ~/.candy-code, or back at the default with null. For the test suite, which pins it into its sandbox so a test that presses Enter on a Bootstrap::chat()-built Chat can never add its prompt to the developer's own ↑ history.
static usePermissionMode(?string $mode): voidRegister --permission-mode <mode> for this process. See useModel() for why this is a static rather than a parameter.
static useMaxCost(?string $maxCost): voidRegister --max-cost <usd> for this process. See useModel() for why this is a static rather than a parameter, and usePermissionMode() for why it is stored RAW: the number is judged by Bootstrap::maxCostUsd(), which throws PermissionConfigException inside bin/candy-code's dispatch try — where it becomes the same exit-2 usage error (with the JSON error document under --output-format json) that an unusable $CANDY_CODE_MAX_COST or maxCostUsd setting already produces — rather than as an uncaught fatal at registration time.
static useMaxTurns(?string $maxTurns): voidRegister --max-turns <n> for this process. See useMaxCost() for why this is a static storing the RAW value: the number is judged by Bootstrap::maxTurns(), which throws PermissionConfigException where the dispatch can catch it — one-shot runs in NonInteractive::run()'s own pre-flight try, the TUI through the backend construction bin/candy-code wraps — so a ceiling that is present and unusable refuses the launch with exit 2 rather than silently running uncapped, exactly as a bad --max-cost does.
static useAgentPreset(?string $name): voidRegister --agent <name> for this process. See useModel() for why this is a static rather than a threaded parameter, and for the clear-what-you-set contract this honours: null (and the empty string) clear the preset as surely as they set one, so an in-process relaunch cannot inherit an earlier launch's verdict. The name is NOT judged here — \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::chat() applies it through the Chat's own switch at launch, where the roster is real.
static configPathOverride(): ?stringThe config FILE --config named; null means discover.
static modelOverride(): ?stringThe model --model named; null means fall back.
static agentPresetOverride(): ?stringThe agent preset --agent named; null means the plain launch default.
static tuiErrorLog(): ?stringWhere the TUI's error_log redirect landed; null means untouched.
static sessionLaunchMode(): string'new' (the default), 'continue', or 'resume'.
static sessionLaunchTarget(): ?stringThe id or name --resume named; null with 'resume' opens the picker.
static sessionLaunchPresetId(): ?stringThe id --session-id pre-allocated (D1, RS-DRIVER a); null with no flag.
static incognito(): boolWhether this launch keeps nothing (useIncognito(), C-SES-7.c).
static restricted(): boolWhether this launch cannot run code (useRestricted(), C-SEC-7.b).
static safeMode(): boolWhether this launch ignores all trust (useSafeMode(), C-SEC-7.b).
static promptHistoryPath(): ?stringWhere the ↑/↓ prompt history lives when the default is overridden.
static permissionModeOverride(): ?stringThe RAW --permission-mode string; validation defers to the gate.
static maxCostOverride(): ?stringThe RAW --max-cost string; judgment defers to the resolver.
static maxTurnsOverride(): ?stringThe RAW --max-turns string; judgment defers to the resolver.
static hasMcpClient(int $pid, string $memoKey): boolWhether $memoKey already sits in this pid's client bucket (a memoised NULL counts — presence is array_key_exists, not truthiness).
static mcpClientFor(int $pid, string $memoKey): ?McpClientThe client bucket's entry for $memoKey, or null.
static rememberMcpClient(int $pid, string $memoKey, ?McpClient $client): voidMemoise the client built for $memoKey at its build instant — the same moment that stores the config digest (MCP-3), so 'at launch' cannot straddle two versions of the file.
static takeMcpClientsBucket(int $pid): arrayHand back THIS pid's whole client bucket and drop it — the stop seam's half of stopMcpServers()'s per-pid rule.
static hasMcpToolShape(int $pid, string $memoKey): boolWhether this pid already holds a derived shape for $memoKey.
static mcpToolShapeFor(int $pid, string $memoKey): ?McpToolShapeThe memoised shape for $memoKey, or null.
static rememberMcpToolShape(int $pid, string $memoKey, ?McpToolShape $shape): voidMemoise the derived shape — the MCP-7 cache law: the roster derives once per config memo key and never re-reads mid-session.
static mcpConfigDigestFor(int $pid, string $tierPath): ?arrayThe launch's stored digest bytes for $tierPath, or null when this launch stored none for it.
static rememberMcpConfigDigest(int $pid, string $path, array $digest): voidStore the digest beside the client memo it was decided on. Public because the builder that stores it is pinned by census to live in Bootstrap and call THIS seam at the memo point — the store itself stays private to this shelf.
static hasLspClient(int $pid, string $root): boolWhether $root is already resolved in this pid's LSP bucket — a memoised NULL counts (root with none configured).
static lspClientFor(int $pid, string $root): ?LspClientThe memoised client for $root, or null when none started.
static rememberLspClient(int $pid, string $root, ?LspClient $client): voidMemoise the outcome for $root — including the null, so the config is read once per process.
static takeLspClientsBucket(int $pid): arrayHand back THIS pid's whole LSP bucket and drop it.
static readLedgerFor(int $pid, string $root, \Closure $mint): ReadLedgerThis pid's ONE ledger for $root; $mint runs only on a miss (the ??= semantics live here so the store stays behind the shelf).
static backgroundShellRegistryFor(int $pid, string $root, \Closure $mint): BackgroundShellRegistryThis pid's ONE shell table for $root; $mint runs only on a miss.
static hasBundlesMemo(string $key): boolWhether the bundle scan for $key already ran this process.
static bundlesMemo(string $key): ?arrayThe memoised bundle list for $key.
static rememberBundlesMemo(string $key, array $bundles): arrayStore and return the scan result — = $bundles expression semantics.
static keybindingsAppliedDigest(): ?stringThe digest of the keybinding map the LIVE registry holds, or null when nothing was noted yet.
static rememberKeybindingsAppliedDigest(?string $digest): voidNote the applied keybinding map digest (TUI-4a).
static stopMcpServers(): voidStop every MCP server THIS PID started.
static registerMcpShutdown(): voidTHE SHUTDOWN SEAM, and it had to be created: bin/candy-code runs Program::run() (or \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\NonInteractive::run()) and then falls off the end of the script, and a grep for register_shutdown_function across src/ and bin/ found nothing at all. A stopServers() that is never called leaves an orphaned third-party process per configured server after every session, which is worse than never starting them.
static stopLspServers(): voidStop the language servers THIS process started — the shutdown hook's callback, and the way a caller owning a process lifetime (a test, an embedder) hands them back early. This pid's bucket only, for the reason stopMcpServers() gives. Idempotent.
static registerLspShutdown(): voidRegister stopLspServers() to run at exit, once per process image, BEFORE the first server starts — so nothing can acquire a server without the stop. Same coverage and the same gaps as registerMcpShutdown().
static registerBackgroundShellShutdown(): voidTHE SHUTDOWN SEAM for background shells — same shape and same once- per-process-image reasoning as registerMcpShutdown(): a forked child inherits the hook, and stopBackgroundShells() acts only on THIS pid's bucket, so a tool child's exit tears down the shells that child itself spawned (none, in the ordinary case — the registry it hands home is rows without handles) and never touches the parent's live shells.
static stopBackgroundShells(): voidStop every background shell THIS pid holds a handle to, and release the per-pid bucket. PUBLIC for the shutdown-hook reason stopMcpServers() states, and idempotent the same way: teardown kills by recorded group, and the handle map empties with the bucket.
static egressProxyInstance(): ?EgressProxyProcessThe launch's egress proxy — the self::$egressProxy shelf read (C-TOOL-4.g). \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::egressProxy() owns starting it; consumers (the jail builder in \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\Sandbox\SandboxFactory::fromSetting()) only ever READ this, so a probe path can never spawn a child.
static egressProxyResolved(): boolWhether the launch has resolved its egress answer (null-is-final law).
static markEgressProxyResolved(): voidRecords the launch's FINAL answer when no relay is asked for (C-TOOL-4.g): the setting is not allowlist, or this host's jail never reads a socket — so the shelf stays empty and later reads do not re-consult the config.
static setEgressProxy(EgressProxyProcess $proxy): voidPark a started proxy on the shelf and note the owning pid — the pair stopEgressProxy() acts on. Called only by the starter, after registerEgressProxyShutdown() has run, so a stored handle can never outlive its shutdown hook.
static registerEgressProxyShutdown(): voidTHE SHUTDOWN SEAM for the egress proxy — same shape and same once-per-process-image reasoning as registerBackgroundShellShutdown(): a forked tool child inherits the hook, and stopEgressProxy() acts only when THIS pid is the one that started the proxy, so a worker's exit never kills the parent's live relay — while the parent's own exit always reaps it, because the jail's only egress path dies with the launch that promised it.
static stopEgressProxy(): voidStop the launch's egress proxy if THIS pid owns it, and clear the shelf. PUBLIC for the shutdown-hook reason stopBackgroundShells() states, and idempotent the same way: EgressProxyProcess::stop() reaps its group and discards the scaffold, and a child inheriting the hook sees a foreign pid and leaves the parent's relay running.
static useEgressProxyForTesting(?EgressProxyProcess $proxy, bool $resolved = true): voidTEST SEAM (C-TOOL-4.g): put the egress shelf in a chosen state — a stand-in started proxy, or the launch's final "no proxy" answer, or (null + unresolved) the untouched pre-resolution state. Clears the shutdown-registered flag ONLY when handed a proxy to stand in for, so the next starter re-arms its hook against the stand-in.

static withResolvedMaxToolSteps(EngineBackend $engine): EngineBackendRaise or keep the step ceiling on a freshly built engine - one place so Bootstrap::backend()'s echo path and Bootstrap::backendFor()'s real path cannot drift on it.
static withResolvedReasoningEffort(EngineBackend $engine): arrayC-PRV-1.b: the configured tier is lowered only where it SHAPES.
static resolvedServiceTier(): ?stringC-PRV-3.a: the configured service-tier WORD — 'fast', 'default', or null when nothing valid is set. Environment first (a human who exports CANDY_CODE_SERVICE_TIER means it for this process), then the layered user config read the same way selectedModelName() reads its key. An unrecognized value is not a tier: like the model env's junk it asks nothing rather than guessing, and the settings schema's enum already refuses such a value on the write side.
static withResolvedServiceTier(EngineBackend $engine): arrayC-PRV-3.a: the configured fast tier is lowered only where the pair the engine ACTUALLY carries shapes it. default never refuses: it is the standard lane, which every pair is on whether or not it can leave it, so applying it just clears any armed fast leg. fast consults \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\ShapesServiceTier::serviceTierFor() on $engine->provider() — NOT on an unwrapped primary. The earlier shape unwrapped a FallbackProvider, copied from withResolvedReasoningEffort(), where the unwrap is sound because effort rides the REQUEST and reaches whichever provider instance answers; the tier is no request field. It is a provider leg \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::withServiceTier() mints by overlaying $this->provider — which, under a fallbackModels block, is the wrapper, and the wrapper implements no such interface. So the door said yes, the engine stored the word, and the wire stayed clean on the production path (a block with fallbacks): the set-but-ignored this door exists to ban. A wrapped pair therefore comes back UNTOUCHED with a reason beside it, and the word is deliberately not stored either, so a status surface reads the truth (no tier armed) instead of a promise this wire will not keep. Delegating a tier THROUGH the wrapper is not merely wider — a block spans several provider+model PAIRS whose families differ on fast eligibility (Anthropic gates speed by family), and one wire value for all of them could buy the premium on a model that never asked for it; the per-pair resolution belongs to the C-PRV-3.b seam. The reason half is unsaid by this caller for the documented shelf reason above; saying it is that same seam.
static withConsolePermissionPrompt(EngineBackend $engine, PermissionGate $gate, bool $enabled): EngineBackendAttach the console approver, or hand the engine back untouched.

static app(?string $root = null, ?string $tuiErrorLog = null, ?string $initialPrompt = null): AppBuild the pane shell the CLI binary runs interactively: an App hosting the very chat() model this class already builds (§5 E7, the MERGE branch).
static settingsWriter(?string $root): \SugarCraft\Code\Config\Settings\SettingsWriterThe launch's settings write door (N-P2): its "You" tier goes through writeUserConfig() — the one writer config.json has — and its project tier only to a trusted project's settings.local.json. Built once per launch by workspace(), which registers it for Chat's /model (N-P3b); app() reuses that instance for the settings editor.
static launchTrustDialog(?string $root): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Tui\TrustDialogThe launch dialog for an interactive TUI start (C-SEC-5.d): the \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::pendingProjectTrust() census of $root wrapped in a dialog, or null when the root declares nothing pending or has already been asked this process. Only app() calls this — the interactive shell is the only surface that builds an App, which is what keeps -p and serve dialog-free by construction.
static resetTrustDialogLatchForTesting(): voidTest seam for the once-per-process ask latch — production never resets it; the process exiting does.
static dockFromUserConfig(): ?DockLayoutThe docked-pane layout the layout setting names, or null — which \SugarCraft\Code\App\App::dock() resolves to the launch default — when the key is absent, malformed, or left over from a build whose manifest this one cannot read. Failing soft here is the whole point: a bad geometry blob is a stale file, not a reason to refuse to start.
static renormalizeDock(DockLayout $dock): DockLayoutBoot-time validation of a restored dock manifest (candy-code-once-007): a layout saved at one terminal size is applied at another, so drop slots naming a pane that cannot dock here and renormalize the column shares of the ACTIVE sides so they never claim more than half the usable columns together (the pair rule withColumnShare() enforces live but a restored manifest bypasses). Which panes are shown is NOT touched by width: a too-narrow terminal is handled at render time by DockLayout::resolve()'s degradation ladder, so the persisted choice survives a visit to a small window.
static paneAutoShowFromUserConfig(): PaneAutoShowThe auto-show memory the layout blob's userToggled list names (ISS-049) — pane values the previous session's user touched by hand, so a closed pane does not ride back in on the next activity. Same fail-soft as dockFromUserConfig(): the list is an annotation on the layout key, and a malformed row is dropped, never fatal — its worst outcome is re-enabling one auto-dock the user meant to silence. Rows naming a non-dockable pane are dropped too: they can never be consulted, and storing them would launder a hand-edited config into shell state.

LaunchNotices final class

The launch-warning shelf: what one launch decided to say, once per message on stderr, and what the transcript being built gets to carry.

MethodSummary
static reset(): voidEmpty the launch-scoped shelves. Called by Bootstrap::chat() at the top of each launch, before any warning can be raised — what the transcript being built carries is a fact about THIS launch.
static reported(string $message): boolWhether stderr already carried this exact sentence in this process.
static markReported(string $message): voidClaim the sentence for the process so reported() answers true for it from now on.
static record(string $message, int $limit): voidPut one warning on the transcript shelf: clipped to the row bound if it needs clipping, de-duplicated, and capped — past the cap the message lands in the overflow set instead, to be counted by rows().
static rows(): arrayThe transcript rows for this launch, in raise order, with the overflow tail appended when there is one.
static droppedMessages(): arrayThe messages record() dropped once the transcript shelf filled its cap — the CLIPPED sentences behind the synthesised "...and N more" row rows() appends.
static pair(string $warning): stringThe pair regex's group, or the whole sentence when the collector's shape drifted — dropping a warning from the aggregate is never an option; paying for it in characters is.
static grantRows(array $warnings): arrayThe transcript rows for a narrowed-grant flood: ONE header row — the count, then as many compact grant pairs as fit inside LAUNCH_NOTICE_MAX_CHARS — plus ONE tail row counting what the pack could not fit. At most two rows, whatever the fan-out.

McpDecision final class

The MCP config-decision path: where each tier's server file is, what it declares, and whether this launch may act on it — computed without starting anything.

MethodSummary
static mcpConfigDecision(?string $root, \Closure $requireRoot, \Closure $projectMcpIsTrusted, \Closure $recordRefusal): arrayWhere this project's .mcp.json is, and whether this launch is allowed to start the servers it names — WITHOUT starting any of them.

static mcpDisabledByEnvironment(): boolTHE SPELLING behind Bootstrap::MCP_DISABLE_ENV, one place so the narrower truthy vocabulary — only 1, true, yes, case-insensitive — cannot drift into the flag-style default-everything-on convention. The vocabulary itself is EnvBool::isTrue(), the single owner of the narrow house law; this method is one of its consumers. Deliberately NOT the !== false && !== '' && !== '0' shape the other switches use: here the DEFAULT-ON side must be every value, so a launcher that cannot control what its environment carries (a shard runner inheriting an operator shell) still gets the documented default unless it sees one of the three words.

Starts nothing.
static mcpLivenessSnapshot(array $decision, \Closure $memoClient): ?arrayWhat THIS PROCESS has actually started, for the /mcp panel — reading the Bootstrap::$mcpClients memo, NEVER consulting Bootstrap::mcpClient().
static mcpPinRefusals(array $decision, \Closure $memoClient): arrayC-SEC-5.a: the servers the memo client's admission check refused — command, args or env drifted from what mcp trust fingerprinted.
static mcpConfigMemoKey(array $decision): stringMCP-3: the memo key for a decision. With NO resolvable user tier (an unowned home, or the disabled switch) this is exactly the canonical project path — the key every pre-MCP-3 reader and writer used. Whenever the home resolves, the key is the two paths joined by a NUL whether or not the user file exists yet: widening on resolvability rather than on existence is what keeps a file created mid-session from missing the memo and double-building the client. A path cannot contain NUL, so no pair of real files can collide with a single-path key.
static mcpConfigChangedSinceLaunch(array $decision, \Closure $storedDigest): ?boolE703-α: has .mcp.json changed since the launch that memoised it?
static mcpConfigDigest(string $path): ?arrayThe digest of $path's CURRENT bytes, or null when they cannot be read.
static mcpConfigRows(array $entries, array $shadowed = []): arrayMCP-3: the row builder both tiers of mcpServerInventory() read through — one source for the skipped sentence (N-2/ISS-091) and for the type/detail projection, so the listing says the same words about the project file and the user file. Lives OUTSIDE the inventory's own span on purpose: the AW documentation arm slices that span for its zero-sink claim and quotes this pair's rules; a second method in the slice would blur which body owes which pin.
static mcpUserTierRows(array $decision, array $shadowed): arrayMCP-3: the five user* listing keys, or the silent defaults when the user tier has nothing to say. The same three broken-shape reports as the project tier, through the same Lang sentences — an unreadable home file is described exactly like an unreadable project file, because from here it is the same kind of thing: bytes the operator cannot launch until they can be read.

ForeignCommandDiscovery final class

Discovers slash-command files from OTHER coding-CLI conventions — Claude Code's .claude/commands and opencode's command/commands pair, user and project — mirroring what \SugarCraft\Code\Skills\ForeignSkillDiscovery proves for skills: the class is a DIRECTORY LIST plus a merge order, and every containment decision stays in CommandLoader::loadFromDirectory() so this port has exactly one implementation of "may this path be read" rather than a second one tuned to foreign paths.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly CommandLoader $loader = new CommandLoader())
discoverClaude(string $projectRoot): arrayClaude Code's trees: ~/.claude/commands and {projectRoot}/.claude/commands, tagged SkillSource::Claude. Project before user, the walk last-write-wins, so the operator's own copy wins a name inside this convention (PROJECT < USER) — the OPPOSITE bias CommandLoader::loadAll() draws between the native tiers, where the project file out-ranks the user one; a native project command is the operator committing an override to the repo, while a cloned foreign tree is someone else's format arriving by git clone, which must not redefine what the operator hand-wrote at home.
discoverOpencode(string $projectRoot): arrayopencode's trees: BOTH of its spellings — the singular command directory \SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\BuiltIn\ProtectFilesHook names alongside the plural one, since reading only commands would silently drop the files opencode itself reads on the machines that follow its docs — in the legacy ~/.opencode pair and the XDG ~/.config/opencode pair, plus both project trees. Tagged SkillSource::Opencode; later directories win inside the convention (plural beats singular, XDG beats legacy), the ordering rule inherited from \SugarCraft\Code\Skills\ForeignSkillDiscovery::opencodeTiers().
discover(string $projectRoot, array $bundles = []): arrayEvery foreign tree, tier-first: both conventions' PROJECT dirs in convention order (Claude, opencode — the same cross-format tie inside a tier that \SugarCraft\Code\Skills\SkillManager::loadAll() draws at spec < claude < opencode), then the same trio with bundle trees FIRST inside each tier (see bundleDirs()), USER dirs in that same order. The walk order IS the precedence: last write wins, so opencode-user outranks everything foreign, and the whole result outranks nothing native — see the class doc-block for why being the floor is the point.
static bundleDirs(array $bundles): arrayThe command trees the given bundles contribute, in the same directory => [anchor, tier, badge, bundle-name] shape claudeDirs() builds (where the fourth slot is null). A bundle is anchored at ITS OWN directory — the containment boundary a bundle's contents may never cross, whichever tier installed it — and badged SkillSource::Bundle so the popup can say where the row came from.
