MethodSummary
static prompt(string $ref = '', bool $security = false, ?int $pr = null): stringThe prompt /review [<tree-ish>] or /security-review [ref] submits: the canned body, closing on the @diff mention (optionally scoped to $ref) that makes the scanner attach the very change being reviewed — or, when $pr names a pull-request number, on its @pr:<n> mention instead, which scopes the same review to the PR as filed on the host (C-AGT-6.d). $pr wins when both are handed: the caller's parse already refuses to mix the two, and the PR form is what was asked for.
static refError(string $ref, string $root): ?stringWhy $ref cannot carry a review turn, as the row the transcript should answer with — or null when the ref may (C-AGT-2). Two gates, in the order the scanner itself enforces them:
static prError(string $number): ?stringWhy $number cannot carry a --pr review turn, as the row the transcript should answer with — or null when it may. One gate only, deliberately: the ContextMentions::isPrNumber() rule the mention scanner itself enforces, because a spelling the scanner would refuse can never attach and the review would run against nothing. There is no gh-side probe here the way refError() pre-resolves a git ref: the design makes an unreachable host a NOTICE inside the turn (the model reads it and says what it could not see), not a refused command — see the class docblock. An empty $number is the flag with no argument: refused.

BuiltInCommand final class

MethodSummary
static new(CommandSpec $spec): selfA row with no dispatch: palette-only until withHandler() gives it one.

The hint painted by the slash menu is a spec concern (CommandSpec::$argumentHint); this is the ROUTING concern — which spellings dispatch — and it lives here so a row and its gate cannot be added apart.

ManagedConfigTier trait

The managed (machine-wide) settings tier: its read seam, its pin-only aiming, and the layer it hands the merged-config walk.

MethodSummary
static systemConfigPath(): stringThe managed tier's read target — \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH unless a pin has aimed it elsewhere through useSystemConfigPath(). --config does NOT move this path: that override replaces layer 4 and nothing else, and the settings editor's doors never consult this method at all — no write seam in src/ resolves to the managed path, which \SugarCraft\Code\Tests\Config\ConfigWriteProducerDocumentationDriftTest pins as structure.
static useSystemConfigPath(?string $path): voidAim the managed-tier READ at another path, for pins; null (or blank, same law as useProjectRootForSettings()'s blank refusal) restores the fixed /etc/candy-code/config.json. Deliberately not an environment variable — see \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH for why a movable managed path is the tier's own defeat. Not stored through LaunchContext: this is a test seam, not a launch flag, and keeping it here says so.
static managedLayer(): arrayTHE MANAGED TIER SITS ON TOP OF THE SESSION TIER (G1-L7, CCOPS-6): the read-only machine-wide file (\SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::systemLayer(), aimed by systemConfigPath()) outranks the session tier as well — its whole purpose is a control the person being managed cannot undo by re-choosing in the settings view — while the environment and flags still outrank it, for exactly the stated SessionSettings reason. It carries only \SugarCraft\Code\Config\LayeredSettings::LAYERED_KEYS, so no unlayered permission key reaches a reader through it, and like the session tier it is laid on the merged result, not handed to LayeredSettings::merge(). Both halves of the tool-removal diff get it too, so a managed narrowing can never read as a project-tier removal — and can never be blamed on one.

static path(callable $configDir): string

static readOrAccuse(callable $configDir): arrayThe launch-seam reader: previous record plus a "be suspicious" bit.
static fingerprint(?string $path): ?stringsha256 of a policy file's exact bytes, or null when it does not exist. Read failure counts as "absent": a file that cannot be read cannot be loaded either, so both snapshots agree on nothing-to-hash.

static refreshUserConfig(callable $configDir, ?string $hashBeforeWrite, ?string $hashAfterWrite): voidS-H10: an in-app config write must not accuse itself on the next launch.

SettingsWriter final class

The settings editor's write door (roadmap N-P2, Appendix N §4.4) — a SEPARATE door from Chat's onConfigChange, so that callback's census stays exactly provider and theme (\SugarCraft\Code\Tests\Config\ConfigWriteProducerDocumentationDriftTest), and itself censused by \SugarCraft\Code\Tests\Config\Settings\SettingsWriterCensusTest.

MethodSummary
static new(string $userConfigPath, \Closure $userConfigDoor, ?\Closure $userConfigMutate = null): self
withProject(?string $root, bool $trusted): selfThe project the project-local tier writes for, and whether it is trusted.
targetPath(SettingsTier $tier): ?stringThe file a tier writes, or null when that tier cannot be written — and null for the session tier, which writes no file at all.
tierRefusal(SettingsTier $tier): ?stringWhy a tier cannot be written at all, or null when it can.
refusal(SettingsTier $tier, string $key, mixed $value): ?stringWhy setting $key to $value on $tier is refused, or null when it may be written.
refusals(SettingsTier $tier, array $set, array $unset = []): arrayEvery refusal for a whole change set, keyed by setting key ('*' for the tier itself). Empty means write() would proceed.
current(SettingsTier $tier): arrayWhat $tier's file holds now, read STRICTLY: a missing file is [], and a file that exists but is not a JSON object throws — the editor must not preview (or write) a change over a file it cannot read.
static patched(array $current, array $set, array $unset = []): array$current with $set applied and $unset removed — what the file will hold after write(), for the save preview.
write(SettingsTier $tier, array $set, array $unset = []): stringWrite a change set to $tier's file and answer the path written.
mutate(SettingsTier $tier, \Closure $change): ?stringRead $tier's file, let $change decide, and write — all under ONE cross-process lock, so a read-modify-write (append a rule, grant a trust root) cannot lose a concurrent writer's edit the way current() + write() can.
grantTrust(string $trustKey, string $root): stringAdd the project at $root to the $trustKey list in the user's config.json — the confirmed trust action. User tier only, by construction: a project file cannot carry a trust key at all. Like every trust grant it applies from the NEXT launch, because each list is frozen per process.
revokeTrust(string $trustKey, string $root): stringRemove $root from the $trustKey list; see grantTrust().
static trustKeys(): arrayThe trust lists the confirmed action may edit: the schema's Frozen permission lists that canonicalize DIRECTORY roots — today exactly the trustedProject* grants, each defined with an AbsolutePathValidator. The C-SEC-3.b per-origin opt-ins are Frozen permission string lists too, but they hold ORIGIN NAMES, not paths, and grantProjectTrust() appends realpath'd directories; the validator's presence is what tells the two shapes apart, so name lists stay out of this roster (pinned by SettingsWriterTest::testOnlyTheTrustListsAreTrustKeys).
static sessionRefusal(SettingDefinition $definition): ?stringWhy $definition may not be set on the session tier, or null when it may. One predicate for the writer and for the docs that list the tier's keys (sessionKeys()), so the two cannot disagree.
static sessionKeys(): arrayThe keys the session tier accepts, in schema order.
static keyRefusal(SettingsTier $tier, string $key): ?stringWhy $tier never takes $key, whatever its value and whoever writes — or null when it may. Static, because it depends on the schema alone: the settings view asks it as soon as a change is staged, so a key the chosen tier would refuse is flagged on its row long before the save preview (refusal() adds the value checks and the tier's own availability on top).

contentTokens(): intEvery billed category except the reservation and what is left — the totalTokens() half.
tokensOf(ContextCategory $category): ?intThe tokens of one category's row, null when it was not measured.
bar(int $cells): arrayOne bar segment per row, in row order, apportioned by the largest remainder method so the segments sum to EXACTLY $cells whenever any row carries tokens (all-zero rows get an empty bar rather than a fabricated first segment). Null rows weigh 0 — an unmeasured category claims no space it cannot account for.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly CompactorConfig $config, private readonly array $exchangeSummaries = [])

config(): CompactorConfigThe config this compactor's tiers are measured against — read by a notice that has to name the tier that actually fired (a percentage, or an absolute cap when that is lower, roadmap 2.9) rather than assume 95%.

The unit is the message, not the exchange: both halves of one oversized exchange are truncated when each alone reaches the tier, and several exchanges can each contribute an oversized message sharing the remaining budget. The METHOD NAME says "exchange" because the overflow this tier exists for — §12.2 E18's single un-sendable exchange — usually contributes exactly one; what it counts and trims is messages, and the notice the caller writes says so.
shouldSendReminder(array $messages, int $tokenLimit, ?int $calibratedTokens = null): boolDetermine whether a soft reminder should be sent to the lead agent.
compactSkills(array $messages): arrayApply skill-aware compaction as a separate pass from message-history compaction.
compact(array $messages): arrayCompact a message array through stages 1-5.
exchangesToSummarize(array $messages): arrayThe user/assistant exchanges a compact() of $messages would replace with one-line summaries, in the order it would replace them and with the exact text it would hand stage 2.
groupSimilarExchanges(array $messages): arrayStage 3: Group consecutive identical exchanges into a single entry with count prefix.
compactFileReferences(array $messages): arrayStage 4: Replace the output of a successful Read call with a metadata line like "[file: path/to/file.php, N lines]".
removeToolResults(array $messages): arrayStage 0: older tool output becomes a placeholder naming its call — the same age rule, by the same figures, the engine applies to an over-budget request (roadmap 2.2-1, \SugarCraft\Code\Context\Pruning\Strategies\ToolOutputAgeStrategy::select()).
removeNavigationSteps(array $messages): arrayStage 5: Remove navigation steps — the output of a Bash call whose whole command was a lone cd, ls or pwd (NAV_COMMAND_PATTERN).
filterSkills(array $skills): arrayApply skill budget constraints to a list of active skills.
savingsPercentage(): intReturn the percentage of context space saved after the last compaction.

InstructionFileLoader final class

Loads instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the other agents' aliases in FILENAMES) from the repo root, the operator's personal ~/.candy-code/AGENTS.md — or ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md where that is absent — and resolves forced-instruction glob patterns from config.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly string $repoRoot, private readonly array $forcedInstructions = [], ?ImportResolver $importResolver = null, private readonly ?string $personalDir = null, private readonly array $excludedGlobs = [], private readonly array $projectForcedInstructions = [], private readonly bool $walkToRoot = false, ?callable $remoteFetcher = null)
loadRoot(): arrayLoad CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and their aliases (FILENAMES) from the repo root.
loadDocuments(): arrayEvery whole-session instruction document, in prompt order — the ancestor and root files loadRoot() reads, then the forced matches loadForced() reads — each with the path it was read from.
loadPersonal(): arrayThe operator's personal instruction documents under ~/.candy-code (roadmap 5.14j; the persona files join per C-CTX-4.b) — the instruction files that follow the PERSON across every checkout rather than arriving with one. The head is PERSONAL_FILENAME, AGENTS.md; behind it ride PERSONA_FILENAMES — SOUL.md, the operator's voice and standing behavior, and USER.md, facts about the operator. Zero to four entries, head first and personas in const order, in the path-keyed shape loadDocuments() returns. When the head does not exist, Claude Code's personal memory file ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md stands in FOR THE HEAD (roadmap 6.4): operators who have invested in that convention get their context without being asked to duplicate it, and the two are never both read — the head wins whenever it is a file the containment gate ADOPTS; a containment-refused head records its refusal and hands the stand-in role to the fallback (INT-M2, round r10 fix-lane). The stand-in answers for the head slot only: a persona has no ~/.claude spelling and no candidate other than itself.
personalDir(): ?stringWhere the personal instruction file lives: the directory handed to the constructor, or ~/.candy-code under HomeDirectory::owned().
recordDeferral(string $path, string $why): voidRecord that a document this loader DID read was nonetheless not inlined, because the caller's own budget had no room for it.
static pointer(string $path, int $bytes): stringThe one line that stands in for an instruction file that is not inlined: what it is, how big, and the path to Read it from.
static maxPointerBytes(): intThe ceiling pointer() enforces, for a caller pricing pointer lines.
ancestorRoot(): ?stringThe monorepo root whose instruction files are in scope for this $repoRoot, or null when there is none.
loadForced(): arrayResolve glob patterns from config and load matching file contents.
loadForPath(string $touchedPath): ?stringLoad nested instruction file for a touched path.
emittedPaths(): arrayThe real paths whose bodies have already been emitted into the model's context this session.
refusedPaths(): arrayThe instruction files this loader declined to read — or read and did not inline, for budget (readBounded(), recordDeferral(), and an @import the gate deferred) — and why.
announcedRefusals(): arrayThe refusedPaths() entries already announced to the user mid-session — the export half of $announcedRefusals, for \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\CarriesSessionState.
markRefusalsAnnounced(array $paths): voidUnion $paths into $announcedRefusals — a union for the reason markEmitted() is one, and cast for the same reason.
refresh(): voidForget everything this loader read and emitted, so the next load reads the files from disk again — the CLAUDE.md half of a prompt refresh point (/clear or a rewritten history — compaction, rewind; step 1.A-2).
forDelegationView(): selfA loader whose next steps belong to a delegation run, not to this session (ISS-065, the full fix).
markEmitted(array $paths): voidUnion $paths into the emitted set — see emittedPaths().
announcedInstructionUpdates(): arrayThe envelope export of $announcedInstructionUpdates: each entry is one JSON-encoded [path, fingerprint] pair.
instructionUpdateLedger(): arrayThe raw ledger for \SugarCraft\Code\Context\InstructionDiffTracker::capture() seeding and the announce guard's live read — the same map the envelope exports, without the pair encoding.
instructionUpdateFingerprint(string $path): ?stringThe fingerprint already announced for $path, or null when the row was never said. The guard reads this live (not a capture-time snapshot) so a merge that lands after the tracker was captured still silences it.
recordInstructionUpdate(string $path, string $fingerprint): voidWrite one announced row through into $announcedInstructionUpdates — called by the tracker beside its own ledger entry.
forgetInstructionUpdate(string $path): voidForget $path's entry — the tracker's revert leg (a change cancelled back to the frozen bytes must let a later edit be said again).
markInstructionUpdates(array $entries): voidUnion encoded announcedInstructionUpdates() entries into the ledger — the merge half of self::ANNOUNCED_UPDATES_KEY, a union for the reason markEmitted() is one.

The answer is to leave the prefix alone and say the true date on this tail row, but ONLY on the steps where the two disagree: while they agree the row would re-render the same bytes the model already read in <env>, so an unconditional line would just widen the row and re-send it as "changed" state on every write.

SummarySafeguardVerdict enum

What the safeguard audit (plan_comparison.md CTX-4) made of a model-written compaction summary. Carried on \SugarCraft\Code\App\HistoryCompactedMsg::$safeguardHold as a detail string when — and only when — it is HOLD, and read at the three landing sites that consume a model summary: \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::landModelCompaction() refuses the typed route and degrades the parked one to the heuristic fold, the two background-summary slots (Chat's ahead-of-need arm and the served host's) discard the summaries rather than offer them for a later splice. Every other route, and every PASS and FILL, behaves exactly as it did before this existed.

Cases: PASS · FILL · HOLD

PHP also provides cases().

withoutNudges(): selfThis ledger with every nudge anchor cleared — the cooldown after a prune or a compress.
withMode(?PruningMode $mode): selfThis ledger with the session's own mode set (null: follow the configured one).
withDefaultMode(PruningMode $mode): selfThis ledger following $mode wherever the session set none.
effectiveMode(): PruningModeThe mode in force: the session's own, else the configured one.
memoryFlushDue(): boolWhether the pre-compaction memory flush has yet to run in the current compaction cycle (roadmap 2.11) — see $compactionCycle.
withMemoryFlushed(): selfThis ledger with the memory flush recorded for the current cycle, so no route flushes again until the next compaction lands. Recorded when the flush is DECIDED, before it runs: a flush that fails costs the compaction nothing and is not retried in the same cycle.
activeBlock(): ?CompressionBlockThe step summary the projection applies, or null (range blocks: activeRangeBlocks()).
apply(LedgerDelta $delta): self$delta applied; applying the same delta again changes nothing.
deltaSince(self $before): LedgerDeltaWhat this ledger holds that $before did not, as the delta that takes $before here (roadmap 3.B-3's live ledger frame, DCP §13.2 G): every prune and dropped <turn-context> row it added, and every block it added, in the order they were made. A delta carries only additions — the one kind of change a turn makes — so a block $before already held and this ledger merely deactivated is not in it; applying the delta to $before re-derives that consumption (withBlock()).
refsFor(iterable $messages): arrayThe ref every tool result in $messages is shown under: its fixed one when it has one, else a PROVISIONAL one — $nextRef onwards, in order of first appearance. Pure: the same rows and ledger give the same refs, and appending rows never changes the refs of the rows before them, which is what keeps a turn's requests byte-stable while its refs are still provisional. A result with an empty call id gets none. User rows are numbered in the same order (rowKeys(), roadmap 3.B-4).
withRefsAssigned(iterable $messages): selfThis ledger with every provisional ref in $messages fixed — the refs refsFor() showed, now kept. Called where a turn ends, over the conversation in the order the model read it.
refOf(string $toolCallId): ?intThe fixed ref of $toolCallId's result, or null when it has none yet.
toolCallIdForRef(int $ref): ?stringThe tool-call id whose result holds the fixed ref $ref, or null.
syncAgainst(iterable $callIds, iterable $contextRowKeys): selfThis ledger with everything that names a row the conversation no longer has forgotten (DCP §13.2 B "sync", its syncCompressionBlocks): a prune or a ref whose tool call is gone, a dropped <turn-context> row whose bytes no row carries, and — deactivated rather than removed, so its id is never reused — a block whose boundary call is gone. A /rewind past a row, or a compaction that summarised it away, leaves the ledger exactly as clean as the rows. $nextRef and $nextBlockId never go back.
syncAgainstHistory(iterable $history): selfsyncAgainst() over a session's stored rows — what the host holds between turns: every call id a row makes or answers, and every stored <turn-context> row. It also counts the host compactions' boundary rows (\SugarCraft\Code\Host\CompactionService::isCompactionBoundary()), which is how a /compact or 85% compaction that landed moves the compaction cycle (withCompactionBoundaries()).
freedTokens(): intEstimated tokens this ledger takes out of what the model is sent: every prune, every dropped <turn-context> row, and every ACTIVE block's replaced rows less its summary — the status bar's −52K pruned.
isEmpty(): bool
isPruned(string $toolCallId): bool
prune(string $toolCallId): ?PruneEntry
dropsContextRow(string $content): bool
toArray(): array
static fromArray(mixed $raw): selfRebuild from toArray(), LENIENTLY (DCP's loadPruneMessagesState): an entry it cannot read is skipped rather than failing the whole ledger, since losing one prune costs only context while refusing the ledger would lose every other one with it. Anything that is not an array is an empty ledger.

ContextProjector final class

Builds the conversation a request sends from the conversation's rows plus a ContextLedger (roadmap 2.2-1, DCP §13.2 C). Wired at \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime::buildMessages(), ahead of \SugarCraft\Code\Messages\HistorySanitizer.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withRefTags(bool $refTags = true): selfA projector that tags every tool result with its ref (step 4) — what a request the model can name rows in is built with. Off by default: a strategy reading the projected conversation sizes outputs without tags.
project(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger): ProjectedContext
static rangeBounds(array $messages, array $keys, string $fromKey, string $toKey): ?arrayWhere a range block's first and last rows sit in $messages, or null when either is gone (the block is then inert): a user row by its key, a step from the assistant row that opened it through the last of the results that answer it — so no call is ever cut from its result.
static expandedSummary(CompressionBlock $block, ContextLedger $ledger, array $seen = []): stringThe summary a range block shows, every (bN) placeholder replaced by the summary of the block it names — recursively, each block at most once along a path, so a corrupt cycle cannot loop.
static protectedOutputs(array $rows, array $calls, array $refs = []): stringThe verbatim outputs of the protected tools (PruningPolicy::COMPRESS_PROTECTED_TOOLS) among $rows — what a range summary carries whole, since a Task report or a Skill body cannot be fetched again (DCP appendProtectedTools). Empty when there are none.
static callsById(array $messages): arrayEvery call an assistant row in $messages issued, by id.
static stepOpening(array $messages, string $toolCallId): ?intThe index of the assistant row that issued $toolCallId, or null when no row in $messages did.

EmergencyPrune final class

The prune the engine makes when a step's request is over its budget (roadmap 2.2-1; DCP §13.2 D, "only at the over-max emergency").

MethodSummary
static propose(array $projected, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): ?LedgerDeltaThe delta to apply, or null when nothing worth a cache rewrite can go.
static strategies(): array
static oncePerCall(LedgerDelta $delta): LedgerDelta$delta with one prune per call id, the first rule's — the ledger keys by id, so a second entry would only double-count LedgerDelta::freedTokens(). Shared with TurnStartPruning, which runs the same rules.

LedgerDelta final readonly class

A change a PruningStrategy proposes to the ContextLedger (roadmap 2.2-1, DCP §13.2 B): the tool results to prune, the superseded <turn-context> rows to drop, and the step summaries to apply (2.4-1). ContextLedger::apply() is idempotent, so a delta applied twice — or replayed after it crossed a process boundary (2.2-2) — leaves the ledger as one application did.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withPrune(PruneEntry $entry): self
withDroppedContextRow(string $key, int $tokens): self
withBlock(CompressionBlock $block): self
withNudge(string $key, string $kind): selfThis delta with a nudge of $kind anchored on row $key (roadmap 3.B-4).
withNudgesCleared(): selfThis delta clearing every anchor before it adds its own.
merge(self $other): selfThis delta followed by $other, as one. A clear in $other drops the anchors this one would have added.
isEmpty(): bool
toArray(): arrayThe plain-array form a frame carries across the fork (roadmap 3.B-3's \SugarCraft\Code\Events\ContextLedgerChanged): the parent unserializes with allowed_classes => false, so no object may ride it.
static fromArray(mixed $raw): selfRebuild from toArray(), LENIENTLY like ContextLedger::fromArray(): an entry it cannot read is skipped, and anything that is not an array is an empty delta. Applying a delta is idempotent, so one that lost an entry costs only that entry.
freedTokens(): intEstimated tokens the delta frees from the projected request.

NudgePolicy final readonly class

When to remind the model that its context is filling up, and where the reminder sits (roadmap 3.B-4, DCP §13.2 E / §4.7) — the model's own context-management tools (Prune, and Compress when it is offered) are worth nothing if it never thinks to use them.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withContextTokens(int $min, int $max): self
withNudgeFrequency(int $rows): self
withIterationThreshold(int $results): self
static isKind(string $kind): boolWhether $kind is one this policy writes.
static text(string $kind): stringThe fixed text of a $kind nudge, wrapped in its tag; '' for no kind.
static appendTo(string $content, string $kind): string$content with the $kind nudge on its own last lines. Idempotent.
static stripFrom(string $text): string$text with every reminder block the model echoed removed (DCP #608: models copy whole reminder blocks into their replies).
decide(int $tokens, array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger): LedgerDeltaThe anchors to add before the next request — or the cooldown's clear — as a delta the turn applies to its ledger; an empty delta when nothing is due.

What ContextProjector::project() answers: the conversation as the next request sends it.

Cases: Strategy · Harness · User · Model

What a call's ARGUMENTS become when the ContextLedger prunes its input rather than its output (roadmap 2.3): the projector rewrites the assistant row's call, never the history.

PrunedOutputPlaceholder final class

The text a pruned tool result is replaced with (roadmap 2.2-1, DCP §13.2 C step 3): one line naming the tool and its main argument, so the model still knows WHAT it looked at and can re-run exactly that call if it needs the output again —

How much of a session's context pruning happens on its own (roadmap 3.B-2, DCP §13.2 B "PruningMode", §4.13 manual mode).

The limits every PruningStrategy works inside (roadmap 2.2-1, DCP §13.2 D): which tool outputs are never pruned, and the age rule's three figures — opencode's PRUNE_PROTECT / PRUNE_MINIMUM and its two-turn guard.

PruningStrategy interface

One deterministic pruning rule (roadmap 2.2-1, DCP §13.2 D): reads the conversation as the model currently sees it and proposes what to take out. A strategy never applies its own proposal — the caller decides whether the delta is worth a cache rewrite — and the same input always yields the same delta.

MethodSummary
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

RefTag final class

The short name the model reads and writes for one tool result — r17 — and the tag that carries it on the wire, <ctx-ref r="17"/> (roadmap 2.2-2 / 3.B-2, DCP §4.3 and §13.2 C step 4).

MethodSummary

static label(int $ref): stringHow a person or the model writes $ref: r17.

static stripFrom(string $text): string$text with every tag removed, each with the newline in front of it.
static parse(string $written): ?intThe ref a person or the model wrote — r17, R17, 17 or a whole <ctx-ref r="17"/> tag — or null for anything else (zero and negative numbers included: refs start at 1).

SugarCraft\Code\Context\Pruning\Strategies

DuplicateCallStrategy final class

Newest wins (roadmap 2.3; DCP's deduplication, Cline's duplicate file reads): the output of a call that a NEWER call answered again is pruned.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

ErroredInputStrategy final class

The input of a call that failed long ago is blanked (roadmap 2.3, DCP's purge-errors): once $turns user turns have passed since a call failed, its arguments are sent as placeholders but for the main one (PrunedInputPlaceholder::blanked()). The error it answered with is kept — that it failed, and why, is what the model needs; the large edit it tried is not.

MethodSummary
static new(int $turns = self::TURNS): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

StaleReadStrategy final class

A read the file no longer matches is pruned (roadmap 2.3, Cline's stale file reads): the output of a Read older than a SUCCESSFUL Edit or Write of the same file (CanonicalArguments::path()) is sent as a placeholder — the model would be reasoning from text that is not there.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

SupersededTurnContextStrategy final class

Leaves out every <turn-context> row but the newest (roadmap 2.2-1, the W4 1.A-2 follow-up).

MethodSummary
static new(): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

SupersededWriteInputStrategy final class

A superseded write's content is elided (roadmap 2.3, DCP's supersede-writes): the content argument of a successful Write is sent as a placeholder once a LATER successful Write of the same file, or a later successful read of the whole file, exists — either one holds what the file says now, so the old content is the largest thing in the request that nobody needs.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta

ToolOutputAgeStrategy final class

The age rule (roadmap 2.2-1; opencode's session prune, DCP §13.2 D): older tool output becomes a placeholder naming the call, newest output and the last user turns stay verbatim.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
propose(array $messages, ContextLedger $ledger, PruningPolicy $policy): LedgerDelta
static select(array $rows, PruningPolicy $policy): arrayThe rule over plain rows, oldest first. A row is either a user-turn marker (['userTurn' => true]) or a tool output (['key' => …, 'tool' => name, 'tokens' => int, 'placeholderTokens' => int], plus 'keep' => true for output the caller must keep verbatim for its own reasons — it still counts towards the protected newest output). Answers the keys to prune => the tokens each frees, or nothing when the total is under the policy's floor.

SugarCraft\Code\Context\Sections

FamilyPrompt final readonly class

The per-model-family paragraph of the base identity prompt (roadmap 5.10): a short note for the families candy-code is run against — DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.8 and MiniMax — plus Aider's two end-of-prompt reminders, lazy and overeager, switched on per family.

MethodSummary

MaximsSection final readonly class

The core.maxims layer (prompt_expand.md §9.13): the handful of statements of what this harness values in a report, voiced as reasoning rather than as emphasis. §4.7 is why the layer exists at all — CRITICAL:, IMPORTANT: and the second-person obligation formula spend their own urgency on every line they touch, so a prompt that marks nothing up is the prompt that can be marked up when something genuinely needs it — and §4.24 is where most of the lines come from, restated in this project's voice rather than transplanted with their 2025 scaffolding (no banned-phrase list, no numeric ceilings, no token ladders).

MethodSummary

PlanModeSection final readonly class

The plan-mode contract (roadmap 5.7-1): present in the system prompt only while the session's gate is in plan mode, so the model is TOLD what the gate already enforces (PermissionGate::evaluatePlan()) instead of discovering it one denied call at a time. Cline's lesson (05-cline.md §3.1) is the reason it is both: a plan mode enforced only by prompt runs rm the first time the model forgets, and one enforced only by the gate spends a step per refusal.

SugarCraft\Code\Diagnostics

NoticeSink final class

One session's runtime-notice inbox: the per-instance half of the mid-session transcript seam (Appendix O §4.2, roadmap O-2a).

MethodSummary
static new(): selfA fresh, unarmed sink: it drops every notice until arm() runs.
record(string $message): boolSee RuntimeNoticeSink::record().
transportDropped(): intNotices this process's transport refused and has not yet reported. Test and diagnostics seam; the report itself rides flushDropReport().
flushDropReport(): boolSend the owed "N notices dropped" row, if any, through the transport. Returns true when nothing is owed or the row got through; false while the pipe is still refusing (the count is kept for the next attempt). Public so a child about to exit can make one last attempt.
recordStructured(string $kind, array $payload): boolRecord a STRUCTURED notice frame (C-CTX-6.e): $kind names a reader contract and $payload carries its fields, framed as RuntimeNoticeSink::STRUCTURED_PREFIX + a JSON object. The prefix head is 0x01, a byte no plain runtime row can begin with — chosen deliberately because the default record() trim eats NUL (its charlist contains "\0"), so a \x00-head frame would arrive mangled. Only RuntimeNoticeSink::KIND_MEMORY_RECALL is defined; an unknown kind is refused, because a producer inventing kinds without a reader mapping would park datagrams in drains that can only ever drop them.
static decodeStructuredFrame(string $line): ?arrayParse a drained line back into its structured fields, or null when it is a plain row, a malformed frame, or a frame whose payload shape fails the $kind's contract. Readers branch on this BEFORE minting a row so a dropped frame parks nothing: the worst case is the notice row's own silence, never a half-parsed row.
hasPending(): boolSee RuntimeNoticeSink::hasPending().
drain(): arraySee RuntimeNoticeSink::drain().
beginTurn(): voidSee RuntimeNoticeSink::beginTurn().
arm(bool $crossFork = true): boolSee RuntimeNoticeSink::arm().
isArmed(): boolWhether arm() has run on this sink, on either backend.
hasTransport(): boolWhether arm() got the cross-fork transport rather than the array.
notifyOnceWhenPending(\Closure $notify): boolSee RuntimeNoticeSink::notifyOnceWhenPending().
cancelPendingNotification(): voidSee RuntimeNoticeSink::cancelPendingNotification().
isNotificationArmed(): boolWhether a notifyOnceWhenPending() watcher is installed.
forgetInheritedWatcher(): voidForget an inherited read watcher WITHOUT running its canceller — the forked-child half of RuntimeNoticeSink::enterForkedChild().
reset(): voidSee RuntimeNoticeSink::reset().

RuntimeNoticeSink final class

The MID-SESSION half of the transcript seam: a process-wide inbox any subsystem can put a user-visible warning into once the alternate screen is already up, drained by \SugarCraft\Code\Chat on a subscription tick.

MethodSummary
static warn(string $message, ?string $detail = null): voidReport a warning on BOTH channels: error_log() for the complete record, and the transcript inbox for the surface an interactive user actually has.
static record(string $message): boolPut a notice in the inbox WITHOUT touching stderr.
static recordStructured(string $kind, array $payload): boolPut a STRUCTURED notice frame in the inbox without touching stderr (C-CTX-6.e). Same armed-drops law as record(); the framing, kind whitelist and MAX_CHARS bound (tail-title shed, count kept) are NoticeSink::recordStructured()'s, documented there.
static isStructuredFrame(string $line): boolWhether a drained line is a structured frame at all (before any decode) — the branch pumps take to route a row to its typed constructor instead of a plain notice.
static decodeStructured(string $line): ?arrayParse a drained line back into its frame fields, or null for a plain row, a malformed frame, or a failed kind contract.
static recallRowText(int $count): stringThe one prose source of the recall row's sentence (C-CTX-6.e): the frame carries only numbers and titles, and every reader — the TUI row's content, the served session's web payload — spells the same catalog line, so legacy readers keep seeing today's byte-shape.
static hasPending(): boolWhether a poll would find anything, WITHOUT consuming it.
static drain(): arrayTake everything pending and clear it.
static beginTurn(): voidOpen a per-turn notice budget of TURN_NOTICE_LIMIT transcript rows (E199).
static arm(bool $crossFork = true): boolCreate the cross-fork transport, so notices raised inside \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::completeAsync()'s child reach the parent's transcript instead of dying with it.
static transportDropped(): intNotices this process's transport write refused and has not yet reported.
static flushDropReport(): boolOne more attempt to send the owed "N notices dropped" row; see NoticeSink::flushDropReport().
static isArmed(): boolWhether arm() has run in this process, on either backend.
static hasTransport(): boolWhether arm() got the cross-fork transport rather than the array.
static notifyOnceWhenPending(\Closure $notify): boolCall $notify once, on the event loop, the next time a notice arrives on the cross-fork transport (E193).
static cancelPendingNotification(): voidTake any notifyOnceWhenPending() watcher back off the loop.
static isNotificationArmed(): boolWhether a notifyOnceWhenPending() watcher is installed.
static reset(): voidDrop everything — queue, transport, and the E199 turn budget — so a fresh arm starts as unbudgeted as a process that never heard of the cap.
static process(): NoticeSinkThe process's own sink: the one a TUI launch arms, and the one every emitter reaches when no host has routed elsewhere.
static current(): NoticeSinkThe sink this process's emitters write to and its drain owner reads: whatever routeTo() routed to, else process().
static routeTo(?NoticeSink $sink): voidRoute this process's notices to $sink; null routes back to process().
static using(NoticeSink $sink, \Closure $body): mixedRun $body with $sink current, then restore whatever was current.
static enterForkedChild(NoticeSink $sink): voidThe forked-turn-child half of the per-session seam: make $sink this process's sink for good, and make the process a WRITER ONLY.

FormatRunner final class

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfA runner with no commands at all — the feature is off until configured.
withCommands(mixed $settings): selfThe same runner with $settings — the raw formatCommands value — laid over its map. See the class docblock for the shape and the tolerance.

A live jail WRAPS each command line at run time with the project root writable (the formatter must rewrite exactly the file the edit wrote, so the jail's writable root is the edit's root — no wider, no narrower); when the jail cannot start on this host the format is SKIPPED with the refusal as its note, never run unconfined — a sandboxed scope that quietly degraded to bare execution would teach the operator the opposite of what sandboxScope says. null (the default, and the answer whenever the scope is not requested or bashSandbox is off) leaves every command line byte-identical to the pre-scope shape.
withAuto(bool $enabled, bool $projectTrusted, ?callable $binaryPresent = null): selfThe same runner with the FormatAutoTable arm set: $enabled is the formatAuto settings bit, $projectTrusted the launch's answer to the hooks-trust gate, and $binaryPresent an optional presence seam — the exact \SugarCraft\Code\LSP\LspLauncher::fromConfig() shape, EDT-2's reasoning carried here: the caller (the frozen launch, not this class) holds the config read and the trust check, so it hands both down, and a test can probe the table without any host formatter installed.
autoArmed(): boolWhether the auto arm is live: the settings bit AND the trust gate.
commands(): array
timeoutSeconds(): float
commandFor(string $path, ?string $root = null): ?stringThe command that formats $path, or null when its extension has none — the explicit map first, then the auto arm (C-TOOL-5.b): an explicit entry wins per extension even with the arm live, an extension switched off with false stays off, and auto candidates are probed only when handed the $root to probe them in (with the arm off, an omitted $root answers exactly what it answered before the arm existed).
format(string $path, string $root): ?FormatReportFormat $path, or null when there is nothing to format: no command for its extension, a path outside $root, no regular file there, or a file too large to hold a restore baseline for.

An empty root (a context built with no workspace) is passed as null: anchoring at '' would anchor at / and invent paths the tool never opens.

Formats the file a Write or Edit (or each file an ApplyPatch) just changed with the user's formatCommands map (FormatRunner), and — the half that needs the launch, not just the config — RECORDS the rewritten file into the session's ReadLedger, so the formatter's own change never reads back as "somebody edited this behind the model's back". supervisor(): BackgroundSupervisor

Answers the first valid one for a given asking; the answer file is the record, so a second answer to the same asking reports already with the first reply attached rather than overwriting anything — and so does a RESTARTED server that never saw the question, reading the record instead of trusting empty memos (F3). A re-issued identical call is a NEW asking with a fresh token: its memos were purged by that token (F2), and a row answering its predecessor cannot settle it here either, because this method only ever answers what the ask file still holds open.

compactedHistory(ContextCompactor $compactor, string $inputText, array $baseHistory, array $summaries, \Closure $tokenLimit, \Closure $estimate, string $prefix = '', bool $tierNotice = false, ?CompactionSource $source = null): arrayWhat compacting $baseHistory does to the TRANSCRIPT and to nothing else: the compacted history plus the echoed command and the answer line. Chat::compactionChanges() commits it and releases the summarization latch beside it.
static messagesFromWire(array $wire, array $original): arrayRebuild a list<Message> from the wire arrays ContextCompactor::compact() returns, REUSING the original Message objects for every exchange compaction preserved in full.
static compactionWire(array $history): arrayThe wire a ContextCompactor is handed: $history's AGENT-VISIBLE rows only.
static tierTokenCount(int $calibratedEstimate, array $history): intThe numerator every between-prompt tier reads (ISS-015).
static blockedAttempts(array $history): intHow many attempts have run into the 95% blocking tier since the conversation last got a turn out: each blocking refusal (Chat::foregroundBlockedResponse()) in the rows after the newest agent-visible assistant reply, plus each /compact typed among them. Zero whenever there is no refusal in that span, so /compact on a session that was never blocked compacts exactly as it always has.
attemptCompactor(ContextCompactor $compactor, array $history): ContextCompactorThe compactor a compaction of $history runs with: this session's, with blockedAttempts() fewer exchanges preserved (never fewer than one).
static withCompactedRowsHidden(array $original, array $rewritten, int $rewrittenCount): arrayA compaction of $original's agent-visible rows, laid out so that nothing is deleted (roadmap 1.B-3).
spendCapCompactionNotice(float $spentUsd, float $capUsd, string $tail, bool $unpriced = false): stringThe sentence both spend-cap compaction arms open with, kept in ONE copy because it is one fact said twice.
compactCommandCapNotice(float $spentUsd, float $capUsd, bool $unpriced = false): string/compact's spend-cap answer: the shared sentence plus the advice to raise the cap (to twice the spend so far) and run the command again for model-written summaries. See spendCapCompactionNotice().
parkedTurnCapNotice(float $spentUsd, float $capUsd, bool $unpriced = false): stringThe 85% tier's spend-cap answer: the shared sentence plus the fact that the prompt goes out against the heuristic rewrite regardless — no advice to run /compact, for the reason spendCapCompactionNotice() gives.
safeguardHoldRefusal(string $detail): string/compact's answer when the CTX-4 safeguard audited the model's summary and found structural collapse: refuse outright and keep the full history, the same shape as compactCommandCapNotice() — the command reports that nothing was compacted rather than quietly landing junk. $detail is the audit's own sentence (SummarySafeguard::summary()), flattened like every summary-bound string before it reaches a transcript row.
safeguardFoldAdvisory(string $detail): stringThe automatic routes' answer to the same verdict. They do NOT hold: the 85% tier's prompt is already typed and parked, and refusing it would 400 a turn the user already pressed Enter for. The fold lands on the heuristic — which is what the pre-model tiers always wrote — and this sentence makes the report own why. Same trailing-space family as the fold sentences in modelSummaryFallbackPrefix().
summarisingNotice(int $exchanges): string/compact's answer while the model writes its summaries: the transcript compacts when HistoryCompactedMsg lands, not now.
parkNotice(int $tokenCount, int $tokenLimit, int $exchanges): stringThe notice Chat::scheduleParkedCompaction() writes ahead of the prompt it parks. $tokenCount is ESTIMATED tokens of the pre-compaction history and $tokenLimit the PROVIDER-COUNTED window; the sentence names the unit of each because they are not the same kind of number.
modelSummaryFallbackPrefix(HistoryCompactedMsg $msg): stringThe sentence a model-written compaction's report opens with when the model did not deliver: its call failed (the error, flattened by sanitizeSummaryLine()), or it answered with nothing usable. '' when the summaries arrived — the report then needs no preface.
static compactFocus(string $inputText): stringThe focus a /compact <focus> command asks the summary to steer toward (roadmap 2.12): everything after the command word, trimmed, in either spelling the dispatcher accepts (/compact text and /compact:text). '' for a bare /compact, and for anything that is not the command — the automatic tier has no focus.
compactionHookContext(string $event, array $payload, string $sessionId, string $projectRoot): HookContextThe context a PreCompact / PostCompact hook is handed (roadmap 2.12), smuggled through the tool-shaped HookContext exactly as the turn events are (\SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\HookManager::sessionStart()): toolName is the event name — the only slot a matcher tests — and toolInput is the JSON $payload, encoded the way CRUSH_TOOL_INPUT is documented (slashes and non-ASCII unescaped, invalid UTF-8 substituted so one bad byte cannot empty the payload). model/provider are empty, per the turn-event precedent.
static preCompactRefusal(HookResult $verdict): ?stringWhy a PreCompact verdict stops the compaction, or null when it lets it run. An ASK fails closed — no compaction path can put a question to anyone — and a silent refusal still gets a sentence.
compactionBlockedNotice(string $reason, bool $parked): stringThe transcript line a refused compaction leaves (roadmap 2.12). UI-only on every route: the reason is the operator's, and \SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\HookEvent::stderrToUserOnly() says it never reaches the agent. On the parked route the prompt still goes out, against the uncompacted history, and the sentence says so.
preCompactPendingNotice(): string/compact's answer while a PreCompact chain runs off the render loop on the heuristic route (no model to ask): the transcript compacts when the hooks have answered.
static latestCompactSummary(array $history): stringWhat a PostCompact hook is handed as compact_summary (roadmap 2.12): the summary rows the model now reads in place of what was condensed — every agent-visible SUMMARY_ROW_PREFIX row of $history, marker stripped, one per line, bounded at COMPACT_SUMMARY_HOOK_MAX_CHARS.
static renderFocusForSummary(string $focus, string $hookGuidance): stringThe user-role message that steers a summarization (roadmap 2.12): the /compact focus and a permitting PreCompact hook's note. '' when there is neither, and then no message is sent, so an unfocused request keeps the exact shape it always had. Each part is escaped with PromptFence::escape() like every other carried text.
buildSummarizationRequest(?Backend $backend, ContextCompactor $compactor, array $probeHistory, ?string $parkedSubmission, ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, string $focus = '', bool $background = false, ?array $conversation = null, ?\Closure $claimMemoryFlush = null): ?arrayThe half of a model-written compaction that is the same on both routes: decide whether there is anything to ask, and build the request.
historyFingerprint(ContextCompactor $compactor, array $history): HistoryFingerprintThe fingerprint of the compaction $compactor would run over $history now (roadmap 2.10): the exchanges and prior summaries buildSummarizationRequest() derives from the same history, so a held summary's fingerprint and this one compare like for like.
static aheadOfNeedAllowed(int $tierTokens, ?string $heldModel = null, string $currentModel = ''): boolThe ahead-of-need skip rules (C-CTX-5.b, mirroring OpenCode's): both hosts' dispatch blocks ask their request arm through this one gate. A session under AHEAD_OF_NEED_TOKEN_FLOOR never asks — the prefetch is pointless on histories a compaction handles quickly anyway. And a summary held under a different model than the session now runs is not the next model's work: every request — the dispatch arm's and the idle watch's alike — stamps its model into the held slot's identity exactly like the session id, so a switch discards the old records instead of splicing another head's writing into this model's context. The drop arm consults only aheadOfNeedModelMatches(): the floor is a REQUEST rule, and applying it on the way out would discard already-paid summaries of a small-window session that was never expected to clear it (MINOR-2, round-1 review).
static aheadOfNeedModelMatches(?string $heldModel, string $currentModel): boolThe model half of the skip rules on its own — the whole drop-arm test once a slot is held. A slot stamped under another model is not this model's work and goes; an unstamped legacy slot is left alone, and a matching stamp keeps the paid records in hand however small the session is.
static splicedSummaries(array $summaries, array $history): arrayAn ahead-of-need summary map (roadmap 2.10) made ready for a compaction of $history: the per-exchange records as the model wrote them, and the state block re-audited against $history — its derived headings (the files, the latest unresolved request) re-read off the transcript as it stands NOW rather than as it stood when the summary was requested, and any heading the model left empty filled the same way. A map with no state block gets the heuristic one, as every other route does.
static cacheReusingSummaryInstruction(array $exchanges, array $priorSummaries, string $steer = ''): stringThe final user row of a summary sent as the conversation's own request (\SugarCraft\Code\Backend\SummarisesWithCache, roadmap 2.4-2): the preamble, the record contract (COMPACT_SUMMARY_PROMPT), and an INDEX of the exchanges rather than their text — the text is the conversation above, already in the provider's cache, so repeating it would pay for it twice. Each exchange is named by the opening of the user's request, numbered in conversation order, so the numbered records still map back by position. A carried prior summary and the steer (/compact's focus, a PreCompact hook's note) follow, as on the tool-less route.
withJournal(?\SugarCraft\Code\Memory\CompactionJournal $journal): selfA copy that journals every model-written summary to $journal.
journal(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Memory\CompactionJournalThe journal summaries are appended to, or null.
static summaryRejection(Message $reply, int $sourceChars): ?stringWhy a summarization reply is thrown away whole (roadmap 2.5), or null when it may be used: a reply the provider cut short at its length limit ends mid-record and mid-block, and a reply NOT SMALLER than the text it was asked to condense is not a compaction at all. Either way the landing compacts on the heuristic and says why, through the ordinary modelSummaryFallbackPrefix() error route.
static parseCompactionReply(string $reply, array $keys, StateSummaryTemplate $fallback): arrayThe landing's summary map for a usable reply: the per-exchange records (parseExchangeSummaries()) plus the state block under StateSummaryTemplate::SUMMARY_KEY — the model's block, audited against $fallback (each missing or empty heading filled from it, the derived headings always taken from it), or $fallback alone when the reply carried no block. The block is cut out of the reply before the records are parsed, where its lines would otherwise read as facet continuations. A reply with neither a record nor a block maps to nothing, exactly as before.
static auditCompactionReply(string $reply, array $keys, StateSummaryTemplate $fallback, string $sourceText): arrayThe same parse with the CTX-4 coverage audit alongside it: the landing summaries plus the safeguard's report (null when there was no model text to audit at all — a reply that wrote nothing is the ordinary model_empty fold, a verdict this class does not re-litigate). The audit reads the model's OWN words only (SummarySafeguard); the returned summaries are byte-identical to parseCompactionReply()'s because the fill happens there before anything is measured.
static heuristicState(array $history): StateSummaryTemplateThe heuristic state block for $history (roadmap 2.5): the sections StateSummaryTemplate::fromHistory() reads off its rows, merged with the newest state row an earlier compaction left in it.
static renderExchangesForSummary(array $exchanges): stringThe user-role half of the summarization request: the exchanges, numbered, in the order \SugarCraft\Code\Context\ContextCompactor::exchangesToSummarize() returned them, so the model's numbered records map back by position.
static priorSummariesFromHistory(array $wireHistory): arrayThe prior summaries to carry into a re-compaction, marker stripped and text verbatim.
static renderPriorSummariesForSummary(array $priors): stringThe third message of a re-compaction request: the carried prior summaries wrapped in the <prior-summary> tag, followed by the merge rules self::PRIOR_SUMMARY_NOTE.
static parseExchangeSummaries(string $reply, array $keys): arrayTurn the model's numbered records into the key => summary map \SugarCraft\Code\Context\ContextCompactor::withExchangeSummaries() wants.
static sanitizeSummaryLine(string $text): stringOne bounded, control-byte-free line — same treatment Message::describeToolCall() gives a model-authored tool label, and for the same two reasons: the text is untrusted, and it is going somewhere that assumes one line.
static withoutParkedSubmission(array $history, string $prompt): array$history with the parked submission's own rows removed — the prompt Chat::scheduleParkedCompaction() echoed and the UserPromptSubmit notes it wrote immediately ahead of it — for the pre-turn checkpoint (see Chat::dispatchTurn() for what "pre-turn" keeps and why).
static contextReminderMessage(int $tokenCount): MessageBuild the soft, non-blocking reminder message Chat::dispatchTurn() appends whenever ContextCompactor::shouldSendReminder() reports the conversation has crossed its share of the budget (CompactorConfig::$reminderThreshold, 70% by default — which is why neither this docblock nor the message names a percentage as if it were fixed). Rendered with a distinct Role::System (a dim "system: …" line, see \SugarCraft\Code\Renderer; it is agent-visible, so not the italic "notice: …" of a UI-only row) rather than the Role::Assistant bubble used for the hard idle-compaction prompt, so the two are visually distinguishable and this one never blocks the turn it rides along with.
static withoutContextReminders(array $history): arrayDrop every context-usage reminder from a history.
static isContextReminder(Message $msg): boolWhether $msg is one of contextReminderMessage()'s own products.
static contextCompactedMessage(int $beforeMessages, int $afterMessages, int $savedPercentage, int $tokenCount, int $tokenLimit, ?CompactionSource $source = null): MessageThe notice the 85% tier (ContextCompactor::shouldCompact()) leaves behind after rewriting history under the user.
intraExchangeTruncation(ContextCompactor $compactor, array $wire, array $baseHistory, int $tokenLimit, \Closure $estimate): ?arrayThe INTRA-exchange rescue of the 95% blocking tier (prompt_plan.md P4.S4, backlog §12.2 E18).
static messageWithContent(Message $message, string $content): MessageA copy of $message with $content swapped in and EVERY other field carried across verbatim.
static clipOlderToolOutputs(array $history, int $keepRecentRows = self::CLIP_KEEP_RECENT_ROWS, int $headChars = self::CLIP_HEAD_CHARS, int $tailChars = self::CLIP_TAIL_CHARS): arrayOlder tool outputs cut to head and tail, the newest exchanges kept whole.
static contextTruncatedMessage(int $truncatedMessages, int $tokenCount, int $tokenLimit, ?CompactorConfig $config = null): MessageThe notice the intra-exchange rescue writes when truncating oversized messages lets a turn through (prompt_plan.md P4.S4, backlog §12.2 E18).
static blockingTierLabel(CompactorConfig $config, int $tokenLimit): stringThe blocking tier that actually fires on a $tokenLimit-token window under $config, named the way a notice can state it: "the 95% blocking tier" (the configured percentage), or "the 120000-token blocking cap" when an absolute cap (roadmap 2.9, CompactorConfig::withForegroundBlockingTokens()) is lower than that percentage of the window — the same min(percent, cap) rule CompactorConfig::foregroundBlockingTokenThreshold() applies, so the sentence names the threshold that was really crossed.
foregroundBlockedRows(string $inputText, array $history, int $tokenCount, int $tokenLimit, ?Message $compactionNotice = null): arrayThe rows the 95% blocking tier's refusal commits (Chat::foregroundBlockedResponse() has the full account of when it is reached and why retrying works): $history, then $compactionNotice when the compaction freed anything, then the unsent prompt as a UI-only echo unless $inputText is '' (the transcript already carries it — the parked route), then the refusal itself, UI-only and opening with BLOCKED_TURN_PREFIX so blockedAttempts() can count it.
thrashBreakerNotice(int $times = IdleCompactionPolicy::REFILL_LIMIT): stringThe refusal the thrash breaker appends (Chat::thrashBreakerRefusal() says when and why): $times compactions in a row — the session's compaction.refillLimit (CompactorConfig::$refillLimit), else IdleCompactionPolicy::REFILL_LIMIT — came straight back over the tier with the turn unsent. It names no percentage and no /compact, for the reasons given there.
refillCount(int $current, bool $stillOverTier, bool $turnSent): intThe thrash breaker's run after an automatic compaction settled (ruling P8.S5-R6, argued on Chat::withCompactionOutcome()): reset when the rewrite got under the tier, extended when it did not AND the turn went unsent, held when the turn went out anyway.

ContextMeter final class

How full a session's context window is: the token estimate every context tier reads, its E17 calibration against what the provider really counted, the window it is measured against, and the idle-compaction question asked of the pair (roadmap O-2c, Appendix O §4.2 "token estimate calibration").

MethodSummary
static new(): self
rawTokens(array $history): intThe PRE-calibration proxy — TokenEstimate::ofText() (chars/4 for ASCII/Latin, heavier per character for CJK, other scripts and emoji) + 10 per message, plus every inlined attachment.
estimate(array $history, ?float $calibration): intThe estimate every context tier reads: rawTokens() scaled by the session's last estimate-vs-real observation when one exists.
limit(Backend $backend): intThe window every context tier is a percentage of: the backend's provider-reported context window when it implements \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\ReportsContextWindow and reports a positive one, else ContextWindow::FALLBACK_TOKENS. The figure is MODEL-AWARE and provider-reported; no literal here is a contract.
shouldPromptIdleCompaction(int $tokenCount, ?\DateTimeImmutable $lastActivityAt, int $tokenLimit, int $idleSeconds = IdleCompactionPolicy::IDLE_SECONDS): boolWhether the idle-compaction prompt is due: idle longer than $idleSeconds AND the estimate past the whole window. The caller supplies the limit because the backend is what it can see, and the idle bound because the session's settings are.
calibrationFrom(?int $estimateAtDispatch, ?Usage $usage): ?floatThe calibration factor one settled turn implies, or null when the turn observed nothing (and the session's existing factor must stand).

ContextSources final class

WEB-3a: the structured half of /context — one pure-data builder that answers context.sources AND measures the /context panel's breakdown, so the two surfaces can never fork the measurement (VIS-2a's single-writer law, extended to the wire).

MethodSummary
static measure(CommandContext $context, ?array $instructionFiles, ?int $historyTokens = null): ContextBreakdownThe session breakdown /context reports and context.sources rides: prompt layers from a backend that assembles its own prompt, tool schemas from an engine backend, the ledger's pruning, and the cache-break watch.
static priceInstructionFiles(?string $root): ?arrayThe instruction documents this root's prompt splices, as names and sizes only (roadmap VIS-2a): Bootstrap::instructionLoader() is the memoized instance the system prompt itself is built from, so the panel reads the loader's own record. A loader that cannot be built leaves the figure null — the unknown-honesty rule every other part of the panel follows.
static instructionRows(?array $files): ?arrayC-CTX-3.a: the one row builder for priced instruction files.
static answer(?WorkspaceContext $workspace, ?ContextBreakdown $breakdown, ?array $instructionFiles, ?array $mcpInventory = null, ?array $mcpLiveness = null): arrayThe whole context.sources answer. The session half rides $breakdown (null when no session is on screen — every session figure is then honestly absent rather than zero); the workspace half is read from $workspace. $mcpInventory is injectable so tests pin the shaping without a live .mcp.json; null runs the read-never-run census — C-MCP-4.a feeds it the FULL nine-key \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\McpDecision::mcpServerInventory() shape, so both tiers' rows reach the wire.

EventLog final class

The durable, per-session event log a host writes before it broadcasts (roadmap O-2b, Appendix O §4.8 / §6.4 / §6.8): one session_events row per durable event, numbered by a seq that is monotonic per session and never reused.

MethodSummary
static new(EnhancedSessionStore $store, int $retain = self::DEFAULT_RETAIN): selfA log over $store's session_events table.
withRetain(int $retain): selfA copy keeping $retain events per session (below 1 keeps all).
store(): EnhancedSessionStoreThe store the log writes into.
retain(): intEvents kept per session; 0 is unbounded.
append(string $sessionId, string $type, array $data = [], ?int $tsMs = null): intWrite one durable event and return its seq.
since(string $sessionId, int $afterSeq = 0, int $limit = self::PAGE_SIZE): arrayOne replay page: $sessionId's events after $afterSeq, oldest first, at most $limit.
latestSeq(string $sessionId): intThe newest seq in $sessionId's log, 0 when it has none.
oldestSeq(string $sessionId): ?intThe oldest seq still retained for $sessionId, null when the log is empty.
isReplayable(string $sessionId, int $afterSeq): boolWhether a client holding everything through $afterSeq can catch up by replay (Appendix O §6.8 step 3). False when retention has already dropped an event it never saw, or when the cursor is AHEAD of the log (it belongs to another database); both mean "resync from a snapshot".

InProcessEventSink final class

The relay target of one in-process client that follows sessions of a non-primary root (PL-5c-A design, section 3). The gateway fans a workspace host's events out to it through RelayTarget::deliver(); the sink queues them in arrival order and hands them to the client's listeners on the loop, at most DELIVERY_BUDGET per tick, so a backlog never holds the serve loop.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly string $id, private readonly Gateway $gateway, private readonly LoopInterface $loop, private readonly \Closure $fanOut)
id(): string
isOpen(): bool
accepts(?string $sessionId): boolFalse for a session stopped by an overflow: its events are discarded before any cursor moves.
viewerSessions(): ?arrayAn in-process client is an owner: it has no viewer pin.
deliver(?array $message, string $text, ?string $coalesceKey, bool $ephemeral, ?int $seq, ?string $sessionId): void
unfollowed(string $sessionId): voidThe gateway no longer forwards $sessionId: stop listing it, keep what is queued (it is delivered before the notice).
follow(string $sessionId, int $cursor): voidThe client subscribed to $sessionId from $cursor: clears any stop, drops the undelivered entries of the session (a replay from the host supplies them again), and sets the cursor.
unfollow(string $sessionId): voidThe client unsubscribed from $sessionId: forget it and purge its owed events. This is the routed divergence from the primary path (see the class docblock): the primary feed keeps envelopes it already queued. Latent: no bundle calls unsubscribeSession() yet, so this purge is reached only through the door, and no shipped bundle exercises it.
followedSessions(): array
flush(): voidHand every queued envelope to the listeners now, without the per-tick budget. Used by disconnect(), which delivers what the client is owed before it leaves. A call from inside a delivery does nothing: the running pump delivers the queue in order.
close(): voidThe client left: nothing further is delivered, and the queue is dropped.

InProcessHostServices final class

The HostServices a channel plugin runs against, served by the candy-code host it runs inside (PL-5c). Each call goes through Dispatcher::invoke(), the same gates and the same handler functions the WebSocket path runs, but with no socket, no loopback dial and no JSON-RPC frame: an answer's value is taken through the wire's encoding, so a bundle holds the values a wire client decodes.

MethodSummary
static new(Dispatcher $dispatcher, LoopInterface $loop, ?Gateway $gateway = null): selfAn in-process host over $dispatcher, whose events are drained on $loop. With $gateway, calls and events of sessions on other roots route through it (PL-5c-A); without one, the door serves the primary root only.
static bundleFactory(Dispatcher $dispatcher, LoopInterface $loop, ?Gateway $gateway = null): \ClosureThe factory the serve hands each channel bundle (PL-5d): one in-process client per bundle, all over the primary root's dispatcher, routed through $gateway when one is given.
connect(): PromiseInterfaceOpen the in-process client: the hello the wire makes first. Resolves once the host has answered it; a hello that is refused rejects with its RpcError, and any other failure while opening the client rejects with the throwable itself.
disconnect(): PromiseInterfaceClose the in-process client. Events it was already owed are delivered first (the primary feed's and the routed sink's), then the client leaves the host, which drops its feed subscriptions and its routed subscriptions. Called from a primary-feed listener, the owed routed events are delivered inside this call. Called from a routed-sink listener, the sink's remaining backlog is dropped instead of delivered: the running sink delivery cannot re-enter, and the client is closed before the listeners after the caller hear the envelope (PL-5c-A sink design, section 3.4). The primary queue is not touched by that drop. A later connect() starts with no follows (see the class docblock).
isConnected(): PromiseInterfaceWhether the in-process client is open and has said hello.
hello(): PromiseInterfaceMirrors server.hello (inventory row 1). Opens the client on first use; a second hello on the same client is the wire's already_initialized conflict.
subscribeSession(string $sessionId, ?int $afterSeq, ?\Closure $cursor): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.subscribe (row 2). A $cursor is read on every call and its value is the resume point, as the wire's reconnect re-follow reads it (ServeBridge::follow in scripts/channel-bridge/src/Candy/ServeBridge.php, the only surviving copy): a re-follow after a server.overflow notice resumes from the seq the bundle has applied, not from the $afterSeq it first followed with. $afterSeq is the resume point only when no cursor is given. A cursor of null or 0 opens from a snapshot.
unsubscribeSession(string $sessionId): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.unsubscribe (row 3). Best-effort like the wire wrapper: once the client has disconnected there is nothing left to unfollow, so this returns quietly rather than throwing not-initialized.
sendTurn(string $sessionId, string $text, string $delivery, ?string $idempotencyKey, array $images, array $documents): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.send (row 4).
createSession(?string $name, ?string $permissionMode): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.create (row 5). The primary root only: a bundle asks for another root with createSessionIn().
createSessionIn(string $root, ?string $name, ?string $permissionMode): PromiseInterfaceThe root form of createSession() (PL-5c-A, section 2.6): the session is created in $root, through its workspace host when $root is not the primary root. The id is bound to that root, so later calls find it by sessionId alone.
respondPermission(string $sessionId, string $askId, string $reply, ?string $note): PromiseInterfaceMirrors permission.respond (row 6).
cancelSession(string $sessionId, string $mode): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.cancel (row 7).
sessionSnapshot(string $sessionId, int $limit): PromiseInterfaceMirrors session.get (row 8).
execCommand(string $sessionId, string $name, string $args): PromiseInterfaceMirrors command.exec (row 9).
pendingPermissions(): PromiseInterfaceMirrors permission.pending (row 10) on the primary root.
pendingPermissionsIn(string $root): PromiseInterfaceThe root form of pendingPermissions() (PL-5c-A, section 2.6): the pending asks of $root's workspace host, with the top-level root set. Items carry no root of their own.
subscribeEvents(\Closure $listener): PromiseInterfaceRow 11: each event the followed sessions emit reaches the listener as its envelope array, EventEnvelope::toArray(): the params of the wire's event notification (PL-5d, decision c). A routed session's events carry root as well.
subscribeFollowResults(\Closure $listener): PromiseInterfaceRow 12: accepted so a bundle registers at construction, and never fired. The wire fires follow results only on a reconnect re-follow, which this door has no path to (see the class docblock). The first follow's answer is subscribeSession()'s return value.
followedSessions(): PromiseInterfaceRow 15: the session ids this client follows, the primary feeds' first, then the routed sessions in the order this client subscribed to them.

RemoteSessionHost final class

The client side of a candy-code.v1 endpoint: the SessionHost surface a TUI attached to a running candy-code serve drives, spoken as JSON-RPC over the connection (roadmap O-8a, Appendix O §4.9).

The workspace gateway forwards calls this way (\SugarCraft\Code\Server\Workspace\Gateway).
onEvent(\Closure $listener): \ClosureHear every event notification: the envelope's fields (sessionId, seq, type, turnId, durable, data), and the raw notification text beside it for a listener that relays it. Answers the detach.
onClose(\Closure $listener): \ClosureHear the connection end, with why. Called at once when it already has.
close(string $reason = 'client closing'): voidEnd the connection with a normal close. Idempotent, and final: a deliberate close never reconnects (ISS-114), even mid-backoff.
hello(): PromiseInterfaceserver.hello, once: answers the server's handshake result (protocol, server version, root, limits, principal).
helloResult(): ?arrayThe handshake's answer, once hello() has had it. @return array<string, mixed>|null
serverRoot(): ?stringThe root the server serves, as its handshake named it.
open(?string $target = null, int $pageRows = self::SNAPSHOT_PAGE_ROWS): PromiseInterfacePick the session this client follows and subscribe to it from a snapshot: a new one when $target is null, else the session whose id or name is $target, or whose id is the one starting with it. Rejects with a not-found RpcError when nothing matches, and ambiguous when a prefix matches more than one.
static resolveTarget(array $items, string $target): arrayThe session among $items that $target names: an exact id, then an exact name, then the one id that starts with it.
sessionId(): ?stringThe session open() chose, once it has.
sessionName(): ?string
serverCommands(): arrayThe cached command.list roster (C-SES-7.f): command name to "server" or "client". Empty until open()'s fetch answers — and it answers exactly once, so callers treat an absent name as "run it here", never as "the server refused".
lastSeq(): intThe highest durable seq this client has seen for its session.
snapshot(): arrayThe snapshot the subscription started from. @return array<string, mixed>
history(): arrayThe session's transcript as the server held it when this client subscribed — the rows a TUI paints first.
submit(string $text, string $delivery = 'queue'): PromiseInterfacesession.send: start a turn with $text, or queue / steer / interrupt the running one ($delivery). Answers the admission ({admitted, turnId?, queueId?, …}).
cancel(?string $turnId = null, string $mode = 'hard'): PromiseInterfacesession.cancel: stop the running turn ($turnId, when known), hard or soft at its next step boundary.
answerPermission(string $askId, PermissionReply $reply, ?string $note = null): PromiseInterfacepermission.respond: answer the open question $askId. The first answer any client gives wins; a later one is refused already_resolved.

SessionEvent final class

One thing that happened in a session, in the shape a host broadcasts it (roadmap O-2f, Appendix O §6.4 envelope / §6.5 catalogue).

MethodSummary
static new(string $type, array $data = [], ?string $sessionId = null, ?string $turnId = null, ?int $tsMs = null): selfAn event of $type. Whether it is durable follows from the type (isDurable()).
static typeIsDurable(string $type): boolWhether $type is one Appendix O §6.5 marks durable.
isDurable(): boolWhether this event is written to the session's log before it is heard.
withSeq(int $seq): selfA copy stamped with the seq the EventLog allocated for it.
