SessionHost final class

One open session, driven without a screen (roadmap O-2g, Appendix O §4.3).

MethodSummary
static new(string $sessionId, WorkspaceContext $workspace, array $history = [], ?TranscriptStore $transcripts = null, ?SessionLock $lease = null, ?CompactorConfig $compactorConfig = null, ?array $customCommands = null, ?\Closure $mcpProvider = null, bool $ephemeral = false, ?string $ephemeralName = null): selfA host for $sessionId over $workspace.
static transcriptsFor(WorkspaceContext $workspace): TranscriptStoreThe store a host saves through when none was named.
sessionId(): string
isEphemeral(): boolC-SES-7.e: true for an incognito host — created with session.create {ephemeral:true}, never written to the store.
ephemeralName(): ?stringC-SES-7.e: the name carried by an ephemeral host, which has no store row to read it from. Null for a persisted host (its name lives in the sessions table); for an ephemeral host it is the name given at create, and the summary falls back to it.
customCommands(): arrayThe session's command map — the workspace's file rows merged under the launch-frozen MCP prompt rows (C-MCP-2.b: command.list and command.exec answer from exactly this map, the same table submit() resolves, so a listing can never promise a row exec will refuse).
todos(): \SugarCraft\Code\Todo\TodoListThe session's todo list (roadmap 3.C), as its Todo tool last wrote it.
workspace(): WorkspaceContext
history(): array
queued(): array
isBusy(): boolWhether a turn (or a submission parked behind off-thread work) holds this session.
turnId(): ?stringThe id of the turn in flight, when the runner started one.
spentUsd(): floatWhat the session has spent, as the provider reported it.
snapshot(): SessionSnapshotThe session as a client first sees it (SessionSnapshot).
onEvent(\Closure $listener): \ClosureHear this session's events — durable ones once the log numbered them, ephemeral ones live (TurnRunner::listen()). Returns the closure that detaches the listener.
modelOverride(): ?arrayC-WEB-1.a: the {provider, model} pair this session's served /model switched to, or null while it still runs the launch row's pair. Lives for exactly as long as self::$sessionBackend does — the host dies, the override dies with it, and the next open resolves the saved choice through the launch's own layers.
primaryAgentOverride(): ?stringC-AGT-4.b: the preset name this session's /agent use switched the primary agent to, or null while it runs the plain session default (use default stores null exactly like the terminal's revert). The serve path honours the name: each turn dispatch resolves it against the roster and narrows through PrimaryAgent::apply(), so the badge and the wire agree while the host lives. The same host-lifetime law as self::$modelOverride: a restart resolves the launch roster afresh and finds no override.
onSummaryChanged(?\Closure $hook): voidC-WEB-1.a: bind (or pass null to clear) the hook that hears a summary change with no status transition behind it — self::$onSummaryChanged.
events(): ?EventLogThe session's durable event log, or null when its store keeps none.
announce(SessionEvent $event): ?SessionEventRecord $event for this session through the path a turn's own events take — logged first when durable, then heard by every listener — for the facts only a driver knows (a prompt queued, the session's status). Returns the event as heard, or null when a durable write failed.
permissionMode(): ?PermissionModeThe permission mode this session's turns run in: the one set by setPermissionMode(), else the workspace gate's, else null when the backend has no gate at all.
setPermissionMode(?PermissionMode $mode): voidRun this session's NEXT turns in $mode (null: the workspace gate's). The turn in flight keeps the gate it was forked with. Whether a client may choose $mode is the caller's question (ServerConfig::admitsPermissionMode()).
permissionGate(): ?PermissionGateThe gate this session is consented by — the session resolution: the session's own mode over the base rules when it names one, else the base gate itself. backend() recomputes this per dispatch and then folds the primary agent's own mode on top, so an agent hat narrows turns only — it never widens out-of-turn consent. Out-of-turn side-effect surfaces (generate.submit) must consult this, not the bare workspace gate, or a bypass-admitted session would run tools freely in-turn yet be refused at the RPC door (R15 MAJOR-1).
grants(): SessionPermissionMemoThe session's remembered "always" answers.
pendingAsks(): arrayThe questions the running turn is blocked on, oldest first.
answer(string $askId, PermissionReply $reply, ?string $note = null): ?PermissionResolvedAnswer the open question $askId, first answer wins (Appendix O §6.7). An always the question offers is remembered as this session's grant for every later turn. Returns how the question was settled, or null when no open question has that id — it was answered already (see resolution()), cancelled with its turn, or never asked here.
resolution(string $askId): ?PermissionResolvedHow the question $askId was settled, when it was settled recently here.
cancelSoft(): boolAsk the running turn to stop at its next step boundary, letting the tool in flight finish (cancel_soft, Appendix O §5.1). The turn settles on its own; nothing is healed here.
removeQueued(int $index): ?stringDrop the queued prompt at $index (0 is the next to go out).
submit(string $text, ?SubmitOptions $options = null): TurnTicketSubmit $text to the session (see the class docblock for the order it is judged in) and say how it was admitted.
cancel(?string $turnId = null): boolCancel the turn in flight — or a submission parked behind off-thread work — when $turnId is null or names it. Its running tool rows are healed into the same "interrupted" rows the TUI writes, so the next request's wire has no tool_use left unanswered. Queued prompts stay queued and go out with the next submission's settle; a caller that wants them gone clears them (clearQueue()).
clearQueue(): intDrop every queued prompt; returns how many there were.
pump(): intFold whatever the running turn has reported since the last fold into the transcript — running placeholders and finished tool rows, through the TranscriptProjector the TUI's live pump uses — and hand every event to the runner's listeners and log. A server calls this on its own tick; what is still on the inbox when the turn settles folds then.
tick(int $now): intAdvance this session's due /loop rows (C-AGT-1.b) — the generic per-session clock a server calls on its own tick (C-AGT-4.e reuses it).
release(): voidLet go of the session's lock and its /loop rows; the host must not be used after. Dropping the ephemeral rows keyed to this session is what makes a served loop die with its session (C-AGT-1.b) — a row nobody fires is a row nobody promised to fire, so close must clear the promise.
appendNotice(string $text): voidC-MCP-4.c: one UI-only notice row from a later-landing process event — today the served mcp auth login beats that \SugarCraft\Code\Host\ServedMcpLogins collects and \SugarCraft\Code\Protocol\ServerContext::pump() routes. The row enters history, save and the message.created announcement exactly like a command's own row, carrying the notice kind Role::System rows paint with.
contextSources(): arrayWEB-3a: this session's structured context sources for context.sources (\SugarCraft\Code\Protocol\Methods\ContextMethods). Built through the same commandContext() /context runs with and measured by the same \SugarCraft\Code\Host\ContextSources provider — with the history figure taken from this host's own calibrated estimate, exactly as the status bar shows it. No Chat state is reached: the session IS the provider (the seam WEB-3a's brief anticipated).
registerClientTools(string $clientKey, array $specs): stringC-TOOL-6.h: host $specs as this client's tools for the session's NEXT turns, replacing whatever $clientKey held before. Returns the registration id every later answer for these tools must carry. Throws with a one-word verdict when the batch is not shippable (ClientToolRegistry::register()); who may call this at all — a connection holding Write scope, behind server.clientTools — is the protocol step's door (6.i), not this substrate's.
forgetClientTools(string $clientKey): voidC-TOOL-6.h: drop $clientKey's registrations (its connection closed — the ruling that kills a client's tools with it) and settle its open calls as errors, so a child blocked on one of them learns the truth instead of waiting out its deadline.
resolveClientCall(string $callId, string $registrationId, string $content, bool $isError): boolC-TOOL-6.h: answer the open client call $callId — first answer wins (the same law answer() keeps for questions). An id not open, a call already settled another way, and an answer carrying a registration id other than the one that opened the call all read the same from here: false. A client re-registered between the call and the answer is exactly the case that id exists to refuse.
onClientCall(?\Closure $hook): voidC-TOOL-6.h: bind (or pass null to clear) the listener that hears each freshly opened client call with the client and registration that must answer it — the handle the serve relay (6.i) forwards on.
runCommand(string $name, string $args = ''): CommandResultRun the built-in command /$name $args (roadmap O-2h, Appendix O §6.3 command.exec) and say what it produced. Its rows are already in the transcript and its effects applied when this returns; off-turn work it started lands later as a row.

SessionSnapshot final class

One open session as a client first sees it (roadmap O-2g, Appendix O §4.3 SessionHost::snapshot()): its transcript rows, whether a turn is running and which, the prompts waiting behind it, and what it has spent.

MethodSummary
static new(string $sessionId, array $history = [], array $queued = [], bool $busy = false, ?string $turnId = null, float $spentUsd = 0.0, int $lastSeq = 0, bool $spendUnpriced = false): self
status(): stringThe session's status word (Appendix O §6.5 session.status): busy or idle.
toArray(): arrayThe wire shape: rows as they are saved (Message::jsonSerialize()) with the finished calls' media refs folded in (mediaBearingRow()), plus the status the rows cannot show.
pagedArray(?int $limit, ?int $beforeIndex = null): arrayThe wire shape with the messages window paged (ISS-058): the newest $limit rows strictly OLDER than $beforeIndex — the row AT that index is excluded, the bound is exclusive-upper — still oldest-row-first inside the page. Null $beforeIndex windows over the whole history. Null $limit answers exactly toArray(). A paged answer says where its window sits — totalMessages, the oldestIndex of its first row in the full history, and hasMoreOlder — so a client that wants the beginning pages older with beforeIndex = oldestIndex (indices are counted from the first row, which appending never shifts).

SpendLedger final class

A session's provider-reported spend against its cap: recording a call's usage, the one definition of "over budget", the refusal and mid-turn notices, and the /budget command's logic (roadmap O-2c, Appendix O §4.2 "Spend accounting").

MethodSummary
static new(): self
static crossedByPreviousTurn(): stringWhat crossed the cap when a freshly submitted prompt is refused: a previous turn, which was allowed to finish. The other refusal site (a turn the 85% tier parked) names its own crossing.
spent(TokenTracker $tracker): floatThe session's provider-reported spend in US dollars. Exactly 0.0 is BOTH "nothing was reported" and "this provider is free", which is why a readout keys off hasReported() rather than off this being positive.
static boundUsd(bool $unpriced, float $usd): stringThe same law as boundAmount() one seam further out: for sums the ledger is not holding — the mid-turn breach event, the compaction refusals, a host snapshot — the caller carries the unpriced bit and the bound is spelled here, so ≥$ has ONE spelling in the app.
hasReported(TokenTracker $tracker): boolWhether any call this session actually reported usage. A READOUT concern only: the cap decision (capReached()) gets the same fail-open from arithmetic — an unreported session's spend is 0.0 and a cap is always positive — not from consulting this.
account(TokenTracker $tracker, ?Usage $usage, ?\Closure $record = null, ?string $model = null, ?string $source = null): voidPut one provider call's reported usage on the session tracker, or do nothing when the provider reported none — a null $usage is "unknown", which must not become a zero-dollar call.
capReached(TokenTracker $tracker, ?float $cap): boolWhether a session has reached its cap — the one definition of "over budget" every enforcement site asks. False whenever there is no cap, and false for a session nothing was reported for (spend 0.0 against a positive cap): the deliberate fail-OPEN that makes a cap a budget guard rather than a security control.
static isUsableCap(float $cap): boolWhether $cap is a spend ceiling this app will act on: a positive, finite number of dollars. 0 and negatives are REFUSED rather than read as "no cap" (opposite intentions), and non-finite is refused because (float) '1e309' is INF, which every comparison treats as no cap at all — and NAN compares false both ways.
refusalNotice(TokenTracker $tracker, float $cap, string $crossing): stringThe notice a turn refused at the cap carries: the state, what crossed it ($crossing), and the three ways out.
midTurnNotice(SpendCapBreached $event): stringThe notice E20's mid-turn abort puts on the transcript. A DIFFERENT promise from refusalNotice()'s: that one refused to start and nothing was billed; this one says a call already happened and the loop stopped before the next.
statusLine(TokenTracker $tracker, ?float $cap): stringWhere a session stands, in the two units it can honestly report. Says "not reported" rather than $0.0000 when nothing has arrived, and says LOWER BOUND once any call came from a model with no price on file.
budgetReply(string $argument, TokenTracker $tracker, ?float $currentCap): array/budget <argument> decided: the answer to print and what happens to the cap. Three forms — bare shows the status, off/none/clear clears, an amount (a leading $ accepted) sets — and anything that is not a usable cap (isUsableCap()) gets the usage line with the cap left alone.

The two cheap side-calls a session makes on its tool-less title backend: the once-per-session auto-title, and the after-every-turn guess at the user's next prompt (roadmap O-2d, Appendix O §4.2 "Dispatch … title scheduling → Host\TitleService").

static new(): selfTitles on, suggestions on (still subject to the env switch and the spend cap).

static sanitizeSuggestion(string $raw): stringReduce the model's guess to one safe line for the input box: <think> blocks dropped, every escape and control byte stripped, the first non-empty line only, a User: label or wrapping quotes peeled off, and the model's "nothing to suggest" answer turned into ''.
static autoTitleEnabled(): boolWhether a session is titled automatically after its first turn: the sessions.autoTitle setting (default on). Off leaves every new session unnamed until /rename — which still asks the title model on demand (regenerateCall() is not gated). Read per turn through \SugarCraft\Code\Config\Settings\UiSettings, so a save applies to the next session that would have been titled. C-M17 adds CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE as the shell's word over every file, and the user tier alone decides: a project may switch this off, never on (userTierAllows()).
static promptSuggestionsEnabled(): boolWhether prompt suggestions are offered at all, by the operator's word: CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTIONS turns them off whatever the settings say, and the promptSuggestions setting (default on) turns them off without it. Neither turns them back on over the other — and a host with no input box still switches them off on top (withPromptSuggestions()). Since C-M17 the setting's user tier decides it the same way the shell does: a project file may switch this off, never on (userTierAllows()).

The autoReview row rides only while the engagement is IMPLICIT — an explicit true or false is already the operator's own word, and the implicit announce is owner-ruled territory (t212) reproduced verbatim, never reworded here. The defaults row rides when any of the three default-on dials (autoTitle, prompt suggestions, away recap) is effectively on. Rows fold into \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap's existing notice channel — nothing in this method starts a call.
static promptSuggestionHistory(): intHow many recent messages the suggestion call is shown: the promptSuggestionHistory setting, else PROMPT_SUGGESTION_HISTORY. USER TIER ONLY: every message is input tokens on the operator's title model after every turn.

toolStartedEvent(ToolStarted $event, ?array $identity, ?string $sessionId, ?string $turnId): SessionEventtool.started, naming the placeholder row when it already has an identity. A placeholder is transient — its finish replaces it with a new row — so it is named only if a save already gave it one, rather than spending a ref on a row that will not survive the turn; the toolCallId is what pairs the start with its finish.
toolFinishedEvent(ToolFinished $event, Message $row, ?array $identity, ?array $replaced, ?string $sessionId, ?string $turnId): SessionEventtool.finished, naming the finished row ($identity) and the placeholder it replaced when that one had an identity.
static mediaRefs(ToolResult $result, ?bool &$truncated = null, ?MediaStore $store = null): ?arrayThe media list a finished tool result projects to (W6.1).
static mediaStoreForSession(?string $sessionId): ?MediaStoreThe session media store a projection adopts through, or null when none can be opened — no session named, a hostile id, an unestablishable home. Null is a degraded fold, not a broken one: refs then name their paths exactly as given, the pre-C-WEB-1.d shape. Public because SessionSnapshot folds the same rows and R16(a) demands the two surfaces share one derivation rather than each opening stores its own way (or, worse, one refusing where the other adopted).
static mediaRefsForPaths(array $paths, ?string $headBytes = null, ?bool &$truncated = null, ?MediaStore $store = null, ?string $resultId = null): ?arrayOrdered media refs for a list of stored artifact paths, cut off at MAX_EVENT_MEDIA_REFS with the truncation flag raised for the caller to stamp onto the event. $headBytes — the bytes the result carried for the artifact at index 0 of the list — sizes and digests only that entry, and rides nowhere else (a head slot without a path means the bytes describe nothing on this event); other path-only refs report bytes: 0 and no digest. Empty (or entirely unpathed) input projects to null so the event key stays absent for old-client compatibility.
static mediaRef(string $path, ?string $bytes): arrayOne artifact ref: identity and path only (C-7). artifactId follows MediaStore's own id rule so a client can fetch by the id list() would report; infotextDigest rides only when the delivered bytes parse as a PNG carrying infotext. Public because the serve RPC reads the same single formatter: generate.status builds its artifact list and media.fetch its mime/kind row from here, never a re-derivation (plan W6.2).
backendEvent(object $event, ?string $sessionId, ?string $turnId): ?SessionEventThe event a non-row backend event projects to: a permission question and its settlement, a delegated run's beat, the step and bill frames, the spend cap, and the streaming deltas. Null for anything else (including the tool events, which need their rows — toolStartedEvent() / toolFinishedEvent()).
assistantCompletedEvent(Message $reply, ?array $identity, ?string $sessionId, ?string $turnId): SessionEventassistant.completed: the settled reply, under the identity of the row it lands as.
static stopReason(Message $reply, bool $softCancelled, bool $spendCapped): stringThe stopReason a settled reply ended on (Appendix O §6.5).

TranscriptStore final class

A session's transcript on disk: saving it (debounced or now), loading it back with its crash repairs, the single-writer lock on it, and the identity of each of its rows (roadmap O-2b, Appendix O §4.2 "Persistence and checkpoints" → Host\TranscriptStore).

MethodSummary
static new(SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $store, ?DebouncedTranscriptWriter $writer = null, ?EventLog $events = null): selfA transcript store over $store. Pass the writer whose pending snapshot a host flushes; null builds one of its own.
withWriter(DebouncedTranscriptWriter $writer): selfA copy that schedules through $writer — how Chat binds the workspace's store to the writer its own flush tick watches.
store(): ?EnhancedSessionStoreThe store transcripts are written to, or null when none persists.
writer(): DebouncedTranscriptWriterThe debounced writer schedule() hands snapshots to.
events(): ?EventLogThe durable event log beside the transcripts, or null without a store.
persists(): boolWhether this store persists anything at all.
schedule(string $sessionId, array $history): voidHand $history to the debounced writer as $sessionId's newest unsaved transcript; see DebouncedTranscriptWriter for when it is written and what a crash can lose.
save(string $sessionId, array $history): voidWrite $history as $sessionId's transcript now, flushing any other pending snapshot first so the two cannot land out of order.
flush(): voidWrite any snapshot still waiting on its debounce tick, now.
hasPending(): boolTrue while a snapshot is waiting to be written.
load(string $sessionId): arrayThe saved transcript of $sessionId as Messages, each "running" placeholder healed (reviveRow()), or [] when the store has none or cannot say.
loadLedger(string $sessionId): ?ContextLedger$sessionId's saved context ledger (roadmap 2.2-2), or null when none was saved, the store cannot say, or nothing persists.
saveLedger(string $sessionId, ContextLedger $ledger): boolSave $ledger as $sessionId's context ledger, now. False when nothing persists or the store refused it — never thrown: the ledger is a cache-stability aid, and a turn is never failed over one.
loadTodos(string $sessionId): ?TodoList$sessionId's saved todo list (roadmap 3.C), read from SessionMeta::$tasks, or null when the session has no metadata row, the store cannot say, or nothing persists.
saveTodos(string $sessionId, TodoList $todos): boolSave $todos as $sessionId's todo list, now — into the metadata row's tasks slot, keeping the row's other fields. False when nothing persists or the store refused it; never thrown, for the reason saveLedger() gives: a turn is never failed over its checklist.
loadPermissionGrants(string $sessionId): array$sessionId's remembered "always" grants as a grant map (\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\SessionPermissionMemo::fromGrants()), or [] when nothing persists or the store cannot say.
savePermissionGrants(string $sessionId, array $grants): boolSave $grants (a grant map) as $sessionId's remembered grants, now. False when nothing persists or the store refused it; never thrown — a grant that is not saved is asked again after a resume, nothing worse.
lock(string $sessionId): ?SessionLockTake the single-writer lock on $sessionId, or null when another process holds it — or when there is no store to lock under.
lockHolder(string $sessionId): ?intThe pid holding $sessionId's lock, when it can be told.
identityOf(Message $message): ?arrayThe [id, ref] $message's row has: the one it carries, else the one a save (or identify()) gave it — the same across every wither of the row. Null while the row has never been saved or identified, and always without a store.
identify(string $sessionId, Message $message): ?array$message's identity in $sessionId, allocated now when its row has none, and kept by every later save. Null without a store.
static reviveRow(array $row): MessageRebuild one saved transcript row for a resume: every field Message::fromArray() can restore — tool calls and results, reasoning, usage, identity — with one repair. A "running" placeholder in a saved transcript is a tool call whose process is gone, so it comes back as the same "interrupted" error row reviveCheckpointRow() makes for /rewind; left as a placeholder it would spin forever for a result that cannot arrive.
static reviveCheckpointRow(array $row): MessageRebuild one checkpointed history row, healing a checkpoint taken while a tool call was still in flight (§1 E7). See Chat::reviveCheckpointMessage(), which delegates here and keeps the full account of why each role and the placeholder are handled the way they are.
static interruptedToolCallRow(string $content, string $callId, string $reason): MessageThe "this call lost its runner" row: a synthetic assistant turn whose error tool_result answers $callId, so the next request's wire has no tool_use left unanswered. One builder for every heal path — a restart (Chat::INTERRUPTED_TOOL_CALL) and a user cancel (Chat::CANCELLED_TOOL_CALL) — so they render and serialise identically and differ only in $reason.

TurnController final class

Submission, queueing and turn dispatch as logic a host runs without a screen (roadmap O-2g, Appendix O §4.2 "Submit pipeline", "Dispatch", "Prompt queueing mid-turn").

MethodSummary
static new(): self
static quoteDraft(string $text): stringOne bounded, control-byte-free excerpt of untrusted draft text, for a notice that is about to be painted.
queuedNotice(int $waiting, string $text): stringThe notice a queued follow-up gets: $waiting is the queue's length with it.
steeringNotice(string $text): stringThe notice a prompt steered into the running turn gets (roadmap 1.C-3).
emptyCustomCommandNotice(string $text): stringWhy a command file whose template expanded to nothing was not sent.
inFlightCommandNotice(string $text): stringWhy a slash command TYPED while a turn runs was not run — the draft is kept, so the notice says Enter will run it.
runCommandInFlightNotice(string $text): stringWhy a command run on the user's behalf (a menu row, Ctrl+N) while a turn runs was not run — the draft was never touched, so the notice says so.
inFlightActionNotice(string $what): stringWhy an overlay action chosen while a turn runs was not run; $what is its label.
readOnlyNotice(string $text, string $session): stringWhy a read-only session did not send $text; $session is its name or id.
bangRefusedNotice(string $command, string $reason): stringWhy !$command did not run: $reason from BangShell::refusal().
bangRunningNotice(string $command): stringThe row a !$command that is about to run adds.
turnHookBlockedNotice(string $blocked, string $text, bool $boxOccupied): stringThe row a prompt a turn hook blocked gets: $blocked is turnHookRefusalReason()'s sentence. $boxOccupied says the user typed a NEW draft while a forked chain ran, in which case the box keeps theirs (losing typed text is the worse error) and the notice quotes the prompt instead of claiming it is still in the box.
expansionFailedNotice(string $text, bool $boxOccupied): stringThe row a forked command-file expansion that reported nothing gets.
hostCommandNotice(string $text): stringWhy a headless host did not run the command $text: a turn holds the session, and a command would rewrite the history that turn is about to append to. A command file is a PROMPT and is not refused by this.
noBackendNotice(): stringWhy a host with no backend sent nothing.
emptyPromptNotice(): stringWhy an empty submission sent nothing.
static isBareMcpAuthCommand(string $text): boolWhether $text is the leading-slash-less mcp auth … command spelling.
midTurnRoute(string $text, bool $workflowControl, SubmitOptions $options): stringWhat a line submitted while a turn is running does — one of the ROUTE_* constants.
static withoutDeliveredSteers(array $queue, array $history): array$queue without the entries the turn that just settled delivered as steers (roadmap 1.C-3).
resolveCustomCommand(string $text, array $customCommands): ?arrayThe file-based command a typed /name … names, with its argument string, or null when it names none.
expandCustomCommand(CommandSpec $spec, string $arguments, \Closure $directive): ?string$spec's template expanded for $arguments, with $directive answering its ` !cmd and @path` forms (commandDirective()).
wrapCommandDelegation(string $expanded, CommandSpec $spec): stringC-EXT-2.e: the fenced delegation directive a subtask: true or agent:-declaring command's expansion rides.
commandTurnModel(CommandSpec $spec, ?EngineBackend $engine): ?arrayC-EXT-2.e: the inline model: of a command with NO delegation key pins exactly the ONE turn its expansion is sent as — never the session, so the next turn runs on the session's model without any restore step.
commandDirective(CommandSpec $spec, string $root, bool $projectCommandsTrusted, ?PermissionGate $gate, ?\Closure $onGateEvaluated = null, array $trustedBundleCommands = [], array $mcpPromptShell = []): \ClosureThe resolver CommandSpec::expandTemplate() calls for the two template forms that leave the string: ` !cmd and @path`.
refuseCommandShell(CommandSpec $spec, string $command, bool $projectCommandsTrusted, ?PermissionGate $gate, ?\Closure $onGateEvaluated = null, array $trustedBundleCommands = [], array $mcpPromptShell = []): ?stringWhy this ` !cmd ` may not run, or null if it may.
customCommandMustFork(string $text, array $customCommands, ?string $resolvedText, bool $projectCommandsTrusted, array $trustedBundleCommands = [], array $mcpPromptShell = []): boolWhether expanding the command file $text names would run a shell, and so has to leave the host's thread.
static customCommandPayload(?string $expanded, array $gated): stringWhat a forked expansion child writes. THE EXPANSION CROSSES THE BOUNDARY BASE64-ENCODED: it carries raw command output, which need not be UTF-8, and JSON's substitution would hand the model different bytes from the ones the synchronous path sent.
static customCommandExpansionFromPayload(string|false $data): arrayRead back what an expansion child wrote ($data, already taken from its payload file). Anything unreadable is a null expansion, which a caller refuses rather than sends.
turnHookContext(string $event, string $prompt, bool $atStartup, ?string $sessionId, string $root): HookContextThe tool-shaped context a turn-lifecycle hook is dispatched with (P7.S2).
turnHookRefusalReason(HookResult $result): ?stringWhy a turn-lifecycle verdict does not permit the turn, or null when it does.
turnHooksMustFork(?HookManager $hooks, array $events): boolWhether this submission's turn-hook chain has to leave the host's thread: a hook on one of $events runs out of process AND this build can fork. Without pcntl the chain runs synchronously as it always did.
static runTurnHooks(HookManager $hooks, HookContext $promptContext, ?HookContext $sessionContext): arrayRun one submission's chain, GATE-FIRST: UserPromptSubmit, then — only when it permitted the prompt and $sessionContext says the event fires — SessionStart, so a SessionStart script never spawns just to learn its prompt was blocked. The one body behind the in-process path and the forked child alike.
turnHookNotes(HookResult $prompt, ?HookResult $session): arrayThe role: system notes a permitted submission carries, in the order Anthropic's insertion-point table implies: SessionStart's note ahead of the UserPromptSubmit note, both ahead of the user's line. A blocked SessionStart stops nothing — its note is discarded and only the reason is said. An empty additionalContext adds no row, so a wired chain that produced no stdout leaves the request byte-identical.
static turnHookResultToArray(HookResult $result): array
static turnHookResultFromArray(mixed $row): ?HookResult
static turnHookPayload(HookResult $prompt, ?HookResult $session): stringWhat a forked turn-hook child writes: both verdicts.
static turnHookResultsFromPayload(string|false $data): arrayRead back what a turn-hook child wrote ($data, already taken from its payload file). A CHILD THAT REPORTS NOTHING FAILS CLOSED: a crashed or truncated payload is a DENY, because "the prompt gate could not answer" letting the prompt through is the widening HookResult::permitsExecution()'s allow-list exists to prevent.
static takePayload(string $file): string|falseWhat a child forkPayload() started wrote to $file — the name ToolIpcFiles::reserve() chose in this process before the fork — read once and discarded either way, including on a failed read, so a half-written payload is never left behind.
static canFork(): boolWhether this build can fork a child and poll it without blocking.
static forkPayload(\Closure $childWork, \Closure $collect, \Closure $inline, CancellationToken $cancellation, float $reapBudgetSeconds = self::REAP_BUDGET_SECONDS, float $reapPollSeconds = self::REAP_POLL_SECONDS): PromiseInterfaceRun $childWork in a forked child and resolve with what its payload decodes to — the one fork + WNOHANG-poll shape behind every piece of a submission that leaves the thread: a turn's script hooks and a command file's shell forms.
userTurnMessage(string $text, bool $resolveMentions, string $root, SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $store, ?PermissionGate $gate, ?\SugarCraft\Code\Skills\SkillRegistry $skills = null, ?\Closure $mcpProvider = null, array $extraAttachments = [], ?\Closure $agentRoster = null): arrayThe user row a submitted prompt becomes, with its mentions attached, plus one notice per mention that could not be.
inlineTier(CompactionService $compaction, ContextCompactor $compactor, array $history, array $wireHistory, int $tokenLimit, int $tokenCount, \Closure $estimate, array $summaries = []): arrayThe automatic tier's synchronous heuristic route for one submission, once the caller has found the tier fired and neither the thrash breaker nor a model-written summary (CompactionService's parked route) took it.
turnPrompt(array $newTurnMessages): ?stringThe prompt $newTurnMessages carries: the content of its last user row, or null when it has none.
checkpointState(array $preTurnHistory, string $draft, ?int $cursor, ?string $sessionId, array $pasteChips = [], int $pasteCounter = 0): arrayThe checkpoint state a dispatch saves: THE STATE BEFORE THE PROMPT, NOT AFTER IT. Every row the submission itself added — the user's line, the hook notes, the 70% reminder — is out, because a resend through the restored draft regenerates all three; the compaction the submission triggered stays in with its reports, because a rewrite is a fact about the transcript, not about the prompt. The draft and caret are the caller's: on the ordinary route the pre-clear buffer, on the parked route whatever the box held when it was parked.
saveCheckpoint(SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $store, ?string $sessionId, ?string $root, array $state): ?\ClosureSave $state as $sessionId's next checkpoint and answer the workspace capture that belongs beside it, or null when there is none to take.
recordTurn(SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $store, ?string $sessionId, array $newTurnMessages): voidThe row's turn count and last-prompt preview, which the session picker shows instead of the system prompt every session shares (Appendix P §3.1). Picker bookkeeping only; never blocks the prompt.
recordMessagesCreated(?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId, array $newTurnMessages, ?TurnRunner $runner = null): arrayAnnounce the prompt row(s) a dispatch commits as durable message.created events in the session's EventLog (Appendix O §6.5), each named by the identity its save will keep (TranscriptStore::identify()) — the same id the turn's own turn.started then cites as its messageId.

TurnRunner final class

Runs one backend dispatch of a session's turn and says what happened in it (roadmap O-2f, Appendix O §4.2 "Backend completion + inbox + generation guard → Host\TurnRunner").

MethodSummary
static new(?TranscriptProjector $projector = null): self
static of(object $owner): selfThe runner belonging to $owner — the fallback a Chat with no workspace-registered runner uses, keyed to its live inbox so every clone of one Chat lineage shares it.
bindActiveSubagentSource(?\Closure $source): selfRead the "Active subagents" list from $source instead of the turn's Task tool (roadmap 4.3-2) — a host that keeps its own background supervisor, or a test. Null restores the default.
activeSubagents(Backend $backend): arrayThe background sessions still running for the host that dispatches through $backend, as BackgroundSupervisor::ownedActiveSummaries() reports them: from the bound source, else from the supervisor the engine's Task tool spawns through. A backend with neither has none.
projector(): TranscriptProjectorThe projector the caller folds this runner's events through.
listen(\Closure $listener): \ClosureHear every event this runner records — durable ones after the log numbered them, ephemeral ones live. The protocol layer's broadcast seam (Appendix O §6.4). Returns the closure that detaches it.
hasListeners(): boolWhether anyone hears this runner's events.
turnIdOf(?CancellationToken $turn): ?stringThe id of the turn $turn dispatched, or null when this runner did not start it.
static backendForTurn(Backend $backend, ?float $maxCostUsd, float $spentUsd, ?CompactorConfig $compactorConfig, ?string $sessionId, SessionPermissionMemo $grants, ?ClientToolRegistry $clientTools = null, ?\Closure $clientCallSink = null): Backend$backend wired for ONE dispatch of a session's turn.
start(Backend $backend, array $history, \ArrayObject $inbox, int $generation, CancellationToken $cancellation, bool $streaming = true, ?\Closure $tokenObserver = null, ?\Closure $reportObserverFailure = null, ?NoticeSink $notices = null, ?AgentManager $agentManager = null, ?TranscriptStore $transcripts = null, ?string $sessionId = null): \ClosureOpen one dispatch of a turn and return the thunk that runs it: a \Closure(): PromiseInterface<Msg> the caller schedules (Chat hands it to Cmd::promise()). The durable turn.started is written now, so it precedes every event the turn can produce.
static drainInbox(\ArrayObject $inbox, int $generation): arrayTake everything this turn queued but the live pump never got to, and leave the inbox empty.
ledger(?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId): ContextLedger$sessionId's context ledger as the next turn will start from it: the stored one when $transcripts persists, else the one this runner kept from the session's last turn, else an empty one.
heldLedger(?string $sessionId): ?ContextLedger$sessionId's context ledger as this runner holds it, or null when it holds none — the store is never read, so the transcript can call it per frame (roadmap 3.B-3: the pruned / distilled badges). Held from every save, a live ledger frame's included.
observeLedger(?CancellationToken $turn, \SugarCraft\Code\Events\ContextLedgerChanged $event): voidApply a running turn's \SugarCraft\Code\Events\ContextLedgerChanged to its session's ledger and keep it (roadmap 3.B-3, DCP §13.2 G) — the mid-turn view of a Prune. Idempotent with the turn's settle, which saves the turn's whole final ledger over it. A turn this runner did not start changes nothing.
saveLedger(?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId, ContextLedger $ledger): voidKeep $ledger as $sessionId's: in this runner, and in the store when $transcripts persists. The one writer of the session's ledger — a settled turn's and a command's (/sweep, /pruning) both come here.
todos(?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId): TodoList$sessionId's todo list: the one this runner holds, else the one the store saved (then held), else an empty one. Held first because the runner is the list's only writer; read at dispatch, never from view().
heldTodos(?string $sessionId): ?TodoList$sessionId's todo list as this runner holds it, or null when it holds none — the store is never read, so the dock pane can call it per frame.
saveTodos(?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId, TodoList $todos): voidKeep $todos as $sessionId's: in this runner, and in the store's session metadata when $transcripts persists. The one writer of the list.
heldContext(?string $sessionId): ?ContextCategories$sessionId's context snapshot as this runner last measured it, or null when nothing has been measured for it — the store is never consulted, so the dock pane can call it per frame, exactly like heldTodos().
saveContext(?string $sessionId, ContextCategories $context): voidKeep $context as $sessionId's snapshot (P-CTX.d's writer: Chat's \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::measureContextCmd() pass). The latest save wins the slot; a failed measurement never calls this, so the pane keeps showing the previous stamp rather than an invented zero.
observeTodo(?CancellationToken $turn, ToolFinished $event): ?TodoUpdatedThe TodoUpdated a finished Todo call means, applied — kept as the turn's session's list and saved — or null for any other event: a different tool, a call that failed (the list did not change), a result a hook replaced so it no longer carries the rendering, or a turn this runner did not start. An applied list is also recorded as the session's durable todo.updated event.
static approvedPlanExit(array $history): ?\SugarCraft\Code\App\PermissionModeToggledMsgThe mode switch an approved PlanExit (roadmap 5.7-2) asks for, read off the turn that just ended in $history — or null when its latest PlanExit result was not an approval, or it called none.
recordToolStarted(?CancellationToken $turn, ToolStarted $event, Message $placeholder): voidtool.started for a call whose placeholder the caller just appended.
recordToolFinished(?CancellationToken $turn, ToolFinished $event, Message $row, ?Message $replaced): voidtool.finished for a call whose finished $row the caller just wrote, named by the identity its save will keep.
recordEvent(?CancellationToken $turn, object $event): voidAny other event the caller folded: a permission question or its settlement, a delegated run's beat, the step and bill frames, the spend cap, a streaming delta. Ephemeral ones are built only when someone listens.
completeParked(?CancellationToken $turn): voidClose a turn start()'s settle parked behind events the caller still had to fold — called once the last of them is applied, or when the caller drops them as superseded.
announce(SessionEvent $event, ?TranscriptStore $transcripts, ?string $sessionId): ?SessionEventRecord a session event that no turn of this runner produced — the prompt's own message.created (roadmap O-2g), written by TurnController::recordMessagesCreated() before the turn starts — through the same log-then-broadcast path the turn's events take, so a listener hears it and a replay reads it under one seq.

TurnSettleWork final class

One decision table, two hosts (the \SugarCraft\Code\Goal\GoalLoop shape): the four side-calls a settled turn may schedule — the next-prompt suggestion, auto-memory consolidation, the turn-mode auto-commit and the dream pass — decided from flags any settle knows and nothing else.

MethodSummary
static plan(bool $carriedOn, bool $goalActive, ?MemoryStore $memoryStore, ?Backend $engineBackend, ?Backend $summaryBackend, ?Backend $titleBackend, array $history, bool $capReached, ?string $sessionId, int $generation, string $projectRoot, array $userConfig, SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $sessionStore, ?TitleService $titleService = null): selfThe table itself. Every argument is something both hosts already hold at a settle: the two flags, the memory store (null when memory is off), the three backends by role — the session's engine, the tool-less summary model, the tool-less title model — the settled transcript, the spend-cap verdict, the session id and the history generation the suggestion message must match, the project root ('' for none), the merged user settings and the session store.

What became of one submission (roadmap O-2g, Appendix O §4.3 and §6.6).

WorkspaceContext final class

Everything a session needs from its project root that is not a screen: the non-UI half of Bootstrap::chat(), built once per root by Bootstrap::workspace() (roadmap O-2a, Appendix O §4.3).

MethodSummary
static new(?string $root = null, array $userConfig = [], ?NoticeSink $notices = null, ?RulesState $rulesState = null, SessionStore|EnhancedSessionStore|null $sessionStore = null, ?SkillRegistry $skills = null, ?PermissionGate $permissionGate = null, ?CommandLoader $commandLoader = null, bool $projectCommandsTrusted = false, array $trustedBundleCommands = [], array $mcpPromptShell = [], ?AgentManager $agentManager = null, ?AgentPoolConfig $agentPoolConfig = null, ?AgentWorkerPool $taskPool = null, ?Backend $backend = null, ?\Closure $backendFactory = null, ?MemoryStore $memoryStore = null, ?HookManager $hooks = null, ?Backend $titleBackend = null, ?Backend $summaryBackend = null, ?float $maxCostUsd = null, ?WorkflowEngineInterface $workflowEngine = null, ?BackgroundSupervisor $backgroundSupervisor = null): selfBuild a workspace. Every collaborator is optional, the way every Chat collaborator is, so an embedder or a test names only what it has.

A from:'user' message sent through it carries an HMAC under the key this workspace pinned at build (AgentInbox::launchKey()), the key the agent's own run verifies it with; a line written into the mailbox by anything else cannot claim the user's authority. Null when there is no owned home to keep mailboxes in (AgentInbox::defaultRoot()).

Null rather than a throw because every Chat collaborator is optional and degrades politely; a caller that cannot work without one says so in its own words.

forget(string $clientKey): voidDrop one client's whole set. Unknown keys are a no-op — a connection that never registered has nothing to forget, and the caller (6.i's disconnect path) must not need to know that.
proxies(): arrayThe proxies the next turn's roster carries, sorted by proxy name so the roster order never depends on connection arrival order.
owner(string $name): ?stringWhich client currently holds the tool named $name — a FULL proxy name (ClientToolProxy::NAME_PREFIX included), which is what a frame and the permission layer both carry.
currentRegistrationId(string $clientKey): ?stringThe registration id a client's CURRENT set answers must carry; null once the client is forgotten. The answer-validation leg in \SugarCraft\Code\Host\SessionHost::resolveClientCall() compares against this, which is how "wrong registration id" and "stale id" become the same reading without a lookup table that outlives a replace.
clientCount(): intHow many clients currently hold a set — a test/telemetry surface, not a hot path.

No reply row is written up front on purpose: the only honest thing to say then is "asked to spawn", and the real answer arrives with the spawn.

One session change a slash command asks for, beside the rows it appends (roadmap O-2h, CommandResult{rows[], effects[]}).

MethodSummary
static clearTranscript(): self
static restoreCheckpoint(array $messages, string $draft, ?int $cursor, ?array $pasteChips = null, int $pasteCounter = 0): self
static switchSession(string $sessionId): self

static async(\Closure $run, ?\Closure $describe = null, bool $armsBackgroundPoll = false): selfOff-turn work. $run starts it and resolves with whatever the TUI routes (a Msg, or null for nothing to show); $describe turns that value into the row a headless driver appends, or null for none. The row is a Message, not a string, because its verdict travels with it (ISS-097): a settled command that FAILED lands a flagged row, and the renderer never sniffs text to find that out.
armsBackgroundPoll(): boolWhether the run registers a background spawn that only the poll advances (async()).
asyncCmds(): arrayThe Cmds an Async effect queues, in order. A run that registers a background spawn is followed by a tick: the run registers the spawn only when it starts, and the Msg carrying its promise does not reconcile subscriptions, so nothing else arms the poll until the next key. The Program runs a batch's members in order, so the tick lands after the spawn is registered and arms the poll. The tick is a rewake tick: a stop it registers waits on rungs the poll advances, and the tick keeps re-queuing itself while one is still due.
static occupyTurn(\Closure $run, CancellationToken $cancellation, bool $workflow = true): selfWork that occupies the session until $run resolves with its report — the text of the UI-only row that settles it, or the row itself when it carries a verdict (ISS-097: /workflow failures resolve, never reject, so the error flag has to ride in the row). $cancellation is the turn's own (Esc Esc, session.cancel), and $workflow marks the run whose /workflow pause|status may still be typed while it holds the session.

static setPermissionMode(\SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\PermissionMode $mode): selfThe session's next turns run in $mode (permissionMode()).
static setModel(string $provider, string $model, \SugarCraft\Code\Backend $backend): selfSwitch the session's backend to $backend (CommandEffectKind::SetModel). Session-scoped, like the mode switch; never persisted.

CommandEffectKind enum

What a CommandEffect asks its driver to do to the session beyond appending the command's rows (roadmap O-2h, Appendix O §4.2).

Cases: ClearTranscript · RestoreCheckpoint · SwitchSession · RenameSession · OpenTitleEditor · OpenMediaForm · OpenVideoPlayer · Async · OccupyTurn · SetPermissionGrants · SetPermissionMode · SetModel · CompactTranscript · SubmitPrompt · SetPrimaryAgent

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

CommandResult final class

What one slash command produced (roadmap O-2h, Appendix O §4.2 and §6.3 command.exec → CommandResult{rows[], effects[]}): the transcript rows it appends, in order, and the CommandEffects its driver applies.

MethodSummary
static new(Message ...$rows): selfA result that appends $rows and changes nothing else.
static reply(string $text, string $reply): selfThe ordinary answer: $text echoed and $reply under it, both UI-only — a local report the model must not be shown on its next turn.
static errorReply(string $text, string $reply): selfThe answer to a command that could not do what was asked: $text echoed, then $reply UI-only AND error-flagged (ISS-097). The flag is the row's own verdict carried from the producer — the renderer paints flagged rows in the error colour and never sniffs the text, so a refusal built through plain self::reply() would paint as an ordinary local report. The echo stays unflagged: it is what the user typed, not what went wrong.
static echo(string $text): self$text echoed and nothing else yet: the answer arrives with an effect.
static failure(string $text, string $output, int $exitCode): selfA command that exited non-zero: the echo, then its output as a Role::System notice — an app-generated failure is not a model reply and must not be replayed to the provider as one. $exitCode is named only when the command said nothing, so the one case where something happened never reads as "nothing happened".
static clientOnly(string $name): self/$name runs only where there is a screen; nothing happened here.
static refused(string $reason): selfThe command was not run, for $reason — a turn holds the session, say. No rows and no wire code: the reason is the answer.
withRows(Message ...$rows): selfA copy with $rows appended after this result's own.
withEffect(CommandEffect $effect): self
holdingTurn(): selfA copy that leaves a running turn running: /workflow pause|status typed while the run they control holds the session. Every other command runs idle, where releasing the turn changes nothing.
isRefused(): boolWhether the command did not run (self::refused() or self::clientOnly()).
isClientOnly(): boolWhether the command did not run here at all (self::clientOnly()).
effect(CommandEffectKind $kind): ?CommandEffectThe first effect of $kind, or null.
toArray(): arrayThe wire shape: the rows as {role, content, uiOnly} and the effect kinds, or the error.

SessionAdmission trait

SessionClientTools trait

Part of the CWPD-14 split of SessionHost.php (lane G4-H, OD-30 guard-first).

MethodSummary
registerClientTools(string $clientKey, array $specs): stringC-TOOL-6.h: host $specs as this client's tools for the session's NEXT turns, replacing whatever $clientKey held before. Returns the registration id every later answer for these tools must carry. Throws with a one-word verdict when the batch is not shippable (ClientToolRegistry::register()); who may call this at all — a connection holding Write scope, behind server.clientTools — is the protocol step's door (6.i), not this substrate's.
forgetClientTools(string $clientKey): voidC-TOOL-6.h: drop $clientKey's registrations (its connection closed — the ruling that kills a client's tools with it) and settle its open calls as errors, so a child blocked on one of them learns the truth instead of waiting out its deadline.
resolveClientCall(string $callId, string $registrationId, string $content, bool $isError): boolC-TOOL-6.h: answer the open client call $callId — first answer wins (the same law answer() keeps for questions). An id not open, a call already settled another way, and an answer carrying a registration id other than the one that opened the call all read the same from here: false. A client re-registered between the call and the answer is exactly the case that id exists to refuse.
onClientCall(?\Closure $hook): voidC-TOOL-6.h: bind (or pass null to clear) the listener that hears each freshly opened client call with the client and registration that must answer it — the handle the serve relay (6.i) forwards on.

LspClient final class

LSP Client that wraps LspConnection with caching, diagnostics tracking, multi-language server support, and graceful fallback to grep when LSP is unavailable.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly LspConnectionInterface $connection, private readonly LspCacheInterface $cache, string $language = 'php')$language is the key the injected connection is registered under. It defaults to php because that is what every caller before step 3.F meant; LspLauncher passes the configured server's own key.
addServer(string $language, LspConnectionInterface $connection, LspCacheInterface $cache): voidRegister an additional language server.
mapExtensions(string $language, array $extensions): voidRoute files ending in any of $extensions to $language's server.
languageFor(string $path): ?stringThe registered language whose server owns $path, or null when none does.
disconnectAll(): voidSpeak the shutdown protocol to every server and forget them. In a process that did not start a server this only closes its own copies of the pipes — LspConnection::disconnect() keeps the shared server running for the process that owns it.
use(string $language): selfSwitch the active language server context.
language(): ?string
servers(): arrayAll registered language identifiers.
pumpStderr(): voidE690: forward the between-exchanges stderr drain to every registered connection — the dispatch-entry mirror of \SugarCraft\Code\MCP\McpClient::pumpStderr().
isConnected(?string $language = null): boolWhether a server is registered and connected for the given language.
definitions(string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): arraytextDocument/definition — go-to-definition.
definitionsFor(string $language, string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): arrayDefinitions using a specific language server.
references(string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): arraytextDocument/references — find all references.
referencesFor(string $language, string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): arrayReferences using a specific language server.
hover(string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): ?arraytextDocument/hover — hover information.
hoverFor(string $language, string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0): ?arrayHover using a specific language server.
symbols(string $uri): arraytextDocument/documentSymbol — list symbols in a document.
symbolsFor(string $language, string $uri): arraySymbols using a specific language server.
codeActions(string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0, array $context = []): arraytextDocument/codeAction — get code actions (quick fixes, refactorings, etc.).
codeActionsFor(string $language, string $uri, int $line = 0, int $col = 0, array $context = []): arrayCode actions using a specific language server.
diagnostics(string $uri): arrayReturn cached diagnostics for a URI.
handlePublishDiagnostics(string $uri, array $diagnostics): voidHandle an incoming publishDiagnostics notification from a server.
hasDiagnostics(string $uri): boolWhether ANY diagnostics list — possibly an empty one — has been delivered for $uri. The difference between "the server said this file is clean" and "the server never said anything" is exactly this bit.
freshDiagnostics(string $language, string $path, float $waitSeconds = 5.0): ?arrayHave $language's server re-check the file at $path as it is on disk now, and wait up to $waitSeconds for its verdict (step 3.F; opencode waits 5 s for a document's diagnostics, DIAGNOSTICS_DOCUMENT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS).
outline(string $path): arrayThe symbols declared in the file at $path as a flat, line-ordered outline (line 1-based, depth 0 for top level), for the Read tool's outline of a large file (step 3.F, Zed's read_file outline).
static regexOutline(string $path): arrayoutline() with no server to ask: the declarations declarationsIn() finds, as outline rows.
static declarationsIn(string $path): arrayEvery declaration the one-line regex finds in the file at $path, as SymbolInformation[] — the degraded outline outline() falls back to. Empty for a file that cannot be read.
static uriFor(string $path): stringThe file:// URI for an absolute local path, percent-encoded per segment — the encoding uriToPath() decodes, so the two round-trip; see \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\BuiltIn\LspTool for why the encoding is not optional.
clearFile(string $uri): voidEvict all cached entries for a file, on EVERY registered server.
clearAll(): voidEvict all cached entries across all servers.

LspExchangeLock final class

Cross-process mutual exclusion for one LspConnection, plus the state that must outlive whichever process held it last.

MethodSummary
static new(string $label, ?string $dir = null): selfCreate the lock for a connection the CURRENT process owns, after sweeping the sets dead owners left in the same directory.
static create(string $label, ?string $dir = null): selfFormer name of new(), kept so callers that still use it keep working; the repo's factory rule names the default root ::new(), as the sugar-mcp-client twin \SugarCraft\McpClient\ExchangeLock::new() now does.
static sweepStale(?string $dir = null): intRemove the lock sets in $dir whose owner process no longer exists.
acquire(?float $deadline, \Closure $serverAlive): boolWait for the exclusive lock. Polls LOCK_NB rather than blocking so the wait honours $deadline (microtime(true) seconds, null = none) and gives up the moment the server is gone.
release(): voidUnlock AND close. The handle lives only for the length of one exchange: a descriptor kept open between exchanges would be inherited by every process this one later spawns (a Bash tool, a setsid'd grandchild), and a flock is only released when the LAST descriptor on its description closes — so a holder SIGKILLed mid-exchange would leave the lock held for as long as any such grandchild lived.
load(): LspExchangeStateThe state the previous holder left. Also safe WITHOUT the lock (a predicate reading only the LspExchangeState::$broken latch), because stores are atomic renames: an unlocked reader sees one whole state or another.
store(LspExchangeState $state): boolReplace the shared state.
storeFrame(string $frame): boolRecord the bytes of the frame about to be written (see LspExchangeState).
loadFrame(): string
appendNote(string $method, ?array $params): ?intJournal one server notification and return its sequence number.
notesAfter(int $seen): arrayJournal entries newer than $seen, oldest first.
close(): voidClose THIS process' handle; the files and every other process' handle stay.
destroy(): voidClose, and — in the owner only — remove every file.

HttpMcpServer final class

Client half of the MCP **Streamable HTTP** transport: one endpoint URL, every client message a POST, the reply either a JSON body or a text/event-stream whose data: frames carry it.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $name, private string $url, private array $headers, private Client $httpClient, private readonly ?McpAuthStore $authStore = null, ?\Closure $pidProvider = null, private readonly float $toolTimeoutSeconds = self::DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, private readonly bool $eventStream = false, ?\Closure $onServerMessage = null, private readonly ?\Closure $connector = null)
endpoint(): stringThe endpoint this server was configured with (ISS-042: the auth notice must print the URL mcp auth login keys the store on).
start(): void
stop(): voidEnd the session. A server that issued an Mcp-Session-Id is told so with an HTTP DELETE carrying it (the spec's explicit termination); that is best-effort — a 405 (server does not allow client-side termination), a network error or a dead host must not fail a shutdown. A server that issued no session id has nothing to tear down and gets no request at all.
isUp(): boolE698: for an HTTP server, "up" IS $initialized — the handshake completed and the tool list was cached, and stop() has not ended the session since. There is no process to lose and no persistent connection to drop; each call is its own request, so this answers "did this launch ever talk to it", not "is it answering right now" (that question would cost a wire exchange, which a readout must not).
listTools(): array
callTool(string $toolName, array $args): array
callToolAnsweringRequests(string $toolName, array $args, ?\Closure $onWait = null, ?McpServerRequests $serverRequests = null): arrayC-MCP-3.c (AnswersServerRequests): the same call with an exchange-scoped answerer — server requests inside this call's reply stream (and anything drained off the inbound GET at exchange start) route through $serverRequests instead of the spawn-time desk, and notifications/progress rides $onWait. Unlike the stdio seam there is no deadline pause: the http reply is read after the body arrived, and the answer POST is its own bounded request — the call's own ceiling already covers the walk it happens inside.
pumpStream(): voidBounded drain of the inbound GET: answer whatever the server pushed since the last read, then go. Never reconnects (this transport's calls are self-contained POSTs — see the class note); a stream that ends or breaks closes the channel and the session runs on, buffered. The fork law: only the opener reads, and only the opener closes.
listResources(): arrayMCP-1 wire half. Same gates as the tools/list walk, same per-call ceiling as callTool (toolOptions() — E646 keeps the bound per-request, never blanket), on the session-recovering request() leg because these calls arrive long after the handshake, when the session may have expired.
readResource(string $uri): array
listPrompts(): arrayMCP-2 wire half: the prompts roster rides the identical walk and gates as the resources roster — the capability is the same paginated shape under different member names.
prompt(string $name, array $arguments = []): array
getPrompt(string $name, array $arguments = []): arrayBC forwarder for the pre-rename accessor name.

McpBackgroundCalls final class

The registry behind C-MCP-3.d: a bridged/dispatched MCP call that outlives the background threshold keeps running in a forked child, and its eventual answer lands here as a payload file this user's home owns alone.

MethodSummary
static armed(float $afterSeconds, bool $latchedNonInteractive, bool $turnDriven, bool $serverRequestChannelsBound): boolWhether an armed MCP tool may take the background path at all: the call is one the TURN is waiting on (a heartbeat channel is present) and it has NOT been handed the turn's ask channel or live tail, a live threshold, a run that is not the closed -p latch, the pcntl functions this design forks with, and a home the registry can be kept in. Every failed door means the inline call — the exact behavior from before this feature, byte-identical, including on Windows and every pcntl-less fallback, because backgrounding is an OPT-IN of the turn wiring and a machine that cannot fork simply never gets the fast path replaced.
static directory(): ?stringThe registry directory for the CURRENT HOME, resolved at every use — no memo, because a HOME-sandboxed test and the real launch must not share a registry through a cached path, and a mid-process home move is exactly how the suite isolates. Null when no private home can be determined, which switches armed() off.
static await(\Closure $exchange, float $afterSeconds, ?\Closure $heartbeat, string $server, string $tool, string $callId): arrayRun $exchange in a forked child and wait for its published result, releasing the caller at $afterSeconds with a background outcome while the child keeps running.
static hasFinished(): boolWhether any finished job is waiting in the registry right now — a cheap existence probe, claiming NOTHING: the per-step inbox probe runs on every sequential tool call, and a probe that consumed would deliver the job into the void.
static takeFinished(): arrayClaim every finished job this process can, oldest first, and return the frames their children published. A claim is the rename every later scanner must lose to be excluded, so one row per job however many turns drain at once; the unlink after the read is what makes a dead claimer's stale marker an obvious GC target on the next scan instead of a permanent silence.
static pendingChildren(): arrayChildren this process forked whose exit has not been collected yet. Pinned by the reaping tests: the fast path must hand this array back EMPTY, and a backgrounded job must appear in it until the registry scan reaps it.
static resetPendingChildrenForTesting(): voidTest seam: forget this process's roster (a sandboxed run never forked into it).

McpClient final class

MethodSummary
__construct(private string $configPath, ?Client $httpClient = null, ?AgentPreset $agentPreset = null, bool $unrestricted = false, array $denyPatterns = [], private readonly ?McpAuthStore $authStore = null, private readonly ?\Closure $admit = null, private readonly string $userConfigPath = '')
setAgentPreset(?AgentPreset $agentPreset): voidSet (or clear) the preset of the agent driving this client, so that subsequent listTools()/callTool()/callToolByName() calls are routed through McpRouter::resolveAllowedTools() against the preset's mcpServers allowlist rather than exposing every configured server unconditionally.
forAgentPreset(AgentPreset $agentPreset): selfC-AGT-3: a copy of this client bound to $agentPreset — the production caller setAgentPreset() always lacked. The launch client is shared by every roster (TaskTool's engine and the worker-pool grants both run through the one instance), so scoping one agent could never mutate it in place; instead each preset gets its own handle. Started servers travel BY HANDLE: the shallow clone shares the same McpServer objects (stdio children are never duplicated, and a scoped run talks to the same live server the main agent does), the bookkeeping arrays copy with it, and the router is rebuilt per call (router() caches nothing), so the clone carries no stale routing state. A clone never starts servers — $admit and the config paths stay bound to the original for exactly that reason. The preset branch takes precedence over the launch client's unrestricted flag: routing checks agentPreset first in listTools()/callTool().
configEntries(): arrayMCP-7: the config entries this client read during startServers(), keyed by server name, project tier winning each shared name (the shadow-safe record point is inside startServer()). Metadata only — the lazy-shape decision's eager lookup.
setDenyPatterns(array $denyPatterns): voidSet the global wildcard deny-pattern map (server-name pattern => "deny") forwarded to McpRouter on every routed call, alongside the active agent preset's allowlist, and applied by the unrestricted arm and by startServers() too.
setSandbox(?SandboxBackend $jail, ?string $refusal, string $writableRoot): voidInstall the mcp sandboxScope jail for stdio servers (C-TOOL-4.e).
disableForSession(string $server): voidC-MCP-4.b: refuse CALLS to $server for the rest of this process unless $server was already refused by a launch deny pattern or the active preset — this adds a refusal, it never rescues one. The toggle is exact by name (never a glob), takes effect through isServerAllowed()/router() from the next check onward, and is inherited at clone time by preset handles forked after it (forAgentPreset()). Idempotent.
enableForSession(string $server): voidC-MCP-4.b: undo disableForSession() in this process. Only ever lifts a session refusal — a name still matched by a launch deny pattern stays denied, because the settings map is operator-authored and frozen at launch; telling /mcp enable it had rescued such a server would be the fabrication. Idempotent.
sessionDisabledServers(): arrayC-MCP-4.b: the session refusals currently armed, exact server names.
startServers(): voidLoad and start MCP servers from config.
beginStartup(): voidLaunch every configured server WITHOUT waiting for any of them to come up, then return. Each stdio handshake is left suspended on its wait beat; tick() advances them, and startupStates() reports where each one stands. A caller that must not stall on a cold npx calls this and pumps tick() from its event loop; a server that is still starting simply contributes no tools yet.
startAllBlocking(): voidBlock until no launched server is still starting, pumping tick() as it waits. The synchronous face of the startup state machine, for callers that want the finished server set in hand, as before.
tick(): voidAdvance every in-flight handshake that can make progress, and return at once. Meant to be called periodically from the event loop.
startupStates(): arrayThe startup state of every server launched or refused in the current start cycle: starting, ready, failed or auth-required. Read-only and side-effect free, for the /mcp panel. Servers the config disabled, denied or the admission check refused have no row here; they keep their own reports.
refusedServers(): arrayThe entries the admission check refused in the last startServers() run.
deniedServers(): arrayThe entries the last startServers() run did not start because their name matches a deny pattern (E696). Not reported as a failure: the operator's own setting declined them.
strippedSecretEnv(): arrayThe inherited credential-shaped variables each stdio server was started WITHOUT in the last startServers() run, keyed by server name; servers that lost nothing are absent. Names only, never values. The launch notice reads this: a server needing one declares it in its env block ("GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITHUB_TOKEN}") or the operator lists it in secretEnvAllowlist.
strippedSecretEnvNotice(): stringThe one-sentence launch notice for strippedSecretEnv(), or the empty string when no server lost anything.
sandboxOptOutNotice(): stringNames the stdio servers whose "sandbox": false opt-out was IGNORED because the entry did not come from the user settings file (C-TOOL-4.e), or the empty string when none was. A project-tier .mcp.json must not be able to opt its own server out of the user's jail; the server jails as scoped and the user learns why.
authRequired(): arrayThe http entries the last startServers() run refused for credentials, name => [endpoint URL, HTTP status] (ISS-042). Empty unless one answered 401/403 during its handshake.
authRequiredNotice(): stringThe one-sentence launch notice for authRequired(), or the empty string when nothing was refused. The row's whole product is the command that fixes it — candy-code mcp auth login <server-url> — spelled in the shell form docs/MCP.md documents (the in-chat /mcp auth login only prints guidance; the browser leg cannot run inside the TUI). The URL, not the .mcp.json name, is what the store keys on, so the URL is what the printed argument must be.
stopServers(): voidStop all MCP servers.
pumpStderr(): voidPump every STARTED stdio server's stderr once, between exchanges.
startedSnapshot(): arrayE698: a LIVENESS READOUT of the servers this client has STARTED, with zero side effects — no exchange, no proc_open(), no wire traffic.
listTools(): arrayList available tools, restricted to what the current agent preset (if any) is allowed to see per McpRouter::resolveAllowedTools(). With no preset attached, returns nothing unless $unrestricted was explicitly set at construction time.
callTool(string $serverName, string $toolName, array $args, ?\Closure $onWait = null, ?McpServerRequests $serverRequests = null): arrayCall a tool on a specific server. Rejected when the current agent preset's mcpServers allowlist does not cover $serverName, so a caller cannot bypass listTools() filtering by naming a denied server directly. With no preset attached, rejected unconditionally unless $unrestricted was explicitly set at construction time.
callToolByName(string $toolName, array $args): arrayCall a tool by name across all servers the current agent preset is allowed to see (first match). Tools belonging to servers outside the preset's allowlist are invisible here, not merely unlisted.
listResources(): arrayMCP-1 wire half: every allowed provider server's CURRENT resource roster, keyed by server name (resources are addressed by URI, so the server that owns one must travel with it — unlike the flat tool merge).
readResource(string $serverName, string $uri): arrayRead one resource from one server. Mirrors callTool's refusal ladder exactly — unknown server, server outside the current gates (a caller cannot bypass listResources() by naming a denied server directly), and then the capability question — before any exchange is entered.
listPrompts(): arrayMCP-2 wire half: every allowed provider server's CURRENT prompt roster, keyed by server name. Gate parity exactly as documented on listResources() — same predicate, same skip rules, same fail-closed posture, E677 pump at the dispatch caller.
prompt(string $serverName, string $name, array $arguments = []): arrayFetch one prompt from one server, call shape only. Mirrors readResource()'s refusal ladder verbatim — unknown server, server outside the current gates, then the capability question — before any exchange is entered.
getPrompt(string $serverName, string $name, array $arguments = []): arrayBC forwarder for the pre-rename accessor name.
primeSurfaceRosters(): voidThe launch-time surface pass: bounded resource ROWS and prompt ROWS for every allowed provider server, gathered once and remembered (the $surfaceRosters contract — display and materialization only, never enforcement). Each server is asked under the same isServerAllowed() predicate the strict listResources() and listPrompts() apply, and each server's refusal — no capability, dead pipe, outlived bound — costs only that server's entry: a roster that erased every other server because one answered -32601 would make the whole feature hostage to the least compliant config.
promptsRoster(): arrayThe launch-frozen prompt rows the surface layer materializes into commands (\SugarCraft\Code\Commands\McpPromptCommands). Data, not enforcement — the strict per-call listPrompts() round trip remains the live answer and keeps its throw-on-refusal gates.
resourcesRoster(): arrayThe launch-frozen resource rows the mcp.resources wire method answers (\SugarCraft\Code\Protocol\Methods\McpMethods) — the same one bounded snapshot the panel counts, per allowed provider server that answered. Data, not enforcement, exactly as promptsRoster(): the strict per-call listResources() remains the live gate.
static toolTimeout(mixed $raw): ?floatA bounded entry's toolTimeout as written, or null for "nothing usable": only a positive, finite JSON number is honoured. Both bounded transports read it (stdio since cl-4, http since ISS-042), and null resolves to each server's own DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in its constructor (see buildServer()). The parser reports what the config SAYS; the ceiling policy lives on the servers, one place each.

SseLineParser final class

The SSE wire format as one resumable parser: bytes in through a reader closure, whole events out, and the JSON-RPC reply to a given request id found by replyTo().

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly ?\Closure $read = null)
socketHandle()The socket behind a stream-mode parser, or null once detached.
detachSocket()Hand the socket to the caller and forget it — the transport then owns the close-vs-retain decision (a forked child never closes the handle its parent opened; see the retain law on SseMcpServer).
beginWait(float $seconds, string $label): voidOpen a bounded wait: every read until endWait() carries this deadline and names this label in its timeout refusal. The flood bound restarts per wait, as it did on the transport this reader moved from.
endWait(): void
static parseUrl(string $url, string $name, string $what): arrayParse and validate an http(s) URL into connectable parts. Lifted from the legacy transport verbatim; the transport's origin-law merges call it too, so the refusal wording exists in exactly one place.
static composeUrl(array $parts): stringThe reverse half of the origin merge: parts back into an absolute URL.
nextEvent(): ?arrayThe next complete SSE event: an event ends at its blank line, and one left unterminated by end-of-stream is still examined — a server that closes right after its last data line has said what it meant to.
replyTo(int|string $id, ?\Closure $onFrame = null): ?arrayRead events until the JSON-RPC response to request $id. Only message events (the default type) carry JSON-RPC; the stream may interleave server notifications and server-to-client requests before the response, and those are skipped. A batch inside one event is matched entry-wise.
static matchReply(array $messages, int|string $id): ?arrayThe response to $id among JSON-RPC messages: an entry with our id and a result or error, and no method (a server-to-client request may reuse an id value from its own sequence). Ids compare as STRINGS — a forked process mints pid-tagged string ids while the owner mints integers, and a server that echoes the number back must still match.
readStreamChunk(): stringThe reader the framing loop pulls through: decoded SSE bytes, '' at end of stream, every wait bounded by $waitDeadlineAt. Public only for the @internal deadline seam the transport re-exports.
static connectStream(string $scheme, string $host, int $port, float $timeoutSeconds)The default connector. TLS via php streams with peer verification and SNI on — no option here is a relaxation of what Guzzle's curl handler did by default; the transport moved, the trust posture did not. (Proxy configuration is honoured by neither the moved GET nor any prior sse path; documented in docs/MCP.md.)

SseMcpServer final class

Client half of the MCP **legacy HTTP+SSE transport** (protocol revision 2024-11-05): the client opens ONE long-lived GET with Accept: text/event-stream, the server's first act on it is an endpoint event naming the URI that requests are POSTed to, and every JSON-RPC reply — including the reply to the POST that carried the request — arrives on the GET stream, matched by id. The POST response itself carries only a status: delivery, not an answer.

The library keeps them private and offers no readiness query, so they are read through a scoped closure rather than by widening its API from this side. stderr counts as output because a child blocked on a full stderr pipe never answers.
