callTool(string $toolName, array $args, ?\Closure $onWait = null): arrayBOUNDED BY DEFAULT, like start()'s handshake — see the library's callTool(). Every call carries the entry's toolTimeout or DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (the constructor resolves both); at the deadline the library sends notifications/cancelled, raises the named timeout error, and the bridge turns it into an error payload for the model — a wedged server costs one call, never the session. $onWait — the library's wait beat (item 0.4-b) — still keeps a long call visibly alive until that deadline.
callToolAnsweringRequests(string $toolName, array $args, ?\Closure $onWait = null, ?McpServerRequests $serverRequests = null): arrayC-MCP-3 (AnswersServerRequests): the same bounded call, with an exchange-scoped answerer for whatever the server asks mid-call. The library pauses this call's deadline while the answerer runs, so an elicitation held open for a human does not eat the toolTimeout budget — but it holds the connection's exchange lock meanwhile, and further calls to THIS server queue behind the answer (one pipe, one conversation; the queue is bounded per waiter by its own timeout).
toolTimeoutSeconds(): floatThe resolved per-call bound in seconds — never null since cl-4 FIX-C.
listResources(): arrayMCP-1 wire half. The library transport already exposes a public request() ("resources/list … one call away" in its doc-block) — this method adds only what the adapter owns on top of it: the per-call ceiling (providerDeadline(), never disableable, exactly the callTool policy) and the cursor-walk/error gates that keep a partial or refused roster from masquerading as a whole one.

listPrompts(): arrayMCP-2 wire half. Same machinery as the resources roster — the prompts capability is the same paginated list shape under different member names, and the same gates therefore apply verbatim.

Infotext final class

Byte-compatible codec for the A1111 'parameters' infotext block — the text stable-diffusion-webui writes into PNG metadata and shows in its UI.

MethodSummary
static isSecretKey(string $label): boolIs a server-sourced label credential-shaped? The modelled vocabulary wins over the pattern: 'Token merging ratio' is upstream's own field, not a secret, so canonical labels always answer false.
static containsSecretKey(string $text): boolDoes a raw infotext chunk carry at least one secret-shaped pair? Parameter-anchor lines are checked pair-by-pair (so canonical labels cannot trigger it); any other line is judged on its text before the first colon — prompt prose after a colon is prose, while a stray label: value line (or a prompt line that opens like one) forfeits the chunk's verbatim replay. That over-forfeit is the honest side of the trade: the scrubbed emit() path keeps every legitimate byte.
static emit(GenerationParams|MediaRequest $params, array $extra = [], ?string $prompt = null): stringRender the full A1111 parameters text for a params/request object.
static parse(string $text, bool $stripComments = true): arrayParse A1111 parameters text into a flat map: the reserved 'prompt' / 'negative prompt' keys plus one entry per parameter pair, keyed by CANONICAL label (LEGACY spellings folded onto it), values un-quoted strings.
static applyTo(MediaRequest $request, array $parsed, bool $onlyUnset = true): MediaRequestLoad a parsed infotext map onto a MediaRequest through its withers.

PNG container codec for the A1111 infotext round-trip — no SD server, no library, pure byte work over the chunk framing of ISO/IEC 15948.

static isPng(string $bytes): boolMagic sniff: eight fixed signature bytes, nothing more.

SugarCraft\Code\Media\Capability

CapabilityDiscoverer final readonly class

Resolves "what can this endpoint do" without ever being the reason crush fails to start (plan W1.2).

MethodSummary
forProvider(array $providerConfig, ?SdTransport $transport = null): ?MediaCapability
fromConfig(array $providerConfig): ?MediaCapabilityPure config-authority read, no transport: mediaKinds (non-empty list of image|video) is what switches a provider from "silent" to "declared". Returns null when the config declares nothing media-related.
probe(SdTransport $transport): ?MediaCapabilityThe bounded GET ladder. Order is deliberate: /sdapi/v1/cmd-flags is unmistakably A1111; /object_info unmistakably ComfyUI; /model_info before /v1/models because SGLang-Diffusion serves BOTH (W0.1 probe) and the plain OpenAI door would otherwise shadow it. First affirmative match wins; every failure mode answers null. Every rung demands a decoded JSON ARRAY (a bare true/"ok"/42 body is not a dialect fingerprint), so a captive portal or catch-all 200 falls through the whole ladder.
diagnose(array $providerConfig, ?SdTransport $transport): arrayPer-route verdicts, consumed by the doctor tool's media line (\SugarCraft\Code\Tools\BuiltIn\Doctor; honest diagnosis without a bespoke error model): 'ok' | 'absent' | 'error' | 'not-probed', plus 'config' => 'declared' | 'none'. Same fail-open law: never throws.

Pure: never dials, never throws.

Schema-shaped unknowns (model, true_cfg_scale, task_type, …) ride verbatim — MediaRequest's tolerated-extra path is declared intent — but a mapped field always wins over an identically-named unknown, and the sdapi output-routing/binary knobs drop (they are not scalars a form field could carry, or they were mapped away by name).

recentView(int $maxEntries = self::VIEW_MAX_ENTRIES, int $maxBytes = self::VIEW_MAX_BYTES): arrayThe model-facing read view (C-CTX-3.d): at most the newest $maxEntries compaction entries, and no more than $maxBytes of record/state text in TOTAL, oldest-first. The dream pass reads full-fidelity entries; a recall answer handed to the model must cost a bounded number of prompt bytes, so when the budget runs out the entry it lands on is clipped to equal shares (never to noise: a share below VIEW_MIN_CLIP_BYTES drops the text instead), and older entries past the budget are left on disk. Entries are already redacted at append; this view only reads.
scanFrom(int $offset = 0): arrayRead the journal from a byte offset rather than from its start (ISS-071). The offset is a consumed-until cursor: everything before it has been folded, only the tail still describes work. ends[k] is the absolute byte just past entries[k]'s newline — the offset a later read resumes from — so a consumer that takes a prefix of the entries learns exactly how far consumption reached. aligned is false when $offset cannot describe a position in this file (past its end, or resting mid-line); the caller then resyncs from zero. A trailing line without its newline is a half finished append: it is never returned, and the cursor stays before it.
trimBefore(int $offset): boolDrop the journal's first $offset bytes — the entries a consumer has provably folded — keeping any unread tail (ISS-071). Without this the journal grows for the life of the project and every fold re-reads all history. Returns false when the trim could not be trusted (the file shrank or was replaced under the lock, a lock or write failure); the caller then keeps its byte cursor and loses nothing but space.

buildFactory(callable $factoryFactory): EventSinkFactoryTHE gate for the serve path's per-session factory, mirroring buildSink() one-for-one: a dark config answers EventSinkFactory::dark() without the factory builder ever running (so no HTTP client is constructed and no shutdown hook is registered), and a builder that declines still lands on the dark factory. Callers ask this method, never a second endpoint read.
static sinkFactoryFromEnvironment(): EventSinkFactoryEnvironment-reading shim for buildFactory(): the one call shape Bootstrap's workspace arm uses, so the factory path shares the sink path's single copy of the dark branch.

OtelSink final class

Ungrouped OTLP/HTTP exporter: one POST per render pass, each pass carrying every span it closed in a single body.

MethodSummary
static withTransport(callable $transport, ?OtlpEncoder $encoder = null): self
static withTransports(callable $transport, ?callable $asyncTransport, ?OtlpEncoder $encoder = null): selfBoth legs at once — the shape fromConfig() builds and the tests dial against loopback collectors.
static fromConfig(OtelConfig $config, \GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface $client): self
consume(object $event): void
flush(): void
encodeAll(array $stampedEvents): arrayPure encode arm: renders every span the batch closes, touching no transport. Order-preserving, and since OBS-1-P2 the whole batch's closed spans travel together in ONE body, each carrying the consume-time instant its events were stamped with (C-SES-4.a) — a bare consume() hands one pair with a null stamp, where observe and encode coincide anyway.
encodeDrained(): ?stringRenders every still-open span (shutdown arm) without posting it.
post(string $jsonBody): voidOne bounded POST. Throws when the endpoint refuses the body so the batch layer can carry it; direct users swallow via consume/flush.
hasAsyncTransport(): boolWhether the async leg (C-SES-4.b) was built — the batch layer's switch.
postAsync(string $jsonBody): \React\Promise\PromiseInterfaceHand one encoded body to the async leg without waiting for it. The returned promise fulfils with bool accepted and rejects on transport errors; either way the caller never blocks — this is the arm that takes the POST off the TUI's update() path. A transport that throws SYNCHRONOUSLY (a malformed URL rejects only on connect, but a closure seam can) is folded into a rejected promise so the one contract holds.

OtlpEncoder final class

Hand-rolled OTLP/HTTP-JSON encoding of the typed event DTOs.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly array $resourceAttributes = [])
encode(object $event, ?int $nowUnixNanos = null): ?arrayAbsorbs one event. Returns an OTLP export request body when this call closed a span, null otherwise (event opened/annotated/dropped).
encodeMany(array $stampedEvents): arrayOBS-1-P2 (the one-body half): absorbs a whole batch of consume-time- stamped events and returns EVERY span the batch closed, raw and in arrival order. The caller wraps them in a single exportBody(), so one batch leaves in one POST instead of one POST per closed span. An empty list means the batch closed nothing (openings and annotations only).
drainOpen(?int $nowUnixNanos = null): ?arrayRenders every still-open span (shutdown arm). Nothing arrives after the flush ordering guarantees, so an open span here is a turn whose settle report never came; ending it at its last observed instant is the honest, bounded choice.
evictedCount(): intHow many stale spans the cap has evicted (anomaly counter).
openSpanCount(): intHow many spans are currently open (test/diagnostic surface).
exportBody(array $spans): arrayWraps rendered spans into the OTLP request body this encoder's resource attributes describe. Public since C-SES-4.a: the batch arm hands encodeMany()'s spans here ONCE per batch, which is what makes one batch equal one POST.

ReadOnlyCommands final class

THE one list of shell commands that provably change nothing, and the one judgement of whether a whole Bash line is made of them. Two policies read it:

Does NOT read the setting — autoAllowEnabled() is the caller's to consult.
static autoAllowEnabled(): boolWhether the read-only auto-allow is on (SETTING, default on). The user tier decides; a trusted project may switch it OFF and never back on: the merged value (project included) AND the value without the project tier must both be true.
static compoundIsCovered(ShellWords $parsed, array $item, ?string $projectRoot, bool $readOnlyCovers, \Closure $covers): boolPER-PART COVERAGE of one compound item — a for / while read loop or an if — for SessionPermissionMemo::coversBySegments() (user decision 2026-10-11): the loop is ONE part, covered when its header qualifies (the same rules as the read-only judgement: no substitution, the list's variables in scope, no re-bound name) and EVERY command of its body is covered on its own — read-only in the loop's scope (when $readOnlyCovers), or by $covers, a remembered grant matched against that command's own source text. A cd inside one is never covered by a grant: it moves every later iteration.

The user's SAVED permission rules — the permissionRules array in the user-tier config, the half of the "always" answer that outlives the session. p at a prompt appends one allow-rule here (PermissionPrompt::persistRules() delegates to self::append()); /permissions saved lists them and /permissions forget takes one out (C-SEC-6.a, the step that made this list readable and reversible from the transcript instead of only by hand-editing config).

Returns the removed entries — possibly several for a pattern, since duplicates a hand-edit made all go — and an empty list for no match, which wrote nothing.

static new(): self
static fromGrants(array $grants): selfThe memo held in a session's grant map — see the class docblock for the key spaces. Keys that are not this class's, and patterns the rule grammar refuses, are skipped.

Null for a tool with no subject argument, whose only scope is the tool.
entries(): arrayEvery grant, in the order given, as the user reads it in /permissions: a pattern as written (Bash(git status *) — the bare Bash(git status) granted beside it is the same grant and is not listed twice), an exact call as Tool: <subject> (or its arguments as JSON).
without(int $index): ?selfThis memo without its $index-th entries() row (1-based), or null when there is no such row. A listed Tool(p *) takes its bare Tool(p) with it.
isEmpty(): bool
patterns(): array

allows(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): boolDoes a grant in this memo answer an ask about this call?
static coversBySegments(array $rules, ToolCall $call, ?string $projectRoot, bool $readOnlyCovers): boolPER-PART COVERAGE (user decision 2026-10-11): does a Bash line split — fail closed — into simple commands joined only by |, && and ||, EVERY ONE of which is covered on its own by one of $rules (a remembered segment grant such as Bash(git log *)) or, with $readOnlyCovers, is a read-only command (ReadOnlyCommands)?
static scopeOf(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): stringWhat an "always" on this call would remember, as the user reads it on the modal's a row: the broadest pattern granted (Bash(git status *) — the bare Bash(git status) beside it only covers the same command with no arguments; Bash(sed * | sort * | uniq *) for a pipeline), or, when no pattern fits, this exact command / this exact call. A Bash line gets the exact form when it is a launcher, a destructive command, a writing redirection or a substitution — see the class docblock. Computed on the grantArguments(), so a dropped leading cd shows: cd /repo && git status reads Bash(git status *).
static exactScopeOf(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): stringHow an EXACT-call grant on this call reads: this exact call, this exact command, or — when grantArguments() dropped a leading in-project cd — this exact command without the leading cd, so the user can see the remembered call is the remainder.
static grantArguments(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot): arrayThe arguments a grant is remembered under and checked against: $arguments with a shell-subject tool's (Bash or PtyRun) leading in-project cd <dir> && removed (LeadingCd::strip()), or $arguments unchanged — any other tool, no root, or a prefix that does not qualify. THE one normaliser every grant path shares: patternsFor() and callKey() (and so withGrant(), allows(), Chat's exact-call key and \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\ChildChannel's per-turn memo) and PermissionGate's session-rule check. Applied ONCE: a remainder that itself opens with a cd is a chain, judged as written.
static identityArguments(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): arrayThe arguments that make two calls the SAME call for an exact-call grant: all of them, minus the tool's ANNOTATION_ARGUMENTS. With the root in hand this is computed on the grantArguments(), so a leading in-project cd is not part of the identity either.
static patternsFor(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): arrayThe PermissionRule patterns an "always" on this call grants, or an empty list when no pattern fits and the exact call is remembered instead. See the class docblock's table; judged on the grantArguments().
static callKey(string $tool, array $arguments, ?string $projectRoot = null): ?stringThe exact-call identity: tool name plus canonical JSON of the identityArguments(), so neither key order nor the model's caption makes two calls different.

The compound-statement structure of a ShellWords line: which simple commands are the body of a for or while read loop, or the branches of an if, so a caller can judge a loop as ONE thing whose body must qualify (user decision 2026-10-11) instead of refusing every line that holds a reserved word.

static structuralIndices(array $items): arrayThe ShellWords command indices of $items that are pure syntax — done, fi, a for header, a lone do / then / else, a while's read — nested statements included.

Client final class

One connected client as the protocol sees it: its connection and Outbox, whether it has said server.hello, what it said there, what it may do, what it is looking at, and its request budget.

MethodSummary

An in-process client passes $deliver instead, and every event reaches it as the EventEnvelope itself, with nothing encoded (PL-5c).

viewing(): array
isForeground(string $sessionId): boolWhether $sessionId is in front of the user — the one subscription the soft watermark never downgrades to narration. A client that never said counts every session as in front.
narratesBackground(): boolWhether this client asked for its background subscriptions to be narrated.
wantsNarration(string $sessionId): boolWhether $sessionId should reach this client as narration because the client asked so (client.viewing with narrate) and it is not in front. The soft watermark's own downgrade is the feed's to add.
admit(): boolSpend one request from the budget (a token bucket: RATE_BURST at once, refilled at RATE_PER_SECOND); false when it is empty.
admitBytes(int $bytes): boolSpend $bytes from the byte meter (a token bucket: BYTE_BURST at rest, refilled at BYTE_RATE_PER_SECOND); false when the meter cannot cover the whole frame. The dispatcher consults it on every message BEFORE decoding (CWPD-1): an oversized flood is refused as wire, never parsed.
send(string $text): voidQueue a message that must arrive on a socket. An in-process client has no wire: use emit().

Dispatcher final class

The candy-code.v1 protocol (roadmap O-3b, Appendix O §6): the MessageHandler the WebSocket transport hands every message to.

MethodSummary
static new(ServerContext $context, ?MethodRegistry $methods = null, ?IdempotencyCache $idempotency = null): selfA dispatcher over $context answering every method of the v1 roster (methods()), or $methods when given.
static methods(): MethodRegistryThe v1 method roster, one class per namespace.
context(): ServerContext
registry(): MethodRegistry
start(): voidArm the host tick and the liveness tick, re-adopt the background sessions an earlier process left running, and arm their poll. Idempotent.
drain(float $seconds, \Closure $then, string $reason = 'server shutting down'): voidDrain before stopping (carried from W6 to O-3b; server.drainSeconds): from now on no turn or session is admitted (draining), every client is told the server is going and for how long (server.shutdown with graceSeconds), and $then runs once the turns in flight have settled — or when $seconds have passed, whichever is first. With nothing running, or $seconds at 0, $then runs now. Calling it again while a drain waits cuts the wait short. The turns still running when $then runs are the caller's to cancel.
isDraining(): boolWhether a drain is waiting on running turns.
stop(string $reason = 'server shutting down', float $graceSeconds = 0.0): voidTell every client the server is going (server.shutdown), then cancel the ticks and detach every feed. The sockets are the transport's to close.
onOpen(Connection $connection): void
outboxFor(Connection $connection): ?OutboxThe registered connection's Outbox; null once it has closed.
onMessage(Connection $connection, string $payload): void
onClose(Connection $connection, int $code): void
forgetCredential(?string $tokenId): voidA credential died (token.revoke, or a rotation when $tokenId is null): drop the answers its bucket held. Null forgets every bucket, the owner's included.
invoke(Client $client, string $method, array $params): mixedThe in-process door (PL-5c): runs $method with $params through every gate the wire runs for a request (the hello gate, the method and its scope, the published params schema, the viewer session pin, the idempotency cache) and returns the handler's answer as the wire carries it. The rate meters are not spent, because the caller is the host itself. A handler that answers with a promise gets a promise back, settled with that same answer or with the refusal the wire would send.
static wireAnswer(mixed $result): mixedA result as the in-process door hands it on: its value encoded under the wire's flags (so invalid UTF-8 is substituted, as JsonRpc::encode does), refused too_large when the frame the wire would send for it would pass the ceiling, then decoded back so a caller holds the values a wire client decodes. Nothing is framed here.

logError(\Throwable $e, string $prefix = 'internal error'): voidOne swallowed internal failure, rendered for the server log (ISS-057). Without a sink the line falls exactly as silent as an unlogged error does under logError().

version(): string

SessionFeed final class

One open session's events, fanned out to the clients subscribed to it (roadmap O-3b, Appendix O §6.4–§6.8).

MethodSummary
static attach(SessionHost $host, LoopInterface $loop, float $askTimeoutSeconds = 0.0, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?\Closure $onHeard = null, ?\Closure $log = null): selfA feed over $host, listening from now on.
host(): SessionHost

catchUp(Client $client): boolHand $client the reply streamed so far — its tail, at the byte offset it starts — now, unthrottled. Called when a pane comes to the front: the deltas that follow continue exactly where the tail ends.

Either way the questions still open ride along (pendingAsks), so a client that reconnects mid-question can answer it whatever its cursor. $snapshotLimit pages the reset snapshot to its newest rows (ISS-058); the meta it adds says how the client fetches the rest.

TrustAsks final class

WEB-3b / C-SEC-5.b: the project-trust prompts this server has put — one per pending grant target per untrusted-or-drifted root, for as long as the process lives.

MethodSummary
static discoverPending(string $root, \Closure $broadcast): voidMint the prompts the launch census says this root owes — every pending target from Bootstrap::pendingProjectTrust(), announced through $broadcast exactly once each. This is the one discovery loop both wire doors (the session.subscribe peek and the full context.sources measurement) call, so neither can fall behind the census.
static discover(string $root, TrustTarget $target, \Closure $broadcast): arrayThe prompt for ($root, $target), minting and announcing it on first sighting. The reason sentence is the target's own server.trust.ask.* row — every target has had one since the 5.a census, and the settings row is the one that says out loud what the grant widens (the project's settings layer is dropped until trusted).
static records(string $root): arrayEvery prompt this process has put about $root, minted or settled, in TrustTarget::cases() order — the answer surface restates the truth a measurement found (a session grant that expires with the process, a rejection that must not nag, a pin re-approval still open beside a granted .mcp.json), without minting anything new.
static settle(string $askId, string $decision, ?string $remember, string $sessionRoot, ?SettingsWriter $writer = null): arraySettle $askId — one record, never the root's whole shelf: each pending target keeps its own prompt open until it is answered (or its verdict changes at next launch). The record only ever moves from asked once; every later answer is the same refusal permission.respond gives a settled question, and a project-tier remember is the same refusal it gives a project-tier rule.
static resetForTesting(): voidTest seam: the process-global registry, as every static here owns one lifetime.

The native api.anthropic.com/v1/messages arm (ISS-023).

MethodSummary
__construct(private string $apiKey, private string $baseUrl = 'https://api.anthropic.com', private string $defaultModel = 'claude-sonnet-4-6', ?callable $http = null, ?callable $httpStream = null, private array $modelPrices = [], private bool $promptCache = true, private ?int $contextWindowOverride = null, private ?int $thinkingBudget = null, private ?string $serviceTier = null)
static new(array $config): self
name(): string
messagesEndpoint(?string $baseUrl = null): stringAbsolute Messages URL for a configured root: the root keeps its documented meaning (the bare API root, /v1-suffix tolerated), and /messages is appended here rather than being left to the client.
supportsStreaming(): bool
supportsFunctionCalling(): bool
supportsVision(): bool
supportsDocuments(): bool
supportsJsonSchema(): bool
supportsServerWebSearch(): boolC-TOOL-2.c: this IS the direct Messages wire — the only arm on which webSearchBackend=anthropic means anything. The search runs provider-side inside the same reply (Anthropic's web_search_20250305 server tool), so no client WebSearch call ever needs an endpoint; every other provider gets the refusal sentinel from SearchBackends instead. The setting is read at call-shape time, not built into the constructor, so a mid-session flip lands on the next request — the same law the tool constructor follows.
contextWindow(): int
complete(CompleteRequest $request): CompleteResponse
completeStream(CompleteRequest $request): \GeneratorStreams a turn through POST /v1/messages with stream: true.
embeddings(EmbeddingsRequest $request): EmbeddingsResponse
shapesEffortFor(string $model): bool
serviceTierFor(string $model): ?stringC-PRV-3.a: the Messages API's speed field is a documented family property, not a global one. Per the current Messages API reference, fast mode (higher output tokens per second, premium pricing) is live on claude-opus-5-5 and in research preview on claude-opus-5 and claude-opus-4-8; every other model is a server 400. The answer is family-gated through the same pricingFamily() normalisation the price tables use, so a dated id like claude-opus-4-8-20260115 reads its family row.
withServiceTier(?string $tier): staticC-PRV-3.a: positional clone mirroring self::withModel() — the same stale-$this discipline applies, so a rebuilt default transport re-gates the fast-mode legs against THIS object's tier and model.
costPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): ?floatC-PRV-3.a: fast mode bills a premium the model-keyed table cannot derive, so while this pair shapes the model the answer is null — the existing unpricedModel notice, never a guessed rate. A non-shaper model under an armed tier keeps its standard rate: the wire sends it no speed field, so the standard price is the true price.
cacheCostPer1kTokens(string $model, string $kind): ?floatC-PRV-3.a: the cache-rate door, same pair-precise premium gate.
withModel(string $model): staticThe trait's spread-based rebinder cannot be used here: this class holds a httpClient property that is not a constructor parameter, so the named spread would reject it. Rebuilding positionally keeps every transport seam, price override, cache flag, sizing override, the CTX-1 thinking budget and the C-PRV-3.a service tier intact across a model switch. An injected seam is forwarded as-is; the DEFAULT transport is rebuilt so the clone's closures bind to the clone — a forwarded default closure would keep reading the original's $this and freeze the old tier gating onto the new model's wire bytes.
promptCache(): boolWhether this provider was built to mark prompt-cache breakpoints (the promptCache setting). Whether a given request carries them also depends on its model - see marksPromptCache().
model(): string
marksPromptCache(string $model): boolDoes a request for $model carry prompt-cache breakpoints? Only on the Anthropic arm (the one wire here that spells cache_control), only with the promptCache setting on, and never for a family in NO_PROMPT_CACHE_FAMILIES. An empty id is the configured default, as on the wire (MarksPromptCache).
isAnthropicModel(string $model): boolAnthropic publisher models are the claude-* family; Vertex ids append a version suffix (claude-3-5-sonnet-v2@20241022), so match on the family name rather than an exact id list that would go stale on every model release.
acceptsAssistantPrefill(string $model): boolRoadmap 2.7-2: the Anthropic Messages API (rawPredict) continues a trailing assistant turn as a prefill, so a cut-off Claude reply is asked for its exact rest. Gemini and the legacy route take no prefill and are asked with a user row instead. A Claude model that refuses prefill outright answers with an error naming it, which ReplyContinuation::rejectsPrefill() turns into the same fallback.
parseAnthropicUsage(array $usage, string $model): UsageParses a native Anthropic Messages-API usage object into the provider-counted token BUCKETS (prompt_plan.md P4.S2). Used by the unary :rawPredict reply AND by both usage-bearing events of parseAnthropicChunk() — one document shape, one parse, so the streaming arm cannot drift from the non-streaming one.
traitCostPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): ?float
traitCacheCostPer1kTokens(string $model, string $kind): ?floatUSD per 1K CACHE tokens for $model (the cache half): read prices cache_read_input_tokens / Gemini's cachedContentTokenCount, write prices cache_creation_input_tokens. Null only when the rate it resolves to is unknown or fails validation - the same loud unpriced road as costPer1kTokens().

static anthropicDocument(string $mediaType, string $bytes, string $title): arrayThe Anthropic family's base64 document block, in exactly one spelling: the user-attachment leg above (CTX-2) and the document-gated tool_result leg in \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\Concerns\AnthropicMessagesWire share it (it replaced the inline array this leg used to hand-build — byte-identical output), so a PDF entering through either door presents identically (C-TOOL-2).
static responsesInputFile(string $mediaType, string $bytes, string $name): arrayC-TOOL-2.g: the Responses function_call_output parts list's document member, in exactly one spelling — the tool-result leg in \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\Concerns\OpenAiResponsesWire is its only builder, mirroring how anthropicDocument() is the single Anthropic spelling shared by that wire's two doors. Unlike the Anthropic block (and the chat file part, which nests), the Responses part carries its keys flat, and the filename passes the same control-byte hygiene as filePartName() — the JSON-string hazard is wire-independent.
static geminiParts(UserMessage $message): arrayGemini generateContent: a text part, then one inlineData part per image.
static bedrockBlocks(UserMessage $message): arrayBedrock Converse: a text block, then one image block per image, then one document block per carryable PDF (C-TOOL-2.e). The bytes go RAW - the AWS SDK base64-encodes a blob member itself, so encoding here would send the model base64 of base64.
static announceOversize(string $kind, string $bytes, int $budget): voidSay, once per distinct payload, that a tool-result attachment was over the provider's byte budget and so travels as its text caption only. The wire rebuilds the request every step, so without the memo a screenshot would repeat the notice on each replay; without the notice the user sees a model that "cannot see" an image it was handed.

CacheBreakpoints final class

Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoints, applied wipe-then-reapply on every step.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly bool $marksEnabled = true)
static disabledFromEnvironment(): boolIs the P10.S3 kill switch set? Presence-flag semantics, verbatim from the repo's other flags (\SugarCraft\Code\Support\EnvBool::isSet(), \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::parallelToolCallsEnabled()): unset, empty and the literal 0 read as false; any other text reads as true. Static and side-effect-free so a consumer can consult it once at construction — apply() never calls it, keeping the mark plan environment-independent (see DETERMINISM in the class docblock).
apply(array $messages, array $tools): arrayWipe every breakpoint this class owns, then re-derive the mark set.
observeCacheHealth(?Usage $usage): ?stringConsecutive-zero-reports diagnostic (P10.S3): hand me each response's Usage as it arrives; on the third consecutive report where BOTH cache buckets came back measured at zero — and on every one after — I return the sentence something should eventually print. Null otherwise.
zeroReportStreak(): intHow many consecutive both-buckets-zero reports observeCacheHealth() has counted. Read so the streak can cross a process boundary: the turn that saw a report may run in a forked child whose copy of this object dies with it.
resumeZeroReportStreak(int $reports): voidContinue a streak counted by another copy of this object — the forked turn child's, carried home on its result frame. A negative count is clamped to zero, so a corrupt frame can only under-count, never invent a warning.

HasModelCatalog interface

PRV-1 (§6.5): a provider whose endpoint can answer "which models do you have?" without guessing. Implemented by the OpenAI-compatible transports (openai, custom, sglang), which all speak GET {root}/v1/models; Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex and the offline providers have no such route and their catalogs come from ModelMetadata::candidates() instead.

MethodSummary
catalogKey(): ?stringThe identity of the catalog fetch — normally the server root the list endpoint hangs off. Two providers with the same key share one fetch.
listModels(): ?arrayThe model ids the endpoint reports, in its own order; null when the server cannot be asked or answers with junk. May block on one bounded metadata GET — call from update-side code, never from a render path (ModelCatalog::prefetch() is the sanctioned caller).

HonoursHostPermissionMode interface

The seam for providers whose wire carries its OWN permission dial.

MethodSummary
withHostPermissionMode(?PermissionMode $mode): staticA clone carrying the host gate's current mode, or null when no gate exists (a headless one-shot with no PermissionGate) — in which case the provider sends its dial exactly as it did before this seam: the seam adds a translation, it never invents a mode.

MarksPromptCache interface

A provider that places prompt-cache breakpoints on its requests, and can say for which model it does.

MethodSummary
marksPromptCache(string $model): boolDoes a request for $model carry prompt-cache breakpoints? An empty id names the provider's configured default — the same fallback a request with no model takes on the wire.

ModelCatalog final class

PRV-1 (§6.5): the once-per-process cache in front of the two model-catalog sources, and the merge order the palette and models all render.

MethodSummary
static prefetch(?HasModelCatalog $provider): voidAsk the endpoint once per process for this provider's catalog. Null answers (unreachable host, refused route) are memoised too — the "do not ask again this session" rule ModelMetadata applies to failed downloads. Safe on the update side; NEVER call from a render path.
static prefetchAsync(?HasModelCatalog $provider, ?callable $sender = null): ?PromiseInterfaceThe async sibling of prefetch() (C-PRV-5.c): starts the same once-per-process catalog read on the event loop and hands back the promise that will settle the memo, so a palette open answers at once on the tiers already in hand. Null means NOTHING WAS STARTED — every shape the sync guards refuse (no key, memo already settled or in flight, environment opt-out), plus the providers whose transport has no async path: the dispatch is typed to the two concrete endpoints that speak one, so the custom gateway and anonymous fakes answer null and their callers keep the sync prime byte-identical.
static live(?HasModelCatalog $provider): ?arrayThe live tier for a provider instance, from the memo only — null when nothing was prefetched yet or the fetch failed. Render-path safe.
static litellm(string $providerName, ?ModelMetadata $metadata = null): arrayThe community-database tier for a chat provider name, memoised. The one read of the LiteLLM table happens here (its own first read stays non-blocking: cache as-is, refresh forked). Render-path safe once primed; cold, it takes the bounded cache read the same accessor providers already use for windows and rates.
static family(string $providerName): ?stringThe provider's LiteLLM attribution family, or null for none — the one name→family rule shared by the palette and models all.
static merge(array $base, ?array $live, array $litellm, int $limit = self::MAX_ROWS): arrayThe three tiers merged into the list a picker shows: configured/current first (the ids this session speaks), then the endpoint's live answer, then the community database — deduplicated, capped, in that order. Pure over its arguments.
static resetForTesting(): voidTest seam: forget every memoised tier.

ModelFamily enum

The model families candy-code treats differently (roadmap 5.10): the two the SGLang provider already shapes its sampling, reasoning effort and window around, plus MiniMax, which until now had no family test of its own.

Cases: DeepSeekV4 · Qwen · MiniMax · Other

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
static of(string $model): selfThe family a model id belongs to. Every id no predicate claims is ONE bucket, Other: two unknown ids carry the same behaviour, so a spelling difference between them is not a family difference.

ModelMetadata final class

Context windows and per-token prices for models this package has no table for (roadmap 5.13a), read from LiteLLM's community-maintained model_prices_and_context_window.json — the database Aider sizes and prices every model from.

MethodSummary
static knowledgeCutoff(string $model): ?stringThe published knowledge cutoff for a model id, or null when the family is not in KNOWLEDGE_CUTOFFS — the answer the model-facing line must never guess.
static new(): selfThe production database: the cache under the owned home, refreshed in the background from SOURCE_URL — or nothing at all when OPT_OUT_ENV is set or no home can be established as this user's.
static disabled(): selfA database that knows no model.
static fromTable(array $table): selfA fixed table in LiteLLM's shape — for embedders and tests.
static cachedAt(string $cachePath, ?\Closure $fetch = null, bool $background = false, ?int $now = null): selfThe cache at $cachePath, refreshed through $fetch when it is older than TTL_SECONDS at $now — inline unless $background. The seam new() is built on, public so a test can drive the refresh with no network and no real home.
static disabledFromEnvironment(): boolWhether OPT_OUT_ENV is set: unset, empty and 0 are not.
contextWindow(string $model): ?intThe model's input window in tokens (max_input_tokens), or null when the database does not know it.
costPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): ?floatUSD per 1K tokens for $direction — input, output, or cached (a cache-hit prompt token) — or null when the database has no rate.
entry(string $model): ?arrayThe database row for $model, projected to the fields this package reads, or null. Matched exactly, then case-insensitively, then — Aider's rule — as <provider>/<id> against the row for <id> whose litellm_provider is that provider. No looser match: a self-hosted model that merely shares a name fragment with a hosted one must not be billed at the hosted price.
candidates(?string $providerHint = null, int $limit = 0): arrayPRV-1 (§6.5): the model names this database knows, for filling the model palette and models all without any provider round trip.

OpenAIProvider final readonly class

MethodSummary
static validApis(): arrayThe api key's accepted values — the factory validates against this.
__construct(private ClientContract $client, private string $defaultModel = 'gpt-4o', private array $modelPrices = [], private ?int $contextWindowOverride = null, private ?bool $supportsVision = null, private ?ModelMetadata $modelMetadata = null, private ?string $modelsBaseUrl = null, private ?string $modelsApiKey = null, private string $api = self::API_CHAT, private ?string $organization = null, private ?\GuzzleHttp\Client $responsesClient = null, private string $providerName = self::DEFAULT_NAME, private ?string $apiKeyHeader = null, private ?string $serviceTier = null)
name(): string
catalogKey(): ?stringPRV-1: the version root the factory resolved, normalized for memo identity.
listModels(): ?arrayPRV-1: one bounded GET {base}/models; null when the base must not be asked.
listModelsAsync(?callable $sender = null): PromiseInterfaceC-PRV-5.c: the async sibling of listModels() — the same askable door, the same bounded read, answered on the event loop so a palette open never pays for it on the keystroke path. The promise resolves to exactly what listModels() returns (ids or null) and never rejects. $sender is the endpoint's test seam; production callers pass nothing.
supportsStreaming(): bool
supportsFunctionCalling(): bool
supportsDocuments(): boolC-TOOL-2.e: PDFs ride the chat/completions file part (a data:application/pdf file_data), which the official API accepts on its vision models. The flag stays chat-only — the Responses arm's USER rows keep declining the block (its tool rows carry a native input_file part since C-TOOL-2.g; an earlier note here calling that part a file-ID-only construct was corrected by the same step) — and the model gate is the vision TABLE answer, deliberately not the provider block's supportsVision override: an override buys images (an image_url part any chat model tolerates structurally), it does not teach a non-vision deployment to read PDFs.
supportsVision(): boolWhether the configured model reads image parts: the provider block's override when set, else VISION_MODEL_FAMILIES minus TEXT_ONLY_MODELS. Before this every model answered yes, so an image sent to a text-only model failed the turn with the API's error.
supportsJsonSchema(): bool
withModel(string $model): staticThis provider answering for $model (roadmap N-P3b remainder): the window and the rates below read the configured id, so a model switch through \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::withModel() rebinds it here instead of leaving them the old model's.
contextWindow(): intEvery PRICE_TABLE model is sized here (gpt-4o-mini and the gpt-4.1 pair were priced but fell to an 8,192 default, so Chat's context tiers fired after a few messages on 128k / 1M models). An unknown model answers 0 — "unknown" per ProviderInterface::contextWindow() — so \SugarCraft\Code\Context\ContextWindow::resolve() applies its one named fallback instead of this file guessing a denominator.
costPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): ?float
shapesEffortFor(string $model): bool
serviceTierFor(string $model): ?stringC-PRV-3.a: the public OpenAI surface answers service_tier for every model it speaks for. The field is documented on BOTH arms this class drives (Chat Completions and Responses) with the same value vocabulary, and Fast-mode eligibility is a property of the PROJECT and the model line, not of this file's tables — which ids accept priority changes with every release. An unsupported pair answers with the API's own 400 prose, the same "the API's rejection is better guidance than a local guess" doctrine openAiReasoningEffort() records for effort spellings, so the pair never needs a stale local allowlist here.
withServiceTier(?string $tier): static
complete(CompleteRequest $request): CompleteResponse
completeStream(CompleteRequest $request): \GeneratorStreams completion responses as a generator of deltas.
embeddings(EmbeddingsRequest $request): EmbeddingsResponse

OpenAiModelsEndpoint final class

PRV-1 (§6.5): one bounded GET {root}/v1/models against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — the listing route openai, custom and sglang all speak — shared by every HasModelCatalog provider and by models all.

MethodSummary
static fetch(string $baseUrl, ?string $apiKey = null, ?callable $handler = null): ?array
static fetchAsync(string $baseUrl, ?string $apiKey = null, ?callable $sender = null): PromiseInterfaceThe async sibling of fetch() (C-PRV-5.c): the same single bounded GET {base}/models, dispatched on the event loop instead of the calling thread, so a palette open starts the read and answers at once on the tiers already in the memo. The E646 rule is about LLM calls and holds unchanged — this is still a one-request metadata read, and it still carries the same total discovery budget: the bound that made the sync prime merely annoying on a keystroke is exactly what makes this one safe to leave outstanding. Both bounds name self::DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS — the connector's connect budget and Browser::withTimeout()'s total — so this file keeps naming its one budget (the exemption ProviderConnectTimeoutTest reads), and Browser's default status refusal is re-applied in the callback so the seam below cannot smuggle a 4xx/5xx body past the contract.
static decode(string $body): ?array{"data":[{"id": "..."}]} reduced to the non-empty string ids. A body that is not that shape — including a valid JSON answer with no usable rows — is the same "unknown" as a failed transport, never a partial catalog presented as a complete one.

ProviderResponseException final class

A provider call that ended in an isError CompleteResponse which the retry seam in \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime could not (or was not allowed to) recover from.

MethodSummary
__construct(string $message, public readonly CompleteResponse $response)
static fromResponse(CompleteResponse $response): selfBuild the exception from the error response itself, so the provider's own wording - not a paraphrase - is what reaches the user.

ProviderStreamException final class

A streamed completion that failed AFTER the HTTP response had already started, so no status code is left to say so.

MethodSummary
static fromErrorEvent(mixed $frame, string $prefix = ''): ?selfThe failure an SSE error frame describes, or null when $frame is not an error frame (an ordinary delta, the usage frame, [DONE]'s null).

RebindsModel interface

A provider that can answer for another model without being rebuilt (roadmap N-P3b remainder, 4.1-1).

MethodSummary
withModel(string $model): staticA copy of this provider answering for $model.

ReplyContinuation final class

How a reply that stopped early is asked to go on (roadmap 2.7-2 / 2.7-3): the rows that ask for the rest, and how the rest is joined to what came before.

MethodSummary
static prefills(ProviderInterface $provider, string $model): boolWhether $provider is continued by prefill for $model.
static continuable(AssistantMessage $partial): boolWhether $partial can be continued at all: a reply with text and no tool call. A reply that only thought has nothing to prefill, and one that called a tool is a step, not a cut-off answer.
static rows(AssistantMessage $partial, bool $prefill, string $prompt): arrayThe rows to append to the request so the model continues $partial.
static merge(AssistantMessage $partial, AssistantMessage $next, bool $prefill): AssistantMessage$partial and its continuation $next as the one reply they are: the text joined, the reasoning joined, both responses' usage summed (each was a billed call), the signed thinking blocks concatenated in the order the conversation received them (CTX-1: both attempts' blocks were really shown, and the API only replays a thinking turn whose blocks are all present), and the tool calls and length stop of $next, which is where the reply now ends.
static rejectsPrefill(\Throwable|CompleteResponse $failure): boolWhether $failure is a provider refusing the prefill itself — Anthropic's "This model does not support assistant message prefill" — so the same continuation can be asked for again with a user row.

ReportsServedModel interface

A provider that may talk to a model OTHER than the id it was configured with, and can say which.

MethodSummary
servedModel(): ?stringThe model the server reports serving, when this provider addresses requests to it in place of its configured id and has learned the name — from its own discovery or from noteServedModel(). Null when it adopts nothing, or has not learned the name yet.
noteServedModel(string $servedModel): voidRecord a served model name learned elsewhere — the forked turn child's discovery, carried back across the fork. Ignored by a provider that adopts no served model, and for an empty name.

SglangProvider final readonly class

MethodSummary
__construct(private string $baseUrl, private string $model, private ?string $apiKey, private Client $httpClient, private ?ToolCallParserInterface $toolCallParser = null, private string|float|null $reasoningEffort = null, private array $extraTemplateKwargs = [], private ?string $sessionAffinityId = null, private ?\Closure $serverInfoLoader = null, private ?bool $supportsVision = null, private ?int $contextWindowOverride = null)
static openAiCompatible(string $baseUrl, string $model = self::DEFAULT_MODEL, ?string $apiKey = null, ?ToolCallParserInterface $toolCallParser = null, string|float|null $reasoningEffort = null, array $extraTemplateKwargs = [], ?string $sessionAffinityId = null, bool $discoverServerInfo = false, ?bool $supportsVision = null, ?int $contextWindowOverride = null): self
serverInfo(): ?SglangServerInfoWhat the server said about itself, read once per provider and memoised - null when no loader is armed or the read failed.
servedModel(): ?stringThe served model this provider adopts, for the TUI's labels - read from what serverInfo() has ALREADY memoised (the parent's first frame normally loads it, via contextWindow()), else from what a forked turn child reported (noteServedModel()). Never runs the loader: see ReportsServedModel::servedModel().
noteServedModel(string $servedModel): voidRemember the served name a forked turn child discovered, so the parent's labels can show it. Kept apart from the info memo on purpose: it is a label fact, and it neither marks discovery as done nor changes what addressedToServedModel() sends.
static defaultToolCallParserFor(string $model): ToolCallParserInterfaceThe parser used when the operator named none, chosen from the MODEL: DSML wrapped around the OpenAI-array parser for the DeepSeek-V4 family, the OpenAI-array parser alone otherwise. The one definition of that rule - ProviderFactory::createSglang() asks it at build time for a configured model, resolvedToolCallParser() at request time for an adopted served one. ProviderFactory's private defaultToolCallParserFor() docblock carries the argument for arming DSML by default on that family.
static argumentDecoder(): \ClosureW1.A6 (§12 D6): the truncation-aware function.arguments decoder, handed out so a parser built *outside* this class still reports the §12 D5 MiniMax </parameter> truncation instead of silently degrading to no arguments.
name(): string
shapesEffortFor(string $model): bool
catalogKey(): ?stringPRV-1 (§6.5): the configured base, normalized for memo identity.
listModels(): ?arrayPRV-1: one bounded GET {base}/models; the server's answer or null.
listModelsAsync(?callable $sender = null): PromiseInterfaceC-PRV-5.c: the async sibling of listModels() — same bounded read on the event loop, resolves to exactly what the sync ask returns, never rejects. $sender is the endpoint's test seam; production callers pass nothing.
supportsStreaming(): bool
acceptsAssistantPrefill(string $model): boolRoadmap 2.7-2: every model SGLang serves continues a final assistant turn on continue_final_message (see buildParams()), so a length-stopped or dropped reply is continued exactly.
supportsFunctionCalling(): bool
supportsDocuments(): boolWhether an attached image may go out as an image_url part. The provider block's supportsVision wins when set; otherwise the SERVER answers - /model_info's has_image_understanding, read by the same memoised discovery as the context window - and a server that did not say (discovery off, failed, or an older SGLang) counts as no vision. Erring that way costs an image its pixels, never the turn: the image becomes a named text placeholder and the user is told (\SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::toTypedMessages()), where a guessed "yes" would send a text-only model a part its chat template rejects.
supportsVision(): bool
supportsJsonSchema(): boolTrue because buildParams() forwards CompleteRequest::$jsonSchema as response_format.json_schema.schema, which a live round-trip against the skynet2 SGLang v0.5.16 / MiniMax-M2.7 deployment (2026-08-10) confirmed actually binds output to the schema: the same prompt returns free prose without response_format and schema-conforming JSON with it.
contextWindow(): intW1.A6 (§12 D8), now MODEL-AWARE - and it had to become so, because the single figure it used to return was measured on a model this server no longer runs.
costPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): float
complete(CompleteRequest $request): CompleteResponse
completeStream(CompleteRequest $request): \Generator
embeddings(EmbeddingsRequest $request): EmbeddingsResponseA transport failure or a 2xx body that is not an embeddings payload THROWS instead of returning an empty list. The old silent [] made an outage (model not loaded, 5xx, refused connection) look exactly like "no results", so a semantic-search consumer degraded without ever telling the user why. The wrap mirrors complete()'s: the server's own error.message when it sent one, code 0, and the Guzzle exception as previous so TransientFailure::isTransient() still classifies 5xx/429/ connect as transient and 400 as permanent. A present-but-empty data: [] remains a legitimate empty result.
static isDeepSeekV4(string $model): boolTrue when a model id names the DeepSeek-V4 family.
static isQwen3Next(string $model): boolTrue when a model id names the Qwen3.8 family - the ids the skynet2 deployment serves as Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and the bare alias Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen.md E-70).
static placeSystemRows(array $rows, ?string $systemPrompt): arrayThe one placement rule for system content on an OpenAI-shaped wire (step 1.A-1), shared with CustomProvider: rows already formatted by a provider's formatMessages(), the request-level prompt, out comes the body's messages list.
static systemNoticeContent(string $content): stringA mid-history system row's content as the user-role notice that carries it: fenced in <system-notice> so the model reads it as the harness speaking, not the user. The notice's own fence name is neutralised inside the payload (same terminator rule as \SugarCraft\Code\Context\PromptFence::escape()), so quoted text — a queued prompt, an error message — cannot close it early.
parseUsage(array $usage): UsageParses this endpoint's usage object into the provider-counted token BUCKETS (prompt_plan.md P4.S2). The single place this provider reads usage fields, so parseResponse() and any later carrier agree by construction about what the server actually said.
static errorBodyMessage(GuzzleException $e): ?string§Q8 (qwen.md; E-56): lifts the server's own clean error sentence out of a failed SGLANG HTTP response, or returns null when there is nothing clean to show.
sessionAffinityHeaderValue(?string $sessionId): ?stringThe wire value for one session id: full 64-char lowercase hex, or null when there is no session to be affine to (null or blank id).
sessionAffinityHeaders(?string $requestSessionId = null): arrayThe per-request headers option at a post() site: [] or the one affinity header — for the request's own session id when it names one (step 0.13-a), else the host class's $sessionAffinityId.

SglangServerInfo final readonly class

What a live SGLang server says about itself: the limits and parsers it was launched with, read from its own GET /model_info and GET /server_info.

MethodSummary
static new(?string $servedModelName = null, ?int $contextLength = null, ?int $maxReqInputLen = null, ?string $toolCallParser = null, ?string $reasoningParser = null, bool $reportsToolCallParser = false, ?bool $imageUnderstanding = null): selfDefault root factory, per repo convention - for callers (tests, a future cache) that already hold the figures.
static fromResponses(?array $modelInfo, ?array $serverInfo): ?selfBuilds the snapshot from the two decoded response bodies, either of which may be missing (the endpoint failed or is not served).
static discover(string $baseUrl, ?string $apiKey = null, ?callable $handler = null): ?selfReads both endpoints concurrently and returns what they said - or null, never an exception, when the server cannot be asked. Discovery is an optimisation over the fallback table, so an unreachable host, a 404 from a proxy that only forwards /v1, a 401, a timeout or a non-JSON body must all degrade to "use the table", not fail the session.
static rootUrl(string $baseUrl): stringThe server root the info endpoints hang off: the configured baseUrl without a trailing slash or a trailing /v1 (case-insensitive). A deeper prefix (https://proxy/sglang/v1) keeps everything before the /v1, so a reverse proxy mounted under a path still resolves.
totalWindow(): ?intThe model's total token window - prompt plus output - as the server reports it. When only max_req_input_len is known that figure stands in: it is a few tokens BELOW the true total, so the stand-in can only make an output budget derived from it smaller, never overrun the server.
inputWindow(int $outputHeadroom): ?intThe input budget SglangProvider::contextWindow() reports: the enforced input ceiling less $outputHeadroom, never above the total window - the same min(context_length, max_req_input_len − headroom) arithmetic the transcribed Qwen3.8 constant was derived with, now over live figures. Null when the server reported neither limit.

TransientFailure final class

Decides whether a failed provider call is worth trying again, and how long to wait before doing so (Phase 5 item 8).

MethodSummary
static isTransient(\Throwable $error): boolWhether this thrown failure is worth another attempt.
static anthropicErrorIsTransient(mixed $error): boolWhether a decoded Anthropic error object describes a transient failure.
static responseIsTransient(CompleteResponse $response): boolWhether an error-carrying CompleteResponse is worth another attempt.
static backoff(int $attempt, ?callable $sleeper = null, ?array $config = null, ?\Throwable $failure = null, ?\Closure $onBeat = null): voidSleep the backoff owed after $attempt failed attempts, where $attempt is 1-based.
static jitteredBackoffMicroseconds(int $owed, ?callable $rng = null): intUniform full-jitter draw over [0, $owed] — ISS-074.
static retryAfterSeconds(\Throwable $failure): ?floatThe Retry-After a failed provider call carried, in seconds — the server's own instruction, honoured by backoff() above any locally computed schedule (ISS-074).
static announceRateLimit(\Throwable $failure): voidAnnounce a server-directed wait to the runtime notice sink BEFORE backoff() pays for it (ISS-074 review fix).
static backoffMicroseconds(int $attempt, ?array $config = null): intThe wait owed after $attempt failed attempts (1-based), in microseconds. Zero once no attempts remain, so an exhausted sequence does not pay for a retry it will not make.
static totalBackoffMicroseconds(?array $config = null): intEvery sleep a fully exhausted retry sequence performs, summed.
static maxTotalBackoffMicroseconds(): intThe longest silence any honoured pair of retry settings can produce — totalBackoffMicroseconds() at both settings' maxima. What the smallest permitted idle ceiling is measured against.
static maxAttempts(?array $config = null): intTotal provider calls per seam, including the first: the providerRetryAttempts setting, else MAX_ATTEMPTS.
static baseBackoffMicroseconds(?array $config = null): intThe wait after the first failed attempt, in microseconds: the providerRetryBaseBackoffMs setting (milliseconds, 0..MAX_BASE_BACKOFF_MS_SETTING), else BASE_BACKOFF_MICROSECONDS. 0 retries at once.
static statusIsTransient(int $status): bool5xx, plus exactly 408 and 429.

static new(string $projectId, string $location = 'us-central1', string $model = 'claude-sonnet-4-6', ?callable $predictor = null, ?callable $streamer = null, array $modelPrices = [], ?int $thinkingBudget = null, bool $promptCache = true, ?int $contextWindowOverride = null): self

supportsStreaming(): boolCapability flags carry no model argument, so they answer for the provider's configured default model. A caller that overrides the model per request into the other family gets the other family's protocol (see complete()) but these flags will not have moved.
supportsFunctionCalling(): boolANTHROPIC ONLY, AND THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THIS CLASS, NOT ABOUT GEMINI. Gemini on Vertex does support function calling (tools[].functionDeclarations, answered with a functionCall part), and \Google\Cloud\AIPlatform\V1\GenerateContentRequest::setTools() is vendored. What is absent is the SHAPER: geminiBody() builds no tools key and parseGeminiResponse() reads no functionCall part, because the step that built the Gemini arm scoped tools out. So the honest flag is false - reporting true would let a caller hand this provider tools it silently drops. Whoever adds the shaper flips this with it; the absence is pinned by VertexProviderTest::testAGeminiBodyCarriesNoToolsKeyEvenWhenToolsAreOffered.
supportsVision(): boolClaude and Gemini both read images, as image blocks (anthropicBlocks()) and inlineData parts (formatGeminiContents()) - the request-side image block this used to wait for. The legacy PaLM envelope does not, and gets the attachment as named text instead.
supportsDocuments(): boolC-TOOL-2.e: the Claude arm speaks the Messages document block (CTX-2) and the Gemini arm speaks application/pdf inlineData through the shared encoders, so both native arms carry PDFs. The legacy PaLM envelope speaks neither, and gets the attachment as named text instead.
supportsJsonSchema(): bool
contextWindow(): int

embeddings(EmbeddingsRequest $request): EmbeddingsResponse

isGeminiModel(string $model): boolGemini models are publishers/google - the SAME publisher as PaLM 2 - but a DIFFERENT protocol, so this predicate selects the request document and the RPC, never the endpoint. publisherFor() is unchanged by it and still answers google for both families; endpointFor('gemini-1.5-pro-002') returns the identical resource name it returned before this arm existed.
promptCache(): boolWhether this provider was built to mark prompt-cache breakpoints (the promptCache setting). Whether a given request carries them also depends on its model - see marksPromptCache().
model(): string
withModel(string $model): staticThis provider answering for $model (roadmap 4.1-1): the capability flags below read the configured id, so a model switch through \SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend::withModel() rebinds them here instead of leaving them the old model's.
costPer1kTokens(string $model, string $direction): ?float
cacheCostPer1kTokens(string $model, string $kind): ?floatUSD per 1K CACHE tokens for $model (the cache half): read prices cache_read_input_tokens / Gemini's cachedContentTokenCount, write prices cache_creation_input_tokens. Null only when the rate it resolves to is unknown or fails validation - the same loud unpriced road as costPer1kTokens().
marksPromptCache(string $model): boolDoes a request for $model carry prompt-cache breakpoints? Only on the Anthropic arm (the one wire here that spells cache_control), only with the promptCache setting on, and never for a family in NO_PROMPT_CACHE_FAMILIES. An empty id is the configured default, as on the wire (MarksPromptCache).
isAnthropicModel(string $model): boolAnthropic publisher models are the claude-* family; Vertex ids append a version suffix (claude-3-5-sonnet-v2@20241022), so match on the family name rather than an exact id list that would go stale on every model release.
acceptsAssistantPrefill(string $model): boolRoadmap 2.7-2: the Anthropic Messages API (rawPredict) continues a trailing assistant turn as a prefill, so a cut-off Claude reply is asked for its exact rest. Gemini and the legacy route take no prefill and are asked with a user row instead. A Claude model that refuses prefill outright answers with an error naming it, which ReplyContinuation::rejectsPrefill() turns into the same fallback.
parseAnthropicUsage(array $usage, string $model): UsageParses a native Anthropic Messages-API usage object into the provider-counted token BUCKETS (prompt_plan.md P4.S2). Used by the unary :rawPredict reply AND by both usage-bearing events of parseAnthropicChunk() — one document shape, one parse, so the streaming arm cannot drift from the non-streaming one.
parseUsageMetadata(array $usageMetadata, string $model): UsageParses one Gemini usageMetadata document into the provider-counted token BUCKETS (prompt_plan.md P4.S2).

HttpClientDefaults trait

The single place a provider's HTTP client is configured, so the connect bounds below cannot be set on one provider and forgotten on the next one somebody adds.

JsonFetch trait

The one hand-shape for "GET a URL, take the body as text, decode it as a JSON object/array" that the discovery readers each spelled out separately (\SugarCraft\Code\Providers\ModelMetadata, \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\OpenAiModelsEndpoint, \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\SglangServerInfo).

OpenAiResponsesWire trait

The OpenAI Responses wire (POST {base}/responses) as the sibling arm of the chat-completions SDK path — C-PRV-2.a.

MethodSummary
abstract supportsVision(): boolThe using class answers for itself (SHL-3 T2): images ride the tool row only for a vision-capable model. Both OpenAI arms' host already implements it from \SugarCraft\Code\Providers\ProviderInterface; the declaration exists so this trait's call is defined, exactly as AnthropicMessagesWire declares the same hook for its own arm.

ReasoningExtractor trait

Splits a model's "thinking" out of content regardless of which server-side reasoning parser produced the response - shared by every OpenAI-compatible provider so the split logic lives in exactly one place (previously SglangProvider/CustomProvider/OpenAIProvider each hardcoded reasoning: null independently).

ReassemblesStreamedToolCalls trait

Reassembles OpenAI-shaped streamed tool calls (roadmap X-31a): a streamed reply sends each call as successive delta.tool_calls[] fragments - the first naming the call's id and function.name, the rest carrying pieces of function.arguments that only form JSON once the call is complete.

SessionAffinity trait

The hashed session-affinity header every declared provider transport puts on the wire, so a caching gateway can route one session's calls to the same warm backend (prompt_plan.md P10.S4; Mirrors charmbracelet/crush sessionHeaders(call.SessionID)).

MethodSummary
sessionAffinityHeaderValue(?string $sessionId): ?stringThe wire value for one session id: full 64-char lowercase hex, or null when there is no session to be affine to (null or blank id).
sessionAffinityHeaders(?string $requestSessionId = null): arrayThe per-request headers option at a post() site: [] or the one affinity header — for the request's own session id when it names one (step 0.13-a), else the host class's $sessionAffinityId.

ToolSchema trait

Normalizes a \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\Tool's inputSchema() into a shape that survives json_encode() as valid JSON Schema.

CtagsSymbolExtractor final class

Definitions and references in files of every language universal-ctags knows, for the symbol-level repo map (roadmap 5.5-2). The second producer beside PhpSymbolExtractor, which needs no binary and stays the PHP path.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withBinary(string $binary): selfRun a different executable — a name looked up on PATH, or a path. The seam the tests point at a scripted stand-in, and the place an embedder names a non-default install.
withTimeout(float $seconds): self
binary(): string
available(): boolIs binary() Universal Ctags with JSON output? A stat walk first, then one bounded --version run; memoized per binary.
cacheStamp(): stringThe stamp TagCache stores beside every file this extractor tagged: the extractor's own rule version and the binary's version banner. Either moving — a ctags upgrade can change what its parsers emit, an edited reference scan changes the references — turns every row it stamped into a miss, so no tag outlives the code that made it.
static isUniversalWithJson(string $versionOutput): boolDoes a ctags --version banner name Universal Ctags built with JSON?
extractFile(string $absPath, string $relPath): arrayTags for one file, or [] when ctags is unavailable or the file is unreadable, oversized or of no language ctags parses.
extractFiles(array $files): arrayTags for many files, batched into as few ctags runs as the argv and batch bounds allow. Every file it was asked about, could read and whose batch finished gets an entry (possibly []); a file is ABSENT from the answer when it was unreadable or oversized, when its batch hit the deadline or the output cap, or when the binary is unavailable — so an absent key always means "unknown", and a caller that caches only what it was answered never stores a partial or a missing-binary "no tags".
static parse(string $jsonLines, array $absToRel): arrayDefinition tags out of universal-ctags JSON lines. Pure, so the mapping is testable on a host without the binary. A line that is not a whole JSON tag object (a pseudo-tag, a line a clipped batch cut in half) is skipped; a tag for a path not in $absToRel is ignored.
static references(string $source, string $relPath, array $definitions = []): arrayReference tags for every identifier in $source, by a lexical scan: a name on its own definition line is the definition, not a use of it, and the NOT_REFERENCES keywords and one-character names are left out. Capped at MAX_REFERENCES_PER_FILE.
commandFor(array $absPaths): arrayThe argv for one batch, handed to proc_open's array form — no shell sits between the paths and ctags, so a space or a $ in a file name is just bytes. Absolute paths only, so no argument can read as an option.
static capabilityPresent(string $binary, ?string $pathList = null): boolIs $binary installed and executable?

SymbolGraph final class

The file graph a repo map ranks (roadmap 5.5-3): one weighted edge from each file that REFERENCES an identifier to each file that DEFINES it, built from the Tags PhpSymbolExtractor (through TagCache) yields.

MethodSummary
static new(array $tagsByFile, array $focusFiles = [], array $mentionedFiles = [], array $mentionedIdents = []): self
static fromSummaries(array $definitionsByFile, array $referencesByFile, array $focusFiles = [], array $mentionedFiles = [], array $mentionedIdents = []): selfThe graph from per-file summaries — each file's definition tags and its reference COUNTS per identifier (TagCache::summary()) — so a caller mapping a large checkout never holds a reference tag as an object. new() is this, after counting.

files(): array
edges(): arrayEvery edge of Aider's multigraph, enumerated — one per (referencer, definer, identifier), plus an unreferenced definition's self-edge. The graph itself never holds this list (see the class docblock); it is built here, in the order the ranking walks it, for a caller that wants to read the edges.

fileRanks(?PageRank $pageRank = null): array
rankedEntries(?PageRank $pageRank = null): arrayThe ranked map entries, best first: each definition tag of each (definer, identifier) pair in order of the rank flowing into it, then every remaining file as a bare entry (tag null) — ranked graph nodes first, then the rest by name. Focus files never appear.

TagCache final class

A per-project SQLite cache of Tags, keyed on a file's root-relative path plus its mtime and size. An unchanged file is never tokenized twice.

MethodSummary
static open(string $dbPath): selfOpen (creating if needed) the cache at $dbPath. The file and its WAL sidecars are owner-only (0600).
static defaultPath(string $projectRoot, ?string $home = null): ?string<home>/.candy-code/cache/repomap/<projectKey>.sqlite, or null when no home directory this process owns can be established. A file's reference tags are the bulk of every cache (nine in ten on this tree) and the graph needs only their counts, so a map of a large checkout never holds them as objects.

storeRendered(string $key, string $body): voidKeep $body as the finished map for $key; the oldest past MAX_RENDERED go.

ErrorLog final class

One-line rendering of a swallowed internal failure (ISS-057, Appendix O §6.2): SERVER.md promises "the cause is in the server's log, never in the answer", so every catch that hides the truth from the client renders it here for the log. The class name, a flattened and clipped message, and the throw site — enough to find the bug, and the raw message may still name a path or quote a prompt, which is precisely why it goes to the 0600 server.log and never into the answer. (CW-PAR-05 truth-flip: "never onto the wire" overstated it — an owner-authenticated Admin-scoped server.logs read (LogTail) surfaces these very lines, capped and flattened, on purpose. The line stays off the ANSWER; the operator's own log read is the authorized exit.)

MethodSummary

Server final class

The candy-code serve gateway: one HTTP + WebSocket listener on the SAME ReactPHP loop the engine's forked turns run on (Appendix O §3.2, §4.1).

MethodSummary
static new(ServerConfig $config, AuthContext $auth, ?StaticFiles $static = null, ?MessageHandler $handler = null, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?\Closure $log = null, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?float $requestDeadlineSeconds = null, ?\Closure $share = null, ?\Closure $canvas = null, ?HookWebhooks $webhooks = null, ?\Closure $channels = null): self
start(): stringBind and start answering; returns the bound address.
port(): ?intThe bound port, once started.
url(): stringhttp(s)://host:port as a browser on this machine reaches it (scheme follows TLS).
loginUrl(): stringA sign-in URL carrying a fresh one-time login code in its FRAGMENT, so the code never reaches a request line, a log or a Referer.
loginUrls(): arrayThe sign-in URL under each host a client may dial (ServerConfig::reachableHosts(): the bind address, or this machine's own interface addresses on a wildcard --allow-remote bind, where 0.0.0.0 names nothing a browser can open). One code serves every entry — it is spent by whichever one is opened first.
onCredentialsRevoked(\Closure $listener): voidSubscribe to credential death: $listener gets a viewer token id when that grant is revoked, or null when a rotation revokes every credential. The seam the protocol's idempotency cache hangs off (S-V02).
reloadToken(): ?intserve token --rotate reached this server (roadmap O-3b, carried from W6): re-read the token file and, when the token changed, sign every client out — cookies, tickets and login codes revoked, and every open WebSocket closed with CLOSE_CREDENTIALS_ROTATED, since each was authenticated with a credential that no longer exists. Answers how many sockets were closed, or null when the token did not change.
closeViewerSockets(string $tokenId): intClose every socket a viewer grant opened — the token.revoke arm. A socket is authenticated once at upgrade and keeps its principal for life, so revoking the grant alone would leave the viewer reading. Answers how many sockets closed.
closeDeadViewerSockets(): intClose viewer sockets whose grant has expired (or otherwise left the store).
closeExpiredSessions(): intClose every open socket whose cookie session has lapsed out of the sliding sign-in window (ISS-009): the store expires the session itself at the same deadline, but a socket keeps its principal for life unless someone ends it, so a browser that reloaded, died or went silent for CookieSessions::LIFETIME_SECONDS would otherwise keep reading and writing after its sign-in was gone. Answers how many sockets closed.
connectionCount(): int
stop(string $reason = 'server shutting down'): voidStop accepting, then close every WebSocket with 1001. Idempotent; the loop is left running for whatever else it serves.

ServerConfig final class

Everything candy-code serve binds, admits and serves with, resolved once at start (Appendix O §4.7, §8.3, §8.4).

MethodSummary
