static stateDirFrom(array $env, string $default): stringCANDY_CODE_SERVER_DIR, else the caller's default (~/.candy-code/server).
withHost(string $host): self
withPort(int $port): self
withAllowRemote(bool $allowRemote): self
withAllowedOrigins(array $origins): self
withAllowedHosts(array $hosts): selfhost or host:port, lower-cased, an IPv6 address bracketed (a bare ::1 is taken as the address, not as a port).
withInterfaceAddresses(array $addresses): selfThis machine's own addresses (InterfaceAddresses::detect()), which a wildcard --allow-remote bind answers to and names in its sign-in URLs (reachableHosts()).
withAllowedIps(array $ips): selfThe client addresses admitted beside loopback (Http\ClientAddressGuard): IPs or CIDRs, IPv4-mapped IPv6 ones stored as the IPv4 they carry. An empty list turns the filter off.
withTrustedProxies(array $proxies): self
withDirBrowse(bool $dirBrowse): selfWhether a signed-in client may list directories under $browseRoot (fs.listDirs) and open a workspace there to start a session in — off unless --allow-dir-browse or server.dirBrowse asks for it.
withClientTools(bool $clientTools): selfWhether the client-hosted tools door is open at all (C-TOOL-6.i). Off answers every tools.client.* call with kind client_tools_disabled — registration and result alike, so a client can neither announce tools nor settle a call it learned about before the door shut.
withBrowseRoot(?string $browseRoot): selfThe directory browsing is confined to; null = the user's home.
withWebhooks(array $webhooks): selfAUT-6: the inbound webhook hooks. Values arrive validated (self::webhooksValue()); an empty map means /api/hooks/{name} is not mounted at all — the endpoint answers its 404 like any unknown path, so the feature is default-off by construction rather than by a flag.
withTls(?string $tlsCert, ?string $tlsKey): selfC-WEB-5.a: turn on built-in TLS for the public listener. Both paths or neither — a lone --tls-cert (or lone --tls-key) is refused rather than silently serving cleartext while the operator believes otherwise.
hasTls(): boolWhether the public listener serves over TLS (self::withTls()).
urlScheme(): stringThe URL scheme a browser reaches this server over: https with TLS, else http.
withWebRoot(?string $webRoot): self
withWeb(bool $web): self
withAllowBypass(bool $allowBypass): self
withAllowRoot(bool $allowRoot): self
withPermissionMode(PermissionMode $permissionMode): self
withStateDir(string $stateDir): self
withRoot(?string $root): self
withMaxOpenSessions(int $maxOpenSessions): self
withMaxConcurrentTurns(int $maxConcurrentTurns): self
withDrainSeconds(float $seconds): self0 stops at once, cancelling whatever runs.
withAskTimeoutSeconds(float $seconds): self0 (the default) waits for a permission answer forever.
isLoopback(): boolWhether the bind address is this machine only.
isWildcard(): boolWhether the bind address is every interface: 0.0.0.0 or ::.
reachableHosts(): arrayThe hosts, as a URL authority spells them (no port), that a client on another machine dials this server under: the bind address, or — on a wildcard --allow-remote bind — each of this machine's $interfaceAddresses (IPv4 only on 0.0.0.0), falling back to loopback when there are none. The first is the one a single URL names.
bindUri(): stringThe tcp:// URI the listener binds, IPv6 bracketed.
hostForUrl(): stringThe host as a URL authority spells it (IPv6 bracketed).
admitsPermissionMode(PermissionMode $mode): boolWhether a client may put a session in $mode (Appendix O §8.4).
static answersAsksWithoutAHuman(PermissionMode $mode): boolWhether this mode answers every permission ask without asking anyone (AUT-6 MINOR-1 names the pair: bypass-permissions, dont-ask). One spelling for the question, asked at the launch door (admitsPermissionMode()) and at the schedule-row mode refusal (\SugarCraft\Code\Background\Schedule) — two sites that must agree about which two cases they mean. The hook doors ask NARROWER questions since C-AGT-7.c: hookRefusesMode() for the configured row and hookPermissionModeFallback() for the inherited mode, because dont-ask answers an ask by REFUSING it — unattended is exactly the posture it is safe in.
static hookRefusesMode(PermissionMode $mode): boolWhether a webhook row may name this mode (AUT-6-P2). This is NOT answersAsksWithoutAHuman()'s question: what endangers a turn nobody is watching is the mode that answers every permission ask YES — bypass-permissions, and it alone. dont-ask answers every ask by REFUSING it (it denies everything but reads), so a row naming it asks for the strictest posture a turn can run; refusing that row taught operators to omit the field instead — into the inheritance path below, which until this step widened a dont-ask server's hooks to default.
hookPermissionModeFallback(): stringThe mode an unmodeled webhook runs in (AUT-6 MINOR-1, clamped per AUT-6-P2).
problems(): arrayWhy this configuration may not start, one sentence each; empty when it may. Only CONFIGURATION reasons — the runtime ones (extensions, root) are Preflight's.
static webhooksValue(mixed $value): arrayAUT-6: parse and validate the webhooks map at launch. Every refusal names the hook and the field, because the operator is reading a startup error, not debugging a live request.

ServerConfigException final class

A candy-code serve setting that cannot be honoured: a port that is not a port, an origin that is not an origin, a non-loopback bind without --allow-remote. The message is the user-facing sentence; the CLI reports it at exit 2 because nothing was attempted and a retry cannot help.

StateDir final class

candy-code serve's state directory (Appendix O §4.6; roadmap O-4a): ~/.candy-code/server/, or CANDY_CODE_SERVER_DIR. Owner-private (0700, verified off lstat by PrivateDir) because everything in it is a credential or a handle on one:

MethodSummary
static open(string $path): selfThe state directory at $path, created 0700 when absent.
static existing(string $path): ?selfThe state directory at $path WITHOUT creating it — for the read-only verbs (status, stop, logs, url): asking whether a server runs must not leave a directory behind. Null when nothing is there.
discoveryPath(): string
lockPath(): string
logPath(): string
controlSocketPath(): string
acquireLock(): boolTake the singleton lock and keep it until releaseLock() or this process ends. False when another process holds it — a server is already running from this state directory.
holdsLock(): bool
releaseLock(): void
forgetLock(): voidDrop this process's handle on the lock WITHOUT unlocking it: the process that ran --detach hands the lock to the daemon it forked, which holds the same open file description — an LOCK_UN here would unlock it for the daemon too.
lockHeldElsewhere(): boolWhether SOME process holds the singleton lock right now. Probed by trying it: a lock this process could take is no one's, and is let go again at once.
rotateLog(int $limit = self::LOG_ROTATE_BYTES): boolRotate server.log when it has grown past $limit bytes: .1 → .2, the live file → .1, the oldest generation dropped. Returns whether it rotated; the caller then re-points its stdio at a fresh file (\SugarCraft\Code\Support\Daemonize::redirectStdio()).

SugarCraft\Code\Server\Auth

AuthContext final class

The server's credential state, in one place: the owner token, the read-only viewer grants minted from it, the one-time login codes, the cookie sessions, the WebSocket tickets and the failure throttle. Shared by the auth middleware (which checks) and the API (which mints), so the two can never hold different views of who is signed in.

MethodSummary
reloadToken(): boolRe-read the owner token; when it changed, revoke everything minted under the old one — every cookie session, every unspent ticket and login code, and every viewer grant (D-8: rotation nukes all viewer tokens, no orphans) — so a rotation signs every client out at once rather than at the next restart. Answers whether it changed.
static new(TokenStore $tokens, ?\Closure $clock = null): self

CookieSessions final class

The browser's authenticated sessions (Appendix O §8.2): an opaque id in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, server-side only — the cookie carries the secret, the store keeps nothing but its hash (ExpiringSecrets).

MethodSummary
static new(?\Closure $clock = null): self
static persisted(TokenStore $tokens, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?\Closure $log = null): selfA store that survives a server restart: its hash-only rows live in $tokens' state directory, valid only while that token is.
open(): stringA new session id — the cookie value.
validate(string $id): boolWhether $id is a live session; a live one slides.
revoke(string $id): void
revokeAll(): voidSign every browser out: the token their sign-in was checked against is gone.
count(): int

ExpiringSecrets final class

Short-lived random secrets held only as SHA-256 hashes, each with an expiry and an optional bound value — the one mechanism behind login codes, cookie sessions and WebSocket tickets (Appendix O §8.2).

MethodSummary
static new(float $ttlSeconds, ?\Closure $clock = null, int $capacity = 1024): self
mint(string $value = '', int $bytes = 32): stringA fresh secret ($bytes random bytes as hex) bound to $value.
export(): arrayThe live rows as hash => expiresAt — export()'s counterpart for a store whose owner persists it (WEB-6): hashes only, never a secret, in either direction.
import(array $hashToExpires, string $value): voidMerge rows back in after a restart, binding each to $value. The caller parsed them (a SessionFileStore rejects malformed and expired rows at the boundary); a hash already live in memory keeps its entry — this hydrates, it does not overwrite.
consume(string $secret): ?stringThe value $secret is bound to, consuming it; null when unknown or expired.
peek(string $secret, bool $slide = false): ?stringThe value $secret is bound to, keeping it and — when $slide — pushing its expiry a full TTL from now; null when unknown or expired.
revoke(string $secret): void
revokeAll(): voidForget every secret at once (the credential they were minted under changed).
count(): intHow many live secrets are held.

LoginCodes final class

One-time login codes (Appendix O §8.2): what the URL serve prints carries in its FRAGMENT, so the code never reaches a server log, a proxy or a Referer. The page posts it to /api/login and gets the HttpOnly cookie.

MethodSummary
static new(?\Closure $clock = null): self
mint(): string
consume(string $code): boolWhether $code was live; it is spent either way.
revokeAll(): void

RateLimiter final class

Per-address throttling of failed authentication (Appendix O §8.2): after MAX_FAILURES failures inside WINDOW_SECONDS, the address is locked out for LOCKOUT_SECONDS. A 64-hex token is not guessable at any rate; what this bounds is a login-code guesser and the log noise of a misconfigured client hammering the port.

MethodSummary
static new(?\Closure $clock = null): self
retryAfter(string $address): intSeconds until $address may try again; 0 when it is not locked out.
recordFailure(string $address): boolOne more failed sign-in for $address. Answers true on the strike that TRIPS the lockout — and only on that one — so the caller can write the event to the server log (ISS-008); later strikes inside the window and the lockout itself stay quiet.

SessionFileStore final class

The disk side of the cookie-session store (WEB-6): sessions.json in the server's state directory, holding HASH-ONLY rows — the same sha256(id) keys ExpiringSecrets holds in memory, each mapped to its expiry — written through the house AtomicJsonFile discipline (PrivateRetainedDir:: write: lstat the .partial, umask 077 so the mode settles 0600 BEFORE the rename publishes, rename over the target).

MethodSummary
static forTokenStore(TokenStore $tokens, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?\Closure $log = null): self
load(): arrayThe live rows for this boot: parsed, fingerprint-checked, and pruned of anything expired. A file that disagrees with any of that is treated as absent — and, when it existed but merely carried dead or foreign rows, rewritten at once so pruning lands on disk, not just in memory.
persist(array $rows): boolPublish $rows (in ExpiringSecrets::export() shape) and answer whether the disk now actually holds them. Swallows the RuntimeExceptions of an unusable state directory: durability is a courtesy, and the server has been authenticating out of memory alone until today. WHAT THE ANSWER IS FOR: a caller whose write carries a revocation may not treat "false" as courtesy — see discard().
discard(): boolMake the durable copy UNIMPORTABLE: delete it. A revocation that could not be written must still stand after a restart, and with no readable file load() imports nothing — every live session is signed out at the restart, which is the conservative direction (an availability cost, never a revoked row resurrected). True when nothing the loader could import remains: unlinked now, never there, or behind a directory the reader could not even resolve a path inside.

Tickets final class

Single-use WebSocket tickets (Appendix O §8.2).

MethodSummary
static new(?\Closure $clock = null): self
mint(string $sessionId): stringA ticket bound to the cookie session $sessionId.
consume(string $ticket): ?stringThe cookie session id $ticket was bound to, spending it; null when unknown or expired.
revokeAll(): void
pending(): int

TokenStore final class

The server's long-lived owner token (Appendix O §8.2).

MethodSummary
static new(string $dir): self
withOverride(?string $token): selfA store whose token is $token rather than the file's (null keeps the file). Refuses a token too short to stand in for 256 random bits.
dir(): stringThe private directory the token lives in (created and verified).
token(): stringThe owner token: the override, else the file's, minted on first use.
rotate(): stringReplace the token with a fresh one and return it. Every bearer client and every cookie minted from the old one stops authenticating once the server reloads it.
reload(): boolForget the cached token and read the file again (a serve token --rotate in another process replaced it). Answers whether the token changed. An override has no file behind it and never changes.
matches(string $candidate): bool

ViewerTokens final class

The viewer-token store (X-DESIGN1 D-1, reviews-1103 G4-G): shareable, revocable, READ-ONLY credentials for a second human watching sessions.

MethodSummary
static persisted(TokenStore $tokens, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?\Closure $log = null): selfA store backed by viewer-tokens.json beside the owner token. Nothing touches disk at construction: the state directory is only resolved at first use and the grants file is only ever written when there is a grant to add or a revocation to record — a cold, untouched store performs no write at all, so fixtures that never exercise viewer auth stay exactly as inert as they were.
grant(string $label, ?array $sessionIds = null, int $days = self::DEFAULT_DAYS): arrayMint a grant and return its row WITH the raw token attached — the one and only time the token exists outside the caller's hands.
match(string $candidate): ?arrayResolve a presented credential: the grant row when it is one of ours, still live, unknown-or-expired-or-revoked otherwise. A non-cv1_ candidate answers null without touching disk, so this stays cheap on the owner-token path that dominates every request.
list(): arrayThe live grants, newest first, for the admin listing: id, label, scopes, pinning and the clock stamps. The hash key and — by construction — the raw token are never present.
count(): intHow many live grants the store holds.
onRevoked(\Closure $listener): voidRun $listener with the grant id each time revoke() drops one, so the server can close the sockets that grant opened without waiting for a sweep. Rotation (revokeAll()) is not announced here: it has its own socket sweep in the server.
live(string $id): boolWhether a grant with $id is still live (unrevoked and unexpired).
revoke(string $id): boolDrop the grant with $id; answers whether one existed (the revoke RPC's only consumer-visible bit, and deliberately no richer answer that could probe which ids ever were).
revokeAll(): voidEvery grant dies — the rotation arm of AuthContext::reloadToken(). On a store with no file and nothing in memory this is a true no-op: it creates no directory, writes no file, and so stays safe for fixtures and overrides that never minted a viewer token.

ClientAddress final class

Who sent a request, and over what, as far as this server may believe.

MethodSummary
static of(ServerRequestInterface $request, array $trustedProxies): stringThe client's IP: the TCP peer, or — behind a trusted proxy — the right-most X-Forwarded-For entry that is not itself a trusted proxy. The text is the as-spelled form (the raw hop or stack-given peer); for a bucket or limiter key use key() so one client cannot mint many buckets with repr variants of the same address.
static key(string $address): stringThe canonical bucket key for $address (n04): one client, one limiter row, whatever spelling reached us. A %zone scope id is trimmed to the address it qualifies, an IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (what a dual-stack :: listener reports for every IPv4 peer, and any spelling a proxy-forwarded client can write) folds to the IPv4 it carries, and case/leading-zero compressed hex collapses through the same pack as normalise() does. Two genuinely different addresses never merge: text that is not an IP at all (the only way a key stays unparseable — the peer comes from the stack, and of() already refuses unparseable forwarded hops) stays byte-stable rather than collapsing into a shared '' bucket. Display keeps of()'s raw text; the guard's admission check keeps normalise().
static isSecure(ServerRequestInterface $request, array $trustedProxies): boolWhether the browser reached this server over TLS: a direct TLS connection (C-WEB-5.a — the listener itself answers --tls-cert/ --tls-key, and react/http stamps HTTPS=on on its server params), or a trusted proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto: https. Only a TRUSTED proxy may assert the latter; an untrusted one cannot forge the Secure flag.
static isValidRange(string $range): boolWhether $range is an IP address or an address/prefix CIDR.
static normalise(string $ip): string$ip in its canonical text form, an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:192.0.2.7, what a dual-stack :: listener reports for an IPv4 peer) as the IPv4 address it carries; '' when it is not an IP.
static normaliseRange(string $range): ?string$range (an IP or a CIDR) in canonical form — the address normalised as normalise() does, a mapped prefix shifted onto the IPv4 address (::ffff:10.0.0.0/104 is 10.0.0.0/8), a full-length prefix dropped; null when it is neither.
static inAny(string $ip, array $ranges): boolWhether $ip falls in any of $ranges (IPs or CIDRs; IPv4 and IPv6 never match each other, except that an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address — on either side — counts as the IPv4 address it carries).

The last handler in the chain: /ws to the upgrade, /api/* to the API, /s/{token} to the share pages when this server was told to have them, /canvas/{token} and POST /api/canvas to the sandboxed canvas pages when this server was told to have them, everything else to the static UI — with Responses::SECURITY_HEADERS on every answer except the 101, whose headers belong to RFC 6455, and except the canvas page, whose Responses::CANVAS_HEADERS survive the merge because an explicit header always wins.

SugarCraft\Code\Server\Push

PushPayloadCipher final class

The RFC 8291 aes128gcm payload encoder — implemented in-tree against the specification's own arithmetic, with ext-openssl primitives only (openssl_pkey_derive, hash_hkdf, openssl_encrypt), no new dependency. Every constant below is a spec line, not a preference:

MethodSummary
static new(): selfThe production cipher: random salt and a fresh ECDH pair per message.
withEntropy(callable $saltFactory, callable $localKeyPemFactory): selfA cipher whose randomness is supplied: the two factories answer the 16-octet salt and a local P-256 private-key PEM for each message. This exists so self::encrypt() can be pinned against the RFC 8291 Appendix A worked example; production calls new().
encrypt(string $plaintext, PushSubscription $subscription): stringThe encrypted application/octet-stream body — header and single record, ready to POST — for one subscription's message.

PushSubscription final class

One Web Push subscription as the browser hands it out (PushSubscription.toJSON() under RFC 8030): an endpoint URL, the user agent's P-256 ECDH public key, and the 16-octet authentication secret (RFC 8291 §3.1–§3.2). Both keys ride base64url without padding, exactly as the Web Push JavaScript surface serializes them.

MethodSummary
static new(string $endpoint, string $p256dh, string $auth): self
static endpointRefusal(string $endpoint): ?string
toArray(): array
host(): stringThe push resource URL's host, lowercased, without any port (443 is forced).
origin(): stringThe RFC 6454 origin of the endpoint — the VAPID aud claim value per RFC 8292 §2. The port is never included: endpointRefusal admits only 443, which is https' default and therefore not part of an origin.
requestTarget(): ?string
publicKeyBytes(): string
authSecretBytes(): string

PushSubscriptionStore final class

The Web Push subscription rows (C-WEB-5.d): push.json in the server's state directory, written through the house PrivateRetainedDir discipline — lstat the .partial, umask 077 so the mode settles 0600 BEFORE the rename publishes — exactly like Auth\SessionFileStore keeps sessions.json.

MethodSummary
static forStateDir(string $dir, ?\Closure $log = null): self
static keyHash(string $endpoint): stringThe map key of an endpoint: its sha256, hex. A public function so the unsubscribe side and the file agree without ever storing the raw endpoint as a key.
static ownerKey(string $credential): stringWhat a row records of the ONE credential that subscribed it: the digest of a viewer grant's public id or of a cookie session's id. Digested like the endpoint key, so the session id — itself a credential — never sits in push.json, and pruneCredential() can still find the rows by it.
put(PushSubscription $subscription, string $principal, bool $withName, ?string $credential = null): boolStore (or replace) $subscription's row under $principal. True only when the disk now holds it; an unusable state directory costs durability, never the connection — the client's own retry re-subscribes.
remove(string $endpoint, string $principal): boolDrop the row for $endpoint, but ONLY when it belongs to $principal — one credential class unregistering an endpoint can never drop another class's row (a cross-principal delete is the leak-shaped bug this gate exists to refuse). True when a row was removed.
prunePrincipal(string $principal): intDrop every row owned by $principal and report how many went — the store side of token revocation. Called with a principal whose credential is retired (rotated, logged out, revoked), it leaves that class nothing to notify.
pruneCredential(string $credential): intDrop every row the ONE credential $credential (a viewer grant's id or a cookie session's id) subscribed, and report how many went. The finer sibling of prunePrincipal(): revoking a single share grant or signing one browser out must not take the other viewers' or the owner's rows with it, and a class-wide prune cannot say that. Rows written before the owner was recorded carry none and are never matched here — they age out with the next rotation's class prune.
entries(): arrayEvery live row, each re-validated by PushSubscription::new at load. Rows a later trigger sends to are exactly these.

VapidKeys final class

The server's VAPID signing identity (RFC 8292): one P-256 key pair, created on first use in <state dir>/vapid.key (0600 inside the PrivateRetainedDir-verified 0700 state directory — the same discipline as the owner token, because this private key signs the identity every push service accepts) and reused for every later message so the identity is "consistent across multiple messages" as §2 requires.

MethodSummary
static new(string $dir, ?callable $clock = null): self
withSubject(?string $contact): selfA clone identifying the server as $contact in the JWT's sub claim — a mailto: or https: URI per RFC 8292 §2.1. RFC 8292bis retired the claim; with no argument this class sends the two mandatory ones.
publicKeyUncompressed(): string
publicKeyBase64Url(): string
tokenFor(string $audience): stringThe signed JWT for one push-service origin.
authorizationFor(string $audience): stringThe complete Authorization field value RFC 8292 §3 defines. The private key never appears anywhere in it; neither does the audience beyond the JWT's own aud claim.

Delivers one encrypted push message to one subscription's endpoint — asynchronously, through react/http's Browser, on the server's loop.

MethodSummary

Gateway final class

Multi-root serve (roadmap O-7, Appendix O §4.1 "Phase 7"): the MessageHandler in front of the server's own Dispatcher that sends the requests for OTHER project roots to a workspace-host child per root (WorkspaceHostClient, WorkspaceHostProcess).

MethodSummary
static new(Dispatcher $primary, ServerConfig $config, string $version, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?string $runDir = null, array $childEnv = []): selfA gateway over $primary, the server's own dispatcher for $config->root. Workspace hosts keep their listener and log in <stateDir>/workspaces unless $runDir says otherwise.
primary(): Dispatcher
primaryRoot(): stringThe canonical root the server's own dispatcher serves (a root naming it routes to the dispatcher, as rootFor() null).
start(): voidStart looking for idle hosts to recycle.
stop(string $reason = 'server shutting down'): voidStop every workspace host and the recycling; idempotent.

host(string $root): ?WorkspaceHostClient

rootFor(\stdClass $params): ?stringThe root a request goes to, or null for the server's own dispatcher: the seam an in-process caller shares with the wire (PL-5c-A design, section 2.1).
subscribeGeneration(string $sessionId): intThe generation of the latest session.subscribe forwarded for $sessionId (0 when none).
hasSubscribers(string $sessionId): boolWhether any relay target follows $sessionId.
useRoot(string $root, RelayTarget $target): voidRegister $target as a client of $root: it hears that root's server-scope events.
attachSubscriber(string $sessionId, RelayTarget $target): voidRegister $target as a subscriber of $sessionId, without a subscribe call (the caller made it).
setTargetCursor(string $targetId, string $sessionId, int $seq): voidSet $targetId's durable cursor for $sessionId: the seq it has been sent through.
rewindCursor(string $targetId, string $sessionId, int $seq): voidMove $targetId's durable cursor back, after an overflow the target did not deliver past.
detachSubscriber(string $sessionId, RelayTarget $target): void$target stops following $sessionId; the last subscriber leaving unsubscribes upstream.
detachTarget(RelayTarget $target): void$target leaves the gateway entirely: its root memberships, cursors and subscriptions (as a wire close does).
callQuietly(string $root, string $method, \stdClass $params): voidA best-effort call to $root's host whose answer nobody waits for: the compensation for a late answer (PL-5c-A design, section 4.1).
onOpen(Connection $connection): void
onMessage(Connection $connection, string $payload): void
onClose(Connection $connection, int $code): void
callRoot(string $root, string $method, \stdClass $params): PromiseInterfaceOne forwarded call to $root's host, as a promise of its answer (PL-5c-A design, section 2.1). The gateway's own bookkeeping runs here, for a wire client and an in-process one alike: the in-flight count, the deadline, learn(), the session cleanup of session.delete and the root tag. The caller attaches what is its own: a connection writes the frame and records its subscription, the in-process door records its sink. Exactly one of the answer, a refusal or the deadline settles it.

RelayTarget interface

Something the Gateway fans a workspace host's events out to: a client ConnectionTarget on the wire, or an in-process event sink (\SugarCraft\Code\Host\InProcessEventSink). The gateway keeps every subscriber, root client and durable cursor keyed by id(), so the two kinds share one bookkeeping table (PL-5c-A design, section 3.1).

MethodSummary
id(): stringThe key of this target in the gateway's tables. Never collides with another target's.
isOpen(): boolWhether the target is still connected.
accepts(?string $sessionId): boolWhether the target takes an event of $sessionId (null for a server-scope event). Asked before any cursor moves.
viewerSessions(): ?arrayThe sessions a viewer grant is pinned to, or null for an owner (no pin).
deliver(?array $message, string $text, ?string $coalesceKey, bool $ephemeral, ?int $seq, ?string $sessionId): voidOne relayed event. $message is the whole JSON-RPC notification (null when it could not be decoded); $text is its encoded form. $ephemeral marks a live-only event that may be shed under overflow, coalesced by $coalesceKey when given.
unfollowed(string $sessionId): voidThe gateway no longer forwards $sessionId to this target (its host was lost or retired).

Connection final class

The reason is capped to the 123 payload bytes a 2-byte code leaves in a 125-byte control frame, cut with mb_strcut() rather than substr(): a byte cut can split a multi-byte character (AuditHook idiom).

MessageHandler interface

What the WebSocket transport hands its traffic to. The transport (O-3a) owns framing, limits, control frames and authentication; the handler owns what a message MEANS — the candy-code.v1 JSON-RPC dispatcher (\SugarCraft\Code\Protocol\Dispatcher, O-3b) implements this, and a server built without one runs ProtocolPendingHandler.

MethodSummary
onOpen(Connection $connection): void$connection completed its upgrade and is authenticated.
onMessage(Connection $connection, string $payload): voidOne complete UTF-8 text message, within the size limit.
onClose(Connection $connection, int $code): void$connection is gone; $code is the close code seen or sent (1006 when none).

Outbox final class

One connection's queue of outgoing messages, with byte accounting (roadmap O-3b, Appendix O §6.9).

MethodSummary
static for(Connection $connection, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?\Closure $overflowNotice = null, int $softBytes = self::SOFT_WATERMARK_BYTES, int $hardBytes = self::HARD_WATERMARK_BYTES, float $graceSeconds = self::OVERFLOW_GRACE_SECONDS): self
push(string $text): voidA message that must arrive: a response, or a durable event.
pushEphemeral(array $message, ?string $coalesceKey = null): voidA live-only message: dropped under overflow. With $coalesceKey and a JSON-RPC notification whose params.data.text is a string, it may be merged into the queued message just before it with the same key.

Who is on the other end of one protocol client: the identity a call is judged by (its principal, its credential bucket, its viewer pins), and nothing about how bytes reach it.

DebouncedTranscriptWriter final class

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly float $delaySeconds = self::DELAY_SECONDS)
schedule(EnhancedSessionStore $store, string $sessionId, array $history): voidRecord $history as $sessionId's newest unsaved transcript.
atBoundary(array $history): boolWhether $history has reached a boundary a crash must not lose: a reply (assistant message) appended since the last call, or tool results landing on the last message. A user's own message is not one — it waits for the tick like any change, so submitting a turn stays out of update(). Text that only grows in place inside one reply is not a boundary either, so a streaming reply is not re-encoded per chunk. Stateful by design: the writer is the one object every call shares.
delaySeconds(): floatHow long the tick that writes a pending snapshot waits, in seconds.

hasPending(): boolTrue while a snapshot is waiting to be written.
__destruct()The other half of the shutdown hook. bin/candy-code discards the model Program::run() returns, so the last Chat — and this object with it — can be collected BEFORE shutdown functions run, and the weak hook would then find nothing to flush. Same owner-pid rule as the hook.

attachJsonlMirror(JsonlTranscriptWriter $mirror): selfC-SES-8.g: accept the JSONL mirror this store feeds after each committed transcript save. A service-side mutator, deliberately NOT a with* (S-X06 server-009: that name promises a new instance): EnhancedSessionStore owns a live PDO connection and the identity \WeakMaps, and the object Chat, the hooks and the picker all hold is exactly one per launch — a clone here would fork a second live store whose saves the launch never sees. So it sets and returns $this.
loadTranscript(string $sessionId): ?arrayThe session's transcript as raw message rows, oldest first, or null when there is nothing to resume.
identityOf(Message $message): ?arrayThe [id, ref] $message has, or null when it has none yet: the identity it carries (a reloaded row), else the one a save or assignIdentity() gave its row (roadmap O-2b).
assignIdentity(string $sessionId, Message $message): array$message's identity, allocated now from $sessionId's allocator when its row has none yet - so a host can name a row in an event BEFORE the debounced save reaches it, and that save then writes the same identity (it observes every given ref before allocating any).
appendSessionEvent(string $sessionId, string $type, array $payload = [], ?int $tsMs = null, int $retain = 0): intAppend one durable event to $sessionId's log and return its seq (roadmap O-2b; the session_events table, Appendix O §6.4).
sessionEvents(string $sessionId, int $afterSeq = 0, int $limit = 200, ?int $throughSeq = null): array$sessionId's events with a seq above $afterSeq, oldest first, at most $limit of them - one page of a replay. The rows are fetched in full before they are returned, so no read cursor stays open across a later INSERT (the WAL note on this store).
sessionEventBounds(string $sessionId): array[oldest, latest] seq in $sessionId's log: oldest is null when the log is empty, latest is 0 then. A replay cursor below oldest - 1 has lost events to retention and must resync from a snapshot (Appendix O §6.8).
appendUsageRecord(string $sessionId, Usage $usage, ?string $model = null, ?string $source = null): boolAppend one accounted provider call to the session's durable spend ledger (SES-1) and fold it into the row's cached cost_usd / cost_unpriced in the SAME transaction — the cache and the records may disagree only mid-write, never after one.
usageTotals(string $sessionId): ?arrayWhat $sessionId's durable ledger holds: call count, token sum, dollar sum, and whether ANY row was unpriced — or null when the session recorded nothing (a fresh launch and a session that only ever saw unreported calls are the same answer here, and neither needs a tracker).
usageDayModelRollups(?string $sessionId = null, ?int $windowDays = null): arrayThe durable ledger folded by DAY and MODEL — the rollup OBS-3's /usage answers from. Days come back newest-first, models alphabetically inside a day; $sessionId narrows to one session and null spans every session the table holds. Rows written before the model was threaded carry a null model and group together under it — the renderer says so honestly rather than inventing a name.
usageModelRollups(?string $sessionId = null, ?int $windowDays = null): arrayThe same ledger folded by MODEL alone, newest activity first — the per-model totals /usage prints under the day grid. $windowDays trims exactly as usageDayModelRollups() does, so the totals row, the model table and the day grid answer for one window.
usageSourceRollups(?string $sessionId = null, ?int $windowDays = null): arrayThe same ledger folded by SOURCE alone — the per-work attribution /usage sources answers from (C-SES-8.b). $windowDays trims exactly as usageDayModelRollups() does. Rows carry the delegated prompt tokens the model folds never show, and a source of NULL — every row written before attribution existed — groups together under it rather than being invented a name.
usageRollups(?string $sessionId = null, ?int $days = null): arrayBoth /usage folds answered from ONE read snapshot (OBS-3-P2).
resumedTokenTracker(string $sessionId): ?TokenTrackerA TokenTracker reseeded from the session's durable ledger, or null when the ledger is empty — the SES-1 resume seam. The launch hands the answer to Chat's tokenTracker: argument, whose ?? new TokenTracker() fallback keeps a fresh session starting at zero with byte-identical semantics to every launch before this table existed.
sessionCost(string $sessionId): ?floatThe cached dollar figure on the session row (SES-1) — see SessionStore::sessionCost().
latestResumableSession(): ?arrayThe most recently used session that holds a conversation — a saved transcript or at least one checkpoint — or null when none does.
latestResumableSessionFromCwd(?string $cwd): ?arrayThe --continue pick for THIS checkout (sugar_issues.md ISS-026).
pruneEmptySessions(?string $exemptSessionId = null, int $minAgeSeconds = 3600): intDelete sessions that never held anything: unnamed, no transcript, no checkpoint, no stored message, and untouched for at least $minAgeSeconds. Returns how many went.
checkpoint(string $sessionId, int $index): ?arrayRetrieve a specific checkpoint by index — a live one: a row a rewind moved onto the redo stack is not returned (see redoStack()).
getCheckpoint(string $sessionId, int $index): ?arrayBC forwarder for the pre-rename accessor name.
listCheckpoints(string $sessionId, int $limit = 100): arrayList recent live checkpoints for a session, newest first. Rows on the redo stack are left out (see redoStack()).
restoreCheckpoint(string $sessionId, int $index, ?array $redoTip = null, ?string $root = null): ?arrayRestore checkpoint $index and return its state data.
redoStack(string $sessionId): arrayThe redo stack, lowest index first: the first row is the state the conversation is at, each later one a step /redo can take, the last the state the first rewind left (tip). Empty when there is nothing to redo. Each row carries its workspace outcome (null when none was recorded), read without loading a message body.
redoCheckpoint(string $sessionId): ?arrayTake one step up the redo stack: the row above the lowest becomes the state the conversation is at, and the rows below it are live again. Reaching the tip ends the stack — the tip row is deleted (it is the state after the last turn, not a checkpoint taken before one) and its ref dropped once the write commits; the snapshot commit stays in the object store for the caller's file restore.
discardRedoStack(string $sessionId): voidDelete the redo stack of $sessionId outright — what the next saveCheckpoint() does on its own.
stripSessionCheckpoints(string $sessionId): intStrip EVERY checkpoint row of one session — gc purge --strip-checkpoints (gc-cli-1106 B3). This is the discardRedoStackRows() idiom widened from the redo stack (undone > 0) to the whole session, carrying its laws unchanged: workspace refs are queued before the rows vanish, and collectCheckpointBlobs() runs after, so message blobs only these checkpoints named stop being billed — purge never reimplements blob accounting. Returns the deleted row count.

SessionSearchIndex final class

The FTS5 side table behind withBodySearch (SES-2, plan_comparison §SES-2).

MethodSummary
static new(PDO $pdo, string $module = 'fts5'): selfOpen the index on the session store's connection. Never throws: a database without FTS5 (or one that refused the DDL for any other structural reason) comes back latched, and the caller degrades.
available(): boolFalse once the latch is set; while false every method is a no-op or null.
static observeSyncsForTesting(?callable $observer): voidTest seam: arm (or disarm with null) an observer fired at the top of every syncMessages() body — the pin for "the rebuild sweep runs inside a transaction". Keep the callable side-effect-free: an observer that throws lands in the sync's catch and marks the index dirty, so tests collect values and assert them outside.
needsRebuild(): boolTrue until this process has swept the transcripts (the first body search of a process the on-disk marker does not vouch for pays for it): no marker, a marker from a different INDEX_VERSION, a durably recorded failed sync, or a failure seen since the last sweep.
markBuilt(): voidThe store calls this after a successful clearAll()-plus-sweep, inside the sweep's last transaction: the marker lands atomically with the index it vouches for. A sync failure the sweep swallowed is written into the marker as dirty = 1 instead of being cleared away — this process answers from what it has (retrying a broken sweep on every search is the 128 s freeze all over again), and the NEXT process reads the durable flag and re-sweeps.
syncMessages(string $sessionId, array $bodies): voidUpsert $bodies — message id => body text — as the session's CURRENT indexed set: unchanged messages (hash equal) are untouched, changed ones keep their rowid and replace their FTS row, vanished ones (a rewind shortened the transcript) leave both tables. An empty body indexes nothing, and a message id that never had a row simply gets one.
search(string $query): ?arrayRanked body search: best-matching sessions first (bm25, lower is better), each with a snippet of its best hit. Null means "this index cannot answer" — latched, or a query with no indexable words — which the caller reads as "fall back to LIKE"; an empty array is a real answer meaning nothing matched.
static openForReadOnly(string $dbPath): ?selfOpen the index over a session database for READING only (C-CTX-3.d, the model-facing Memory recall). Null means there is nothing to ask: the database file does not exist, or the connect itself failed — the caller answers "no session index is available", never a throw.
searchScoped(string $query, ?string $cwd, ?string $excludeSessionId, int $limit): ?arrayRanked body search scoped to ONE project root, excluding one session (C-CTX-3.d): the model-facing recall leg. $cwd is the launch's root in the same raw form EnhancedSessionStore::createSession() stores (getcwd() ?: null), matched with = against the sessions table — the law the picker's own latestResumableSessionScoped already keeps; null answers across every root. $excludeSessionId drops that session's rows from the results entirely; the current session must never surface its own transcript back to the model as "a past session".
forgetSessions(array $ids): voidDrop every indexed row of $ids from BOTH tables. The FK cascade already took session_message_rows; the FTS table is virtual and un-cascaded, so this is where a deleted session's text actually goes, and leaving it to the garbage pass alone would keep searchable bodies of a session the user deleted.
collectGarbage(): voidReclaim FTS rows whose anchor row is gone (cascade deletes reach the anchor but never the virtual table). Space reclamation only — reads inner-join the anchor, so nothing stale is searchable before this runs.
clearAll(): voidEmpty both tables (the rebuild sweep starts from here).

listSessionsRanked(SessionQuery $query, array $ranked): arrayRows for the ids $ranked names, kept to every other condition in $query, returned in RANK order rather than recency order — the bodySearch read path of SES-2, where the FTS5 side table has already decided the order and this method only proves the row still qualifies (kind, archived, parent, LIKE search) and wears its snippet. pinnedFirst stays a LIKE-path nicety: a body search is ordered by bm25 from the first row, which is the whole feature.

It lives here rather than as a raw UPDATE on EnhancedSessionStore's side of the door because the memoised listSessions() rows invalidate on THIS connection's sessionWriteSeq: a write that skipped this method would leave the picker showing yesterday's sum out of the very connection that changed it.

GcInventory final class

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly string $dbPath)
collect(int $retentionDays): arrayFull machine-readable inventory. Snake_case keys are the stable JSON layout documented on GcStatus rendering (README + gc subcommand doc).
static reclaimableBytes(PDO $connection): intFree pages times page size — the space vacuum could hand back on this connection, measured NOW. static columnsOf(PDO $connection, string $table): array

Callers that delete must re-probe per file immediately before unlinking — an inode that was free at sweep time can gain a holder at any moment, and a lock that gains one is somebody's running session.

GcOrphanCensus final class

Read-only orphan census for gc analyze (gc-cli-1106 B2).

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly PDO $connection, private readonly string $configDir)
census(int $now): array
orphanJournals(int $now): arrayTranscript journals whose session id is neither live nor inside the tombstone grace window. Non-session-shaped files are never accused (scanJournals' id law), and the whole scan refuses to run without the sessions table (nothing to disprove).
orphanJournalPaths(int $now): arrayThe SAME accusation as orphanJournals(), as targets: accused session id => its journal paths. gc purge --clean-orphan-journals unlinks through this list, so the census and the cleanup can never disagree about which file is an orphan (gc-cli-1106 B3).
orphanRowTarget(string $table, int $now): ?arrayThe accusation predicate for one orphan row family, with the params that complete it: gc purge --clean-orphan-events, --clean-orphan-usage and --clean-imports DELETE through the SAME fragment the census counts with, so cleanup can never reap a row the diagnostic did not accuse (gc-cli-1106 B3 single-source law). Returns null when the family is not accusable at all (missing table, missing session_id, or no sessions table to disprove against).
listStaleLockPaths(): arrayThe stale half as paths, from the SAME sweep staleLocks() counts through: gc purge --clean-locks deletes exactly these, re-probing each inode immediately before its unlink (a lock that gains a holder mid-run is somebody's live session and must survive).
abandonedShadowDirectories(int $now): arrayThe accusation above as targets: hash => {bytes, mtime, path}. gc purge --clean-shadows deletes exactly these directories — same claim-law (a dir any live cwd hashes to is owned; a young unknown may be mid-checkpoint), one walk, no second copy (gc-cli-1106 B3).
expiredTombstoneTarget(int $now): ?arrayThe expired-grave predicate with its params, shared by the count above and gc purge --clean-expired-tombstones below — SessionStore only reaps these opportunistically on its next write, so the census names the reap and purge performs it through the same fragment.

MethodSummary
static websocketUrl(string $url): ?stringThe websocket URL for a user-typed target, or null when it is not an address attach could dial at all (Attach::websocketUrl() — the one mapping, so the handoff arm and the CLI never disagree on shape).
static isLoopbackHost(string $host): boolWhether a host names this machine: loopback BY NAME (localhost, ::1) or a numeric dotted-quad inside 127.0.0.0/8. The 127. leg matches OCTETS ONLY (C-SES-7.g r1): 127.attacker.example starts like an address but RESOLVES wherever its owner points it, and a plain ws:// dial to it would carry the transcript and bearer token in the clear to exactly the stranger this gate exists to refuse.
static dialAllowed(?string $wsUrl): boolThe law the dial obeys: wss:// always, ws:// only to a loopback host. Checked on the mapped URL BEFORE any socket opens, because a transcript is not something to send in the clear to a stranger.
static fitsWithinImportBound(string $content): boolThe one bound session.import enforces server-side, read here so an over-large transcript is refused before the dial instead of mid-wire.
static resolveToken(): ?stringThe owner token, exactly as attach resolves it: the environment override, else the state directory's token file — read, never minted (a client must not create the credential a server has not got). The resolver is deliberately a second reader, not TokenStore::token(), which rotates on a miss.
static push(string $wsUrl, string $token, string $content, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, ?float $answerBound = null): PromiseInterfaceDial, say hello, import the transcript, and hand back the NEW remote session id. The socket attach opened is closed on every settled path — success, wire error, malformed answer or expired answer window — so a teleport never leaves a half-open attachment on the target.

SessionImportLedger final class

The side table that remembers what was imported from where, opened on the session database the way \SugarCraft\Code\Share\ShareStore opens its own table — same file, same WAL, same restrictive umask dance, and the same fail-safe law: a store opened read-only keeps the shape it has, every reader falls to null and every writer is a no-op rather than a crash.

MethodSummary
static atPath(string $dbPath): selfA ledger over the session database at $dbPath. The file is created (or reused) exactly as ShareStore::atPath() does, so opening the ledger of an existing store never re-permissions anything and a fresh one is never briefly world-readable.
path(): string
lookup(string $sourceKey): ?arrayThe stored row for one source key, or null when nothing was imported from it (or the table cannot be read).
remember(string $sourceKey, string $sessionId, int $items, string $digest): voidRecord (or refresh) the import of $sourceKey into $sessionId.

SessionImporter final class

The importer core behind crush import (C-SES-7.b) and its RPC sibling (C-SES-7.e): recognise a foreign (or own-format) transcript, flatten it into Messages, and persist it as a NEW main session whose provider is import:<source>, so the FTS index rides the incremental sync of EnhancedSessionStore::saveTranscript() and an imported session is body-searchable the moment it lands — no rebuild, anywhere.

MethodSummary
static new(?int $maxItems = null, ?int $maxBytes = null): self
withBounds(?int $maxItems = null, ?int $maxBytes = null): selfAn importer with different bounds; the receiver is untouched.
importFile(EnhancedSessionStore $store, string $path, ?ImportFormat $format = null, ?string $name = null): ImportedTranscriptImport the transcript file at $path — a path the person at the terminal named, read exactly once, into $store.
importString(EnhancedSessionStore $store, string $raw, ?ImportFormat $format = null, ?string $name = null, string $sourceKey = 'string:import'): ImportedTranscriptImport an in-memory transcript. $sourceKey is the ledger identity a re-import is compared against; for files it is the resolved path.

ShareStore final class

The shares table — self-hosted share pages (SES-3, COMPARISON §6.5).

MethodSummary
static revokeForSessionsSql(int $sessionIdCount): stringThe statement that revokes every LIVE share published from a chunk of session ids. It lives HERE, beside the table it writes, because SessionStore::deleteSessionTrees() runs it inside the very transaction that removes those sessions (C-SES-3): a session that is gone must not leave /s/{token} answering for the rest of the expiry window. Copying the SQL into the session store would let the schema and its revocation law drift apart unnoticed.
static atPath(string $dbPath): selfA store over the session database at $dbPath. The file is created with the same restrictive umask dance SessionStore uses, so a database that does not exist yet is never briefly world-readable.
path(): string

revoke(string $token): boolRevoke by token. True only when a LIVE row flipped; revoking an unknown, already-revoked or expired token answers false without distinguishing them (same no-oracle law as lookup()).
liveForSession(string $sessionId): arrayLive shares published from one session, newest first — what /share revoke without a token lists when there is more than one to choose between.
liveAll(): arrayEvery LIVE share across ALL sessions, newest first, each paired with its owning session's name when that row still exists.
purgeInertRows(): intgc purge --clean-shares entry point (gc-cli-1106 B3): the publish sweep, callable on purpose. The DELETE law is the private sweepInertRows() verbatim — this mints no second rule, it only lifts the existing one to a named door and reports how many inert rows left the table.

LearnedSkills final class

The versioned store of LEARNED skills — the live half of C-EXT-3.e, under owner ruling R-EXT-2 (plan §6.3): a model-written skill goes live immediately and every landing is announced with an undo door, so the history kept here is what makes that undo real.

MethodSummary
static new(?string $home = null): selfThe store under $home (null: HomeDirectory::owned()), or with no owned home one whose every write refuses — the draft store's own law.
liveRoot(): ?string~/.candy-code/skills, or null with no owned home.
isLive(string $name): boolWhether the user tier holds $name as a plain (non-link) SKILL.md.
liveSkillPath(string $name): ?stringWhere a learned skill's live file is (or was just) written — the path the R-EXT-2 announcement names. Null with no owned home; a name that never survived the sanitiser has no path to name.
create(SkillProposal $proposal): LearnedSkillRevisionWrite $proposal as a NEW live learned skill with saved revision 1, and answer the revision.
patch(string $name, ?string $description, ?string $body): LearnedSkillRevisionPatch the learned skill $name: fields left null keep what the newest saved revision holds; the merged file lands as revision N+1 and becomes the live SKILL.md. Only user-tier skills the store itself wrote (their history carries at least one revision) can be patched — a skill that arrived through /skills accept or a hand-written file is refused, because this store would be overwriting bytes it never versioned.
undo(string $name): arrayThe undo door R-EXT-2's announcement names. Revert $name to the state its saved history holds:
history(string $name): arrayWhat the history directory holds for $name: the live flag, each active revision's number, bytes and mtime (ascending), and how many older revisions sit in the archive. Content is never read here — a listing that slurped every body would be the walk this store refuses.
revisionCount(string $name): intThe revision count a refusal or announcement may quote without walking twice.

Null when no name starts with $partial, or the matches add nothing to it.

The single extractor both the renderer's ✨ skill: <name> head and Chat's loaded-notice read, so the row and the notice can never disagree about what ran.

SkillOrigin enum

WHO put a skill's SKILL.md where candy-code found it — the provenance tier, as opposed to SkillSource, which is the file's FORMAT (native, Claude Code, opencode).

Cases: BuiltIn · User · Project

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
static precedence(): arrayEvery tier, LOWEST precedence first — the one statement of which tier wins a skill-name collision, read by every merge that can shadow a skill (SkillLoader::loadAll(), SkillLoader::manifestTiers(), ForeignSkillDiscovery, SkillManager::loadAll()). The merges are last-write-wins, so the last tier listed is the one that keeps a name.
badge(SkillSource $format): stringThe text inside a listing line's brackets: the tier, plus the foreign format when the file is another tool's (project, foreign: claude). A native skill names its tier only — the format adds nothing there.

Daemonize final class

The one daemonize sequence, in the two shapes its two callers need (Appendix O §4.6; roadmap O-4a).

MethodSummary
static code(): stringThe sequence as PHP source for a php -r launcher: each parent exits 0, a failed fork exits 1, and the code that follows runs in the daemon.

In the ORIGINAL process this returns once the intermediate child has forked the daemon and been reaped.
static redirectStdio(string $logPath): boolPoint stdin at /dev/null and stdout + stderr at $logPath (appending, created 0600). Called by detach() and again after the log is rotated, so the daemon writes to the fresh file rather than the renamed one. Returns false — changing nothing it could not complete — when the log cannot be opened.

McpLoginFork final class

MCP-5: the process slots behind an in-TUI mcp auth login <server>.

MethodSummary
static arm(string $server, array $rest, string $cwd = ''): arrayOpen a login child for $server.
static poll(string $server): ?McpLoginProgressMsgOne non-blocking look at the child: drain output, judge the beat. Never returns null while a slot lives — Cmd::tick() is a ONE-SHOT timer, so silence answers as a waiting beat that Chat uses to re-arm the next look. A gone beat when the slot is absent is Chat's cue to stop re-arming without printing anything.
static isArmed(string $server): boolWhether a slot for $server is live (pins and teardown use this).
static redirectPort(string $server): ?intThe loopback port the announced login URL asked the browser to call back on, parsed from its redirect_uri — the handle C-MCP-4.c correlates a hit callback against, readable while the slot lives and after the done beat retires it. Null when nothing was announced yet or the URL carried no parseable redirect_uri.
static releaseAll(): voidTear every live slot down: SIGTERM, then a blocking proc_close reap. There is no TERM-then-KILL ladder here — the wait is bounded not by an escalation rung but by the child's own deadline (OAuthLoopbackFlow self-exits after its wait budget — 300 s by default, or the explicit --timeout the login line passed through arm() — no matter what signal it sees). TEST HYGIENE ONLY, and nothing on the quit path calls it — by design: a login still running when the TUI exits is deliberately left to finish. The child's loopback bind is to port 0 (OAuthLoopbackFlow), so a survivor cannot block the next login's bind, and a grant stored after the parent is gone still attaches at the NEXT launch, exactly as the done beat announces. That self-exit, not a shutdown rung here, is the process hygiene; the zero-production-caller census is pinned in the fork's own test, so wiring a call site is a product change (quit would abort in-flight logins) that must re-derive this paragraph in the same commit.
static pollCmd(string $server): \ClosureThe Cmd Chat arms after every beat but the last: one poll per second on the shared loop, silent while the child is quiet. The tick is the only sleeper — the TUI keeps painting and taking keys throughout the browser leg, which was the entire point of forking.

MediaStore final class

The artifact home: generated media lands at ~/.candy-code/media/<session>/ — 0700 directories, 0600 files, and a publish that is atomic in the .partial + rename shape this repo already trusts in PrivateDir and Server/StateDir (plan W1.9, Appendix C-3: HOME store for now, a Wave-7 revisit for workspace placement).

MethodSummary
static forSession(string $sessionId, ?string $root = null, ?string $pattern = null, ?callable $writer = null): selfOpen (creating when absent) the store for one session under $root — by default ~/.candy-code/media, rooted at HomeDirectory::owned() so an unestablishable home throws instead of silently storing under a world-writable stand-in.
directoryPath(): stringAbsolute path of this store's 0700 session directory.
sessionId(): stringThe sanitized session directory name this store writes into.
put(string $bytes, string $ext, array $tokens = [], MediaKind $kind = MediaKind::Image): MediaArtifactPublish one artifact under the pattern-shaped name and return the media reference whose path is absolute and whose tokenValues carry the filled map plus the missing_tokens / unknown_tokens notes.
putDocument(string $bytes, string $ext): stringPublish a document artifact and return its absolute path.
list(): arrayEvery published artifact of this session, name-sorted. In-flight .partial files and non-regular entries are not listed.
pathFor(string $artifactId): ?stringAbsolute path of the artifact whose id is $artifactId, or null when the session holds no such file. An id carrying a separator or control byte is refused, not searched — same early-exit law as the session id. (The path itself is always rebuilt from a scandir entry, so a matching id can never steer it out of the session directory; the containment re-check on the found entry is what bounds a planted symlink.)
read(string $artifactId): ?stringBytes of a stored artifact, or null when the id names nothing.
delete(string $artifactId): boolRemove one artifact by id; false when the id names nothing. Age sweeps are sweepExpiredDirs(), not this method.
adopt(string $stem, string $bytes, string $ext): stringTake a copy of bytes the caller already holds under an exact name the caller computes — the fold that makes a transcript ref fetchable when the file it names lives OUTSIDE this store (C-WEB-1.d: a Read of a workspace image carries bytes on the tool result and a workspace path; media.fetch serves only this store, so the projection adopts the copy rather than emitting a ref that could only 404).
static sweepExpiredDirs(int $days, ?int $now = null, ?string $mediaRoot = null): intDelete whole session directories whose last publish aged past $days (review rv-devops-4), returning how many went. Called from the launch retention path (\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\AgentManager::pruneSessionArtifacts()) only when CANDY_CODE_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS is positive — off by default, exactly like the session sweep it joins.
static idOf(string $filename): stringStable artifact id: the stored name minus its final extension.

Hands out transcript row identities for ONE session (roadmap 1.B-1): a monotonic ref (1, 2, 3, …, never reused) and the storage id derived from it, m_<session>_<ref>.

static new(string $sessionId, int $nextRef = 1): selfAn allocator for $sessionId whose next ref is $nextRef (clamped to 1).
sessionId(): string
nextRef(): intThe ref the next fresh row would be given - the persisted high-water mark.

A check that throws once the process a delegated agent run started under is gone — shared by \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\BuiltIn\TaskTool and \SugarCraft\Code\Agents\EngineExecutor, the two places a whole agentic run executes inside a forked child.

PermissionAskRelay final class

The wire one forked member of a concurrent tool group uses to put a permission question to the process that forked it (roadmap 1.C-5).

MethodSummary
static open(): ?selfOpen a relay — the forking side, before the fork. Null when no socket pair can be made; the member then keeps the approver it inherited, which refuses with ChildChannel::GRANDCHILD_REFUSAL: a stated refusal, never a silent grant.
childApprover(): \ClosureThe member's half: drop the turn child's end, give up the inherited copy of the turn socket (ChildChannel::releaseInherited() — this process now has a channel of its own, so the turn's can only be written by accident), and return the approver that puts each question up this relay and blocks until it is answered.
becomeReader(): voidThe forking side's half, after the fork: drop the member's end and make the read end non-blocking so a poll never stalls the reap loop.
readStream(): mixedThe read end, for the reap loop's stream_select(); null once closed.
takeAsks(): arrayEvery question the member has put since the last call, each as the call it is about and the ASK it carries, keyed by ask id. A frame that is not a well-formed ask is skipped; a stream that stopped parsing is closed (the member then sees EOF and settles its question unanswered).
reply(string $askId, ApprovalVerdict $verdict): voidAnswer one question with the turn child's verdict. A member that is already gone costs nothing: the write fails quietly and the reap loop reports the member's own exit.
close(): void
static askId(ToolCall $call): stringThe ask id both ends name a question by — the D1 hash, so it is the id the turn child's own channel will put to the parent.
static verdictFromReply(array $frame): ApprovalVerdictThe verdict a reply frame carries, exactly as the turn child settled it.

static groupsSpawns(): boolWhether a spawn through spawnSpec() lands in a group this package can kill wholesale — true exactly when some detach prefix probed clean. This feeds the background-shell registry's grouped flag: the narration must tell the truth about what kill -- -PGID will reach.
static setDetachedSpawnCandidatesForTesting(?array $candidates): voidForce the detach-candidate list for the duration of a test (null restores host derivation). Clears the memo so the next resolution re-probes; callers must restore null in tearDown.
static childLeadsOwnGroup(int $pid, int $deadlineNs): boolExternal leadership POLL: does this pid lead, or at least fail to contradict, its own process group — judged from OUTSIDE the child?
static detachedSpawnBinary(): stringFirst token of the proven detach prefix — the setsid(1) path when that arm won the probe, the PHP binary when the helper arm won — or '' when this host offers no usable detach at all.
static spawnSpec(string|array $command): string|arrayThe command to hand proc_open(): the original command prefixed by the proven detach wrapper when the host offers one, unchanged otherwise.
static env(array $overrides = []): arrayThe inherited environment with NONINTERACTIVE_ENV forced over it and STRIPPED_ENV_NAMES removed, then $overrides applied last so a site's own required keys (API tokens, hook context) still win.
static scrubbedEnv(array $overrides = [], array $unset = []): arrayenv() with the credentials removed — the environment for the spawn paths whose output the MODEL reads: Bash and Grep (through \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\Concerns\CapturesProcessOutput) and script hooks (\SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\ScriptHook).
static mcpEnv(array $declared = []): arrayThe environment for an MCP stdio server (item 0.14-b, decision D3): scrubbedEnv() with the server's own .mcp.json env block — ${VAR} already resolved — applied LAST.
static strippedSecretEnvNames(array $declared = []): arrayThe inherited credential-shaped names mcpEnv() withholds for a server declaring $declared — sorted, for a launch notice. Names only, never values.
static isSecretEnvName(string $name): boolWhether $name is credential-shaped: one of PROVIDER_SECRET_ENV_NAMES, or a match for a SECRET_ENV_PATTERNS shape. Case-insensitive, because a lower-case github_token is just as much a token and an over-eager scrub costs a script one variable while an under-eager one costs the credential.
static secretEnvAllowed(string $name): boolWhether the installed allowlist lets credential-shaped $name through.
static useSecretEnvAllowlist(array $entries): voidInstall the operator's secretEnvAllowlist for every later scrubbedEnv() in this process (and its forks). Replaces, never appends, so a re-read config cannot accumulate stale entries; blank and non-string entries are dropped, and [] restores the full scrub.
static secretEnvAllowlist(): arrayThe allowlist useSecretEnvAllowlist() installed.
static cdGuard(string $dir): stringThe cd DIR || exit 1 guard line every /bin/sh -c script that must run inside DIR starts with — ONE spelling for Bash and interactiveSpawnCommand() (the copy that kept the old form).
static awaitGroupLeader(int $pid): voidThe detached wrapper makes the child its own process-group leader a moment after proc_open() returns, and the timeout's group kill needs that group id. Read it with a bounded wait so a fast spawn cannot be measured before the wrapper has run. Only leadership ends the wait early: a wrapper that exits before it leads stays a zombie until reaped, and posix_getpgid() still answers for it with its parent's group, so that case pays the cap.
static groupId(mixed $process): ?intThe process-group id a containment-aware kill should target, or null when the child does not lead its own group.
static terminate(mixed $process, int $signal = 15): boolSignal a (possibly wrapped) child in a way that reaches its descendants: group kill when the child leads a group, proc_terminate() otherwise.
static interactiveAvailable(): boolWhether this host can run a child attached to a REAL pty — the gate the layer-C opt-in consults before promising anything.
static interactiveBashMissing(): boolWhether this host needs a Git-for-Windows bash.exe for the interactive path and does not have one — the §6.3 law's stat half. The Windows interactive spawn argv is bash.exe -c (see interactiveSpawnCommand()); ConPTY can carry any program, so the availability gate alone would promise a terminal the plan forbids this path to fall back into: cmd.exe is not a substitute, and its quoting and command grammar cannot carry a bash script. Callers refuse with WindowsShell::BASH_MISSING_NOTICE — naming the install to fix — before a byte is spawned. Pure stat (PATH walk plus one is_file), never a spawn, and on a non-Windows host the family read short-circuits the locate walk to false, so the POSIX cost of the caller's extra gate is zero.
static resetInteractiveAvailabilityForTesting(): voidDiscard the memoized host verdict so the next interactiveAvailable() re-derives it from the same STATs. Testing seam only — production callers never reset a per-process fact mid-run; the reset exists so one host can pin both the interactive-spawn branch and the 126-refusal branch instead of leaving whichever the box does not match as dead code.
static interactiveSpawnCommand(string $command, ?string $cwd = null, array $jailArgvPrefix = []): arrayThe argv for a pty spawn: $command through the platform's bash — /bin/sh on POSIX, Git-for-Windows' bash.exe on Windows (C-TUI-6.d, §6.3) — entered in $cwd when one is given. There is no cmd.exe leg: a Windows host without bash.exe is refused upstream through interactiveBashMissing() before this argv ever reaches a spawn, so the never-fall-back-to-cmd.exe law is structurally kept, not merely documented.
static terminatePid(int $pid, int $signal = 15): boolSignal a child by PID, reaching its group when it leads one and itself otherwise — the proc_open-free twin of terminate().
static killTree(int $pid, float $termGraceSeconds = 0.0): voidKILL $pid AND EVERYTHING IT STARTED — the public group-kill entry point for any site that tears down a forked child of this package (Runtime's parallel deadline, AgentWorkerPool, the custom-command ! runner). A site that runs inside an event-loop callback — EngineBackend's turn teardown and Chat's cancel sites — calls killTreeAsync() instead, which runs this same sequence one loop tick per pass.
static killTreeAsync(int $pid, ?\React\EventLoop\LoopInterface $loop = null, float $termGraceSeconds = 0.0): \React\Promise\PromiseInterfacekillTree() WITHOUT HOLDING THE CALLER'S THREAD — the spelling for a teardown that runs inside an event-loop callback (the Escape-Escape cancel of an engine turn, a Chat tool fan-out or a forked hook chain). Resolves once signal 9 has gone out to the whole tree; like killTree() it never reaps.
static reapAsync(array $pids, float $budgetSeconds, float $pollSeconds = 0.005, ?\React\EventLoop\LoopInterface $loop = null): \React\Promise\PromiseInterfaceCollect already-signalled children of this process on a loop timer instead of a usleep() loop: one WNOHANG pass now, then one every $pollSeconds until every pid is collected or $budgetSeconds is spent. Resolves with the pids it could NOT collect (empty when all were), so a caller with a straggler list can keep them for a later sweep.
static closeOnExec(mixed $stream): boolMark $stream's descriptor FD_CLOEXEC so no command spawned afterwards inherits it; true when the flag is now set.
static locateOnPath(string $binary): stringFirst executable named $binary on the process PATH, or '' when absent.

ProcessReaper final class

Bounded shutdown for a proc_open() child: SIGTERM, a polled grace period, then signal 9 — and only then proc_close().

MethodSummary
static terminateAndClose(mixed $process, ?int $groupPid = null): ?intSIGTERM, poll, signal 9, poll, proc_close().
static terminateAndAwaitExit(mixed $process, ?int $groupPid = null): boolSIGTERM, poll, signal 9, poll — and STOP THERE: never proc_close().
static escalate(callable $signal, callable $isGone, float $terminateGrace = self::TERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS, float $killGrace = self::KILL_GRACE_SECONDS, ?callable $onEscalate = null): boolTHE ladder, single-sourced by E676: signal 15, bounded wait, signal 9, bounded wait — expressed over CALLABLES so the proc_open() children of terminateAndAwaitExit(), the deadline-polling expiry paths of \SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\ScriptHook and \SugarCraft\Code\Config\StatusLineCommand, and the pcntl_fork()ed worker of \SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSessionRunner share ONE escalation sequence instead of each keeping a private copy. Three hand-rolled ladders is one too many: a copy is where a rung drifts.
static escalateAsync(LoopInterface $loop, callable $signal, callable $isGone, ?callable $done = null, float $terminateGrace = self::TERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS, float $killGrace = self::KILL_GRACE_SECONDS, ?callable $onEscalate = null): voidThe same ladder as escalate(), driven by loop timers instead of usleep(): the TERM and KILL waits each tick on $loop at the poll cadence, so a wedged child costs the loop NOTHING while it waits. The gateway recycles hosts on its own event loop; the sync ladder would freeze every other connection's frames for up to both budgets. CLI call sites keep the sync variant — they have no loop to yield to.
static terminateAndCloseAsync(LoopInterface $loop, mixed $process, ?int $groupPid = null, ?callable $then = null): voidAsync twin of terminateAndClose(): ladder on loop timers, then the reap once the child is gone. $then gets the exit status.
static reapWhenExited(LoopInterface $loop, mixed $process, ?callable $then = null): voidReap a child on loop timers, never blocking: answer at once when it has already exited, otherwise poll every POLL_INTERVAL_US and proc_close() the tick it is seen gone.
static reapIfExited(mixed $process, float $budgetSeconds = self::TERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS): ?intReap a child that has ALREADY EXITED, and NEVER signal one that has not.
static waitForExit($process, float $budgetSeconds): boolPoll proc_get_status() until the child is gone or the budget runs out; true if it exited. A bounded poll rather than a blocking wait, for the reason this class exists at all: an unflagged wait is precisely the thing being replaced.

ProcessTree final class

Read-only view of the kernel's process table through /proc — the half of ProcessContainment::killTree() that answers "who descends from this pid, and which process group is each of them in".

MethodSummary
static available(): boolWhether this host exposes a readable /proc/<pid>/stat at all.
static parseStat(string $line): ?arrayThe fields of one /proc/<pid>/stat line this package needs, or null for a line that does not parse.
static stat(int $pid): ?arrayOne pid's parsed stat, or null when it is gone (or /proc is absent).
static snapshot(): ?arrayEvery process the kernel lists right now, keyed by pid, or null when /proc cannot be read. A process that exits between the directory read and its stat read is simply absent — the scan is a snapshot, and its caller (ProcessContainment::killTree()) re-scans until stable.
static descendants(int $pid, ?array $snapshot = null): arrayEvery pid below $pid in the parent→child relation, breadth first, NOT including $pid itself. Read from $snapshot when one is given (so a caller can pair the walk with the states of the same scan), from a fresh snapshot() otherwise; empty when /proc is absent.

The SSRF egress rule, in one place.

SubAgentActivityRelay final class

The wire one forked member of a concurrent tool group uses to hand its SubAgentActivity beats back to the process that forked it.

MethodSummary
static open(): ?selfOpen a relay — the parent's half, called before the fork. Null when no socket pair can be made; that member then runs exactly as it would without one (its beats are dropped), which is a blank row, not a broken turn.
childSink(): ActivitySinkThe child's half: drop the read end and return the sink that writes each beat onto the relay.
becomeReader(): voidThe parent's half, called after the fork: drop the write end (the child holds its own copy) and make the read end non-blocking so a drain never stalls the reap loop.
readStream(): mixedThe read end, for a stream_select() that waits on beats instead of sleeping; null once closed.
drain(): arrayEvery beat that has arrived since the last drain, in wire order. A datagram that does not decode is skipped; the ones around it are kept.
unfinished(): arrayThe latest beat of every run this reader saw start but never saw finish, in the order they started. Meaningful once the member's process has exited and a final drain() has run: then nothing more can arrive, and each of these runs ended without saying so.
close(): void

static runtimeNeedsIt(): boolWhether THIS PHP runtime has the blocking-pipe behavior: the real OS, never WindowsShell's injectable family.
static available($pipe): intBytes readable from $pipe right now, without blocking.
static readAvailable($pipe, int $max = 8192): stringRead what is already waiting in $pipe, at most $max bytes; never blocks.
static runningProbe($process): \ClosureChild-still-running probe for ChildPump::drain(running:).
static stageStdin(string $bytes): ?stringStage stdin bytes as a private temp file for a ['file', $path, 'r'] descriptor (a Windows stdin pipe write can block past any deadline); null when it cannot be written. The caller removes it after the reap.
static drainUntilExit(array $pipes, \Closure $running, float $deadline, int $maxBytes = \PHP_INT_MAX): arrayThe whole Windows read loop for a caller that only collects output: read until the child exits (and a last pass finds nothing) or the deadline.
static pumpUntilExit(array $pipes, \Closure $running, \Closure $onChunk): voidStreaming twin of drainUntilExit(): poll the output pipes until the child has exited and a last pass finds nothing, handing every chunk to $onChunk(slot, bytes) as it arrives. No deadline: the caller's own contract (a long-running agent turn) owns that.

With neither bound the call rides the spawn-time default desk byte-identically to the pre-C-MCP-3.b wire; with the approver bound a elicitation/create is put to the human in the AskUser modal shape, and with the emitter bound each notifications/progress becomes a ToolProgress frame. $elicitationsClosed is the -p latch: once \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\NonInteractive::withoutInteractiveUser() has closed the run, no later binding may re-open the ask channel.
