A stdio tools/call is unbounded by design (E646), and an MCP tool always runs alone — it is a barrier, never ParallelSafe — so without the beat any call longer than the turn's 120 s idle ceiling cost the whole turn rather than just the wait.
withPermissionApprover(\Closure $approver): ToolRelaysPermissionAsks: the turn's ask channel, relayed into the per-call answer desk so elicitation/create reaches the human (the modal shows the AskUser shape, C-MCP-3.b). Once withoutInteractiveUser() has closed the run, a later binding is IGNORED — the -p decision is made once at launch, the same sticky law \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\NonInteractive::withoutInteractiveUser() enforces for AskUserTool.
withToolProgressEmitter(\Closure $emit): selfAcceptsToolProgress: the turn's live-tail channel, fed by notifications/progress frames the server pushes mid-call. Progress is NOT an ask — it survives even a closed -p run, where nobody is queried and the frames only ever stream into the running row.
withoutInteractiveUser(string $why): selfThe -p closure: elicitations cancel and no later approver re-opens the channel. $why rides the same funnel argument the AskUser/ PlanExit closures pass; the bridge stores no copy because a canceled elicitation is announced to the server by its ACTION, and the model learns the silence from the server's own follow-up, not from prose we would invent here.
withBackgroundAfter(float $seconds): selfC-MCP-3.d: arm the background hand-off threshold. Only the interactive turn wiring calls this; even when armed, a copy that later passes through withoutInteractiveUser() is refused by McpBackgroundCalls::armed() through the latch, and the latch cannot be un-closed by re-arming.
static askElicitation(?\Closure $approver, string $server, string $callId, array $questions): mixedAnswer one server elicitation through the turn's ask channel: each schema field becomes a short question in the AskUser modal shape, in declaration order, and the person's words are coerced to the field's declared type. A multi-field form is therefore a SHORT SERIES of modals — the risk the plan disclosed — not a new form UI.
static progressSink(\Closure $emit, string $callId, string $toolName): \ClosureThe sink that turns each notifications/progress parameter map into a ToolProgress frame on the turn's channel, seq counting from 1.
static scrubServerText(string $text): stringOne line of untrusted server copy, safe for a single TUI row / web card line: control bytes collapse to spaces and the two mouse-zone sentinel codepoints are swept, because a progress tail rides marked frames downstream (the fleet's untrusted-content law).
static replyResult(array $raw, string $id, float|int $start, string $server, string $tool, callable $truncate): ToolResultTurn one raw tools/call reply into the ToolResult envelope the bridge has always produced — same announcement, same renderer, same error-flag precedence; only the truncation budget arrives as a closure.
static elapsedMs(float|int $start): intElapsed whole milliseconds since $start; public so the MCP-7 dispatcher stamps identically.

ReadLedger final class

The session's read ledger (roadmap 3.I-2): for every file the model has seen, the state it was in when it saw it — modification time, size, inode and a content hash — so an Edit or an overwriting Write can tell that the file changed on disk afterwards and refuse to act on a stale picture of it.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
static bindTo(object $owner, self $ledger): voidBind $ledger to $owner for as long as $owner lives — how a \SugarCraft\Code\Chat with no workspace keeps the ledger its embedder handed it without a constructor slot: the owner is the inbox every mutate() clone of one conversation shares by identity, the key \SugarCraft\Code\Host\TurnRunner::of() uses for the same reason.
static boundTo(object $owner): ?selfThe ledger bindTo() bound to $owner, or null.
static in(iterable $tools): ?selfThe ledger $tools share, or null when none of them carries one.
observe(string $path, int $mtime, int $size, int $ino, ?string $hash): voidRecord what the model now holds of $path from a stat signature and the hash of the bytes it saw — Read's half, which hashes as it reads. $hash null means "not hashed"; staleness then rests on the signature.
record(string $path, ?string $bytes = null): voidRecord $path as it is on disk now, whose bytes are $bytes — the writers' half, called after their write landed so the model's own change is the new baseline. Without $bytes the file is hashed when it is small enough.
forget(string $path): voidDrop $path: the model itself deleted or moved it (ApplyPatch), so its absence is not a change somebody else made behind its back.
has(string $path): boolWhether the model has seen $path this session.
static hashContext(): \HashContextA fresh hashing context in the ledger's algorithm, for Read's pass over the file.
staleness(string $path, ?string $currentBytes = null): ?stringWhy $path is stale — 'deleted' or 'modified' — or null when it is not, including when the model never read it.
changedSinceRead(): arrayEvery recorded path that is no longer what the model saw, most recently read first, as path => 'deleted'|'modified'. A moved stat signature over unchanged bytes (a touch, an atomic rewrite of the same content) is not a change, and its entry is re-based so the next scan skips the hash.
notice(): stringThe turn-context paragraph naming the files that changed since the model read them, or '' when none did. Paths are as recorded (canonical); the caller's fence escapes them like every other payload.
toArray(): arrayThe ledger as plain arrays, for a payload that is decoded with allowed_classes => false.
recordedSince(array $before): arrayThe entries recorded since $before (an earlier toArray()): every path that is new or was re-recorded — what a forked child has to carry home, since merge() of an unchanged row is a no-op anyway.
merge(mixed $payload): voidFold a toArray() payload in: per path, the entry recorded last wins. Malformed rows are skipped, never fatal — the payload crossed a process boundary and may come from an older build.

MethodSummary
__construct(private string $toolCallId, private string $content, private bool $isError = false, private ?int $durationMs = null, private ?string $imageBytes = null, private ?string $imagePath = null, private ?string $imageProtocol = null, private ?string $diff = null, private ?Usage $usage = null, private ?DenialKind $denial = null, private ?string $documentBytes = null, private ?string $documentName = null, private ?int $exitCode = null)$imageBytes/$imagePath/$imageProtocol bridge this type to \SugarCraft\Code\ToolResult's image-carrying fields (W1.G2 E1/E2): this is the Tool-interface result type the LIVE \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime/\SugarCraft\Code\Backend\EngineBackend agentic loop actually produces and consumes, so an image-bearing tool (e.g. \SugarCraft\Code\Tools\BuiltIn\Doctor) needs a real place to put its bytes on THIS type, not only on the parallel Crush\ToolResult that only Chat's own (production-unreachable) registerTool() dispatch consumes.
static denied(string $toolCallId, DenialKind $kind, string $detail): selfA call that was stopped before it ran: the error result whose text is $kind's rendered reason and which CARRIES $kind, so every consumer downstream can tell a refusal from a failure without reading the text.
toolCallId(): string
content(): string
isError(): bool
durationMs(): ?int
exitCode(): ?intThe process exit status a shell-shaped tool ran to, or null when the tool ran no process (or never got one to report). Display-only: the model reads the text, which already carries whatever the tool printed, so this rides the structure for the transcript's exit N label.
imageBytes(): ?string
imagePath(): ?string
imageProtocol(): ?string
hasImage(): bool
documentBytes(): ?string
documentName(): ?string
hasDocument(): bool
diff(): ?stringRaw unified diff produced by an edit-shaped tool, or null.
hasDiff(): bool
usage(): ?UsageProvider spend the tool itself incurred (a delegated sub-agent run), or null.
denial(): ?DenialKindWhich of the three ways this call was stopped before it ran, or null when it was not stopped — including when it ran and failed with text that merely LOOKS like a refusal.
withDenial(?DenialKind $denial): selfThe same result marked as stopped-before-it-ran by $denial (null clears it).
withContent(string $content): selfThe same result with its model-visible text replaced and EVERY other field kept — the seam \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime's rewrites (annotate, the UTF-8 scrub) take, so a rebuild cannot drop a field that was added after it was written. Spelled-out positional rebuilds are exactly how $usage would have leaked off a Task result between the tool and the turn's accounting.
withUsage(?Usage $usage): selfThe same result carrying $usage as the tool's own provider spend.
toArray(): arrayThe provider wire-shape only -- $diff is deliberately absent, exactly like the image fields and the document fields: it is renderer-side presentation data, and inlining a whole unified diff here would duplicate it into every chat-completion request's token budget. $usage is absent for the same reason: it is accounting, not something the model reads. So is $denial: the model reads the refusal in the text, which still opens with the kind's prefix, and the structural kind is for the parties that must not trust that text.

name(): string

promptGuidance(): stringGeneric git discipline beside the tool that runs it, for ANY repository: inspect, stage by name, commit, and each safety rule stated WITH the reason it exists — a failed pre-commit hook means no commit landed, so the next --amend would land on the PREVIOUS one, which is exactly why --amend is checked against the exit status and --no-verify never used. Spelled as numbered steps and a message template rather than free prose because the sequence is genuinely fragile and the model performs it through THIS tool.

static fromCatalog(ToolBuildContext $context): selfBuild from the catalog and wire standing intents into the nudge seam (C-CTX-3.f). The catalog build is the one moment the memory router and the path-nudge tracker are both in hand — ToolBuildContext carries them — and launching tools is the only caller that ever has both, so this is where the bind lands without widening LaunchContext. The tracker re-walks intentNotes() on every consult, so a note saved mid-session answers the next tool call; withWriter() copies (the per-agent delegation of C-AGT-3.b) deliberately do NOT re-bind — a delegation steers from the session's own intents, not from notes only the agent could see.

TaskTool uses it to re-point a delegation's Memory at the per-agent store its preset's memory: tier selects; the tool's behaviour is otherwise the writer's, so the re-bind changes where notes land, nothing the model sees. The launch root and any session the turn already bound are carried through — a delegation's sessions recall must still scope to the same project and exclude the same current session.
withShellOwner(?string $owner): selfThis tool bound to session $owner (C-CTX-3.d). Memory reads no background shells — it claims AcceptsShellOwner because the seam IS the engine's per-turn session-id binding (C-TOOL-3.c), the only one a tool can take without the engine knowing the tool: a sessions recall needs the current id to exclude it. Null — a caller the engine has not bound on this turn (a standalone build; launch-built rows carry it only until the per-turn bind lands) — leaves the exclusion off, exactly like the shell tools' untagged rows.

The spawn happens in the turn's forked child; the supervisor stamps the session as the HOST's, so the host's own supervisor adopts it on its next poll and announces the result (BackgroundSupervisor::adoptHandedOff()).
withWorktreeManager(?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\WorktreeManager $manager): selfThe same tool, able to isolate a run (roadmap 4.9): an agent whose preset says isolation: worktree runs in a git worktree of its own, created through $manager on a branch of its own — its tools jailed to that tree, its Bash refused paths outside it, its environment and hook root naming it (EngineBackend::withWorktreeRoot()). On the way out a tree that holds no work is removed with its branch; one that does is kept, and the report names where.
backgroundSupervisor(): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSupervisorWhat a background run is spawned through, or null when none is bound.
withDelegationLimits(int $maxDepth, ?int $maxConcurrent): selfThe same tool under other nesting caps (roadmap 4.7-3): delegated runs at most $maxDepth levels deep, at most $maxConcurrent of them at once in the session. A null $maxConcurrent caps nothing. The settings rows that set them are N-P4f's.
withDelegationScope(?string $scope): selfThe same tool, counting its seats for $scope instead of the engine's session — what a background daemon passes, so its agent counts against the session that started it rather than against itself.
withDelegationSlotRoot(string $root): selfThe same tool, keeping its seat files below $root (a test seam).
delegationDepth(): intHow deep the agent calling this tool runs: 0 for the session's own.
nestedFor(int $depth, string $parentAgentId, \Closure $emitter, ?string $scope): selfThe copy a delegated run at $depth is handed, so it can delegate one level further: its frames go out through $emitter (the delegating run's, which reaches the parent from any process the run is in) naming $parentAgentId, and its seats are counted in $scope. Never backgrounds: a background agent is announced into the session's conversation, which a nested run is not having.
withEngine(EngineBackend $engine, ?\Closure $heartbeat = null, ?\Closure $subAgentEmitter = null): self
withSiblingSpend(SiblingSpendLedger $ledger): selfThe copy \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime::executeConcurrently() runs as one member of a concurrent group: its delegated run records each step onto $ledger and counts its siblings' records in its spend-cap check. Only the engine path uses it; the pool path is never parallel-safe, so it is never a group member.
boardMember(array $args): ?\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\Board\BoardMemberThe participant this call becomes on its batch's shared board (roadmap 4.5): the agent it names and its short description. Null for a call that will run in the background — it hands off and returns before its peers start, so a peer could only ever post to it unheard — and for one that names no agent, which is refused before it runs.
withBoard(\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\Board\Board $board): selfThe copy \SugarCraft\Code\Runtime::executeConcurrently() runs as one member of a parallel batch that shares a board (roadmap 4.5): its run is offered BoardRead and BoardPost over $board (this member's view), and the board's news reaches it as a notice on its next tool result. The board's tools are the harness's, not the preset's: a tools: list does not narrow them, but a disallowedTools: entry naming one keeps the run from it.
subAgentEmitter(): ?\Closure
withSubAgentEmitter(\Closure $emitter): self
withActivityClock(\Closure $clock): selfThe same tool, pacing its activity frames by $clock instead of wall time — how a test makes the SubAgentActivityBuffer flush interval deterministic (a clock that always reads "later" flushes every item at once; a frozen one holds them all for the finished frame).
withActivitySink(ActivitySink $sink): selfThe copy a forked member of a concurrent group runs: every beat goes to $sink (the member's datagram relay) instead of the turn-pinned emitter, which would drop it from this process — see StreamsActivity.
withPermissionApprover(\Closure $approver): selfThe copy a forked member of a concurrent group runs (roadmap 1.C-5): every question its delegated run raises goes to $approver — the member's \SugarCraft\Code\Support\PermissionAskRelay — instead of the turn child's channel, which refuses from any other process. A copy with no engine bound has no run to gate and is returned as is.

The one-call-per-message pattern this prose exists to break is the dominant latency cost of delegating on this harness: every un-batched spawn pays a full model round-trip before the next worker even starts, while a message carrying N Task calls forks all N at once for a single step.

Fetches one URL and refuses everything that aims at this machine or its network. The defence is resolve-once-then-dial:

MethodSummary

A null leaves that bound as it is. The result cap is toolOutputCapBytes, through withMaxOutputBytes().

WebSearch class

Deliberately NOT final, unlike its sibling built-ins: isParallelSafe() answers static::class === self::class, and the suite's loopback-fixture harnesses subclass this tool to drive it. The network seam, though, is no longer the subclass hook it used to be — the old fetch() override — it is the transport closure the constructor accepts and hands to SearchBackends::new(), so a test stubs one HTTP call without reaching through the class hierarchy, and every other step (query validation, the SSRF host checks, status mapping, JSON decode, formatting) stays on the real code path.

MethodSummary
__construct(?string $endpoint = null, ?int $timeout = null, ?int $maxResults = null, ?callable $resolveAddresses = null, ?callable $isBlockedAddress = null, ?callable $transport = null, ?string $backend = null)THERE IS NO DEFAULT ENDPOINT. The constructor argument wins, then CANDY_CODE_SEARCH_ENDPOINT, then the webSearchEndpoint setting (roadmap N-P4e: user tier only, since it decides where every model-composed query is sent); an empty value counts as unset, and a setting that is not an http(s) URL is ignored rather than dialled. Until one is set the tool still constructs — Bootstrap, Chat and /websearch build it unconditionally, and the model is better told why a search failed than shown no tool — but every call is an error naming the variable. The shipped default used to be http://skynet2.interserver.net:8080/search: a private host, over CLEARTEXT http, so every model-composed query (which routinely quotes code, file names and error text from the user's repository) crossed the network unencrypted to a third party, unprompted under the default bypass-permissions. Switching it to https would still have sent every user's queries to one maintainer's box; the honest default for a third-party data flow is none.
isParallelSafe(): boolSame reasoning as WebFetch::isParallelSafe(): a search round-trip is seconds of waiting, writes nothing locally, and strands no session-scoped state in a forked child.

name(): string

False — the default, and the only value a project file could ever want — keeps them.

hardened(): boolWhether THIS jail runs the hardened flag set on this host: opted out by bashSandboxNestedUserns, or told not to by the probe. Unknown means yes — the hardened set is the safer reading, and production probes before it wraps (the same memo Bash::sandboxRefusal() fills).

Null when the file cannot be read: a kernel without the interface answers "unknown", never "no".

EgressBridge final class

In-jail half of the egress path: a TCP front-end that relays to the host side's unix-socket EgressProxy.

MethodSummary
static stub(string $autoload): stringThe php -r program that starts the bridge from the jail argv tail (C-TOOL-4.g). The bridge process is spawned by the jail's own argv, which cannot carry structured data, so the path to the autoloader is baked into the code at build time — the single source being \SugarCraft\Code\Background\BackgroundSupervisor::autoloadPath() at the call site. argv after the option separator is <unixPath> <tcpPort> -- <program> <args...> — the shape Bubblewrap::argv() appends; the FIRST -- is consumed by PHP itself (php -r reports its code string as argv[0]), the second separates the bridge's own arguments from the command's, because the command may legitimately contain -- of its own. runFromArgv() owns that contract, unpicked apart in tests.
static runFromArgv(array $argv): intThe argv contract of stub(), as a method so the parse and its fail-closed refusals are testable without spawning anything. A shape mismatch exits 2 WITHOUT running the program: a mis-built jail tail must never degrade into "command ran, no relay" (the command would believe the network is reachable when nothing was forwarded) nor into executing an unintended argv slot.
static bind(int $tcpPort = 0, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): ServerInterfaceBinds the jail-local front-end. Exposed separately from run() so the bind-before-fork ordering itself is testable.
static relay(ServerInterface $tcpListener, string $unixPath, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): voidAttaches the TCP→unix relay to a bound listener (non-blocking).
static resolveProgram(string $program): stringTurn the command's first word into an executable path for run()'s pcntl_exec. A path is a path — returned untouched. A bare word is searched along PATH, the way execvp would, because pcntl_exec is only execv. A word nothing on PATH can find comes back UNCHANGED on purpose: the child's exec failure then still lands on the bridge's honest 127, and no new exit code enters the jail's vocabulary.
static run(string $unixPath, string $program, array $programArgv = [], int $tcpPort = 0, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): intFull bridge: bind first, fork, exec the command in the child, and in the parent relay egress until the command exits — returning its exit status (128+signal when it died on one).

name(): stringWhat to call this backend in user-facing prose — lowercase, one word.

Per backend, exactly like the doctor row's remedy arms: bubblewrap's story is Ubuntu's AppArmor userns restriction, Seatbelt's is the OS-shipped /usr/bin/sandbox-exec that stopped running the profile. One sentence hard-coding either story misadvises the other OS's user, which is worse than naming no story.

It must name the failure the backend actually produces — a jail that denies by policy answers "Operation not permitted", not "Read-only file system".

SearchBackends final class

The search-backends module: pick a backend, dial it.

MethodSummary
static new(?string $name, ?string $endpoint, int $timeout, ?callable $transport = null, ?callable $resolveAddresses = null, ?callable $isBlockedAddress = null): SearchBackendBuild the backend $name asks for.
static guardedDialAddress(string $host, \Closure $resolve, \Closure $blocked): arrayResolve the host once and refuse it if ANY answer is blocked, else return the first answer to dial. The check this replaced asked gethostbyname() for one v4 answer, so an AAAA-only name at ::1, or a record set mixing public and private, passed; it also read an unresolvable name as "not blocked" and let the fetch resolve again.
static openHttp(array $request, string $dialAddress): arrayThe default transport: dial the vetted literal, never the hostname — the same resolve-once-then-dial shape as WebFetch: handing the name to the stream layer resolved it a second time, so a TTL≈0 record could answer public to the guard and private to the dial. The name stays where the peer needs it, in Host: and in ssl.peer_name for SNI and certificate checks. Redirects are switched off at the wrapper (it otherwise follows 20, unchecked); the caller turns the 3xx it now sees into a refusal. The body is read in chunks and abandoned once past MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE, so a hostile endpoint costs at most one chunk over the cap in memory rather than whatever it chooses to stream.
static serviceDial(string $host, \Closure $resolve, \Closure $blocked): arrayThe hosted-path twin of guardedDialAddress(): a fixed service host, the same resolve-once-then-dial discipline, refusal wording that names a SERVICE rather than a configured endpoint (nobody configured this host — the build did).
static hostedFailure(string|false $body, array $headers, string $service): ?stringThe shared failure read of a hosted response: connect failure, the 5 MB bound, then the status classes, in the order WebSearch has always applied them (size BEFORE connect-false, because a partial read is a different story from no story). Null means the response is answerable.
static decode(string $body): array|stringDecode a hosted JSON body: the array on success, the refusal sentence otherwise (same parser bound and clipping as the SearXNG path).
static locationSuffix(array $headers): string" to <Location>" for a redirect refusal, so the user can see what to configure. The value is remote text headed for the model, so control bytes are stripped and its length is bounded.

AwayTracker final class

The away stamp behind the focus recap (C-TUI-3.g, GAP-UI-N4) — the terminal-agnostic half of "recap when I get back".

MethodSummary
static focusLost(?float $at = null): voidStamp an absence. $at is the injectable clock (seconds); production calls with no argument and reads the monotonic timer, so an operator's clock adjustment (NTP slew, DST shim) can never invent or erase away time the way the wall clock could.
static focusGained(?float $at = null): ?floatEnd the absence: the length in seconds when the regain closes one of at least AWAY_SECONDS, null for a shorter gap or for a regain with no stamp to close. The stamp is consumed either way — a counted absence must never be countable twice.
static recapEnabled(): boolWhether the automatic recap may speak at all. The schema's read point for SETTING_KEY. C-M17: CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_AWAY_RECAP is the shell's word over every file, and the user tier alone decides — a project may switch this off, never on (same form as \SugarCraft\Code\Permissions\ReadOnlyCommands::autoAllowEnabled()).
static reset(): voidDrop a held stamp. Test seam; the regain path already consumes.

ComposerVim final class

The vim-operator state the COMPOSER keeps above the sugar-forms Vim layer (plan_comparison.md §3 TUI-3 Cut A; the C-TUI-1 step added counts, the change operator and text objects).

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly ?string $pending = null, public readonly string $register = '', public readonly bool $registerLinewise = false, public readonly ?string $pendingScope = null, public readonly ?int $count = null)
static empty(): self
pendingCleared(): selfSame register, nothing armed (operator, scope or count) — the "forgotten" cleanup the caller re-routes with.
isArmed(): boolWhether ANY part of the multi-keystroke grammar is waiting for its next key.
claimsKey(string $rune): boolWhether THIS state claims the plain Char in NORMAL state. Instance method on purpose: 0 (and every lib-bound motion, whose claim only matters for predicate completeness) keys on the armed count, so an unarmed 0 stays the lib's line-start motion and d0 survives the count grammar.
static resolve(KeyMsg $key, TextArea $input, self $state): arrayA key arrived while the grammar is armed (isArmed()).
static start(KeyMsg $key, TextArea $input, self $state): arrayA plain Char in NORMAL state with nothing armed (the caller has the same guards; this method trusts them). Arming keys return the widget untouched; acting keys edit through the widget's own public surface, and the Insert entries (o/O, and C through the enterInsert half of this class's rule for c) enter Insert by FEEDING the widget the i key — the lib owns its state machine, so this class never pokes $vimState (it could not: there is no setter).
static wordEndCol(string $line, int $col): intOne-past the last character of the word e lands ON from $col (exclusive-start walk: at least one cell right, skip a punctuation/ whitespace run, then consume a word run) — the classic e-boundary over the lib's [a-zA-Z0-9_] word characters. $col at/after EOL answers $col back, so de/d$ at the end of a line produce the empty span the caller beeps on. Line-local, like every other motion here: the lib's w is line-local too, and an app-side e that crossed rows the w cannot would be two notions of word in one composer.

DiffGutter final class

The old-file/new-file line-number gutter for a unified diff — the column \SugarCraft\Code\Renderer::renderDiff() paints to the left of each diff row so a reviewer can tell *which line of the file* a change lands on (Phase 8 item 1; before this, the diff box was raw diff -u text with add/remove colouring and nothing else).

MethodSummary
static forDiff(array $lines): selfBuild the gutter for a whole diff block.
static none(int $rows): selfA zero-width gutter: what the renderer falls back to when the viewport is too narrow to spend columns on line numbers, and what forDiff() returns for an unnumberable diff.
static fileHeaders(array $lines): arrayWhich rows are file headers rather than diff content, under exactly the rule sugar-diff's UnifiedScan documents (diff /index are unambiguous; --- /+++ count only while no hunk is open, because a deleted SQL comment arrives here as --- users table).
static isHunkHeader(string $line): boolWhether this row is a hunk header at all, numberable or not — the one pattern lives in UnifiedScan::isHunkHeader(), so the gutter and the scan can never disagree about where a hunk starts.
static isNumberableHunk(string $line): boolWhether this row is a hunk header whose numbers may be trusted — the precondition the split layout needs before it derives two line-number columns from \SugarCraft\Diff\Writer\SideBySideFormat.
static sideWidth(int $digits): intDisplay width of ONE side's number column in the split layout: the old file numbers ride the left column, the new file numbers the right, so each half pays $digits plus the separator instead of the unified gutter's two number columns. 0 digits means no numbers at all — then no column either, the same opt-out none() gives the unified paint.
static sidePrefix(?int $number, int $digits): stringThe number column for one side of a split row: a right-aligned line number followed by the separator, or blank cells where the side has no line (a pure insertion has no old line, a pure deletion no new one). Mirrors format() half-for-half so both paints pad identically.

PaneDragController final class

The mouse gesture state behind pane docking: one drag in flight, or idle.

MethodSummary
static idle(): selfThe no-gesture state every frame starts in.
isIdle(): bool
beginResize(Side $side, int $grabCol): selfA press landed on divider:<side>:r<row> — the pointer now owns that side's band width until the release.
beginDockDrag(string $paneId, int $pressX, int $pressY): selfA press landed on one of a docked pane's header surfaces — its frame header (pane:<id>) or the menu-bar tab standing for it (panetab:<id>, the live-report fix: dragging the bar label must move the pane exactly like dragging the box top). NOT yet armed: a release that never left the tolerance must still complete the plain click the chrome tracker would have completed — focus from the header, the dock toggle from the tab.
beginSplitResize(int $grabCol): selfA press landed on the seam between the band and the live-agent column (splitdiv:r<row>) — the pointer now owns that column's width until the release. Armed at the press, like a side resize.
isSplitResizing(): bool
splitColumns(int $pointerX, int $originCols, int $min, int $max): intThe live-agent column width the pointer asks for, clamped to [$min, $max]. Delta from the grab, like resizeColumns(): the column sits right of the seam, so dragging LEFT by n grows it by n.
isResizing(): bool
isDockDragging(): bool
isArmed(): boolWhether the dock drag has travelled far enough to BE a drag. A resize is armed at the press by definition — grabbing the divider column IS the intent.
dragSide(): ?Side
dragPaneId(): ?string
withMotion(int $x, int $y): selfFeed one motion event to the gesture in flight.
pointer(): arrayWhere the pointer of a dock drag last was, 1-based terminal cells — the press until the first motion arrives. The renderer resolves it through dockDropSide() each frame to paint the drop target the release would land on, so what is highlighted and what the release does can never disagree.
isPreviewed(): boolWhether any motion preview actually mutated the model during this resize — see withMotion().
resizeColumns(int $releaseX, int $currentWidthPx, int $sideMinCols, int $centerRoomPx): intWhich band width the pointer asks for, in content columns, clamped into the frame the dock itself will enforce.
dockDropSide(int $releaseX, int $centerFromCol, int $centerToCol): ?SideWhere a released dock drag lands: Left band, Right band, or null for "the middle of the centre — cancel". $centerFromCol/$centerToCol are the centre column's 0-based inclusive frame span as last painted.
static dropEdgeCols(int $centerFromCol, int $centerToCol): intHow many of the centre's outer columns, on each side, belong to the facing side's drop target — the one rule dockDropSide() and the renderer's drop-target outline share.
static insertIndex(int $releaseY, array $slotTopsAbs): intThe slot index a release asks for on the drop side: how many of that side's currently-painted docked slots START above the release row. $slotTopsAbs is those 0-based frame rows in slot order; a release above every slot inserts at 0, below every one appends.

ScreenReaderMode final class

The screenReader switch and the presentation helpers behind it (plan_comparison.md §3, C-TUI-6.i).

MethodSummary
static enabled(): boolWhether the screen-reader presentation is on right now.
static border(Border $border): BorderThe frame to draw where $border framed a box: the same emptiness Border::hidden() paints — all thirteen slots are spaces — but carrying $border's titles verbatim, embedded ones included. The title text is the one part of a bordered box a screen reader CAN narrate, so it is exactly what must survive the shed frame; dropping it would trade decoration for information loss.
static glyph(string $text): string$text with every Box Drawing glyph (U+2500–U+257F: the frame, divider and junction runes the renderer paints) replaced by a space, so a line-drawn panel reaches the reader as content on blank paper instead of a rattle of strokes. Text, padding and every other block's glyphs (arrows, checkmarks, spinner dots) pass through untouched — the spinner is motion, not glyphs, and it is pinned through AgentLiveRegistry::staticSpinner() instead.
static menuRow(int $n, int $of, string $label, bool $selected): stringOne menu row as text: a > marker on the selected row (the mode must never carry selection on reverse video alone), the label, and a textual position as n/of in plain digits and one slash — a locale-neutral form that is the whole contract: no translation keys sit behind it. When the mode is off the row is the bare label: the caller's own reverse-video path is untouched there, so 6.j's off-mode pins stay byte-identical.
static cue(): ?\ClosureThe attention cue for a state change worth narrating — a BEL character as a Cmd::raw() closure, which makes it a command: the Chat update() arms return it and the Program writes it on their own turn. view() must NEVER emit it; rendering is pure, and a BEL hidden in a painted frame would fire on every repaint diff. Null when the mode is off, so an unwired call site is a no-op, not a stray byte.
static paneIcon(Pane $pane): stringThe pane’s identity picture, or the empty string in screen-reader mode: the icon names the pane no better than the text label beside it already does, so a reader is handed the label alone. Off-mode callers get the byte-identical icon.
static cursor(): stringThe one-cell list cursor: a plain > where a reader narrates words, the house small triangle otherwise. Both are width 1, so the marker column does not shift when the mode flips.

SugarCraft\Code\Tui\FirstRunWizard

FirstRunWizard final class

The first-run provider setup: a two-step sugar-forms model with no I/O.

MethodSummary
static open(?array $providerTypes = null, string $seedKey = '', ?int $availableCols = null): selfOpen on step 1. $providerTypes exists for pins and for a host that already holds the roster; null asks the live ProviderFactory::availableTypes(). $seedKey pre-types the step-2 field (pins, and any later headless prefilled offer); an empty value — the only value the interactive launch ever passes — leaves the field blank. $availableCols is the cell budget the pill row gets on screen (NN-01: the host passes the frame width its wizard renderer clips at); the RadioPills row then windows around the selection instead of overrunning the clip. Null — and any nonsense non-positive value, which degrades to null rather than throwing: a decorative fit knob must never brick the first launch — keeps the legacy full unwindowed row.
step(): int1 = picking a provider, 2 = typing its key.
selectedProvider(): ?stringThe pill currently selected; null only on a degenerate empty roster.
notice(): ?stringThe last refusal shown in the wizard, or null.
update(Msg $msg): arrayAnswer a message. The first element is null once the wizard closed; the second carries the action the host must execute, if any.
static shouldOffer(bool $hasSelectedProvider, bool $hasConfiguredProvider, bool $isInteractiveTty, ?string $stampPath = null): boolWhether THIS launch should offer the wizard: the session has no provider selected yet, the config names no provider at all, and a real interactive terminal is attached — and no earlier dismissal was stamped. The first three answers belong to the caller because they are host state; this class reads only its own stamp file, so every quadrant stays pinned without a filesystem surprise inside a model.
static isDismissed(?string $stampPath = null): boolWhether a dismissal stamp exists and is readable (body non-empty).
static markDismissed(?string $stampPath = null): voidRecord the dismissal: the wizard will not be offered again. Best-effort under the owned-home cache directory (mode 0700 on the way in, same as the MacAltNotice stamp); an unwritable cache only means offering again, never an error to the operator. The stamp body is the candy-code version it was recorded under, for the human who later wonders.
view(): stringThe wizard as lines: title, the active field's own view, the key hint, and the refusal notice when one is showing. Fitting and framing are the host's layout concern when the wiring step mounts it; nothing here chases a width.

The action object the host consumes: kind plus, for the kinds that decide values, the provider the operator stood on and (for FirstRunWizardActionKind::Finish) the masked-typed key itself.

MethodSummary

static skip(?string $provider = null): selfPlain skip carries no provider; the login deferral carries one.

FirstRunWizardActionKind enum

What the operator decided in the first-run wizard — the wizard itself is I/O-free by construction (same law as the \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\MediaForm\MediaForm and \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\DirectoryPicker\DirectoryPicker widgets it mirrors): the model returns an action object, and the host executes the consequence.

Cases: Finish · Skip · Cancel

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

OpenFirstRunWizardMsg final readonly class

"Open the first-run wizard" — the message a driver sends the shell when the launch decided the operator needs a provider (or the operator asks for the setup flow by name). Mirrors \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\MediaForm\OpenMediaFormMsg: the command decides, the shell owns the slot. There is no payload to seed — the wizard opens exactly the same way every time, and the current provider is deliberately absent: FirstRunWizard::shouldOffer() already refused launches that have one.

DisplayOverrides final class

The ui-config display-override analog (crush-media W3.9, plan §5.5): the ui.mediaDisplayOverrides map keys one entry per row prop in A1111's element-id convention "<section>/<Label>/<prop>" — the verbatim example being txt2img/CFG Scale/step — and the props are exactly PROPS: value, minimum, maximum, step, visible.

MethodSummary
static elementId(FieldSpec $spec): stringThe id one row is addressed under, without a prop suffix.
static keyFor(FieldSpec $spec, string $prop): stringThe full override key for one row prop.
static forElement(FieldSpec $spec, array $overrides): arrayThe typed-valid subset of the map for one row: a prop counts only when its key is present AND its shape fits the widget — booleans for visible, numerics for the range props of a slider/number row, a widget-matched type for value. Anything else reads as no override at all, never as a coercion attempt.
static apply(array $specs, array $overrides): arrayFold the map into a row lattice, returning [keptSpecs, changedProps] — keptSpecs keyed exactly like the input minus any visible:false rows, changedProps keyed by wire key with the row's accepted props (so the owner can reshape only the widgets the ranges actually moved on).

DraftContextSection interface

A section whose rendered rows recompute from the LIVE draft rather than only its own fields (crush-media W3.5): the Hires accordion's final-size preview reads width/height/hr_scale from whatever the user last committed anywhere in the form. MediaForm applies the context in bodyLines() immediately before painting the focused section, so the preview can never drift from what collect() would fold.

MethodSummary
withDraftContext(MediaRequest $context): selfSame section, remembering the draft its view rows read from.

FieldSpec final readonly class

One declarative row of the generate form (crush-media W3.4): key, label (a tui.genform.* id), widget kind with its §2-table range/step/default, the DTO bridge (the wire name IS the key), and the A1111 infotext label. ONE registry feeds the form, the request bridge, the infotext table, and (later) presets — a control exists in exactly one row here, so a number cannot drift between surfaces.

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
static coreRows(): arrayEvery core txt2img row (§2.1/§2.2) owned by the W3.4 Prompt and Params sections, in display order. Later steps append their rows in-step: W3.5 adds the Extra/Hires/Refiner groups, W3.7 the img2img/inpaint groups, W3.8 the advanced escape hatch.
createField(string $key, ?array $choices = null): FieldBuild the sugar-forms widget this row describes, already coerced onto its lattice with the row's default. $choices overrides the feed for option-bearing widgets (a runtime /samplers set); a select with no option source fails fast — a silent empty dropdown would hide a wiring bug until a user finds it.
withDisplayProps(array $props): selfA copy with display-override props folded in (crush-media W3.9, the ui-config analog): minimum/maximum/step move the widget range and value re-seeds the row's default — the pre-fill a fresh form opens on. Typing and widget-sense belong to DisplayOverrides, the parse boundary; this door trusts what it was handed.
optionLabels(?array $choices = null): arrayThe option labels for this row: the runtime feed wins, the row's fixed options are next, the registry default is last.
static latentUpscalers(): array§2.8's six latent upscale modes, verbatim. Like sampler names these are wire identifiers displayed as-is (data, not UI copy); the server's own /upscalers names join them through ChoiceFeed when a client is configured.
static noneLabel(): stringThe dropdown's neutral "off" entry (refiner checkpoint, W3.5).
static useSameLabel(string $nounKey): stringThe hires dropdowns' "Use same …" sentinel label for one noun row.
static disclosureRows(): arrayThe W3.5 disclosure groups (§2.1/§2.3): the Extra variation-seed rows, the whole Hires. fix accordion, and the Refiner pair. Every range, step and default below is the §2-table number verbatim.
static wave4Rows(): arrayThe W3.7 img2img/inpaint registry (§2.6/§2.7). Every range, step and default below is the §2-table number verbatim; the radio rows carry their option labels (§2.7 spellings) and bridge label↔index at the wire. Present-but-gated: while Wave4Gate is closed no section collects these rows, so the registry exists to pin the vocabulary and coercion in tests long before the editor ships.
static resizeModeOptions(): array§2.7's four resize modes, verbatim A1111 spellings — wire index = position.
static fillOptions(): array§2.7's masked-content options. EXACTLY FOUR (C-1): fill, original, latent noise, latent nothing — a fifth entry or a 5-way split would be a Forge/SD.Next concept, not stock A1111, and is a CRITICAL defect. UI default is "original" (index 1); wire index = position.
static maskInvertOptions(): array§2.7 mask mode: inpaint the masked region or its complement.
static areaOptions(): array§2.7 inpaint area: whole picture (false) or only masked (true).
belongsTo(string $sectionKey): boolDoes this row's section still want it visible given the draft state? (W3.5 owns conditionals.)

applyTo(MediaRequest $draft, mixed $value): MediaRequestFold a widget value for this row into the draft (the wire bridge).

FieldValuedSection interface

The door a Section opens when its widgets carry wire-keyed values (crush-media W3.4): the form can then hydrate every such section from a flat value map (PNG infotext import, preset load) and read the same map back out (preset save, infotext emit) without either direction going through a Forms\Form composite — the sections drive their fields directly, exactly as the shell already does.

ImportPng final class

The PNG-info import channel (crush-media W4.4).

MethodSummary
static extract(?string $bytes): ?stringThe local channel alone: the parameters chunk of a PNG, or null when the bytes are not a PNG, carry no such chunk, or it is blank.
static fromInfotext(string $text, MediaRequest $draft): MediaRequestThe paste-params door: fold an infotext string over a draft locally, under the same onlyUnset law the chunk import uses. Never throws — Infotext::parse() tolerates legacy and unknown keys by design, dropping server-sourced secret-shaped ones per Infotext::isSecretKey().
static import(string $bytes, MediaRequest $draft, ?callable $serverInfo = null): arrayLocal-first import of a PNG's parameters over $draft.
static serverInfoFor(string $base64, ?array $settings = null, ?SdTransport $transport = null): ?stringThe production server channel, zero-dial by construction: null (and no socket opened) unless the profile configures an SD base AND speaks a family the import runs over. Mirrors GenerateImage's capability gate — a declared family the import cannot run over (png-info is sdapi-only dialect, so the W7-implemented sglang still zero-dials here) or an image-less mediaKinds roster refuses before any request; a parsed-unknown mediaFamily stays the discovery table's business, not this gate's.

MediaForm final class

The media generation form (crush-media W3.1, Shape A): a full-band, App-owned modal in exactly the \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\Settings\SettingsEditor mold — plain-letters keys, hand-drawn rounded chrome, view-local click zones, and no I/O of its own.

MethodSummary
static open(?MediaRequest $request = null, ?array $runtimeChoices = null, ?array $scriptDescriptors = null, ?array $optionsMap = null, ?array $presets = null, ?\Closure $persistPresets = null, ?array $displayOverrides = null, ?string $savePattern = null): selfOpen the form over $request (a fresh draft when null) with the W3.4 registry sections: Prompt and Params. $runtimeChoices is an optional ChoiceFeed map — the HTTP hop lives in the App seam, never here, so this constructor stays deterministic and network-free. $scriptDescriptors is the same doctrine for W3.6: the raw /sdapi/v1/script-info payload fetched upstream, null until supplied; $optionsMap carries the W3.8 /sdapi/v1/options payload for the Advanced tab's key completion, same rule.
static fromSections(array $sections, ?MediaRequest $request = null, ?MediaPresets $presets = null, ?\Closure $persistPresets = null): selfOpen over a caller-supplied section list (W3.4's registry seam): the draft seeds every section's widgets exactly as open() seeds the placeholder.
sections(): arrayThe registered sections, tab order (the wiring seam for later lanes).
draft(): MediaRequestThe draft as it stood when the form opened — collection never mutates it.
collectValues(): arrayThe current widget values across every FieldValuedSection, keyed by wire name (preset save / infotext emit, crush-media W3.4).
hydrateFields(array $values): selfPush a flat wire-keyed value map (PNG infotext import, preset load) into every value-carrying section and refresh the draft from the rebuilt widgets. Junk values are refused by the sections' own injection, so an import can never forge an off-lattice number.
withLastSeed(?int $seed): selfTeach the ♻ row the seed of the last settled generation (W3.5 seam: the shell calls this when a result lands while the form is open; until then the row honestly reports "not set").
state(): MediaFormState
withStatus(string $status): selfA one-line status from the shell (a refused dial, a staged preset).
collect(): MediaRequestThe draft with every visible section folded into it, in tab order.
update(KeyMsg $msg): arrayAnswer a key. The first element is null when the form closed; the second carries the action the shell must execute, if any.
click(string $zoneId): selfA completed click on one of the view's zones; anything else is ignored.
wheel(int $notch): selfOne wheel notch: positive scrolls down the list.
beginEdit(): selfStart editing the highlighted row's field; read-only rows stay put.
pendingPresetName(): stringThe name currently typed on the Presets tab, trimmed ('' when none).
saveFocusedPreset(): selfThe shell-side s binding (crush-media W4.1): save the current values under the typed preset name through the injected persist door. Payload bytes never ride along — the save folds collectValues(), and the image source rows are section-local, not lattice fields. Refusals land as a '!' status exactly like the Presets tab's Save row.
withClipboardImage(string $bytes): selfThe W4.2 clipboard paste: the host persists the bytes first (volatile temp law) and hands them here; the img2img section takes the slot, or the refusal message rides the form status. Nothing is validated twice — ImageIngress::fromBytes() is the single door.
attachedPng(): ?ImageIngressThe first PNG attached on the Image tab, or null when none is — the subject the i import reads (self::importAttachedPng()). JPEG/GIF sources never qualify: the infotext lives in PNG chunks.
importAttachedPng(?callable $serverInfo = null): selfThe shell-side i binding (crush-media W4.4): import the attached PNG's parameters over the draft, local chunk first and the gated server png-info helper second (ImportPng::import()). The imported fields land on the draft — the wire truth Generate folds from — under Infotext's onlyUnset law, so nothing the user already set is clobbered. Widget rows re-derive from the draft the next time the form opens; mid-session the draft is authoritative on its own. Refusals land as a '!' status exactly like the paste door's.
view(Theme $theme, int $cols, int $rows): stringThe view, exactly $rows lines of exactly $cols cells.
naturalSize(Theme $theme, int $maxCols, int $maxRows): arrayThe box size that shows this form's content without cutting any of it (P-IMAGE-MENU): the widest of the title line, the FULL tab strip (the scroll marks are FormTabs::naturalWidth()'s no-cost absence, so the strip never lands cut when the popup is centred in a wide band), the longest label+value row of every visible section, and the footer hint chain / status line — plus the box's own chrome. Clamped into [MIN_COLS, min(maxCols, MAX_COLS)]; full band width only when content genuinely demands more.
zones(Theme $theme, int $cols, int $rows): arrayThe click targets view() paints, in view-local cells (row 0 is the top border), as [row, from, to (exclusive), zone id] — computed from the same frame math, exactly like the settings editor's.

VideoSection final class

The Video tab (crush-media W5.6, plan §6.2/§6.5): the Wan2.2 / LTX-class parameter rows landing in the generation popup.

MethodSummary
static forDraft(MediaRequest $draft, ?bool $enabled = null, ?EndpointFamily $family = null, ?bool $dualCfg = null, ?array $settings = null): self
key(): string
label(): string
visible(MediaFormState $state): boolThe kind gate: a video-less host does not get the tab at all.
rows(): array
fieldAt(int $row): ?Field
withField(Field $field): Section
valueAt(int $row): string
collect(MediaRequest $draft): MediaRequestFold the tab into the draft under GenerateVideo's wire names. Hidden, the draft passes through untouched (W3.7 draft-identity law); visible but never ENGAGED, likewise — the tab's mere presence must not stamp video defaults (or the resolution's width/height) onto an image run, so an untouched tab collects as identity too. Once any row was edited (or a frame admitted, or a video preset hydrated), the frames value is snapped on the way out (SEND SNAPPED) and every other row lands verbatim.
fieldValues(): array
withFieldValues(array $values): self
withDisplayOverrides(array $overrides): selfThe ui-config display-override analog (§5.5) over this tab's rows: <Label>/visible: false drops a row from render AND collect, and a numeric <Label>/value re-seeds the widget. Tolerance parity: ids that name nothing here are silently ignored.
static videoKindEnabled(?array $settings = null): boolThe kind door, zero-dial by construction and FAIL-CLOSED for the tab: the strip gains a Video tab only when the provider's mediaKinds roster explicitly names 'video' — the brief's literal "visible only when mediaKinds includes video". This is deliberately the inverse of the tool-side doors (\SugarCraft\Code\Tui\MediaForm\ImportPng and GenerateVideo's capability refusal), which fail OPEN because a refusal at the entry point must not punish an un-declared host; a tab advertises a capability, and advertising one nobody declared would stamp its rows (and their resolution) onto every image run's draft. An un-declared host still reaches video via the tool itself.

SugarCraft\Code\Tui\Menu

MenuCascade final class

Turns a MenuTree and a MenuCursor into painted MenuPanel boxes — the whole geometry of a nested cascade:

MethodSummary
static layout(MenuTree $tree, MenuCursor $cursor, Theme $theme, int $titleCol, int $top, int $cols, int $rows, bool $marked = false): array

MenuCursor final class

Where the user is in the menu: which top-level menu is open (1-based, 0 when the menu is closed), which row is highlighted in every panel opened down from it, and whether the deepest row's submenu is previewed without having been entered (hover()).

MethodSummary
static closed(): self
static open(int $index, MenuTree $tree): selfOpen the 1-based top-level menu, highlighting its first selectable row. An out-of-range index yields the closed cursor.
isClosed(): bool
absolutePath(): arrayThe path into the tree of the deepest highlighted row, in MenuTree vocabulary: [menu-1, r0, r1, ...]. Empty for a closed cursor.
key(string $key, MenuTree $tree): MenuStepFeed one key. A choice (Enter/o on a leaf) reports it in MenuStep::$chosen and leaves the cursor where it is — closing the menu is the caller's call, since the dispatched command may want the tree gone or a notice printed in its place.
hover(array $path, MenuTree $tree): selfPoint the cursor at $path (dropdown indexes below the menu bar) as a mouse hover would: highlight it, and when it is a submenu row preview that submenu WITHOUT entering it. A path that does not exist in $tree, or lands on a row the cursor may not rest on, leaves the cursor alone.

MenuNode final class

One row of one menu: a leaf (command or toggle), a submenu header owning children, or a separator. Immutable in the house shape — a toggled check rides withChecked() and returns a new node, so an open menu never mutates the tree a caller handed it.

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
static command(string $id, string $label, string $icon = '', bool $enabled = true, ?string $zone = null): self
static toggle(string $id, string $label, bool $checked = false, string $icon = '', bool $enabled = true, ?string $zone = null): self
static submenu(string $id, string $label, array $children = [], string $icon = '', bool $enabled = true, ?string $zone = null): self
static separator(): self
withChecked(bool $checked): self
selectable(): boolMay the cursor rest on this row and may Enter choose it? Separators and disabled rows: no.

MenuNodeKind enum

What a MenuNode IS to the menu: the four shapes a nested-menu row can take. MenuBar grew out of a flat list<string> and has no shape concept at all (every row was an implied command); the kit needs the discriminator because the cursor may only stop on MenuNode::selectable() rows, the cascade draws separators and check columns differently, and only a MenuNodeKind::Submenu row may carry an open panel beneath it.

Cases: Command · Toggle · Submenu · Separator

PHP also provides cases().

MenuPanel final class

One rendered menu box: its painted lines (top border first, bottom border last — a windowed panel's ellipsis and filler rows live inside the box as ordinary lines) and where it sits. Position is screen truth: col is the 1-based column of the left border, row the 0-based screen line of the top border line, so the caller paints $panel->lines[$i] at line $panel->row + $i and composites later panels over earlier ones.

MethodSummary
static new(int $col, int $row, array $lines, array $nodes, array $path, int $firstRowIndex): self
width(): intVISIBLE width of the box — every line shares it, and the width law caps it at cols. Mark::zone sentinels and their id bytes are click metadata, not screen cells, so the marked twin measures the same width as the painted one (child placement depends on it).

MenuStep final class

The result of feeding one key to MenuCursor::key(): where the cursor ended up, plus — when the key was a choice (Enter/o on a leaf) — the node chosen. A plain move, or a key the cursor does not bind, carries no choice; the caller dispatches on MenuStep::$chosen and then re-renders from MenuStep::$cursor.

MethodSummary
static new(MenuCursor $cursor, ?MenuNode $chosen = null): self

MenuTree final class

The whole menu bar as a tree: every top-level entry is itself a submenu (its dropdown rows), so the kit has no "menu vs row" type split — a path is a plain list of 0-based indexes and rows() answers it.

MethodSummary
static new(array $menus): self
rows(array $path): arrayThe rows addressed by $path: [] yields the top-level menus, a path to a submenu yields its children, anything else yields no rows.
node(array $path): ?MenuNode
pathOf(string $id): ?arrayThe path to the node with $id, or null when the id is absent. Depths walk document order (menus left to right, rows top to bottom), so a duplicated id resolves to its first occurrence.
leaves(): arrayEvery command and toggle leaf in document order, disabled rows included: this is the tree's inventory of actions, not a cursor rule. Separators and submenu headers carry no action and stay out.

ShellMenu final class

The shell's five-menu bar (R-MENU-1): Session · Agent · Tools · View · App as a MenuTree built from CommandRegistry::all() — the same "derived, not declared" law \SugarCraft\Code\Tui\Components\MenuBar was rebuilt on (its docblock at MenuBar.php:59-73), just nested.

MethodSummary
static tree(?App $a = null, ?array $rows = null): MenuTreeThe bar tree for one frame.

VideoPlayerScreen final class

The full-screen video player surface (crush-media W5.4).

MethodSummary
static preparing(string $path, Mode $mode): selfThe band placeholder while the build promise runs.
static ready(string $path, Player $player, Mode $mode): selfThe screen after a Player answered the build.
static failed(string $path, string $error, Mode $mode): selfThe screen after the build answered an error sentence.
player(): ?Player
update(CoreMsg $msg): arrayDrive the inner Player. Video ticks and rebuilds, keystrokes the gate forwarded, and resizes are the Player's own contract; everything else — including a late PlayerReadyMsg on an already-closed screen — is a no-op. Returns the Player's Cmd verbatim so its tick cadence rides the Program, never a cadence invented here.
stop(): voidStop playback and release the shutdown registration. Idempotent — the Player's own stop latch survives every rebuild, so a second call (close, then teardown) is free.
static adopt(Player $player): voidClaim a freshly built Player for process-lifetime safety BEFORE the "Preparing…" answer can be lost (the app may quit between the build and the message landing). One hook for the whole process; the memo always holds the newest player.
static reattach(Player $player): voidMove the shutdown memo onto a Player that re-minted itself under an already-adopted wrapper (R13-C1). Unlike adopt() this stops NOTHING: the video Player is immutable, so every handled key returns a fresh wrapper around the SAME live decoder — halting the superseded one here would kill the stream the new wrapper is playing. The old wrapper's own stop() stays harmless: its memo guard simply no longer matches, and Player::stop is latched.
static registerShutdownTeardown(): voidArm the shutdown stop once (house precedent: Bootstrap's MCP/LSP shutdown registration). PHP runs shutdown functions on every exit that is not SIGKILL — normal quit, the Ctrl+C quit chord, and a fatal — which is the coverage the frame-loop-free exits need.
static stopActive(): voidStop the adopted player if one is still live (teardown entry).
static hasActivePlayer(): boolTest seam: the current shutdown state of the memo.
static activePlayer(): ?PlayerTest seam: the memoized live player itself — identity checks need the instance, not just presence.
clipsLines(): boolWhether the frame renderer may width-clip this screen's output. Graphics blobs are protocol bytes — a truncate would corrupt them — so they answer false and the renderer trusts the geometry this screen asked the Player for at open.
view(Theme $theme, int $cols, int $rows): stringCompose the band: placeholder, error card, or the Player's blob with the scrubber chrome — appended as a plain row on text modes, pinned to the band's bottom row with absolute cursor operations on graphics modes (the phlix law: the blob is ONE logical multi-row write, so a "\n" chrome would land inside row 3 of the picture, not under it).

SugarCraft\Code\Workflows

AgentCeilingReachedException class

P0-3 config.maxAgents: a dispatch that would cross the run's agent ceiling. A plain RuntimeException to every caller that already catches one (the stage loop turns it into the stage's failure); its own type so a type: map stage (P1-2) can tell "this run may dispatch no more" — which fails the whole stage and admits no further item — from one item's own failure, which only drops that item.

BudgetExhaustedException final class

P1-7 config.maxTokens / config.maxCost (or the run's external token budget): a dispatch that would start with the run's spend at or past its ceiling. Its message begins "budget exhausted (spent X of Y tokens|USD)". A subclass of AgentCeilingReachedException because it is the same run-wide "dispatch no more" refusal — a type: map stage stops admitting items on either — while the stage loop tells them apart: a budget stop PAUSES the run (resume under a raised ceiling continues), the agent ceiling fails it.

CpuCount final class

The host's CPU count, for the default workflow width (P0-3, Workflow::defaultConcurrency()).

MethodSummary

JsonPointer final class

RFC 6901 JSON pointer resolution over decoded workflow documents — the one resolver the condition grammar (StageCondition pointer:) reads typed rows with, written to the EXACT semantics of the engine's {{name.<pointer>}} interpolation helper so both surfaces answer the same leaf for the same spelling:

MethodSummary
static resolve(mixed $document, string $pointer): arrayResolve $pointer against an already-decoded document (json_decode with assoc=true, so objects are PHP arrays).
static resolveJson(string $json, string $pointer): arrayResolve $pointer against a JSON text, such as a row of the engine's WorkflowEngine::TYPED_RESULTS_CONTEXT_KEY map. A text that is not valid JSON reaches nothing — never a thrown error, because a run context is data and the callers answer a miss fail-closed.
static isWellFormed(string $pointer): boolWhether every ~ in $pointer starts a legal escape (~0 or ~1). Resolution itself tolerates a stray ~ (it simply names a member with a tilde in it, as the interpolation helper always has); this is the LOAD-time check a grammar key can refuse on, so a typo such as ~2 is reported where it is written instead of quietly missing.
static tokens(string $pointer): arrayThe unescaped reference tokens of $pointer, root first.

StageCondition final class

The C2 fixed-op stage condition: parse (at load time) and evaluate (at dispatch time) of a stage's when: clause and a loop's until: clause.

MethodSummary
static parse(array $clause, bool $allowLoopLeaves = false): arrayNormalize and validate an author clause, refusing anything the grammar does not carry. The returned shape is what the engine evaluates; never re-feed an author clause into evaluate() directly.
static evaluate(array $clause, array $context): boolAnswer a parsed clause against a run context. Fail-closed by construction: an unknown node, op or value type at run time reads unsatisfied, never true, never thrown — the load-time parse is what guarantees shapes, and a hand-built clause that bypassed it must not turn an engine bug into a crash.
static plainKind(mixed $value): stringPlain-language phrase for a value's kind, so an authoring error reads "got text" rather than leaking PHP's type names ("string", "array").

Public for the reason every house lock helper is testable: a contender that wants to hold the lock OUTSIDE the engine — a test, an operator's battery script — must take exactly this file, not a lookalike.

TaskBuilder final class

Fluent builder for assembling a WorkflowTask.

MethodSummary
agent(string $agentType): selfSet the agent type (e.g. 'architect', 'coder', 'reviewer').
prompt(string $prompt): selfSet the task prompt text.
tools(array $tools): selfSet the list of available tools for this task.
timeout(int $timeout): selfSet the timeout in seconds for this task.
retries(int $retries): selfSet the number of retries allowed for this task.
isolation(Isolation $isolation): selfSet the workspace isolation level for this task.
name(string $name): selfSet an optional human-readable name for this task.
outputSchema(array|string|null $schema): selfConstrain this task's terminal turn to a JSON schema.
model(?string $model): selfThe model THIS task runs on (S2). The registry hands over the trimmed YAML string; null keeps the session's model byte-identical to today. Whether a named id is servable is decided ONCE, at dispatch, by the same ladder a delegation consults (\SugarCraft\Code\Agents\ModelChoice); a stage whose ask cannot be honoured refuses rather than dialing a stand-in. inherit is the delegation spelling kept alive here: it defers to the agent's own preset model, exactly as it does for a Task.
reject(string $pattern, int $atLeast = 1): selfReject the verifier's verdict when its completed output MATCHES a pattern.
resource(string $resource): selfO3: serialize this task's stage against every other stage naming the same host resource ('gpu', 'display', …). A blank name names nothing and is refused HERE, not silently dropped at the lock.
lockWaitSeconds(int $seconds): selfHow many seconds to wait for resource() before the stage fails loudly. Negative bounds are refused at build time; 0 is a legitimate ask-once-and-give-up.
stallTimeout(int $seconds): selfSet the idle-stall window in seconds (C7). Values below 1 are refused at set time — an instant-expiry window is never what an author meant; omit the key to stay on wall-clock bounds alone.
restarts(int $restarts): selfSet the stall-restart budget (C7): re-dispatches allowed when a worker EXPIRES SILENT, counted apart from retries(). Negative caps are refused at set time; 0 is the legitimate "never restart a stall".
input(array $spec): selfC9 fan-in join: attach an input: spec — a join over PRIOR stages' recorded rows, injected under the fixed input handle into this task's interpolation context immediately before its prompt is assembled. The spec is validated and normalized at set time by trustedJoin(); the engine never re-checks the shape.
votes(int $votes): selfP1-4: convene a verifier PANEL of $votes independent dispatches of this verifier, run concurrently on the stage's budget. The verdict passes when at least quorum() votes do not reject. Verifier slot only (the engine refuses any other placement before dispatch). 1, the default, is the single-verifier path, byte-identical.
lenses(array $lenses): selfP1-4: one lens per vote — {{lens}} in the verifier prompt becomes that vote's lens, so the panel judges from diverse perspectives (correctness, security, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical ones. The list's length must equal votes() (checked at build).
quorum(int $quorum): selfP1-4: how many votes must NOT reject for the verdict to pass, 1..votes (checked at build). Unset = the majority, floor(votes/2)+1.
preset(string $name): selfP1-6: run this task as the named agent preset (.candy-code/agents/<name>.md, resolved by the engine against the same roster Task uses). The preset supplies its system prompt, tools, disallowed tools, model, effort, isolation, step cap and permission mode; any key this task sets itself wins. An unknown name refuses the run before anything is dispatched. agent/Tasks::agent() stays a display label.
effort(Effort|string $effort): selfP1-6: the reasoning effort this task's agent asks for — low for mechanical stages, the high tiers only for the hardest judge/verify stages. A closed set: anything outside it is refused.
static trustedEffort(Effort|string $effort): EffortP1-6: the one parser for an effort spelling — an Effort case or its exact lowercase value.
static defaultQuorum(int $votes): intP1-4: the default quorum of a $votes panel — a strict majority, floor(votes/2)+1.
static trustedLenses(array $lenses): arrayP1-4: the lens-list shape law, shared by lenses() and the YAML loader: a non-empty list of non-empty strings (trimmed).
static verifierPanel(int $votes, ?array $lenses, ?int $quorum): voidP1-4: the cross-key law of a verifier panel, judged once all three keys are known (builder build() and the YAML loader): lenses, when present, name exactly one lens per vote, and a quorum can be met by the votes there are.
static trustedJoin(array $spec): arrayC9: the builder's parse-don't-validate gate for input: join specs.
static pcreErrorText(): stringLast PCRE compile failure as readable text (shared with the engine's fail-closed scan).
build(): WorkflowTaskAssemble and return the immutable WorkflowTask DTO.

Tasks final class
