WorkflowBuilder final class

Fluent builder for assembling a Workflow value object.

MethodSummary
name(string $name): selfSet the human-readable name of the workflow.
description(string $description): selfSet the brief description of what the workflow does.
stage(string $name, TaskBuilder|array $tasks, bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false): selfAdd a sequential stage: one task, or a list of tasks run one after another (roadmap 4.10-1).
parallel(string $name, array $tasks, bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false, array $from = []): selfAdd a parallel stage containing multiple tasks that run concurrently.
static fromSource(array $from): arrayP1-1: the SOURCE half of a from: spec — the one law the PHP builder and the YAML loader share (the loader coerces chunk/max itself and re-raises this method's refusals naming the file and stage). Exactly one of glob, stage or context:
pipeline(string $name, array $stages, bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false): selfAdd a pipeline stage containing nested stages that chain output to input.
map(string $name, array $from, array $steps, bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false): selfP1-2: add a type: map stage — every item of the from: source flows through $steps INDEPENDENTLY, with no barrier between steps (item A can be in step 3 while item B is in step 1); up to the stage width of item chains run at once. See WorkflowEngine executeMapStage() for the full run law and the stage's JSON output.
static mapStep(TaskBuilder $task, ?array $when = null): arrayP1-2: a task step for map(), optionally guarded per item by a when: clause over the item's earlier steps.
static mapVerification(string $name, TaskBuilder $task, TaskBuilder $verifier, ?array $when = null): arrayP1-2: a verification sub-stage step for map() — $task does the item's work, $verifier judges it (votes/lenses/quorum allowed).
static stepClause(array $clause, string $at = 'map step'): arrayP1-2: a map step's when: with every leaf's step: spelled stage: (the condition grammar's own key); a leaf carrying both is refused.
static clauseStages(array $node): arrayEvery stage name a NORMALIZED clause reads.
maxConcurrent(?int $n): selfSet how many agents of a parallel stage run at once (P0-3). Null, the default, leaves it unset: the engine runs Workflow::defaultConcurrency() of the host's CPUs, min(16, max(1, cpus - 2)). 0 is the explicit "no cap" — every task of a parallel stage is dispatched at once (the linter warns on it).
maxAgents(int $n): selfSet the run-wide agent-dispatch ceiling (P0-3, config.maxAgents, default Workflow::DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS). Every dispatch counts — retries, stall restarts, loop rounds and an included workflow's agents — and a dispatch past it fails its stage with "agent ceiling reached (N)".
maxTokens(?int $tokens): selfP1-7 config.maxTokens: a HARD run-wide token ceiling, checked before every dispatch (stage, task, fan-out item, vote, retry, loop round, included workflow). A dispatch that would start at or past it does not start; its stage fails "budget exhausted (spent X of Y tokens)" and the run PAUSES, so a resume under a raised ceiling continues. Also feeds {{budget.remaining}} and until: {budgetBelow: N}. Null clears it.
maxCost(int|float|null $usd): selfP1-7 config.maxCost: a HARD run-wide USD ceiling, with exactly the maxTokens() semantics ("budget exhausted (spent X of Y USD)"). Null clears it.
withVerification(string $name, TaskBuilder $task, TaskBuilder $verifier, bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false): selfReturn a builder with a verification stage appended: a task runs, then a verifier validates its result.
uses(string $name, string $included, array $with = [], bool $capture = false, bool $cache = false): selfAdd an include-compose stage (C11): the stage's body is the whole of another registered workflow, run to completion as ONE outer stage row.
timeout(int $seconds): selfSet the per-stage timeout in seconds.
when(array $clause): selfC2: attach a when: condition to the stage most recently added by stage(), parallel(), pipeline() or withVerification(). The clause is normalized and refused at call time by StageCondition::parse() — malformed grammar never rides into the built workflow (the same law the YAML loader enforces, and the same raw-English InvalidArgumentException shape TaskBuilder::reject() uses).
loop(array $loop): selfC4 + P1-5: attach a loop: round policy to the stage most recently added by stage(), parallel() or withVerification(). The map is closed — max (whole number ≥ 1), until (a C2 clause, which here also admits the loop-only leaves {dry: N} and {budgetBelow: N}) and the optional accumulate — normalized and refused at call time, the same raw-English InvalidArgumentException shape when() rides. A pipeline() stage and a uses() stage refuse it, so a built workflow can never carry a round policy its runner would not honour.
static parseAccumulate(mixed $accumulate): arrayP1-5: the ONE loop.accumulate parser (builder and YAML loader): {pointer: <RFC 6901>, key?: <RFC 6901>} → the same shape, both pointers checked well-formed ("" is legal: the whole row / item).
static clauseUsesOp(array $node, string $op): boolWhether a NORMALIZED condition carries a leaf with $op anywhere in it.
minSuccess(int|string $threshold): selfP1-3: attach a minSuccess: partial-failure tolerance to the stage most recently added by parallel(). The threshold is a whole number of agents (>= 1) or a "NN%" string (1-100%) of the stage's agents, rounded UP. Absent (the default) means all must succeed — byte-identical to every pre-P1-3 stage. When met despite failures the stage COMPLETES, its output ends with a [k of n agents failed: name (status), …] casualty line, and {{<stage>.failed}} interpolates the JSON list of failed result names. A minSuccess stage is exempt from stopOnFirstFailure(): cancelling siblings on the first casualty would defeat the tolerance the stage declares.
announce(string $template): selfP2-2: attach a settle announcement to the last stage — a template interpolated when the stage settles (its own {{<stage>.output}}, pointers and {{<stage>.failed}} in scope) and emitted on the run's announcement stream (WorkflowResult::$announcements, the engine's sink). Any stage shape may carry one.
static parseMinSuccess(mixed $threshold): arrayThe ONE minSuccess: parser, shared by minSuccess() and the YAML loader: an int (or quoted whole number) >= 1 normalizes to ['count' => n], an "NN%" string with NN in 1..100 to ['percent' => NN]. Floats, fractions and anything else are refused.
static requiredSuccesses(array $minSuccess, int $agents): intHow many of $agents must succeed under a normalized threshold: the count as written, or the percentage of $agents rounded UP (never 0).
static minSuccessLabel(array $minSuccess): stringThe author's spelling of a normalized threshold, for diagnostics.
stopOnFirstFailure(bool $stop): selfConfigure whether a parallel stage stops immediately on the first agent failure.
build(): WorkflowAssemble and return the immutable Workflow value object.

WorkflowEngine final class

Executes workflows sequentially, stage by stage.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly WorkflowRegistry $registry = new WorkflowRegistry(), private readonly AgentWorkerPool $pool = new AgentWorkerPool(), private ?AgentManager $agentManager = null, private readonly string $model = 'claude-sonnet-4-6', private readonly string $provider = 'anthropic', private readonly ?PermissionGate $permissionGate = null, private readonly ?string $environmentRoot = null, private readonly ?array $toolRegistry = null, private ?HookDispatcher $hookDispatcher = null)
model(): stringThe model every stage's agent is dispatched on.
provider(): stringThe provider label every stage's agent carries.
permissionGate(): ?PermissionGateThe gate this engine's sub-agents carry, or null when none was given.
setAgentManager(AgentManager $agentManager): voidAttach the AgentManager that parallel-stage sub-agents register with.
setAgentRoster(?iterable $roster): voidP1-6: the agent roster a task's preset: <name> resolves against — the list \SugarCraft\Code\Cli\Bootstrap::agentRoster() builds (built-ins < foreign < native project < native user presets), the same tiers Task resolves names in. Without one the engine falls back to its AgentManager's roster; with neither, a plan naming a preset is refused before anything is dispatched. Null clears it.
setAgentRosterSource(?\Closure $source): voidP1-6 / C5: setAgentRoster(), deferred — $source is called (once) the first time a preset has to be resolved or named, so a host can wire the session's roster (which reads preset files from disk) without paying for it on a run that names no preset. A source that throws leaves the engine with no roster, which refuses a preset run loudly.
presetNames(): ?arrayC5: the preset names a preset: may name on this engine — for WorkflowLinter::lint()'s $presetNames — or null when the engine has no roster at all (the lint then leaves the engine's pre-flight to refuse). Sorted.
static presetsNamedBy(Workflow $workflow): arrayC5: every preset name $workflow's tasks name, at any depth (stage, agents, pipeline steps, verification, map steps) — empty when none does, so a caller asks the roster only when it must.
setCpuCount(?int $cpus): voidPin the CPU count the default parallel width is computed from (P0-3: an unset maxConcurrent runs min(16, max(1, cpus - 2)) agents at once). Null restores host detection. A mutable-service setter for the setAgentManager() reason.
concurrencyFor(Workflow $workflow): ?intThe width a parallel stage of $workflow runs at (P0-3): the explicit maxConcurrent when one is set, null (no cap) for an explicit 0, and Workflow::defaultConcurrency() of the host's CPUs when unset.
agentManager(): ?AgentManagerThe AgentManager parallel stages route through, or null when none is set.
bindEngineBackend(EngineBackend $engine): voidPoint this engine's stages at the session's CURRENT backend, so every stage agent runs that backend's real tool loop (EngineExecutor).
bindHookDispatcher(?HookDispatcher $hookDispatcher): voidLate and mutable for the same reason as bindEngineBackend(): the session build site owns the hook chain and hands it over only after the launch workspace closes, through \SugarCraft\Code\Hooks\HookManager::armWorkflow(), before the engine's first run. Null keeps the constructor's documented unarmed contract — the engine announces nothing. The CLI verb seat never calls this, so a headless run stays byte-identical to the shape it has always had.
run(string $workflowPath, array $context = [], ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?int $budgetTokens = null): WorkflowResultLoad a workflow from the registry and execute it with the given context.
runFromPhp(callable|string $workflowClass, array $context = []): WorkflowResultExecute a workflow directly from a class name or callable that returns a Workflow.
runWorkflow(Workflow $workflow, array $context = [], ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?int $budgetTokens = null): WorkflowResultExecute a Workflow value the CALLER built — the model-authored plan the Workflow tool parses with WorkflowRegistry::fromYamlString() (roadmap 4.10-2) — through the same stage loop, declaration checks and fail-fast rule as run().
runPlan(Workflow $workflow, string $planYaml, array $context = [], ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?int $budgetTokens = null): WorkflowResultP1-8: run a Workflow-tool (model-authored) plan AS A RESUMABLE RUN.
resumePlan(string $runId, ?Workflow $workflow = null, ?string $planYaml = null, ?array $context = null, ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?int $budgetTokens = null): WorkflowResultP1-8: resume Workflow-tool run $runId with $workflow — the plan as it stands now, possibly edited; null re-reads the stored plan, which is what /workflow resume <runId> does.
runRecordDirectory(): stringP1-8: the directory this engine keeps run records in (.running/ under the registry's user tier) — capture files live in <runId>.stages/ under it (stageCapturePath()).
setAnnouncementSink(?\Closure $sink): voidP2-2: stream every announcement as it is made — $sink($line, $meta) with $meta = ['kind' => announce|truncation|casualties|budget|ceiling, 'stage' => ?string, 'workflowId' => string]. Called synchronously on the run's own path; a sink that throws is the caller's bug and is swallowed so it can never break the run. Null (the default) streams nothing — the lines are still collected on WorkflowResult::$announcements.
setRunStartedSink(?\Closure $sink): voidTell the caller a Workflow-tool run's ID the moment it exists, while the run is still in flight. The ID otherwise reaches the caller only in the final result, so a process killed mid-run (the model path exits 143 with no pause record) would leave the user nothing to resume by. The plan is stored at claim time, so the ID is resumable from this point on.
pause(string $workflowId): voidPersist the current state of a workflow so it can be resumed later.
resume(string $workflowId, ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null, ?int $budgetTokens = null): WorkflowResultReload a paused workflow from its persisted state and continue execution.
listWorkflows(): arrayList all available workflows from the registry.
status(string $workflowId): WorkflowStatusReturn the current status of a workflow run.
captureStageOutput(string $interruptId, int $stageIndex, StageResult $stageResult): stringS3: write a captured stage's FULL output to the run-scoped capture file, and return the text downstream stages see in its place: the file's path, up to CAPTURE_PREVIEW_BYTES bytes of the output, and — when the output was longer — a marked truncation naming the file's size. The write publishes by rename, the same discipline as the pause file: a reader never sees half a capture.
static stageCapturePath(string $pauseDir, string $interruptId, int $stageIndex, string $stageName): stringWhere a captured stage's output lands: a run-scoped directory beside the pause record — <pause-dir>/<id>.stages/<index>-<stage-slug>.txt. Public so a reader (a test, a follow-up agent told the path) can resolve the layout from the run's own facts, not from a second copy of the naming rule. Capture files OUTLIVE the run's clean terminal: withdrawal removes the pause record, not the work products — see WORKFLOWS.md.
setSignalPauseHandler(?\Closure $observer): voidInstall (or clear with null) the observer the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler consults on a cooperative pause — see self::$signalPauseHandler. Call BEFORE the run that may be signalled; the handler reads the property at signal time.

hasFindings(): bool

Literal-English rows like the lint report.
static readPauseLedger(string $workflowsPath, string $identifier): ?arrayRead the paused-run ledger for an identifier the way the engine's own pauseFileFor lookup does, minus the in-process memo it cannot share: exact <id>.json first, then a per-file match on the recorded workflowId (run ids are re-minted per process, so a file whose NAME is a stale id but whose CONTENT records the asked-for id must still be found). Returns null when no readable file names that run — a live run's per-stage detail lives in the engine's private result memo, not on the file plane, and the command prints its plain status line instead (reported seam).

It is the scheduling half of what \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::scheduleAutoCommit() does today, returned as a raw factory instead of a Cmd: the host wraps it in its own machinery (Cmd::promise for the TUI, a loop task for a server).
withTrailer(string $trailer): self
withSessionId(string $sessionId): self

Null when nothing is left to commit; a string says why nothing can be.
commitEdit(string $absolutePath, \Closure $subject, ?array $workspace): ?arrayCommit the one file an Edit/Write just changed. Its subject is $subject applied to the file's path relative to the work tree (see CommitMessageWriter::fromDescription()). Null when there is nothing to commit — not in this work tree (a nested repository's file included), ignored, or unchanged; otherwise the commit's outcome.
commit(array $paths, string $subject, string $kind = 'edit'): arrayCommit $paths (relative to the top level) as they are in the work tree, with $subject and the trailer, running the user's hooks. On failure the paths are unstaged again and the reason is the hook's or git's own words.
changedPaths(): arrayEvery path the work tree changed since HEAD — modified, added, deleted, renamed (C-AGT-6.a, roadmap GAP-GIT-03, for /commit). Unlike self::dirtyAmong(), which filters a candidate list, this walks the whole tree with no pathspec, and it KEEPS a rename's source: git add -A over both sides records the move, while staging only the destination would split it into an unrelated deletion left behind.
draftDiff(array $paths): stringThe bounded diff self::commitAll() drafts a message from: the same byte cap the turn-mode commit feeds the title model, so a manual /commit asks it with exactly what an automatic one would (C-AGT-6.a).
commitAll(string $subject): arrayCommit EVERY changed path through the hardened self::commit() path, recorded with kind command — which is what lets /undo revert a manual /commit (C-AGT-6.a, roadmap GAP-GIT-03): undo() reverts every kind but snapshot, and the record is session-scoped exactly like the turn-mode commit's, so the session's own /undo finds it first.
hasCommits(): boolWhether this session has made an auto-commit in this repository.
undo(): arrayRevert the last commit if this session made it — Aider's /undo: git checkout HEAD~1 -- <files> and git reset --soft HEAD~1, so the files and the index go back and nothing else moves. A snapshot of the user's own changes is un-committed instead: reset --soft then unstage, so their changes are back where they were — uncommitted, in the files.

CheckpointDiff final class

What changed in the project's files since a workspace checkpoint (item 3.A-2, /diff [n]): the changed paths and a unified patch, checkpoint on the left, the files as they are now on the right.

Neither side is the work tree, so the answer cannot drift while it is being read.

summaryLines(): arrayOne line per changed path, M path style, in git's order — the same screen-safe treatment as the patch, since a path is file-system text.

CommitMessageWriter final class

The one-line Conventional-Commits subject an auto-commit carries (step 3.G): Aider's commit prompt asked of the cheap tool-less title model, and what to do when there is no model, or its answer is unusable.

MethodSummary
static request(string $diff, string $context = ''): arrayThe request for the title model: the prompt, then the diff and the request that produced it.
static subjectFrom(string $reply): ?stringThe model's reply as a commit subject, or null when no line of it is usable. A reply without a type gets chore: .
static fallback(array $paths, string $verb = 'update'): stringA deterministic subject for $paths when there is no model to ask or its answer was unusable.
static fromDescription(string $description, array $paths): stringThe edit-mode subject: the description the model already wrote for the Edit/Write call ("Rename the legacy config helper"), typed by the path it touched. edit mode asks no model per edit — that would be an unbilled call inside the tool chain on every edit — so the call's own description is the message.

GhRunner final class

One bounded gh invocation at a time, for the reads the app makes of the user's own GitHub host — today the @pr:<n> mention (\SugarCraft\Code\Attachments\ContextMentions's pr leg), which shows the agent a pull request as filed rather than as the working tree claims.

MethodSummary
static new(string $cwd): selfA runner whose calls start in $cwd and let gh find the repository.
static available(): boolWhether a gh executable is on PATH at all — a stat walk, no spawn.
withTimeout(float $seconds): selfBound each call at $seconds.
cwd(): string
capture(?int $maxBytes, string ...$args): arrayRun gh <args> retaining at most $maxBytes of each stream (null: no bound) and hand back the capture's OWN account of the cut — the bytes each stream dropped and whether the cut landed mid-line — for a caller that announces truncation itself rather than failing on it.
shellCommand(string ...$args): stringThe POSIX sh line for the same argv, for inspection only: nothing spawns through it. capture() hands proc_open the argv itself, which is what runs on Windows too, where this string would be read by cmd.exe and is not a command anyone should trust.

GitRunner final class

One bounded git invocation at a time, for the code that drives git on the app's own behalf — workspace checkpoints (item 3.A-1), auto-commit (3.G) next — and for the reads it makes for the model: the environment block's git fields and the @diff mention (capture()).

MethodSummary
static new(string $cwd): selfA runner whose calls start in $cwd and let git discover the repository.
static available(): boolWhether a git executable is on PATH at all — a stat walk, no spawn.
withGitDir(string $gitDir, ?string $workTree = null): selfPin the repository (--git-dir) and, optionally, its work tree.
withIndexFile(?string $indexFile): selfRun against $indexFile (GIT_INDEX_FILE) instead of the repository's own index.
withInheritedGitEnv(bool $inherit = true): selfKeep the inherited GIT_* location and config variables instead of scrubbing them. For a READ of the user's repository as the user would see it — the environment block, @diff — where an exported GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES (or GIT_DIR) is the user's own statement of where their repository is. A checkpoint pins its repository with withGitDir() and must not be redirected, so it never sets this.
withTimeout(float $seconds): selfBound each call at $seconds.
withDeadline(?float $epochSeconds): selfShare one wall-clock budget across every call: a call starting after $epochSeconds fails as timed out without spawning, and one starting before it is bounded by whichever of the two limits comes first.
cwd(): string
gitDir(): ?string
workTree(): ?string
deadline(): ?floatThe shared wall-clock deadline, or null when only the per-call bound applies.
run(string ...$args): arrayRun git <args>.
runWithInput(string $input, string ...$args): arrayRun git <args> with $input on its stdin — update-index --stdin, update-ref --stdin. The input goes through a private temp file and a file descriptor for the child's stdin, because the bounded spawn closes the stdin pipe at once by design.
capture(?int $maxBytes, string ...$args): arrayRun git <args> retaining at most $maxBytes of each stream (null: no bound) and hand back the capture's OWN account of the cut — the bytes each stream dropped and whether the cut landed mid-line — for a caller that announces truncation itself rather than failing on it.
shellCommand(string ...$args): stringThe POSIX sh command line capture() would spawn, for the one caller that has no bounded spawn left: \SugarCraft\Code\Context\EnvironmentBlock's branch read on a build with proc_open disabled hands it to shell_exec, which takes no environment argument, so the scrub and the GIT_* pins have to ride in the string. It is POSIX-only by nature — shell_exec on Windows is cmd.exe — so a Windows caller must not use it. It does not change directory: such a caller passes -C <dir> in $args.

PrStatusCache final class

C-AGT-6.e (R13): the PR + CI read-out behind the web's session chips.

MethodSummary
static observe(?string $branch, ?string $root, LoopInterface $loop): ?arrayRegister the watch for one summary build and answer from the cache.
static sweep(): voidOne refresh beat: drop dead watches, then fetch at most the one entry whose due time passed longest ago. Bounded work by construction — a summary storm cannot queue a gh run per row through one sweep.
static verdict(mixed $rollup): stringFold one statusCheckRollup array into the chip's single word.
static useFetcherForTesting(?callable $fetcher): void
static useClockForTesting(?callable $clock): void
static clearForTesting(): voidFull process-state reset, seams included; test setUp and tearDown.

ShadowGarbageCollector final class

Bounded garbage collection for ShadowRepo directories (item 3.A-2, the W2 hand-off from 3.A-1).

MethodSummary
static collectIfDue(string $gitDir, int $looseObjectThreshold = self::LOOSE_OBJECT_THRESHOLD, string $pruneExpiry = self::PRUNE_EXPIRY, ?int $now = null): arrayCollect the shadow repository at $gitDir if it is due.

ShadowRepo final class

The private git directory workspace checkpoints use for a project that is not a git work tree (item 3.A-1; opencode's snapshot dir, Kilo/Cline's shadow repository).

MethodSummary
static forRoot(string $root, string $baseDir): ?selfThe shadow repository for $root under $baseDir, or null when $root is not an existing directory.
gitDir(): string
workTree(): string
refusal(): ?stringWhy this shadow repository cannot be used, or null when it can.
ensure(GitRunner $git, array $excludes): ?stringCreate the repository on first use, with $excludes as its info/exclude. Null on success, the reason otherwise.

WorkspaceCheckpointer final class

Snapshots of the project's FILES, one per user turn, so a turn's edits can be undone (item 3.A-1). /rewind --files|--both, /undo, /redo and /diff (item 3.A-2, \SugarCraft\Code\Chat::handleRewindCommand()) are built on restore(), changes() and trees().

MethodSummary
static new(string $root): selfA checkpointer for the project at $root.
withShadowBase(?string $directory): selfWhere shadow repositories for non-git projects go; null (the default) refuses non-git projects.
withCaptureBudget(float $seconds): selfBound a capture at $seconds instead of CAPTURE_BUDGET_SECONDS.
root(): string
static refFor(string $sessionId, int $index): stringThe pinning ref for checkpoint $index of $sessionId. A session id that is not a safe ref component is hashed, so any id maps to a valid, distinct name.
static refusalFor(string $root): ?stringWhy checkpoints are refused at $root, or null when they are allowed.
static forgetDisabled(): voidRe-enable every directory a timed-out capture switched off. For tests.
capture(string $sessionId, int $index): arraySnapshot the workspace for checkpoint $index of $sessionId and pin it.
restore(array $workspace): arrayPut the files back the way checkpoint $workspace recorded them.
changes(array $workspace): array|stringWhat a restore of $workspace would change: [status, path] pairs as git diff --name-status <checkpoint> <now> spells them (A = created since, so a restore deletes it; D/M/T = a restore rewrites it), empty when it would change nothing, or the reason no answer is possible.
trees(array $workspace): array|stringThe runner, the snapshot's tree and the tree the workspace would snapshot to now — what CheckpointDiff compares — or the reason no answer is possible. Unlike restore() and changes(), a HEAD that has moved since the checkpoint is not a refusal here: a diff changes nothing, and the commits since are part of what it shows.
static dropRefs(array $workspaces): voidDelete the pinning refs of every captured shape in $workspaces, one update-ref --stdin per repository. Best effort: a repository that is gone has no refs left to leak.
static copyRefs(array $pairs): voidPin each captured shape's commit under a second ref, for a session copied by /branch.
static isCaptured(mixed $workspace): boolWhether $workspace is a pinned snapshot (as opposed to a refusal, a failure, or something that is not a stored shape at all).
static diffTrees(GitRunner $git, string $from, string $to): ?array[status, path] pairs of git diff-tree --name-status <from> <to>, or null when git failed.

Configuration

Settings come from five layers, read through LayeredSettings. On a key present in more than one file, the highest listed file wins; row 5 is the machine's and outranks the rest.

#FileWhoseRead when
1<root>/.candy-code/settings.jsonthe project's, committedthe project root is listed in trustedProjectSettings and an entry point named it
2<root>/.candy-code/settings.local.jsonthe project's, git-ignoredsame gate as row 1
3~/.candy-code/settings.jsonyours, hand-authoredalways, when $HOME resolves
4~/.candy-code/config.jsonyours, partly written by the CLIalways, or at the file --config <path> names; with no resolvable home directory, a launch refuses
5/etc/candy-code/config.jsonthe machine administrator; read-only to candy-codealways

Project trust is opt-in. A cloned repository cannot change your settings, and its settings, hooks, .mcp.json and !`cmd` shell blocks are read only after you list the project root under the trustedProject* keys (see permissions and safety). A project's skills, rules and agent presets load from the repository without that listing; only a project skill's pre-approvals (allowed-tools) wait for trustedProjectCommands. Every key, its default and when a change takes effect are in docs/SETTINGS.md. Environment variables are in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md. Themes, keybindings and output styles have their own pages: THEMES.md and KEYBINDINGS.md.

Permissions and safety

Every tool call passes a PreToolUse hook chain, whose last entry is the PermissionGate. The gate decides in three steps: a circuit breaker that denies rm -rf / and rm -rf ~ in every mode, then your rules (first match wins), then the active mode. Set the mode with --permission-mode, CANDY_CODE_PERMISSION_MODE, or permissionMode in config, and switch it in the TUI with /permissions mode. Alt+M toggles plan mode only.

ModeRuns without askingAsks, or is refused
defaultread tools such as Read, Glob and Grep, and read-only shell lines (ls, git log, grep and similar)asks for writes, other shell commands and network calls; -p refuses them
accept-editsin-project Edit and Write, mkdir, touch and rmdir on paths below the working directory, and read-only shell linesevery other shell command asks, rm, mv and cp included, as does WebFetch
planread-only Bash, and Markdown plans in .candy-code/plans/refuses everything else, and asks for WebFetch and WebSearch; the model leaves with PlanExit
autocalls the SafetyClassifier passesa security finding asks; other flagged calls are refused, or reviewed by the title model with autoReview
dont-askread-only tools, such as Read and Greprefuses everything else, WebFetch included, without prompting
bypass-permissionseverything, except the circuit breaker and your explicit deny rulesnothing

Two notes. The circuit breaker and deny rules hold in every mode, bypass-permissions included. The Bash sandbox is off by default (bashSandbox). The security model is summarized in the security section, and the full gate is in docs/PERMISSIONS.md.

76 slash commands, one row per spec file under builtin-commands/. The same rows sit in the marker block of docs/COMMANDS.md. Tools

Every plain launch builds 38 built-in tools. The runtime name is the one a permission rule or allowedTools entry uses; the class is the file under src/Tools/BuiltIn/. The permission class is the one each tool declares with its #[BuiltInTool] attribute, or, for Task, BoardRead and BoardPost, which carry no attribute, the one ToolCatalog declares for them. read-only and no-ask tools never prompt; write-capable tools go through the mode's rules; mode default tools fall through to the mode's own answer. Sessions, checkpoints, undo and rewind

  • Sessions. Each conversation is a session in ~/.candy-code/session.db. /sessions lists and searches them, /rename names one, /fork and /branch split a conversation, /handoff starts a fresh session from a state summary, and /session-pin keeps one at the top of the list.
  • Checkpoints. A checkpoint is taken for each turn that edits files. /diff shows what changed since a checkpoint.
  • Undo and rewind. /undo takes back the last turn, or reverts the last auto-commit. /rewind [n] [--chat|--files|--both] restores an earlier checkpoint for the conversation, the files, or both. /redo steps forward again over what was taken back.
  • Cost and pruning. /usage folds the durable spend ledger by day, model and source, /budget caps a session's spend, and /pruning sets how the session prunes its context.

The FAQ answers the common versions of these questions: how do I undo what the agent changed, how do I keep a session from being pruned, and how do I cap the cost.

Hooks, skills, MCP and sub-agents

  • Hooks. Sixteen hook events, starting with PreToolUse. A hook returns allow, deny, modify or ask, and /hooks lists the chain and its log. Full reference: docs/HOOKS.md.
  • Skills. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file. Ten are built in. /skills lists and toggles them, and the Skill tool loads one by name. Full reference: docs/SKILLS.md.
  • MCP. Servers listed in .mcp.json are started after you trust the project, and /mcp lists, adds, logs in to and removes them. candy-code mcp serve runs the stdio host. Full reference: docs/MCP.md.
  • Sub-agents. The Task tool runs a preset as a sub-agent, and /agents lists the roster and opens a running agent's view. Presets are authored as described in docs/AGENTS_AUTHORING.md; the roster is in docs/AGENTS.md.

Server, web UI and editors

  • candy-code serve runs sessions headless behind an authenticated WebSocket. It binds 127.0.0.1 by default; any other address needs --allow-remote. Pin the clients with --allowed-host and --allowed-ips.
  • candy-code attach connects a terminal to a running server, and the CandyCodeWeb page drives the same sessions from a browser.
  • candy-code acp runs the Agent Client Protocol on stdio for editors. docs/ACP.md has the setup for Zed. JetBrains IDEs and Neovim take the same command and argument in their own ACP agent settings, as the guide describes.

The wire protocol and its auth model are in docs/SERVER.md.

Maintenance: gc, usage and doctor

candy-code gc reports and reclaims disk used by the session store. The verbs run from a read-only look to a destructive purge, and the order below is the order to use them in. Only gc purge and gc vacuum write. gc vacuum writes only with --force; gc purge asks you to confirm at the terminal unless you pass --force, and in JSON mode it needs --dry-run or --force.

The session store is created on the first run. On a machine that has never started candy-code, the commands below stop with cannot open the session store, so start candy-code once first (even candy-code -p "hello").

candy-code gc status                         # where the bytes are (read-only)
candy-code gc sessions --sort size --limit 20 # one row per session, real bytes (read-only)
candy-code gc analyze --top 10                # ranking, growth and orphan counts (read-only)
candy-code gc purge --older-than 90d --dry-run   # plan the purge; writes nothing
candy-code gc purge --older-than 90d --force     # the same plan, applied

Always run --dry-run first and read the plan. gc purge needs at least one filter, strip or clean flag, and it never prunes a session that --keep-latest protects. Each flag is documented in docs/GC.md.

  • candy-code usage prints the durable spend ledger, the CLI form of the /usage command. See docs/USAGE.md.
  • candy-code doctor runs the install checks and reports each row, including the sandbox row that says whether the Bash jail is enabled. /doctor runs the same checks inside a session.

Troubleshooting and FAQ

  • The TUI says "echo" and the model never answers: FAQ. Provider setup problems are in TROUBLESHOOTING.
  • candy-code exits 2 immediately and will not start: TROUBLESHOOTING. The exit codes are listed at the top of that page.
  • Skills or MCP tools are missing, or a hook never fires: skills, MCP, hooks.
  • Every Bash call is refused: TROUBLESHOOTING. Why a prompt appeared at all: FAQ.
  • Session store errors: TROUBLESHOOTING. The full troubleshooting guide has more than twenty entries; start with docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

Security model

  • Model output is untrusted. Tool calls, edits and shell commands go through the permission gate; the circuit breaker, your rules and the mode decide each one.
  • Project files are ignored until trusted. A project's settings, hooks and .mcp.json are read only after you trust the project, and a changed MCP server definition is refused until you approve it again.
  • The server listens on loopback. candy-code serve binds 127.0.0.1 by default, and every client must authenticate. Put TLS in front of it before you expose it.
  • Secrets are plain text on disk. Provider keys saved by candy-code login sit in ~/.candy-code/config.json unless you pass --keychain. The session database is not encrypted.
  • The Bash sandbox is opt-in. With bashSandbox off, a Bash call runs with your privileges. When it is on, Seatbelt runs on macOS and Bubblewrap on other systems.

The threat model, trust boundaries, supported versions and how to report a vulnerability are in docs/SECURITY.md.

Demos

VHS-recorded GIFs of every PHP example shipped with the app; the workflow YAML under examples/workflows/ ships without a recording. Six VHS tapes ship in .vhs/. Each tape is rendered to a GIF by the CI job in vhs.yml, which commits the result; the GIFs are not rendered by hand.

Chat

A chat session on examples/echo-chat.php, with Markdown-rendered replies. Tape: chat.tape.

Agents

The sub-agent dashboard from examples/agent-dashboard.php. Tape: agents.tape.

CLI

The command-line help, from ./bin/candy-code --help. Tape: cli.tape.

Diff

The unified diff rendered for an Edit result, from examples/edit-diff.php. Tape: diff.tape.

Media form

The generation form, from examples/media-demo.php. Tape: media-form.tape.

Permission

A permission prompt for a guarded tool call, answered with n, from examples/permission-prompt.php. Tape: permission.tape.

Key classes

The public classes a library user is most likely to touch, grouped by namespace under SugarCraft\Code\.

ClassMethodDescription
Providers\ProviderInterfacecomplete(CompleteRequest): CompleteResponseThe single LLM abstraction: one batch completion
Providers\ProviderInterfacecompleteStream(CompleteRequest): GeneratorThe same call, yielded as streaming chunks
Providers\ProviderInterfacesupportsStreaming(), supportsVision(), contextWindow(), costPer1kTokens(model, direction)Capability and cost introspection, so callers do not guess
Backend\EngineBackendnew(provider, model)Factory; bridges the chat Backend seam to the agent engine
Backend\EngineBackendwithTools(tools), withHooks(manager), withSkillRegistry(registry), withMaxSteps(n)Fluent wiring of the agent loop; each call returns a new instance
Backend\EngineBackendcomplete(history, ?onToken, ?onEvent, …): MessageRuns one bounded agentic turn, emitting tool-lifecycle events
Hooks\HookManagerregisterBuiltIns(): voidRegisters ProtectFilesHook, ConfirmRemoveHook and AuditHook
Hooks\HookManagerpreToolUse(HookContext): HookResultGates a tool call: allow, deny, modify or ask
Hooks\HookManagerresolveAsk(ask, approved, feedback)Settles an answered ask into a final allow or deny
Skills\SkillRegistryfindForPrompt(prompt): arrayMatches discovered SKILL.md files to the current turn
Skills\SkillRegistryforPaths(paths): arrayPath-scoped skills for files a tool just touched
Skills\SkillRegistryisAutoInvocable(name), isUserInvocable(name), isContextFork(name)Frontmatter flags, enforced
Agents\AgentPreset__construct(name, description, tools, disallowedTools, model, permissionMode, maxTurns, skills, mcpServers, …)Readonly sub-agent descriptor: model, tool allow and deny lists, skills, MCP allowlist, effort, isolation
MCP\McpClientstartServers(), stopServers()Launches and tears down the configured stdio and HTTP MCP servers
MCP\McpClientlistTools(), callTool(server, tool, args, …), callToolByName(tool, args)Discovers and invokes MCP tools, filtered by the active preset's allowlist
Permissions\PermissionGateevaluate(ToolCall, ?projectRoot, ?sessionId): PermissionDecisionEvaluates a call against the active mode, behind the mode-independent circuit breaker
Permissions\PermissionGatemode(): PermissionModeOne of default, accept-edits, plan, auto, dont-ask, bypass-permissions
Workflows\WorkflowEnginerun(workflowPath, context, …): WorkflowResultExecutes a YAML multi-stage agent pipeline
Workflows\WorkflowEnginerunFromPhp(workflowClass, context): WorkflowResultThe same, from the PHP builder DSL
Workflows\WorkflowEnginepause(id), resume(id, …), status(id): WorkflowStatusStage-granularity pause and resume across a signal
Session\SessionStorecreateSession(id, provider, model, ?systemPrompt, ?name, …)Opens a session row in the SQLite (WAL) store
Session\SessionStoreaddMessage(sessionId, message), addToolCall(sessionId, messageId, toolCall)Appends a turn and its tool calls, foreign-key enforced
Session\SessionStorelistSessions(limit), forkSession(id), renameSession(id, name)Back the /sessions, /fork and /rename commands
Session\SessionStorepruneSessions(daysOld, ?exemptSessionId): intOpt-in retention sweep; never drops a named or resuming session
